PREFACE 

The utter impossibility of reconciling the teachings and practices of Jesus Christ and His Apostles with the Doctrines of the Trinity in their various and conflicting statements has caused the author to try to find out the true relationship of Jesus Christ to His Divine 

Father; as the Scriptures declare Jesus Christ to be the "Son of 

God," "Son of the Father," "Angel of God," "Angel of the Covenant," "Word of God," "First-born of all creation," "The beginning of the creation of God," "The Word made flesh," and a host of other quotations too numerous to mention, where Christ declares His dependence upon His Divine Father for His existence, doctrine, works, and for all that He is, has, and does. 

The author wishes to show the many inconsistencies, contradictions, and absurdities of the doctrines of the Trinity with the Christian teachings and practices of Jesus Christ and His Apostles, and do his bit in assisting to bless, instruct, ennoble, and save mankind.

Christianity and The Trinitarian 

Doctrine 

CHAPTER I. 

Our Divine Father in heaven, being the only uncreate, absolute and independent person, spirit, being or thing, is, in the very nature of the case, the creator and sovereign Lord of all other spirits, persons, beings or things; whatsoever be their nature, substance, essence or state of existence.

Our Divine Father being the creator and sovereign Lord of all other rational persons, spirits or beings without exception, as soon as a created intelligence came into existence, the law governing the relation of that intelligence belongs exclusively or absolutely to our Divine Father in heaven as creator and sustainer of all things. 

The glory, honor, and precedence of all our Divine Father's creation belong exclusively and unqualifiedly to our Divine Father's glorious and well-beloved Son the Word who was the first-born creature of all our Divine Father's creation. God, our Divine Father's glorious Son the Word, who in His superangelical state of existence was the first intelligence of our Divine Father's creation coming under the absolute and independent authority of our Divine Father's power, was therefore the first to meet the demands of His Divine Father's rule of law by which every rational character is to be tested. 

Because of our Divine Father's love for the Word, the first-born Son of all His creation; and because of the Word's perfect obedience, love and devotion to His Divine Father, the author of His being, life, and power, His Divine Father chose to use Him as His agent in the making of all things else of His creation; so that He might have the preeminence over all things else of His Divine Father's creation. 

Thus did the well-beloved and glorious Son, the "Word of God," by choice of His Divine Father become the agent of God, His Divine Father, in the creation of all angels, worlds, principalities and powers; but His God, our Divine Father, likewise chose Him to be the Re-

deemer and Savior of the human family by incarnating the Word, His first-born Son of creation in a body of flesh and blood through the operation of His spirit. 

Thus did our Divine Father's glorious and well-beloved Son, the Word, through choice of our Divine Father and the Son's obedience and devotion to His Divine Father's will become head over all His Divine Father's creation, both men and angels, being subject unto Him so that He became not only a superangelical spirit being but perfect man through the creative power of His Divine Father's omnipotent spirit.

It is our Divine Father's in heaven absolute prerogative of right, as Creator and Life-giver or Father to exercise absolute and independent jurisdiction over the first-born Son of His creation, the Word, and all creatures and things created through Him as His agent--because of His obsolute perfection in love, power, knowledge, wisdom and universal presence-so our Divine Father has absolute and unqualified right to say what is the law which should govern between, not only Himself and His creatures, but between His creatures likewise.

To be in a state of salvation is not only to believe in God, our Divine Father in heaven, but to render oneself in full harmony with the knowledge he receives in full performance of duty both toward 

God, and His fellow creatures.

To be in harmony with God, our Divine Father's plans and purposes, one must fully subscribe or conform his life's conduct to good uses as laid down in the precepts and doctrine of God's glorious Son, the Word incarnate who was appointed the Prince, Governor, and Savior to those only who abide by His rules of government. A prince means a governor or ruler who holds His sway of authority from Him who clothed him with authority; and He who has all power and authority is the God and Father of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ and of all things else besides. 

The perfect man, Adam, was made a prince and ruler of the earth; but Jesus Christ, God's glorious Son, the Word incarnated, was made a prince and ruler of mankind by our Divine Father in heaven as the creator and sustainer of all things visible and invisible All power and authority belong and reside in our Divine Father in heaven as the creator of all spirits, persons and things other than His own immutable being, and all power and authority reside in Him absolutely and independently, and is exercised by Him personally or mediately through His created agencies.

When our Divine Father in heaven grants power or authority to anyone he is under obligation to exercise that authority in perfect harmony with His Divine Father's will under the penalty of death and destruction.

We have conclusive scriptural proof that Adam was to render servile obedience to his Divine Creator for his dominion of life and government in the earth, the same as the incarnate Word, God's glorious Son, was to render obedience to His Divine Creator for 

His dominion over men and angels.

All life and being, and all right to life and being is terminated or sustained by our Divine Father in accordance with His righteous laws and purposes. The giving and upholding of all life and being are the gifts of our Divine Father in heaven; and His granted grace of repentance through faith in His glorious Son, the incarnate Word, who gave His flesh and blood as a vicarious atonement in man's behalf, is man's only means of salvation from death and self-destruction to the life eternal, immortal, and everlasting.

The incarnated Word of God, our Father's in heaven only begotten Son, through Whom He revealed, manifested, represented and executed His plan for man's salvation from death and the grave is God's only mediator between Himself and His creatures. It is God our Divine Father's will that fallen man should be ransomed from death and the grave; but man's inability, in his fallen state, to make restitution unto his Divine Creator for the transgression of His law, necessitated that some righteous person not of the fallen race of Adam should pay the debt of redemption for man who fell through Adam's transgression. As man was of himself unable to give to his 

Divine maker his just deserts of perfect obedience of fealty and devotion, because of the inherent imperfections of Adam transmitted to him, it necessitated a ransomer or redeemer who was able to pay to Divine justice the debt which man owed to his Divine Creator. 

The Divine grace of our Father in heaven provided a redeemer in the person of His glorious, superangelical, first-born Son of all creation, the Word, by incarnating His glorious Son, the Word, in a robe of flesh and blood through the infinite, absolute and omnipotent power of His spirit. So the Word, the first-born Son of our Divine 

Father's creation, was incarnated, conceived, and born of the Virgin Mary through the creative power of our Divine Father's spirit, to the end that He would give the body of His perfect manhood as a ransom for the redemption of mankind, "that whosoever believeth on him should not perish but have everlasting life," through the

resurrection from the dead at the second appearing of Jesus Christ. 

Thus did God, our infinite Father transfer His superangelical, glorious first-born Son of all creation from the plane of a superangelical spirit-being or person to a perfect human plane by incarnating His first-born Son of all creation by conception and generation of a woman with a perfect human body that He might become the Ransomer or Redeemer of mankind by giving His body of flesh and blood in sacrificial offering for all who through faith and repentance accept Him as their Lord and Redeemer by turning from sin unto God.

That the Word, God's first-born Son of all creation, was created perfect, harmless, holy, and undefiled; and that He remained so throughout His preexistent, antemundane state of existence until He was begotten by the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father through His incarnation, conception, and generation of a woman, the Virgin Mary; and that He maintained during His earthly life an immaculately pure and stainless life from sin; He proved to the world and to His infinite God and Father the absolute perfection of His life by the things which He taught, and the things which He suffered. 

God's glorious Son, the "Word of God," is the only person created or born, who was both created and also born by the immediate operation of His Divine Father's spirit. God's first-born Son of creation, as a superangelical spirit-being was called the "Word of God," but after His incarnation, conception and generation as man He was called God's only begotten Son, Jesus, the Christ. He being in the beginning created, and in the fullness of time conceived by the immediate operation of His Divine Father's spirit, so that He is the only being, person or spirit, who was begotten in His creation or begotten in His incarnation, conception and generation by the immediate operation of His Divine Father's spirit without any other intervening agency of His Divine Father in heaven. All things else of our Divine Father's creation not only existed after His glorious Son, the Word's creation; but all things else of our Divine Father's creation were created through His glorious Son, this superangelical spirit, the "Word of God;" and in this respect He has the preeminence over all others of His Divine Father's creation; and the glory of participating in all the works of His Divine Father's creation other than His own personal being which is the only exception according to the Divine record.

It was the purpose and the plan of our Divine Father in heaven that the Word, His first-born Son of all creation, should become a

perfect man so that He would not only have the preeminence in creation only, but also the preeminence in the plan of salvation and redemption of the world; and for this purpose God caused the Word, His first-born Son of creation, to become incarnate that He might become a perfect man to fulfill the place of Adam, who had fallen from grace through disobedience to God's commands and the requirements of His holy law. 

Though the glorious Son of God, the Word, was superior to the angels, yet He condescended to take upon Himself the form and fashion of a man for the ostensible purpose of giving His body, by making it a vicarious atonement or sacrifice for fallen man, that by the grace of God He might taste death for every man, by fulfilling the requirements of God's holy law in man's room and stead, that whosoever would, through repentance, turn to God should not perish, but have everlasting life.

The incarnate Word, Jesus Christ, God's only begotten Son, was to fulfill for Adam, the representative of our race, the requirements. of God's holy law. For this purpose God sent His beloved and glorious Son, the Word, into the world that He might take upon Himself the penalty of death due to Adam's transgression. Thus 

Christ, the Word incarnated, died for man in order to pay the ransom price for Adam and his offspring, that through faith and obedience to Him their redemption is complete.

God received in man's behalf the vicarious atonement of His glorious Son, the incarnate Word, Jesus Christ as a substitute for the life of Adam and his posterity in order that penitent man might be justified through faith in Christ.

This sin offering made by Jesus Christ had been foreshadowed by the ceremonies which God caused the children of Israel to annually perform in connection with their atonement day as required by law. 

The application of the merit of Christ's sacrifice is made available to those only who through faith and repentance have the answer of a good conscience toward God. The merits of Christ's death is available to all, but is effective only to those who accept Jesus Christ the Son of God as their atonement of the New Covenant for the reconciliation of all men unto God. Christ died for man's sin, and God raised Him from the dead for the justification of man. 

The shedding of the blood of Jesus Christ, the perfect man, was God's chosen way whereby He could be just and thé justifier of man through a substitute for the forfeited life of Adam and his posterity. The justice of God accepts the life-blood of the perfect

man Jesus to the end that in due time the value of that sacrifice might be made available for the benefit of all men in every age and clime.

To be brought in harmony with God, man should know something of God's provision; that through the grace of repentance toward 

God; man must believe that the shed blood of Jesus Christ is the purchase price of his redemption from the penalty of sin which is death; and that it is the only way, means or manner in which man has the opportunity to be reconciled to God. 

There is no other plan given among men than that provided by our Divine Father in heaven through the Word incarnate, our Divine Father's only begotten Son Jesus Christ, whereby we must be saved. 

Our Divine Father's superangelical first-born Son of all creation was incarnated by His Divine Father's spirit into our humanity that He might die for man, because man being cut off from his earthly life might through Christ's death for man be engrafted through Christ's blood to partake of everlasting life through a glorious resurrection at the appearing of Jesus Christ at the end of this Gospel Age which is near at hand, even at the door of the next century, according to Divine revelation.

The purpose of the incarnation of God's first-born Son of all creation, the "Word of God," was that a way might be opened for man to be reconciled to God. The plan included or embraced all mankind in the sin and death of Adam in order that the basis for reconciliation made by the blood of Jesus, all who would believe unto repentance toward God and be obedient to Him might have the benefit of it. 

Adam and all his posterity became mortal, that is, subject to death as enemies of God; but the shed blood of Jesus Christ opens the way for all to be reconciled and made the friends of God. 

When fully conformed to God by repentance and reformation the death of His Son reconciles us to the saving of life and the giving of immortality; for God gave His Son to be the death or destruction of sin for us, who knew no sin that we might be made the righteousness of God in Him. "God, by and through the blood of His Son Jesus Christ, hath made us fit to be partakers of the inheritance with Jesus Christ by translating us from the power of darkness into the kingdom of His dear Son, in whom we have redemption through His blood, even the forgiveness of sins."

There is but one Divine person who is the only true and living God, even our heavenly Father; and one mediator between God, our

heavenly Father, and man; even God's only begotten Son, the incarnate Word, Christ Jesus, who for our sake freely gave Himself as a vicarious sacrifice that we might have the opportunity for justification unto life through His blood. This great gift, of eternal life, by the grace of God, proceeds through our Lord Jesus Christ the only begotten Son of our Divine Father in heaven by reason of our Divine Father's holy condescension to give to us His only begotten Son, and the Son's willingness to give Himself in sacrifice for man's redemption as a propitiation for our sins; for such is the 

Divine provision for our remission of sin, and reconciliation to God; and those only are lost to life and immortality who refuse the overtures of God's love, mercy and grace.

Our Divine Father shows mercy unto every one whose heart remains true to Him, and strives continually to do His will, notwithstanding he may fall into sin a hundred times a day. If such an one will turn to our Divine Father with a penitent and contrite heart, and confess his sin, and conscientiously resolve to try not to offend further, our Divine Father graciously pardons.

The covenant and rules of action declared by our Divine Father in heaven for man's justification, is a binding contract between our divine Father and the penitent sinner that the agreement between the parties is to be sacredly and solemnly binding between the parties. No one who is out of harmony with God's plan of redemption through Christ, can be considered competent to enter into covenant with God. There can be no lasting blessing come to man, save the reconciliation of man to God. There is no unconditional promise made by our Divine Father to save anyone without demonstrating his faith and repentance toward Him. This test is necessary to put upon the sinner in order to teach the necessary lesson, not for the gratification of our Divine Father in heaven, but to prove the faithfulness and devotion of the one entering into covenant with Him. All who are reconciled and at peace with God, will have the right, according to God's covenant, to immortality and the life eternal. People are justified by repentance through faith in the shed blood of Jesus Christ, and are begotten by the spirit of God as jointheirs with Christ of God's kingdom.

Christ is the go-between or mediator between God and man, with full power to convey to man the terms of reconciliation with God. 

The New Covenant of atonement made through Jesus Christ, involves the greatest sacrifice on the part of God, and also on the part of His Son Jesus Christ, as it is the covenant of sacrifice both on

the part of God in giving His Son, and in God's Son Jesus Christ giving Himself for the redemption of the world. 

The Christian is justified by faith in the shed blood of Jesus Christ; and his reconciliation is complete at the time of compliance with the terms of the covenant of repentance toward God. 

God's law, or law covenant and commands were good and just; but the imperfections of men were against God's holy law and commandments and worked death in man because of his weaknesses. 

But God gave the law covenant that sin might appear sinful, and work death to the good of man, to the salvation of every soul who would believe unto repentance. Christ is the end of the law covenant to all who through faith and repentance accept the atonement of Jesus-Christ the Son of God as their means of atonement and reconciliation with God; but those who are careless, indifferent, unconcerned, or disregard, or reject God's offer of reconciliation through the vicarious atonement of His Son Jesus Christ must comply with or suffer the penalty of God's broken law. 

To the Christian saint God's law covenant may be said to be abolished, abrogated or legitimately commuted; but to non-believers, villains, and reprobates God's law covenant is in full force, and they must be judged and executed according to God's law covenant. 

Was the law covenant a failure that it was abolished, abrogated, or legitimately commuted? Absolutely not! It was just, holy, good; but man's failure to keep the law, was no fault of the law, but that of man. The law covenant was made for man's good as a standard of perfection for which to strive to the saving of life for all who attained unto it; but through the weaknesses of the flesh no man kept the law and was condemned by it to death and destruction. 

It is generally conceded that God's glorious Son, that superangelical spirit-being who was the beginning of God's creation, the "Word of God" who became incarnated in human flesh and was called Jesus the Christ, God's only begotten Son is the only person who fulfilled God's pure law; and having done this for Himself, He still went further and suffered the penalty of God's broken law for man, in his place, room and stead that whosoever believeth on Him should not perish but have everlasting life through His name by the resurrection from the dead at Christ's second coming.

Christ is the end of the law covenant for righteousness to every one that believes, as it is He who puts an end to the law for all who believe by nailing it to His cross; that is, Christ dying for the sinner takes every penitent sinner's place in death and restores him through

the resurrection from the dead to the life eternal and immortal at 

His coming to earth again.

What the law could not do because of the weakness of the flesh of man, God sent His first-born and only begotten Son Jesus Christ, the incarnate Word, in the likeness of sinful flesh; and because of sin in man condemned sin in the flesh by offering His flesh as an atonement for man's sin to the end that penitent man be restored to life and immortality at the resurrection of the just when Christ comes to reign upon the earth.

The law covenant demonstrated beyond all question of a doubt that there could be no life granted under the law to mankind without the sacrifice of Jesus Christ as a ransom and sin offering for the souls of men, for all men have sinned and come short of keeping the law.

God never interferes with the free moral agency of His creatures. 

He does not compel sacrifice or even obedience; but He essentially delights in the loving devotion and adoration of His creatures. 

It will be observed that our Divine Father in heaven accomplishes His purposes by means of covenants or solemn agreements to do the things involved in the covenants; and offers a just recompense of reward for obedience and devotion thereto.

Our Divine Father is always faithful and true to His covenants and agreements; and those who are prompted by love to do His will can look forward with full and complete assurance that faithfulness on his part will result in full benefit to himself. The secrets of the 

Lord are with them that fear Him; and His covenants are to make men know Him.

Jesus Christ who as the "Word of God" incarnated, is the chief of all men as well as the chief of angels, He being superior to them all, chose, with the full liberty of His free moral agency to do the will of His Divine Creator and Father both in the creation and redemption of mankind.

Because of the everlasting blessings accruing to the penitent and reformed sinner, none should be unwilling, but all anxious to do 

God's will in all things. 

Our glorious savior Jesus Christ, our Divine Father's Son, was as willing and as anxious to offer Himself as man's sacrificial atonement as was His Divine Father to give Him in sacrifice for man's redemption. Both, our Divine Father, and His only begotten Son 

Jesus Christ showed alike the same gracious and compassionate spirit toward fallen man.

So anxious was Christ to do His Divine Father's will that He said in reference to the death He was to die for man: "I have a baptism to be baptized with; and how am I straightened till it be accomplished." So anxious was Christ to do His Divine Father's will that 

He lived in anxious suspense for the will of His Divine Father to be fulfilled in Him.

The basis for the reconciliation of man to God is the shed blood of Jesus Christ poured out according to the terms of God's covenant by sacrifice. No sacrifice other than that of Jesus Christ is required to meet the requirements of God's law, and penitent man is ransomed or redeemed from death through the resurrection from the dead to the life ternal, immortal, and everlasting.

All that man can do in his own behalf in order to salvation, is his full and complete consecration to do God's will in accordance with the New Covenant proffered through the blood of God's only begotten Son, Jesus Christ.

People are brought into saving grace through Christ's mediatorial office, only in so far as they conform to the provisions of acceptance through faith and repentance toward God. The acceptance of the vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ by the penitent sinner, is an acknowledgement of his sin and repentance toward God, and is effective unto salvation to all who keep a good conscience toward God, in thought, word and deed, through sanctification of his person to good uses.

The fact, that our Divine Father in heaven, chose His glorious first-born Son of all creation, the Word, to become incarnated and generated by a woman who was under the law which He gave to Moses, made Him subject to all of its provisions and disciplines as a man; and in this He differs nothing from us as to its provisions. 

This Christ did to the full satisfaction of God's holy law. But Christ did more than that, for He not only filled to the full all its provisions for Himself as a man, but submitted Himself as a vicarious sacrifice to make an atonement for man who failed to keep God's covenant, in order, that through His death for man, man by the grace of repentance toward God, and faith in God's only begotten 

Son as a vicarious atonement might have life and immortality.

Christ invites all to participate in His sacrificial atonement when 

He said to His disciples: "Take, eat, this is my body; drink, this is my blood which is shed for many for the remission of sins." 

The Holy Eucharist or Lord's Supper is representative of the actual giving by Christ of His flesh and blood as the spiritual food

by which Divine grace is conveyed and supplied to the souls of men; and the only basis for the reconciliation of penitent man to God. 

Christ Jesus is a means, as well as the mediator given to man by our Divine Father to bring man back to obedience to His Divine Father. 

The scriptures have made the plan of man's salvation clear; and when man learns that he is a sinner, and that the vicarious sacrifice of Jesus Christ is the only means provided on the part of our Divine Father in heaven for man's redemption from sin and death; and is effective only by faith and repentance on the part of each person entering into covenant with God, man will be more prone to consecrate himself to the service of God. 

Through obedience, penitent man's faith in the shed blood of

Jesus Christ for man, becomes man's sacrifice, and each one so acting individually can be assured that God accepts the human life of Jesus Christ given for man, in the shedding of His blood for man, is the sacrifice, as it were, of each penitent given in His own person, so that the death of Jesus Christ is accepted by our Divine Father in heaven in the place, room and stead of that of the penitent sinner; and the penitent sinner is released from death through the resurrection from the dead unto eternal life at the appearing of Jesus Christ. 

It is purely the grace of our Divine Father in heaven, that the penitent sinner, through faith in the shed blood of Jesus Christ given in His behalf, accepts Christ's sacrifice as the sinner's offering unto justification of life and immortality.

The penitent sinner is justified through faith in the atonement of Jesus Christ made in his behalf, and is accepted by our Divine Father as the same as that which he personally owes; and he is made an heir of God and a joint-heir with Jesus Christ and His saints of the life eternal and immortality. This is the most glorious inheritance that can come to man; and those who thus become conformed to 

God our Divine Father should look forward to a glad and glorious resurrection unto the life eternal, immortal, and everlasting happiness to reign with our Divine Father, Jesus Christ, God's glorious 

Son, His angels and His saints forever.

All who enter into covenant with God through His only begotten 

Son Jesus Christ must be transformed from mortal to immortal beings before God's covenant is fully realized by man. The sacrifice of Jesus Christ is the only all-sufficient sacrifice for the sins of man past, present, and future; and it is effective unto salvation for all who repent, believe and obey Him; but those who reject Him and do despite to these means of God's grace; the sacrifice of Jesus

Christ is of no efficacy and all such are lost to God's means of grace, and must meet the judgments of God's law, and be condemned by it. 

Since all have failed to keep the law and are found transgressors of God's law covenants, man must die; and a perfect life substituted, if man is to be made to live; but how this was accomplished, was not in the realm of man to provide, since all of Adam's race transgressed through him as the representative of the race. Thus there must be a substitute furnished, if man is to live, not of Adam's race, which it is not in the power of man to supply; and how is it accomplished? Our Divine Father in heaven makes the way possible for man's redemption by choosing His glorious first-born Son of all creation, the Word, and by the power of His omnipotent spirit creates the Word into a perfect man by incarnating Him in a physical, human body by conception and generation of woman that He might give the life of His perfect manhood in substitution for the life of Adam which was lost through transgression. 

The ransom price the giving of Christ's body and blood in sacrifice for the restoration of the life of man-does not of itself constitute the reconciliation of man to God, as this only constitutes, on God's part, the faithful performance of His part of the covenant; and it remains for man through faith and repentance, to fulfill his part of the covenant in order to reconciliation with God. 

There are many who will be saved who have no accurate knowledge of the truth of God's plan of salvation, because they have a good conscience toward God; but what an immense multitude there would be who would glady accept the ransom sacrifice of Jesus Christ through repentance and reformation unto salvation, if they had an accurate knowledge of God's beneficent and glorious plan of salvation, by the grace of repentance through the sacrificial atonement made by Jesus Christ.

It is a great sin against God and a crime against humanity that the ministry of the Church for above a thousand years have been so bewitched by Satan and his counterpart the Antichrist and head of the Roman Catholic Church, the Pope of Rome, who forced upon the world the Antichrist doctrine of three Divine persons in the Deity or a triune God, instead of teaching the true doctrine of the strict unity of our Divine heavenly Father in one person, uncreate, absolute and independent; and that He is Creator, God, and Father of all spirits, persons, beings and things other than His own being of one person to the exclusion of all others.

The doctrine of the Trinity or triune God, has been the greatest

curse and sin against Christianity that has come into the world; and has caused more confusion, and the destruction of more precious souls than any other agency of the devil.

The doctrine of the creation, incarnation, conception, and generation of God's first-born Son of all creation, the Word, is the doctrine taught by Jesus Christ, and His apostles, and prophets to the exclusion and anathema of all other doctrines; and those who teach contrary doctrines to this one of the incarnation, conception and generation of God's glorious first-born of all creation in the person of Jesus Christ, God's only begotten Son, are antichristian.

The time has come that the "Mother of harlots and abominations of the earth," should be judged according to her deeds, and her blinded subjects released from their chains of superstition and ignorance that they may behold the Son of all righteousness in His beauty, grandeur and sublimity.

The gift of our Divine Father's only begotten Son, the incarnate Word Jesus Christ, opens the way for man's reconciliation with God our Divine Father; but the knowledge of man concerning the plan provided for man's reconciliation and salvation has been obscured by creeds, disciplines, dogmas, and denominational literature that those who would be saved through the knowledge of the truth are hindered from entering into covenant with God for the want of the knowledge of truth.

Before man can accept the plan of salvation or fully comply with its provisions he must have a knowledge of its provisions, as it is hard to conceive and little to be expected that many would without knowledge, blindly conform to the requirements of the provisions of the covenant which is essential to saving faith. How then can those rightfully answer to God's covenants with man who have no right knowledge of the terms of God's covenant or how can they believe that of which they have no knowledge?

It was the complete consecration and sanctification of God's glorious Son, the Word incarnated, known as Jesus the Christ, who by His filial devotion to His Divine Father was made perfect and won for Himself the title of "King of kings, and Lord of lords" by what He did and suffered. By reason of Christ's unswerving devotion in following His Divine Father's righteous course under the most trying conditions, His Divine Father raised Him out of death and the grave to His own right hand in heavenly places, that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow of things in heaven and things

22 

in earth, and every tongue confess that Jesus is Lord to the glory of God His Divine Father.

The inability of one contracting party, that of man, because of his fallen, imperfect state, necessitated a mediator to remove the disability of man to contract or enter into covenant with his Divine Creator, our Father in heaven. This Christ Jesus, the incarnate 

Word of God does, by giving His human body in vicarious sacrifice for man, and reinstates him to God's clemency and mercy through repentance and faith in the efficacy of His atonement. The establishment of God's New Covenant with man which He made through His own incarnate Son, removes man's disability to enter into covenant with His Divine Father.

It was with the ancestors of Judah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob especially that God made His promises to give them an heir through which all the families of the earth would be blessed. Therefore when 

God said that He would make a New Covenant with Israel and Judah He chose the house of Judah through which the promised prince and Messiah Jesus Christ, His only begotten Son, the Word incarnated, should be born. It was with the descendants of Israel that God made the law covenant; but Israel, Judah and all their descendants were too imperfect to keep the law; but God, our Divine 

Father, had designated and appointed His first-born Son of all creation before the foundation of the world, as the perfect vicarious sacrifice which should be offered for man.

Thus God caused His first-born Son of all creation, the Word, to become incarnated by a Jewish virgin who conceived and generated Him. He kept the law of God perfectly, and fulfilled all what the law and the prophets said concerning Him. Thus, the first-born creature of all of God's creation, the Word, being incarnated by a Jewish virgin named Mary who conceived Him by the spirit of God and generated Him. He was born a Jew under the law; and He being a lineal descendant of the house of Judah according to the flesh, kept the law perfectly, and thereby became the rightful heir of every blessing promised to Israel and Judah. 

Wherefore, when God said, that He would make a New Covenant with Israel and Judah, it follows that God would make His covenant with one who held all the rights and qualifications that Israel, Judah and their descendants could have held if they had been perfect. 

The New Covenant could not have been made with any natural child of Adam's race because of imperfections both inherited and actual. For this cause God's glorious first-born Son of all creation

offered Himself to His Divine Father in man's behalf to remove the disabilities of man. He entered into covenant with His Divine Father by offering for man the required sacrifice, of the death of a perfect man, for the purpose of affecting reconciliation of man to God; because it required the sacrifice of a perfect man who had God's pure law fulfilled to suffer the penalty of God's broken law in behalf of man who defaulted.

Christ is the end of the law covenant and the mediator in the making of the new covenant which was consummated between God and man at the time of the slaying of Jesus as the real passover lamb for man on the fourteenth day of the Jewish month Nisan A. D. 33.

Jesus met with His disciples at Jerusalem and ate the passover lamb as enjoined by the law upon all the Jews. Jesus being the one foreshadowed by the passover lamb slain in Egypt by the Israelites, He was the one to fulfill the picture, which required His life by the shedding of His blood. It was necessary for Jesus to eat the passover before He died as an Israelite. On this occasion of the passover 

Jesus instituted the memorial of His death for man as the New Covenant in His blood; and as they were eating the passover, Jesus took bread and blessed it, and broke it, and gave it to His disciples and said, "Take, eat, this is my body;" and He took the cup and gave thanks, and gave it to them saying, "Drink ye all of it, for this is my blood of the New Testament which is shed for many for the remission of sins." 

These blessed words were spoken by Jesus, God's glorious firstborn Son of all creation, the Word incarnate, who only upon all the earth at that time was competent to understand and express the full meaning of the passover. Jesus here, in the Holy Eucharist of the "Lord's supper," is referring to His broken body, and to His shed blood which was poured out at the same feast as that of the paschal lamb which foreshadowed the slaying of Jesus, God's passover lamb for the remission of the sins of many.

A testament is of force after men are dead, otherwise it is of no force while the testator lives. Therefore, it was necessary for Jesus to die before the ransom price for man's sin could be paid in the death of Jesus.

Seeing that the real contracting party on behalf of Israel and all of mankind is Jesus Christ, God's only begotten Son, the Word incarnate, the law covenant ended on the fourteenth of the Jewish month Nisan 33 A. D., and the new covenant inaugurated by Jesus 

Christ the testator of God's covenant on the same day.

It was the man Christ Jesus through which the covenant was made that died for man for which it was made; that through the death of Jesus Christ man might be restored to God's favor by repentance through faith in God's only begotten Son, Jesus Christ, the Word incarnate. 

On account of the incompetency of mankind to enter into covenant with our Divine Father in heaven, it necessitated a mediator to stand between God and His incompetent creature, man, as man's representative. Who then, could be the mediator in the New Covenant for man? Certainly no one of the fallen race of Adam is competent; for all such were out of harmony with God and under the bondage of sin and death. Essentially, then, Jesus, the incarnate Word of 

God alone, the only perfect man in all the earth, and He from heaven, is not subject to the bondage of sin and death can enter into covenant with His Divine Father in behalf of man as the only competent one in all the earth of mankind who can contract with His God Creator and Father, for the redemption of man. 

The covenant of the New Testament, then, is made with man through our Divine Father's only begotten Son Jesus Christ, the Word incarnated, who removes man's disability or incompetency, to act for himself, by offering His own body as a vicarious atonement for man so that man through the grace of repentance and reformation is justified through faith in Jesus Christ, God's only begotten Son.

This one act, the vicarious atonement of the mediator Jesus Christ in the behalf of man puts man in a position to be reconciled to God by means of repentance through faith in Christ. Man approaches unto God by and through the mediator between God and man, the incarnate Word, Christ Jesus. The basis of the New Covenant is 

Christ Jesus' own blood shed for man which gives promise of better things for mankind than the old covenant could possibly give, as Christ Jesus the mediator in the New Covenent between God and man, is able to save to the uttermost all who with a penitent heart accept His sacrificial atonement in their behalf.

Our Divine Father in heaven gave His first-born Son of all creation, the Word, for man's redemption by incarnating His glorious, beloved Son the Word into a body of flesh and blood. Christ Jesus, the Word incarnate fulfilled the law both for Himself and also for man. Christ fulfilled the law in His own behalf by living up to all of its requirements and provisions incumbent upon man for its fulfillment, and then fulfilled for man, who had transgressed God's holy

law, the penalty of death due him, by giving His body of perfect manhood as a vicarious atonement for penitent man, that whosoever accepted Him as their Lord and redeemer should not perish but have everlasting life through the resurrection at the appearing of Jesus Christ when He comes to reign. Then will be the general assembly of the Church of Jesus Christ. For it is written: "Then are ye come unto mount Sion, and unto the city of the living God, the heavenly

Jerusalem, and to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and Church of the first-born which are written in heaven, and to God the judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect, and to Jesus the mediator of the New Covenant, and to the blood of the sprinkling, and to the city of the living God." 

The whole scheme of the gospel is a presentation of the law covenant consummated or fulfilled in Jesus Christ, and the inauguration of the New Covenant. The paschal lamb represented the atoning sacrifice of Jesus Christ. The Lord's Supper or Holy Eucharist is the Lord Jesus' memorial sacrament of His death which He tasted for every man, woman and child of mankind, which purchased for the penitent sinner all the rights the perfect man could have had, had he kept the law. 

The everlasting happiness of man is dependent upon certain characteristics and principles akin to that of the Divine character; and when he is at peace and in full harmony with God through reconciliation, man will be happy, immortal, and blessed forever more. 

To God, our heavenly Father, is due all the honor and glory for man's existence of being, privileges and powers, as all of these are of our Divine Father's pure grace, and He has the power to terminate them whenever it pleases His righteous purposes, or He may extend them forever to those who seek to do His will.

God created man a rational being after His own image and likeness that man may choose obedience to his creator and live forever or choose not to obey and be destroyed with an everlasting destruction from the presence of God and His power. 

Even after man chose to disobey his Divine Creator, still God did not abandon him to his just fate; but infinite love did all that infinite wisdom could do to call back wandering man back to himself. 

In man's fall, God's name was involved; for God was man's creator and beneficent Father, and it grieved God that His creature, man, had turned aside from the pathway of righteousness. God would teach man that in Him only are the issues of life and immortality, and every good of man.

God has set a limit to sin and wickedness, and He will not permit Satan, evil spirits or evil men to live out of harmony with Him forever; for He has set a day in which He will judge the world and all things in righteousness whether for good or bad, all will have to stand before the judgment bar of God and receive His just deserts of life and immortality or be delegated unto everlasting destruction.

God permits man to have a complete and full lesson in sin and its disastrous effects but exhibits His gracious, loving kindness, commending man to His love, that He might bring him safely to Himself and preserve him an immortal being forever; but those who persist in sin and wickedness to the demoralizing of their soul, them will God destroy.

God demonstrates that with Him justice, wisdom, love and power operate in perfect harmony; and that He does not act arbitrarily, but accomplishes His purposes through covenants.

God's patience, long-suffering and mercy, are always manifest with innumerable illustrations, and examples which operate in perfect justice, that man might know the way to God and the life eternal; but those who will not forgive those who trespass against them will not be forgiven their trespasses, who trespass against their Divine Father.

All spiritual and moral forces involving obedience originate and belong to our Divine Father in heaven, and have direct claim and jurisdiction over the civil when not in harmony with the spiritual and moral as Divine obligations, and should be recognized by all civil authorities as binding on the conscience to the exclusion of all others with God as the only arbiter, judge and executor of His laws, and the only discerner of the human conscience. Therefore, no authoritative decision can come either from ecclesiastical or civil sources over the conscience arbitrarily to the prejudice of the mind or spirit of the human soul in its highest conception and knowledge of duty, as it is God's right alone to rule and reign in the heart of the believer; and all other rules or theories to the contrary are devoted to the propagation of error. For our Divine Father has given no person, association, government, or power authority to act for Him as supreme judge over the individual conscience, and all are therefore amenable only to him in things religious, so long as he does not interfere with the spiritual, moral or civil rights of others. 

This principle lays down the proposition that all men are, by their Creator, made alike of one blood; and alike are equal in the right to the control of their life; and that each one is, in so far, his own

master to rule his life on an equality with that of all others, in order that the judgment of one's conscience, in things pertaining to God, be subject to God only and is not to be infringed upon by anyone, as every one must act for himself personally in obedience to his 

Divine Creator.

CHAPTER II 

Mortal man who lives not in a state of perfection but of error which is contrary to our highest good, is greatly in need of instruction in righteousness, intellectually, morally and civilly in order to come into possession of Divine truth, so as to live the life eternal; and as all men are by nature equally entitled to the free exercise of conscience in religious affairs, there should be no compulsion placed upon others of lesser intelligence to enforce religious and moral conduct wherein they do not interfere with the moral, religious and civil rights of others. These are cardinal doctrines in the American, of freedom; and every individual is guaranteed under the Constitution. to the outward practice of religion according to his conscience in so far as he does not interfere with the equal rights of others. 

These principles lay down the proposition that all men are, by their Creator, made free moral agents to practice the outward form of religion accordingly, as they understand the commands of God. 

That it is the right of the individual to form his own personal judgments about his obligations toward his Divine Creator and his fellowmen; but the "man of sin," "the son of perdition," the Pope of 

Rome; and the "Mother of harlots and abominations of the earth," the Roman Catholic Church, claim to be the supreme judge on earth over all religion and morals and the director of the consciences of men to the exclusion of all others; and brands as heretics all baptized persons professing Christianity who choose for themselves what to believe or not to believe contrary to their teaching and dogmas. For above a thousand years all exercising their right of faith and worship not in keeping with the dictates of the Pope of the Roman Catholic Church incurred upon themselves perforce all the pains and penalties that pertain to heresy according to the Roman Catholic Church, which literally means, that no one has a right to life and liberty who opposes the dictates of the Roman Catholic Church; but the Christian ideals and lofty concepts of the leaven of Christianity could not be smothered, and the protestant reformation of liberty of conscience, and freedom of worship gained such vast proportions that the Roman Catholic Church could no longer enforce her iniquitous inquisitions upon all dissenters. 28

The beloved Apostle of Jesus Christ, John the Revelator of modern history, concerning the papal beast in speaking of the Roman Catholic Church says: "In her was found the blood of the prophets and of the saints, and all that have been slain upon the earth for the word of God."

The Pope claims to be the vicegerent of God, and the vicar of Jesus Christ; and that all religion and morals are exercised by him as head of the Church by virtue of his supremacy over all spiritual affairs; and that he claims the right to annual any and all laws or acts of government that would injure the Catholic Church or attack their rights as interpreted by their standard of citizenship. 

The Pope imputes and arrogates to himself the vicegerency of God which he claims by virtue of his office as the head of the spiritual realm of God upon the earth, as the exerciser of the functions of God. Such villainous, reprobate, antichristian pretensions and claims for sinful, wicked, ungodly, satanic mortal men to make as to try to rob God of His Divine authority and sovereignty, belongs solely to the spirit of Antichrist, the man of sin, the son of perdition, who exalteth himself above all that is called God; and sits in the temple of God, showing that he himself is God, claiming the right to annul all laws or acts of government which are contrary to his individual, personal decrees as head of the Church. 

Nations as well as individuals owe their allegiance to our Divine Father in heaven as their creator, upholder and sustainer; and anyone claiming, as the Pope does, the vicegerency or substitute for the godhead of our Divine Father in heaven, and delegates to himself the right to proscribe and punish schism or heresy of his religious dogmas through inquisitions and murders, in order to subject the people to himself, cannot escape God's just retribution of condemnation.

Since free speech and a free press are requisite to freedom of worship, it is easily to be seen that Christianity has been shackled and subdued in its workings from early history down to modern times; and even now, in most countries of the earth, religious freedom is very much restricted where it is not prohibited because of some dominant creed. promise the principles of their religion by adopting some pagan forms to gain prestige and converts. Jesus Christ only for the remission of sins; and of the keeping of 

God's holy sabbath of rest on Saturday the seventh day of the week which were all changed by the Pope of Rome through imperial decree.

The changing of the doctrine of Deity or divinity of our Divine Father in heaven, the only true and living God, to the doctrine of three divinities or Deities, called God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Ghost at the beginning of the fourth century, which calumniated in the establishment of the Nicene creed A. D. 325, enforcing all to be baptized in the name of the Trinity by imperial decree under penalty of excommunication, disfranchisement, and confiscation of goods. The changing of the sabbath day from Saturday, the seventh day of the week to Sunday the first day of the week followed hard on and became a law in 336 A. D. 

The Emperor, Constantine the Great, about the year 312 A. D., began to evidence an interest in the compact system of Christianity which flourished even in the face of persecution; and after a great military victory in which he considered Christianity had greatly helped him to win, came out boldly in his advocacy of certain features of Christianity; and he began to favor the bishop at Rome in his cherished supremacy over the Christian Church upon his compromising various principles of Christianity by substituting certain heathen features introduced into the Church through various heathen, Platonic, and Alexandrian philosophers; and in three twenty-one passed the first law making it obligatory upon all except the farmerfolk to rest on Sunday. Constantine also adopted the doctrine of the

D., and required all persons not only to believe in three Divine persons, but to be baptized in their names; and had the Trinitarian formula incorporated in the scriptures contrary to the custom, writing, and practice of Christ's apostles, bishops and evangelists who baptized only in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins until the days of Constantine the Great who was the principal

corrupter of the teaching, practice, and customs of the holy apostolic Christians.

Laodicea 336 A. D.

This blessed privilege of direct communication with Christ's Divine Father without the intervention of any save Jesus Christ His glorious incarnate Son, the Word, "we can enter with boldness into the holiest place through the blood of Jesus by a new and living way which He has consecrated for us through the veil of His flesh; and having such a high-priest over the household of God, let us draw near with a true heart in full assurance of faith."

Let us know something about how that branch of service performed by the Levitical priesthood in the cleansing away of sin was performed. The person who had committed sin brought his victim to the door of the tabernacle. Upon the head of this victim he placed his hand for a moment, and confessed his sins, and by this impressive act signified that he had sinned, and was worthy of death, but that in his stead or place he consecrated his victim and transferred his

guilt through it to Jesus Christ the true sacrifice for penitent man's sin.

The law demanded the life of the transgressor for his disobedience which must be atoned through the shedding of the life blood, of which the sacrificial victim was the representative vehicle conveying the guilt of man before the Lord as an atonement for sin. The bringing of the sacrificial victim was a confession of the sin of the individual, and the slaying of the sacrificial victim transfers, by the grace of God, the guilt of the penitent sinner to the victim, not directly, but indirectly, through the vicarious atonement of Jesus

Christ, which was the only perfect sacrifice for man's redemption. 

All other sacrifices for man were but types and shadows of the merits of Jesus Christ's offering for sin.

CHAPTER III 

When Jesus returns to this earth with the holy angels in clouds of glory to raise the righteous dead and translate His living saints into immortal youths to share with Him His own God-given immortality; then, will the ransomed see the most beautiful scene ever beheld; for it will stand solitary, unique, and perfect in its overwhelming grandeur and sublimity; but to the unbelieving and rebellious it will mean death and everlasting destruction from God's presence and power.

Then, at Christ's second coming, all who will not recognize and accept our Divine Father in heaven, as the only uncreate, absolute and independent one in His being, person and spirit; and the only one subsisting in the one person, nature, essence, and substance comprehending that supreme being whom we call our God and Father will be cut off from all life and being as sentient creatures; for apart from Him, nothing else has existence outside of His creation, and is therefore finite and dependent in all things upon our Divine Father absolutely and unqualifiedly for their being, existence and powers, and all that they are and have. Even the first-born Son of our 

Divine Father, Jesus Christ the Word incarnate, in whatever stage of His existence is subject to His Divine Creator and Father the same as that of all other beings, persons and things whatsoever; for apart from our Divine Father nothing else whatsoever has any existence, power or authority, as they are always dependent, finite creatures and things of our Divine Father's creation and subject to 

His Divine providence.

The Holy Spirit is the spirit of our Divine Father's person, and it is not a person or thing apart from Him; but it is the willing, choosing, designing, purposing executive power of our Divine Father's person, and through it only does our Divine Father operate, whether immediately, personally, or mediately through His created agents. 

Our Divine Father is the only unit, spirit, or personal being, who in Himself, of Himself and by Himself is absolute and independent of all persons and things other than His own personal, unqualified ego of self-consciousness which in Himself is absolute and independent of all persons and things other than Himself. 46

Jesus Christ and all other persons or things are one with God only by reason of their creation by Him and their subjection to Him and apart from God our Divine Father in heaven they have no existence or power whatsoever; and are therefore dependnt upon our Divine 

Father for all that they have and do. Therefore, since our Divine 

Father only is uncreate, absolute and independent in His person and powers, all things else are created by Him and dependent upon Him, because our Divine Father whose person, nature, essence and substance are different from all other persons and things, as He only is uncreate, abolute, and independent in His person and powers, while that of all other persons and things, are creatures and things of our Divine Father's creation, and are finite, because they are create and dependent upon our Divine Father for their creation, existence and powers; for they receive their person, being and powers from our Divine Father; and none can enter fully into our 

Divine Father's plans and purposes for Him without recognizing his dependence to our heavenly Father his Divine Creator who in Himself, of Himself and by Himself is God to the exclusion of all others.

Every loyal, sentient being of our Divine Father's creation in all time and place whether of men or of angels or of any other essence, nature or substance, will submit to this glorious inexorable truth, "That the Lord our God is one Lord," and that He only is Divine to the exclusion of all spirits, persons or things whatsoever." 

The harmony of all things absolutely and unqualifiedly depend upon the perfect conformity and obedience to the Divine Father's will, power and authority; and any person, spirit or being which does not fully submit to the direction, power and authority of our 

Divine Father's executive, omnipotent, omniscient, omnipresent ubiquitous spirit by which our Divine Father creates, governs, and executes all things according to His will, cannot abide the judgments of our Divine Father when he takes his power to destroy all that is evil.

It is written that our Divine Father gave, to His only begotten Son Jesus Christ at His baptism, His Holy Spirit without measure or unlimitedly to carry out His Divine Father's will; but this power and authority, for the retention of our Divine Father's spirit, depended solely and absolutely upon Christ's obedience to the operations of our Divine Father's spirit; for says Christ Jesus: "I of myself can do nothing, it is my Father that doeth the works." In the various representations of the works of God whether immediately

by our Divine Father, or mediately through Jesus Christ or any other agency whatsoever, it is only and always executed by the spirit of our Divine Father in heaven; and absolutely nothing can ever necessitate there being other divine beings conjointly with or in addition to our Divine Father in heaven whose spirit is omnipotent to perform everything that is an object of power. It is the spirit of 

God that approves or disapproves the acts of all others, and executes all things according to our Divine Father's will whether to glorification or execution of destruction.

No man is truly free until he has done his full duty toward God and all sentient creatures of His creation and the primary concern of every individual should be his religious and moral life; for Christ says: "Seek God and His righteousness first and all needful things will be given you." This slogan of Jesus Christ, the incarnate Word of God, was ever uppermost in His thoughts, purposes, words and works, so much so, that He was wholly controlled by it. To worship 

God, His Divine Father and to serve Him as the only true and living God was what Jesus ever practiced, observed and taught. Divine Father in heaven, and not to Himself; for they say that

Christ is coequal, coessential and coeternal with His Divine Father which is contrary to all nature, science and reason, that a creature could be equal to an uncreated being who is His creator; and the creator of all things else besides Him. 

Following close upon Jesus' baptism by water at the hands of John the Baptist; and also by the baptism of power and authority of the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father in heaven Jesus entered into the synagogue at Nazareth where He had been brought up and stood up to read; and there was delivered unto Him the book of the prophet Esaias, and when He had opened the book, He found the place where it was written, "The spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to preach the gospel to the poor, he hath sent me to heal the broken-hearted, to preach deliverance to the captives, and recovering of the sight to the blind, to set at liberty them that are bruised, to preach the acceptable year of the Lord." 

Jesus then closed the book, and sat down, and began to say unto them, "This day is this scripture fulfilled in your ears." When the people heard these things they were filled with wrath, but Jesus rose up and passed through the midst of them and went His way pro-

claiming throughout all Palestine the fulfillment of this prophecy. 

This Divine and heavenly truth was a proposition to which the people were not willing to readily concede although Jesus' words and works were backed up with supernatural power and authority by the 

Holy Spirit of His Divine Father.

Any scientific principle that can be proved to be the truth, is a proposition to which even the gods must submit; and these propositions we meet in engineering, chemistry, physics, and the allied sciences which the Creator Himself cannot deny, for He is the author of them; but according to many of our theologians, truth is not to be depended on when it conflicts with their religious dogmas. 

They think that truth is well and good in astronomy, geology, chemistry, mathematics, and the allied sciences when it does not conflict with their religion; but the moment it conflicts with their pet theories of religious dogma it is to be abandoned and anathematized! Truth is treated by them like a deceiver, especially in the training of very young children; and is accepted about half of the time by the ministry in sociology, psychology and biology, especially when it appears to support the present-day manners, current morals; and the prevailing religion; but in history, civics, and many other fields it is always open to suspicion; and therefore as a general thing, truth is to be avoided by proclaiming our emancipation from its authority and salutary effects, because it conflicts with our religious orthodoxy. 

Of course our religious leaders must continue to proclaim their devotion to truth in order that they may be able to get people to believe and act upon the things that they have in mind to put across. 

Truth is good, but according to our orthodox religion-not Christianity-it is bad for people to know that the truth does not correspond with orthodoxy, for truth corresponds to facts; and facts are greatly at variance with the orthodox religionists. 

The individual that will not investigate the premises of orthodoxy will remain an infant imbecile or moron concerning the mental and intellectual faculties by which three are one and one is three; and will always be incapable of understanding how these contradictions and falsities are orthodox truths, for God and orthodoxy are altogether different and opposite things, for "God is one" and orthodoxy is three in one or one in three.

God has fixed everything upon a sound scientific basis and has left nothing to chance, His works are all decreed and foreordained, and can be relied upon as true and scientifically correct, as all things in true prophecy are revealed by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father,

and have always proved true, and correct in every respect; and that is why we do know that we are living in the age of the apostasy; and that the Church is being governed largely by the Antichrist, the man of sin and son of perdition, the Pope of Rome; and it is our privilege to find out in what respects the Antichrist's doctrines and dogmas differ from those of Jesus Christ, God's own incarnate Son whom the prophets foretold should come into the world. 

Nothing of this planet has any permanent tenure of itelf, and only our Divine Father who only has the power to create can cause things to subsist by the omnipotent power of His spirit; and therefore no combination of atoms or electrons could choose to form their mode of existence, save but by the power of our Divine Father. 

Physical nature and spirit can play together like mother and child; but both nature and spirit of all creation is dependent upon the spirit of our heavenly Father for their existence and powers. 

All existence is dependent upon our Divine Father in heaven; and all those who do not help Jesus Christ, God's only begotten Son to bear His cross, will have to bear theirs in vain. Rudeness should always be regarded as a regrettable lapse, and the only effective method of demolishing war is to put law on the side of peace, and war on the side of law.

It is a diabolical dispositon of human society to make life trivial and ineffective. The indwelling spirit of man, which we have of God our heavenly Father, by which our brain functions, as God purposed it, should be used as a medium of righteousness connecting two worlds; but those who misuse and abuse their rationality will never get beyond this earthly sphere to curse and blight with their haughty arrogant spirit those who obtain unto that blessed, happy state which lies just beyond this mortal clay.

The spirit of man can be made to function in harmony with God's spirit the same as an instrument with sweet music, if he will only bear in mind that God our Divine Father in heaven is the only living and true God, and there is none other Divine person but He; and that He is perfect and absolute; and that man and all things else whatsoever receive their being and powers from Him; and that they have nothing of themselves.

There is no infallibility in the opinions of experts and of scientists,

but in the truths themselves, as most everything man concludes is in itself a surmise or guess.
