It is not enough for one to be patriotic to his country, but to love all humanity and work for the attainment of relationships that are morally, physically and spiritually better, if we would save ourselves; for in rapid transit we are closer to Europe now than the people of 

Boston were to New York a century ago.

We must have a will to peace and harmony, and place ourselves in a position to repel aggression in every part of the earth. Let the good of the whole people be the paramount law, and guiding star. 

Truth, virtue, love and beauty all transcend the physical concrete matter, because they are spiritual, and it is the spiritual only which is of the greater worth, as it is that which abides forever. 

It is fear that wrecks and ruins everything, and it is the sacred duty and obligation placed upon us to try to banish this demon of fear from the earth, and substitute love in its place both for this world and the world to come.

The scaring and destroying the minds and bodies of people and of innocent children with the hideous terror of an everlasting hell of pain and suffering is one of the greatest crimes one can possibly commit against God and his fellow-men.

Every one should strive to add to the sum-total of good in the world, and be content with a living and noble Christian character. 

Personally, I have no physiological or psychological knowledge how the spirit and intelligence of man can exist apart from the body; but the Scriptures teach that quite a few have been resuscitated by the Spirit of God through the prophets, Jesus Christ and His apostles and various saints; but this I do know, that by means of my spirit 

I can love, think, will, choose, understand, and also perceive that there is a difference between good and evil; and that I will be held responsible for my acts toward my Creator and toward my fellowmen.

It is quite certain that science will never be able to prove that the spirit of man, and the mind of man's spirit cannot survive bodily

death; for no one can explain the spirit of life which we mortals possess, which has been restored by God's spirit through His saints; which is not of ourself, but given of God. 

Modern psychotherapy, in so far as it is understood, is in harmony with the teaching of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ as regards the giving of life-health through the spirit of our Divine Father in heaven. Most all believe that our Divine Father in heaven has that power to restore both body and the spirit of life within it, as we read it was exercised immediately by our Divine Father in raising His beloved incarnate Son Jesus Christ from the dead and exercised by others mediately through our Divine Father's spirit in many notable instances; and were it not for our lack of faith in ourselves and also in our Divine Creator these gifts and blessings would be ours.

Help us, O our Divine Father to understand, and see that without our bodily limitations there will be in Thy holy presence that extraordinary happiness, love and trust, deep and positive, minus all physical ailments and limitations; that we will be enraptured in happy visions, so beautiful, so grand, so sublime, such as eye has never seen nor ear heard, neither has it entered into the heart of man the good things that thou hast prepared for those who love and serve thee out of a pure heart! 

Oh, Thou Christ of God in whose name we pray, because Thou hast exemplified in Thy holy ascension what Thou hast told us, "Because I live, ye shall live also, that where I am there shall my servant be." Lord I believe, help Thou my unbelief, even now I live in Thee, for Thou art in my heart and in my affections; and I feel that I shall always be a stranger in this world, because of Thy vicarious atonement for me. I am dead to this world and live only in Thee! but before I go hence my precious Lord and Master I've got things to do for us both and then I shall await Thy coming for me. Come quickly Lord Jesus for I will be waiting for Thee. Others are here, but they are not close to me, for it was through Thy incarnation and loving sacrifice that I am to live forever. 

Give me a hard heart O Lord! Lord harden Thou my heart against this world with all of its sin and folly. Crucify all my evil inclinations, that I may have Thy unbounded peace and constant communion. I am a stranger in this world entwined with faith, hope, duty, love and responsibility until I have completed the task which Thou hast assigned me; teach me how to perform my mission. 

My soul is sick unto death, and behold I am dying-dying unto

this world. Quicken Thou my mortal body that I may live. Drugs cannot help my soul. I thirst for the Living Spring. Teach me, O

Thou Lamb of God the things for which I should live, as well as the things to which I should die! 

Oh our precious Divine Father, Thou alone art my God and my portion forever, because of Jesus Christ Thy only begotten Son, the incarnate Word, has revealed unto me that Thou alone art God; that Thou art my God, Creator, and Father, as Thou art His God, Creator and Father; and that He is Thy Son even Thy first-born of all creation.

Holy and righteous Father indue me with Thy Holy Spirit's presence, wisdom, and power; and enlighten my understanding, comprehension and discernment that I may be directed of Thee in this task which Thou hast assigned me to do. I, like Thy holy child 

Jesus, know that "I, of myself can do nothing;" but Thou canst work through me to the glorification of Thy name and to the blessing of my fellow-men. All my personal efforts are in vain without 

Thy Holy Spirit's guidance and power.

Only Thou, O my Divine Father art the true and living God, and able of Thy Holy Spirit to grant wisdom, knowledge, and power to guide my pen, and enlighten my mind to write the things Divine! 

Bless me, O Father Divine, bless even me with Thy Holy Spirit, and encourage my heart to the task, for without Thee the efforts of man are vain and folly!

When we contemplate Thy works, O Divine Father, Creator and Lord of heaven and earth, the mighty works of creation and redemption which Thou hast performed through Thy glorious Son, Thy first-born of all creation, the Word incarnate Jesus Christ, our heart is filled with thanksgiving, love and adoration because Thou hast so loved us as to give Thy first-born Son of all creation to become incarnate that He might give His precious body and blood for our redemption.

But the world, O our Divine Father, has a misconception of Thee because the enemy, the Antichrist and man of sin, the Pope of Rome has wickedly sown falsities and persecuted many even to the death to compel Thy saints to blaspheme Thy holy name by the worshipping of himself and the idolatrous images he has set up to be worshipped as Divine persons. 

Our Divine Father in heaven, we pray that Thou wilt forgive all who through mistaken zeal and ignorance are following the idolatrous Antichrist doctrines of the man of sin, the son of perdition,

the Pope of Rome; and we pray that Thou wilt estop those who knowingly are doing despite to Thy spirit of grace by teaching these falsities of satan to draw people after themselves, scattering and dividing Thy flock into sects and denominations of various names instead of Thine, who is the only living and true God. 

I pray that I may find at all times that sweet, tender feeling in my heart for Thee, O Thou Christ of God, for Thy marvelous condescension to become our Savior through Thy holy incarnation and generation through the power of Thy Divine Father's Holy Spirit which, like unto the sweet murmuring summer breeze whispers to my soul, bidding me to come to my Divine Father where the many mansions be, near the great white throne, nigh unto the crystal sea; but the cares of this world and the deceitfulness of worldly pleasures deter me from the full performance of duty to Thy gracious providence for which I humbly pray forgiveness that I may be truly Thy own in mind, body and spirit. 

Keep me, O God, my Divine Father from sin and indifference to

Thee that I do not become careless of my duty to Thee because of worldliness and evil passions crowding out Thy Holy Spirit through which all blessings flow unto me from Thee. 

Oh but to know! How can I know that my Divine Father in heaven will have mercy on my poor soul! How can I know, if I shall ever be able to attain to that blissful, happy state where I can feel that Christ will say to me, "Well done, thou good and faithful servant, enter into the joys of thy Lord! Well did my blessed Lord and Master say, "ye must be born again;"-born or regenerated by the Holy Spirit of your Divine Father in heaven, before ye can enter into the kingdom of God?" Yes my brother, through prayer, praise and adoration, thanksgiving and good will toward God your heavenly 

Father, and loving service to your fellow-men you shall attain unto the life eternal. 

Risk, risk everything! There is nothing too sacred that must not be given to the services of God or good uses for the salvation of your brethren; for everything must be surrendered to God in order to be subjectively His, nothing else will do, it must be all, all! 

True love must grant everything, mutually, gratuitously, the one to the other, without being constrained by any motive of necessity, but spontaneous love. There can always be access and communion between the spirit of man and the spirit of his Divine Creator when man seeks to be in harmony with God's approving spirit. 

Our Divine Father's spirit is the absolute and only real moral

governor of the universe and it is it which approves or disapproves our every act, word and thought and executes God's will upon us in the day of judgment whether to life-eternal or everlasting destruction. It is to the spirit of God as the moral governor of the universe, to which all are responsible and to no other, as it creates, sustains and executes all things in accordance with God's will, so if you would have the approval or commendation of God's spirit you must hold communion and fellowship with God our Divine Father or He will take the approval of His Holy Spirit from you and you will be to Him as a heathen or unrepentant sinner. 

In our loyalty to God we must emulate the spirit of Jesus Christ's loyalty to the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father in heaven; for only by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father does our Divine Father hold communion with His creatures whether immediately of Himself or mediately through His created agencies.

There is nothing so menial in a person as to ask our Divine Father in heaven for the guidance of His Holy Spirit and then turn right around and ask Him to follow you by His spirit into some little two by four sect or denominational division, for He simply will not have anything to do with such heresy and hypocrisy. 

Our Divine Father always accomplishes His work by His spirit through faith; and without faith it is impossible to please God, for 

He is the author of faith, for by faith He created, through His omnipotent spirit, His universe and all things therein, visible and invisible whether they be dominions, principalities or powers so that all things whatsoever are subject to His spirit. 

We are in the heavens right where we are, and this earth is in the heavens; and there are millions of suns, planets and satellites revolving in the heavenly spaces protected and guided by the power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven; and it is this spirit of our Divine Father which gives, grants, indues, baptizes, pours out, imparts and creates in us those powers, gifts and blessings such as Christ's disciples received on the day of Pentecost. 

The gift of the Holy Spirit proceeds only and always from our Divine Father in heaven whether immediately from our Divine 

Father Himself or mediately through His created agencies; for the

Holy Spirit is the spirit of our Divine Father's person and does not exist apart from Him, any more than our spirit can exist apart from ourselves; as we cannot be rational beings without it, so our Divine 

Father in heaven cannot be a person apart from His Holy Spirit, but with it He is one person only; and it belongs exclusively to His

person only; and anyone exercising any gift of our Divine Father's spirit does it in accordance with our Divine Father's will, as our Divine Father's spirit executes all things in accordance with our Divine Father's will; for our Divine Father operates always and only by His spirit, the executing power of His person exclusively, though He may operate by it through others of His creation according to His will and purposes.

Thus did our Divine Father in heaven operate by His righteous spirit through the prophets, through His Son, the Word, both in His superangelical state as His agent in the creation of all things, and also in His incarnate state as Jesus, the Christ our Lord and Redeemer; and also through Christ's apostles and various other saints, directing them as to what they should do, say and write according as His Divine spirit directed them. It was not the prophets, Jesus Christ, and His saints doing the Works, but it was the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven doing these works through. them, for Jesus Christ, His apostles and all the prophets declare and affirm that they of themselves could do nothing Divine but the spirit of the Divine Father operated through them; and that they did not these things themselves.

Thus does our Divine Father's Holy Spirit operate through and in everything and in various ways severally according to our Divine Father's will and purposes; for by it our Divine Father operated through Daniel and other prophets such as John, Christ's beloved apostle, to foretell history unto the end of the world era; and in various other ways did our Divine Father by His spirit indue His Son Jesus Christ with many diversified gifts for the establishment of His Church and also operated through Christ's apostles for carrying on the work of the ministry after Christ's Ascension; for we read that our Divine Father granted His Holy Spirit to His Son Jesus Christ without measure; and to Christ's apostles did our heavenly Father pour out His spirit in such great measure for the edification of the Church, that some prephesied, some interpreted, worked miracles, healed the sick, cast out demons, spoke with tongues, raised the dead and conferred the gift of the Holy Spirit upon believers by the imposition of hands; but these gifts of power and authority of our heavenly Father's spirit proceed always and only from our Divine Father's person whose spirit the Holy Spirit is. 

It is a marvelous and most wonderful thing for an individual to be in such close harmony with his Divine Father in heaven that his Divine Father will operate by His Holy Spirit through him to ex-

ercise a diversity of gifts even to the conferring of the power of His spirit through the imposition of hands; but it is far more blessed to be ordained of our Divine Father through the power of His spirit unto eternal life by the grace of repentance, as it is the choicest and greatest gift which God has ordained for all who accept the vicarious atonement of His beloved Son, the incarnate Word Jesus Christ and acknowledge Him as their Lord and Savior.

No one can attain unto God's holy presence who does not repent of his sins, and accept the atonement of Jesus Christ, God's only begotten Son's vicarious sacrifice, as his own atonement for his sins; and in this we see our heavenly Father's gracious, loving condescension for sinful man in giving His only begotten Son whose precious blood being shed in our behalf hath obtained the grace of repentance for all the world.

The Bible gives us physical instances in which the people obtained mercy from God by the grace of repentance in which His mercy warded off various physical calamities; but how much more wonderful is it to be saved unto a life which shall never end. 

How much, and how often we sin against our gracious, indulgent Father in heaven by failing to perform the good things which it is our duty to do, as well as doing those evil things which He has commanded that we should not do! Those who sin wilfully and deliberately after they have received the knowledge of the truth, and then refuse to do their duty, there remains no more a sacrifice for their sins, as Christ's mediation in man's behalf has no efficacy for those who are incorrigible sinners; those who sin wantonly and deliberately in blasphemous defiance of God's mercy and treat the blood of the 

New Covenant as an unholy thing, God will not save.

It is a swindle, a fraud, a libel, and a lie for anyone to teach the falsity, "That Jesus Christ is a person in the Deity," as it tends in the mind of the believer, to destroy faith in His mediatorial office to say that the Scriptures teach the doctrine that Jesus Christ is coequal, coessential and coeternal with His Divine Father in heaven from whom He received His being, power and authority, and all that 

He is, has and does.

Jesus says, "that He of Himself can do no Divine work but that the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father works through Him according to His Divine Father's will and purposes; and all that He does, of 

His own will, is to follow out the directions according to the power and authority given to Him by His Divine Father."

All things proceed from that uncreate, absolute independent person

our Divine Father in heaven by whose Holy Spirit all other persons and things are made to exist and operate from its power. Therefore, all who are true children of our Divine Father in heaven worship Him only as the only living and true God who is the creator and sustainer of all other persons and things without exception; and those who go a-whoring after other persons, as Divine beings; and tendering to them Divine worship, are idolaters who are in rebellion against our Divine Father's absolute, omnipotent, omniscient, universal rule, power and authority; and who seek to limit His rule in the minds of the people by proclaiming that there are two or more coequal, coessential and coeternal persons who operate in conjunction and equality with Him, so that neither can operate without the consent and co-operation of the other two making him dependent upon the volition of others.

Divine truth rests upon the gospel of Jesus Christ which says, "The Lord our God is one Lord . . . " and though there be things which are called gods to a true follower of Jesus Christ "There is but one God the Father." We should always give thanks to our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ for this glorious truth-that His Divine

Father alone is God individually without any plurality of person, of division or of parts; for there cannot be two or more independent persons in the Godhead of the Deity, as the infinity or absoluteness of our Divine Father who, in Himself, of Himself and by Himself comprehends all Divine attributes and perfections, are infinite in their nature and character and cannot be limited or divided into divisions or parts as these qualities are inherent attributes and qualities of His person and cannot belong to more than one such being.

It is not through a Divine person but through a person whose nature, essence, substance or spirit-being, was the beginning of His Divine Father's creation, the first begotten of our Divine Father's creatures; His glorious Son the Word, who became incarnate in the man Christ Jesus, that He might make satisfaction for man to the justice of His Divine Father in payment of the debt for all who would believe and accept Him as God's Son and Mediator. 

The life of the individual is in his blood and when Christ's lifeblood was shed as an expiratory sacrifice of atonement for man He gave the life of His body to us that whosoever believeth that He is anointed of His heavenly Father to take away the sins of the world should have life everlasting.

The blood of Jesus Christ expiates the sins of all who do not sin

against our Divine Father's Holy Spirit unto death, as it is through Christ's blood that His life is given to us, blessed bread from heaven, whereof if a man eat worthily he shall receive of our Divine 

Father immortality and the life eternal.

Immortality was lost to the human family through the original sin of our forefather Adam, who inherited all the weaknesses of his transgression, which was death, and passed it down to his posterity; but through the atoning blood of Jesus Christ our Divine Father's only begotten incarnate Son who was the first creature of our Divine Father's creation; and who in the fullness of time our Divine Father incarnated and generated Him a human body which was born of a virgin that He might be man's mediator and savior with His 

Divine Father and Creator.

There is no expiation of our sins, save through the life-giving blood of Jesus Christ, God's only begotten Son the sacrificial mediator, as all sacrificial offerings under the law were but types of the true sacrifice, Jesus Christ, which He made for all irresponsible and penitent folk.

The atonement made by Jesus Christ for us is both objective and subjective; objective as to Jesus Christ's atoning sacrifice, and subjective as to man's faith, and repentance toward God; and the acceptance of His Son Jesus Christ as His Lord and Savior.

Christ has accomplished in His death eternal redemption for all by the sacrifice of Himself, so that whosoever wills to do the will of 

His Divine Father in heaven by faith, repentance and good works shall not perish but live forever.

By virtue of the atonement of Jesus Christ for man, all innocent children, and all heathens who have a good conscience toward God are reconciled or made at one with God; but those who know the conditions of the New Covenant of God with man, and then refuse reconciliation through the atonement of Jesus Christ by not exercising faith, repentance and good works toward God; and love and charity toward their fellow-men, will be judged according to the law which will bring upon them self-condemnation; but when man's submitting act of repentance combines with Christ's atonement for man's sin the individual is forgiven and reconciled to God. 

Since our Divine Creator, the Father, is the only true and living God and the only person who in Himself, of Himself, and by Himself is uncreate; and the creator of all things else whatsoever; and since Jesus Christ, the Word incarnate, is our Divine Father's only immediately begotten Son as the first creature of our Divine Father's

creation and also as the only begotten Son by incarnation, conception and generation of a woman through the operation of His Divine Father's spirit, His Divine Father chose Him as the mediatorial sacrifice or atonement to be offered in behalf of the human race so that all penitent sinners, innocent children, and righteous heathens who have no knowledge of the New Covenant of God with man might be saved; but those who have the gospel of the New Covenant, but do not avail themselves of its benefits which is vouchsafed them through the grace of repentance and faith in Jesus Christ as the Son of God and Mediator, the proffered atonement in their behalf is of none effect and they are lost. 

Our Divine Father's glorious first-born Son of all creation who was not of Adam's race, and not subject to the penalty of death because of Adam's sin by inheritance or otherwise, chose as our Divine Father's Son and agent in the creation of all things else of His Divine Father's creation to become incarnated in a body of flesh through the operation of His Divine Father's spirit that He might offer His body in sacrificial atonement for man's sin, to redeem Him from death, all who through faith and repentance would come unto His Divine Father through Him; for all the human race were subject to death because of Adam's sin and it must needs take a sacrifice on the part of Him who was not subject to the debt of Adam's sin to redeem man from the death which natural man was unable to pay which is Jesus Christ the Word incarnate who was our Divine Father's first-born Son of all creation, and not subject to Adam's sin.

To remove man from this state of death of mortality or death incurred by Adam's transgression was God's object in sending His first-born Son of all creation, His superangelical Word into the world, and how does He do it?

Since the representative of our race was Adam; and, because of 

Adam's transgression we are ordained unto death because of his sin, man cannot of himself recover his lost immortality or the state in which our Divine Father created him and would have sustained him forever had Adam not have sinned. Wherefore, it necessitated the need of a redeemer who is not under the curse of death because of Adam's transgression which none of Adam's race is competent to remove, for they are all alike under the same curse and condemnation of mortality. Therefore, it necessitated a redeemer not of the human family of Adam to redeem Adam and his posterity from the curse of mortality by meeting the requirements of God's law in

behalf of Adam and his posterity; and this is just where our great, loving, merciful, compassionate God and Father was so indulgent toward us that He would not permit His rebellious and disobedient children to be cut off from life forever without one more chance to regain the life of immortality by the grace of repentance, all who would accept the vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ His incarnate 

Son who died in man's behalf.

So God our heavenly Father and gracious benefactor had one beloved and only Son who was the "Beginning of His creation, the first created of His creatures" who was called by name the "Word of God," whom our Divine Father caused to be incarnated by the power of His omnipotent spirit in the womb of a virgin of the house and lineage of David, she to be the mother of our Lord and Redeemer Jesus Christ, the incarnate Word. 

This holy Son of God when He was born, was by Divine command, to be called Jesus; for, said the angel to Jesus' virgin mother

Mary, He it is, who is to save His people from their sins, and the penalty of everlasting death. Thus Jesus' Divine Father anointed 

Him with His Holy Spirit and conferred upon Him the power and authority of mediator and reconciler between God and man. 

It is this only begotten Son of our Divine Father, who is this man Christ, the anointed of God who always acted as mediator between His Divine Father and all creation both in His pre-existent or antemundane state of existence and also as man. 

When God, the Creator and Father of all, did create through His first-born Son of all creation, the Word, all worlds, suns, and satellites, principalities and powers, terrestrial and celestial, God said to His glorious, beloved Son the Word, "Let us make man in our own image and likeness with the power of choice or free moral agency so that he may choose as from himself." So the glorious "Word of 

God," our Divine Father's first-born Son of all creation formed man out of the dust of the earth, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of God's spirit, and man became a living soul. 

Our Divine Father told His beloved Word to plant a garden in Eden; and our Divine Father caused all manner of fruits to grow in the garden, and they placed the man in the garden to dress and keep the garden, and said unto him: "You may freely eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden with the one exception of the tree of knowledge of good and of evil, which in the day you disobey to eat thereof, you shall surely die."

Since time as an entity, is of little consequence to the Lord our

God, He reckons a thousand years as one day and one day as a thousand years; and the one in which Adam was created was the seventh day or division of time from the beginning of the world's creation; but Adam chose to disobey his Divine Creator and ate of that forbidden fruit contrary to the Divine command, and met with mortal death in the close of the seventh day or division of time of the world's creation at the ripe old age of nine hundred and thirty years when he died.

Upon Adam's eating of the forbidden fruit, our Divine Father, who foreknew all things from the beginning, promised Adam that in their bearing and rearing of children He would raise up unto them a redeemer who would destroy the works of the Devil who had seduced them into sin, and in the sixty-second generation of man's sojourn upon the earth the promised redeemer came in the person of the Word incarnate and was named Jesus, the Christ. 

Therefore, God's first-born of all creation, His well-beloved, glorious Son the Word through whom His Creator and Divine Father created all worlds, principalities and powers was not of 

Adam's race; but superior both to Adam's race and the heavenly angelic hosts, yet He did not disdain to bow so low as to condescend to leave His heavenly glory with His Divine Father and be incarnated into Adam's race through a virgin of Adam's race born under the law that He might redeem those under the law by giving His body as the redemptive price which Adam owed to his Divine 

Creator our Father in heaven. Wherefore, did our Divine Father's glorious first-born Son of all creation the Word who was not of Adam's race; but who was created anterior to all other created things whatsoever; and was not subject to the penalties due to 

Adam's sins-since He was not of Adam's race-chose to become incarnated into Adam's race for the suffering of death as a vicarious atonement for the human race that He might free man from the prison of death through faith and repentance to a glad and glorious resurrection at the second coming of Jesus Christ.

It was this glorious incarnate Son of God the Word whom our Divine Father chose to be the promised Messiah, Redeemer and 

Savior by placing Him in juxtaposition between Himself and His fallen creature, man, to act as mediator between our Divine Father and us by participating in our humanity, and giving it to ransom us from sin and its penalty, death; and by thus doing Jesus Christ the incarnate Word has secured from His Divine Creator the grace of repentance for all the world.

So grand, so glorious, so sublime and heavenly is the plan of our Divine Father in heaven for the redemption of man that it fills and thrills our heart with love, praise, glory, adoration, and thanksgiving for His wondrous condescension of love, devotion, compassion, sympathy and good-will toward man, that even criminals would fall down upon their face and love, worship, serve and adore Him only, if they only knew of His wondrous love and compassion for the children of men.

Through faith, repentance and good works, all who would return in their allegiance to God, will be, when Jesus comes, forever free from the penalty to sin; but those who refuse to exercise faith, repentance and good works, God's holy law will forever be visited upon the unrepentant sinner and he will be cut off from God's holy presence; and be destroyed in the second death, the death and destruction of the soul forever and ever.

Christ Jesus, the incarnate Son of God is the gift of God to man, as an earnest of his propitiation; and Christ is the instrument by which the atonement of reconciliation is affected through repentance and regeneration in the heart of man.

It was highly fitting that our Divine Father should send the glorious first-born Son of His creation who had been trained in righteous obedience to His Divine Creator who had done so many creative acts through Him; for there were none of all our Divine 

Father's creation who could so well represent our Divine Father in heaven to us, and plead as our advocate with His Father for us, and stand as the arbiter between God and His estranged children; so our Divine Father incarnated His first-born Son the Word in a robe of flesh who so willingly gives His services as to lay down His life for us that all irresponsible, penitent, and reformed persons should have full payment of their debt to God through His vicarious atonement; and only the careless, indifferent, obstinate and incorrigible sinners will be claimed by the judgments of God's law. 

Our Divine Father is so much concerned about us that He provides an atonement for our sins, in that He gives His only begotten Son for a sacrificial offering in our behalf, because we through the representative of our race have sinned unto death or mortality; and he will be saved who brings the sacrifice to the altar which our Divine Father has provided for him by showing good works, faith and deeds suitable or appropriate for works of repentance in full acknowledgment of his debt. Otherwise, the atonement by our beneficent Divine Father in giving us a savior will avail us nothing as

individuals, so long as we do not confess our sins and turn to God. 

It is not the suffering and death of the guiltless victim the incarnate Word Jesus Christ alone that procures for us remission of our sins, but the sacrifice along with our repentance is the means by which our sins are cleansed away. Christ's blood is an atonement or covering for the sins repented and confessed; and for those inadvertantly committed through ignorance; but let no one think that he is forgiven through the blood of Jesus' atonement in his behalf without repentance and reformation.

Our Divine Father is not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance; and He gave His only begotten incarnate Son, for this cause, that whosoever believeth on Him, and acknowledges Him, through baptism in His name, should receive the gracious acknowledgement of our Divine Father's Holy Spirit of approval.

The penalty due to man's sin, which is death or mortality, is not removed immediately, but mediately by the atonement of Jesus.

Christ through the resurrection from the dead at Jesus Christ's coming again to the earth.

Some will say that the penalty of death is not removed, and that the saint and sinner both alike are held under its power; but God's pure law must be fulfilled: "The soul that sinneth, it shall die. . ." but thanks be to God our Divine Father who giveth us the victory through Jesus Christ our Lord," the saint can look forward to a glad and glorious resurrection, and a crown of life that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for him.

CHAPTER IV 

Our Divine Father who foreknew and planned all things for our redemption, foreordained that the Word, His well-beloved and only first-born Son of all creation would voluntarily be offered as a willing sacrifice for the redemption of mankind; and in so far as they were unaccountable infants or repentant toward God to redeem them from death through the resurrection from the dead. For this reason and purpose our Divine Father in heaven incarnated His glorious first-born Son of all creation, and made for Him a reasonable, rational, sensible human soul like unto His brethren, and sent Him into the world in order that He might offer His body as a vicarious sacrifice unto His Divine Father in man's behalf to the fulfilling of the law for all who would repent of their sins and accept Jesus 

Christ, His Son as their Lord and Redeemer.

God has chosen the best plan and means to beget in man repentance and reformation, where He could save Him unto a life eternal by making it safe to prolong His existence through His personal conduct in providing Him with the means of grace. The means have already been supplied on God's part and only awaits for ratification by each individual of the human race as to whether he will accept the means of God's grace or reject it. 

The moral qualities of a sinless human sacrificial atonement in lieu of the death of the penitent sinner which was affected by the blood of Jesus Christ the incarnate Son of God moves mightly upon the heart and conscience of man, as nothing else could possibly do, to beget in man the desired faith and repentance which leads to man's regeneration and salvation. As the suffering, bleeding, dying

Messiah, the Holy incarnate Son of God hangs upon the cross to expiate our sins by making satisfaction to Divine justice, for our mortal souls, it brings tears of repentance and compassion to our eyes to behold such wondrous love and such great condescension as to die to free us from our sin and its penalty of death. Surely God is righteous far beyond all love and compassion of the human heart, that He gave His loving, obedient and righteous Son, His beloved bowels of mercy, for the salvation of wicked ungodly sinners, if they would but repent and return to Him. 65

Notwithstanding all of the love, sympathy, mercy, sacrifice and good will of our Divine Father in heaven; and His great love for our dying souls, He still beholds a great majority of people tramping the broken body and the spilled blood of His crucified Son, our Lord and only reedemer beneath their unhallowed feet through strivings, cursings, and revilings of our Divine Father's holy name; and as an ambassador of Jesus Christ, I plead with you in His name, "Be ye reconciled to God."

While Christ died for all, yet His sacrifice will be of merit or of efficacy to each individual, only in so far, as it turns him from sin to righteousness.

The aim of our Divine Father in the mission of His Son, the incarnate Word to this earth, was to reconcile man to Himself; and thus He received the commission of reconciliation or at-one-ment between God and man. This entailed the fulfillment of the prophecies concerning Christ; and the fulfilling, abrogation or commutation of the law of sacrifices, and the adoption of the New Covenant of faith in Jesus Christ and repentance toward God.

Reconciliation is not only an effected change in the disposition of man toward God; but it is also a change in man's relationship to 

Him, as faith in Christ is the connecting link which binds man to God; which faith, is the voluntary acceptance and obedience on the part of each and every individual to Jesus Christ our Divine Father's Son, mediator and proffered redeemer; as salvation is a personal affair with each individual, and can be had only by each one accepting Jesus Christ as their personal savior.

All the power or authority of Jesus Christ is derived from His Divine Father, so that all power and authority whatsoever He exercised, was from His Divine Father in heaven; but Christ's Divine 

Father has not only made Him head over all created things; but head over all things to the Church, as He is Son and Heir of all things. The law and the covenant were all instituted through Him as He was God's spokesman in all God's covenants with man; for 

God operated through Him in all His plans and purposes. 

Jesus, the incarnate Word, during His public ministry on earth, as the Christ and Messiah was first baptiszed with the fullness of His Divine Father's spirit for the preaching of His Divine Father's doctrines and the doing of His works; for no one can perform a 

Divine work who is not clothed with the power and authority of our Divine Father's spirit. Christ reiterated times and again that He had no power to do a Divine act of Himself and that it was always

necessary that His Divine Father's Holy Spirit operate through Him to perform a Divine work. 

Jesus in His immortal resurrection secured the primacy over the human race by being the first to be raised from the dead by the power of His Divine Father's Holy Spirit unto the life of immortality. Christ was the first of all humanity to be raised immortal from the grave; and in this He has the preeminence over all the children of the resurrection, having secured for us the propitiation for our sins, He ascended on high and sat down on the right hand of His Divine Creator awaiting the time to be sent at the consummation of the age to call back to earth from their graves, all who through faith and obedience have repented of their sins and turned to God that they might be partakers of His glorious resurrection of immortality. Our Divine Father has appointed a day of general resurrection in which all the righteous dead, the penitent, the innocent and those with a good conscience toward God, shall reign with Christ upon the earth a thousand years; after which the judgment will be set, or executed upon all who have refused obedience to Jesus Christ or remained in rebellion against God shall, with Satan and all those wicked angels that kept not their first estate, and death and hell with all who love falsities will be cast into the lake of fire to perish forever in the "Lake of fire," called the "second death."

Our Divine Father who spared not the ancient world, neither the angels that sinned, nor Sodom and Gomorrah how shall we escape if we neglect the opportunity of so great a salvation. Our Divine 

Father in whose power is our every breath of life and of existence, is granting us this respite of time to repent of our sins and accept the gospel by doing justly, loving mercy, and walking humbly with our Divine Creator.

In all ages our Divine Father has not left Himself without witnesses or the world without knowledge of Himself, of His plans and purposes. Jesus Christ our elder brother in creation was our Divine 

Father's great helping agent in the creation of the world, principalities and powers; and the redemption of man; for it was He whom our Divine Father chose to be the "Lamb of God before the foundation of the world to be slain for the redemption of man;" and He therefore promised our first parent Adam that the seed of the woman would crush the serpent's head by destroying the works of the devil; and this promise was kept in memory by offerings and sacrifices in all ages until the promised redeemer came. Thus our Divine Father has given us His only incarnate Son the first-born of His creation in

the person of Jesus Christ in compliance with His promise to Adam, Abraham, Moses, David and all the prophets, that He would raise up a leader from among the children of Israel through which all the families of the earth would be blessed.

Salvation is the rightful possession of contact with the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven through faith and good works, and the only way to liberate a sin-sick soul from the penalties of God's broken law is to take him out of his moral and spiritual degradation and transplant him into a life of pure, noble, virtuous Christian living and conduct.

The great source and center of power in all things is the mighty and universal power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven the consciousness of His spirit has been felt by millions of people all over the world, and all Divine acts, signs, wonders, prophecies, miracles, creations, and every perfect gift have been attributed to it.

The spirit of our Divine Father in heaven is designated by the appellative Holy Spirit, and all power and authority proceeds from our Divine Father in heaven through it and without it no divine act can be performed.

Nothing in God's realm ever happens, but always comes to pass in accordance with the operation of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father, whose spirit is the willing, choosing, designing, purposing and executive power of His person; for without His Holy Spirit He would have no life, power or authority whatever, and there could be no such thing as an existence for anything as it is through our Divine Father's spirit that He created all things other than Himself and no one can exercise Divine power other than our Divine Father whose spirit the Holy Spirit is; but this does not prevent our Divine 

Father from operating by His Holy Spirit through others according to His will and purposes.

Salvation is not to be found in any institution upon the earth, as it is solely subjective in its intent and content, nor is it found in any outward sign, but in the inward grace of righteousness by which one enters into the realm of God and of His Christ. 

The kingdom of God is in the consciousness of individuals and not in some institution or Church. If we cannot see in our lives any likeness to the moral precepts of good character, of truth and of righteousness as exemplified in the life and teachings of Jesus Christ we must put it down that we are not in the realm of God's kingdom whether we belong to Church or not.

The sin and selfishness of those who adhere to Church creeds and disciplines are a travesty upon the Christian religion when all Christ requires is that we confess Him to be God's Son and Mediator and to live a life of good uses with a penitent heart toward God for entrance into His Church; and all who in their conduct exclude 

Christians from their communion because they do not believe in their Trinity exclude themselves from the kingdom of God; for they neither enter into the kingdom themselves, and greatly hinder those who would enter it. So long as the Church fails to reflect Christian character by fellowshipping only those of her creed, she will fail of her Divine mission to be the light of the world; but when its human representatives practice brotherly love; and teach that the religion of Jesus Christ is a religion of present world health, prosperity, peace and happiness as well as a guide to the life eternal, then the Church will become the most popular institutions in the world, and it will be filled with the true worshippers of God and the disciples of Jesus Christ.

Jesus Christ characterizes His Church as a bridegroom and bride, one fold and one shepherd, one lord and one baptism of which He is the bridegroom, shepherd, and Lord, and all who lay claim to be 

Pope or president of the Church of Jesus Christ are false leaders, liars, villains, and thieves.

It is pure nonsense to call an incarnate Deity as being the Son of God or both the Father and Son of Himself or both the Creator and the creature of Himself.

How could God on becoming incarnate be His own Son and Father or God such as Jesus Christ claims He has? Can He be God, Father, and Son of Himself all at the same time? They say that

Christ's Father at the time of Christ's baptism by John in the Jordan river, was in heaven saying in audible voice "this is my beloved Son in whom I am well pleased;" and that still another Divine person whom they call God the Holy Ghost came down from Christ's Father and descended upon Christ whom they call God the Son. 

Thus they have three God persons of the same nature, essence and substance, but only one Deity, of coequal, coessential and coeternal persons, neither of which is either before or after the others, which of course, is a satanic lie; for it is contrary to all truth. For how could God the Father or first person of Himself baptize the second person of Himself, God the Son, with the third person of Himself, called God the Holy Ghost? It is pure nonsense to say that of our 

Divine Father in heaven: "The first person of himself baptizes the second person of himself with the third person of himself."

The spirit of God or Holy Spirit of God's person cannot be a person proceeding from God's person, for it is the spirit of God's person; for there is no such thing as a person without a spirit, but is a person only with it.

Some refer to the interpolated formula of baptism in the last chapter of the gospel of Saint Matthew which neither Jesus Christ nor His apostles ever taught or practiced; for never in history nor in scripture so much as once are we informed that the Christians used any baptism other than in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins during the first century of the Christian era; and the first departure from baptizing in the name of Jesus Christ only, occurs near the close of the third century when Victor I, bishop of Rome began to assert his authority by force, as Pontifex Maximus over the whole Church which included the heathens as well as Christians, which calumniated later in the semi-heathen doctrine of the Trinity of Divine persons in the Deity, and enforced by imperial decree through Constantine the Great.

Those who teach and practice the Trinitarian formula have but little conception of its heathen origin or how silly, absurd, incon-

sistent, and contradictory it would sound to apply their formula in all of its various ramifications to their godhead of three divine persons in the Deity, as first person, second person, and third person as follows: "God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Ghost."

According to the incarnation of the Trinitarian Deity, the first person of God Himself conceives the second person of Himself with the third person of Himself of which neither the first, second nor third person is God Himself, for they are all three in one and one in three or triune, of which neither is God without the other two. Thus none of the three is God; but the one person of which the three persons combined compose, is the true and only living God and who is different from any and all the three, for He is the fourth person which the three Divine persons of the Trinity compose, consisting of God the Father, God the Son and God the Holy Ghost. There is not a single verse of scripture in which the doctrine of the Trinity finds corroboration save the interpolated baptismal passage in the last chapter of the gospel according to Saint Matthew which is contrary to all scriptural teachings, customs and practices which history amply proves. Nowhere in scripture can there be found a single instance where anyone was ever baptized in the name

of three persons nor is it so much as intimated that any of the bishops, presbyters, elders, or deacons contemporary with the apostles or for a half century thereafter ever baptized their converts in any other name than that of Jesus Christ, for the remission of sins; baptism was a baptism unto repentance for the remission of sins in the name of Jesus Christ our atonement, through whom and by whom our sins were atoned and cleansed away through repentance and sanctification of our person unto the Lord through good uses. All who were baptized in good faith in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ unto the remission of their sins were eligible for the blessings of our Divine Father's Holy Spirit through the imposition of hands by the ordained ministry and for membership in the Church. 

The doctrine of the Trinity or three Divine beings in the Deity, whom they call the triune, three in one, or one in three God is a corruption of Christianity, as the apostles of Jesus Christ and their evangelists-out of the thousands of converts which they baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ-never at any time left us any record or even an intimation that they ever baptized any convert in the name of a Trinity of Divine persons or of Deities. In fact and in truth, they never at any time baptized anyone in the name of a Divine person or of a God of which we have any record; but they did baptize in the name of the Son of God, the Lord Jesus Christ and with the spirit of God, the Holy Spirit; but not in the name of the Holy Spirit so far as the scriptures and history inform us, and it takes but little investigation into history or the scriptures to corroborate this statement.

All the Holy prophets, Jesus Christ, and His apostles and evangelists were baptized with the power and guidance of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven; but we nowhere have any record where any of the prophets, Jesus Christ, or His apostles and evangelists were ever baptized in the name of the Spirit of God, the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven, though all these were baptized with its power, guidance and authority, neither do we find that any of this great host of our Divine Father's chosen agents were ever baptized in His name, there absolutely is not one of record either in profane or sacred history that can be proved to be authentically corroborated by them, but there are thousands of instances to the contrary. None of the prophets, Jesus Christ or His apostles ever believed that they were endued with a Divine person; but they did positively believe, and firmly insisted that they were baptized or endued with the spirit of a Divine person whom they called our Father in heaven, the only living and true God. All who received the spirit of God were endued variously and for quite different offices and purposes according to the work for which our Divine Father in heaven ordained and endued them, as each one's mission, or commission varied according to the call and enduement of our Divine Father's Holy Spirit.

To some, our Divine Father by His Holy Spirit gives faith, wisdom, knowledge, discerning of spirits, prophecy, working of miracles, gift of languages or their interpretation; and the gift of prophecy and interpretation according to the office He designed them to fill, as there were apostles, bishops, presbyters, evangelists, teachers, deacons, and elders who were set apart for the edification and directing of the Church by our Divine Father's Holy Spirit. 

The term Holy Spirit is the name of our Divine Father's Holy Spirit; and it is wholly absurd and inconsistent for one to be baptized or indued in the name of the name of our Divine Father's spirit; but it is wholly becoming and consistent for one to be baptized or indued with the power, direction and authority of our Divine Father's spirit called by appellation the Holy Spirit.

No other person can partake of the same person, nature, essence, substance, spirit and being of our Divine Father in

heaven who is infinite, absolute, and independent in his person and powers, and excludes from his person and powers all other persons and power, as objects of his creation. 

Our Divine Father can neither receive or confer anything as not belonging to Himself; and there is absolutely not anything that is not under His power and authority and owe allegiance and devotion. to Him; and hence the first-born creature of all our Divine Father's creation the Word who became incarnate in Jesus the Christ, and who is next to His Divine Father in power and authority, said of Himself, "I of myself can do nothing, it is my Father who doeth the works;" "All things have been given to me of my Father," for 

He as a creature must be different from and subject to His Divine Father, His Creator, and sole Deity, the only living, Divine person and true God, and Father.

If proof of the universality and power of our Divine Father's Holy Spirit were needed, it is manifest in everything. For instance, we take a seed, perchance of wheat or anything else, it will produce after its own kind fashioning itself into a plant like unto the one from which it grew. This manifests a creative power and wisdom far superior to the power or ability of the human mind to reason, comprehend or reproduce its processes.

Our Divine Father has given to nature which unknowingly and unthinkingly is made in conformity to the will and power of our Divine Father's spirit, and nothing of all our Divine Father's creation can of itself change itself from that which it is to something different to itself. Even the poltroon is dependent upon the spirit of 

God for a change of heart, mind, character and disposition to a life of righteous blessedness.

We are so oblivious of our duties and responsibilities that we fail in a great measure to live in conformity to the will, power, and direction of our Divine Father's Holy Spirit, so that in the end, we will, unless due caution is taken, be lost to the kingdom of God. We must be in harmony with the spirit of our Divine Father the same as a radio receiving set is attuned to catch the ethereal waves from the distant transmitting station. Our Divine Father has planned and created everything to be in final subjection to the power and direction of His Holy Spirit until everything comes under the control or power of our Divine Father; and any and all who refuse this compliance to submit their will to follow the directing power and authority of our Divine Father's spirit, will our Divine Father destroy. 

Man only, of all the creatures of earth, has God made after His

image and likeness of rationality and free moral agency of choice to will, and to do of his own volition according as he wills; but this power of choice was delegated to man for the high and holy purpose of free will to glorify his Creator and be a blessing to his fellowcreatures. Our Divine Father desires that in all things man should be like Himself, free to act, think and do in so far as he thinks and acts in righteousness; and so long and in so far as man acts like his 

Creator, will our Divine Father permit man the power of choice to act forever, otherwise, our Divine Father has set a time limit to those who act in opposition to Him, and will take this power from them at the day when He judges the world of mankind. 

Since the spirit of God or of any person is an indivisible unit, it cannot belong to more than one person, as the willing, choosing, designing, purposing and executive power of a person's spirit belongs to him personally and not to another, and cannot be divided among several or two or more persons, as it is a perfect unit in itself and cannot belong to more than one person who is a unit in himself and not more than one unit, as there is no possibility of there being three persons, units or spirits in one person, unit or spirit which is absurd, and self-contradictory; for we know that the spirit of every person is coherent in himself and reaches as far as his self-consciousness does; and the spirit of God only is ubiquitous and universally felt by people throughout all time and place and the only direct medium of communication of our Divine Father with His creation. 

God has planned a program of righteousness for all of His sentient creatures, in that He has given them direction and the power of choice to act with Him in consummating a heavenly kingdom wherein dwelleth righteousness which is composed of people made perfect by righteous service and good will through the mediation and atonement of the vicarious sacrifice of His only begotten Son our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

It is the spirit of man which wills, designs, purposes and executes our desires and aspirations; and only to the extent that the spirit of man is brought into subjection to the spirit of our Divine Father in heaven; and man is made an instrument of righteousness, will he fit into God's program and become a member of God's kingdom. 

If you would enter into the realm of that blessed one whom we call our Divine Father, God, Jehovah you must bring the will of your spirit, affections and aspirations into subjection with the Divine Spirit of our heavenly Father which is the executor of all things Divine and it will guide you in all things Divine which our Divine

Father would have you to do which is the first step toward the realization of the existence and nature of the kingdom of God. 

There are two different elements in man: the personal ego or spirit with its affections and perceptions, and the house of flesh in which it lives; and as the human spirit must needs have a body of flesh in which to dwell as a son of man, so also, must the human spirit needs be furnished with a spiritual body which is immortal to become a Son of God; but before man can enter this immortal, spiritual state in which the righteous shall be made to dwell, a person must be regenerated or born of the spirit of God if he would enter the kingdom of God.

As the human body must be fed to maintain a substantial, physical habitation for the human spirit, so must the immortal body which will be given us by our Divine Father be fed or clothed with righteousness to maintain a spiritual dwelling. 

When man's spirit hungers and thirsts after righteousness like the prodigal son in the scriptures for his Father's house so that he is constrained to say: "I will arise and go to my Father;" then, and not until then will one be in the right attitude for entering the kingdom of God. It is then that our Divine Father in heaven sees the prodigal son afar off and hastens forth to meet him, and falls upon his neck, as it were, and kisses him, clothes him with beautiful robes of righteousness, puts a golden crown upon his head, and shoes of humility upon his feet, and bids the angels rejoice, and make merry, for this his son was dead and is alive again, was lost and is found; and when the prodigal comes into his father's house of many mansions all that the Father hath will be shared with him. 

Oh, prodigal sons and daughters of our God, come to the house of your Divine Father in heaven, where there is abundance, and much surplus to spare, that you may have a right to the tree of life; and have the privilege of worshipping before His great white throne near unto the crystal sea where you may dwell in the blessed glorious sunlight of His smile worlds without end! Hallelujah, Hallelujah! Amen.

The gospel of Jesus Christ in its purity, is the Divine truth of our religion, and it teaches that there is but one God, the Divine Father; and but one Mediator and Redeemer the incarnate Word, the man Christ Jesus; that Jesus Christ the incarnate Word is the 

Son of our Divine Father in heaven; and that the Holy Spirit is the spirit of our Divine Father in heaven. The gospel of Jesus Christ further teaches us that the Word which became incarnate was the beginning of God's creation, the first created of our Divine Father's creatures who in His antemundane state was His Divine Father's agent in the creation of all things else which His Divine Father created. It was this glorious first-born creature of all creation the 

Word through whom His Divine Father created all angels, worlds, principalities and powers; and it was He whom our Divine Father chose before the creation of the world to be our Mediator, Lord and Redeemer by incarnating Him in the flesh of man; and baptized

Those who have done righteously He shall reward with the life eternal, and those who have done wickedly shall be punished with everlasting destruction. The gospel of Jesus Christ is deserving of all praise; and let all know assuredly that they who plunge into dissipation and wickedness are dead already even before they come to their decease. 

The sins of the repentant sinner go before unto judgment, and they become purified and are cleansed away through the vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ; but the sins of the unrepentant follow after them unto judgment, and are judged according to the law and sentenced to eternal death and everlasting destruction.

The teaching that God became incarnate and that while on earth He was known as the Son of God; but after His resurrection He again became God only; as His manhood was again swallowed up or absorbed into His Divinity, and that He was once again the same identical person in essence, nature and substance as He was before He became incarnate; as His pre-existent or antemundane state was purely spiritual. Such a scheme as this is antichristian, a doctrine of Satan and a delusion of hell; for if God became incarnate He was the same person as He was before; and His incarnation made no change in His person but in His mode of existence only, as He only added to His Divine nature a human nature; and when He was crucified He simply substracted His human nature from His Divine nature which again simply changed His mode of existence but not His person, as He, by changing His manner of existence did not change the identity of His person which would be the same as denying Himself or making out that He is that which He is not; but God cannot be Father or life-giver without a Son and the incarnate God could neither be Father nor Son if He Himself is God incarnate; but Jesus Christ not being God incarnate, but the glorious first-born Son of all our Divine Father's creation, the Word, incarnate; our Divine Father, is the incarnate Word's God, Creator and Father which Christ-the name applied to the Word incarnate -claims as His God, Creator and Father, and His God, Creator and Father claims Christ, the Word incarnate to be His only begotten and well-beloved Son.

The gospel of Jesus Christ is not a history about religion, but religion itself, which teaches us the way of life and salvation through faith, hope and charity which is to be exercised on the part of the individual through the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven, as all the motive, executive and operating power of our Divine Father functions through His omnipotent and ubiquitous spirit, the Holy Spirit, which comprehends all Divine power and authority within itself; and belongs exclusively to our Divine Father's person only; and, since the Holy Spirit belongs absolutely and exclusively to our Divine Father who is the only infinite, absolute and independent one in His person, spirit and powers, all things else are dependent upon Him for all that they are, have and do without exception.

The psalmist David felt the universality of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father when he said: "Whither shall I flee from thy presence? If I ascend into heaven thou art there; if I make my bed in hell thou are there; if I take the wings of the morning and dwell in the uttermost parts of the earth, even there shall thy hand lead me, and thy right hand shall hold me."

It is by reason of our Divine Father's Holy Spirit, that we live, move and have our being, as Christ so beautifully and truthfully said of Himself, "Without my Father I can do nothing;" "It is my 

Father who doeth all these works."

It is even by our Divine Father's sustaining spirit, that we are permitted to do things for a time against His will; but the day will finally come, and it is even at the door, when we will not be permitted to deliberately and persistently rebel against the wooings of His Holy Spirit; for He has set a day of judgment in which He will destroy all evil in the second death of utter annihilation. The time of the day of judgment is already set in which our Divine Father will judge the world in righteousness according to the gospel of 

Jesus Christ. They that have done good shall go forth unto the life eternal, and they that have done evil shall be resurrected unto the judgment of destruction. 

Christ said to Pilate: "You would have no power against me, if it had not been given you from above." It is the glory of God to grant freedom and liberty in order that we may choose, as from ourselves, to love, honor, serve and adore him in spirit and in truth "for the Father seeketh such to worship him," but it would be far better for the wicked had they never been born.

It is through the creating, upholding, and sustaining power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven by which we exist, live, choose and act, and it is the ultimate power and authority to which all must come into subjection; for, said Christ of His Divine 

Father: "As the Father hath life in himself, so has he given to the son to have life in himself;" and, as it was so with Jesus Christ, so likewise, it is with us all; for our being and life have been derived from our Divine Father who is the only uncreate, absolute and independent person; and all things else are but creatures and things of His creation without exception. 

Since our Divine Father in heaven is the Creator or Divine Father exclusively and independently in Himself without persons, divisions or parts He is inclusively and exclusively the one and only person in, of and by Himself Divine; and therefore whatever He wills, chooses, designs, or purposes is inevitable, as our Divine Father is absolute or perfect, His spirit is invincible, all-powerful or omnipotent; and He can of Himself, by Himself and for Himself do every consistent thing or that which is an object of power by means of the unlimited power of His spirit.

The power of working miracles or of creating anything is the prerogative of our Divine Father only, whose spirit in itself, of itself, and by itself constitutes all Divine power and authority without any exception whatsoever, as it is the one and only means by which our Divine Father operates whether He does it personally or through 

His agents.

There is no riddle about either nature or evolution to an intelligent child of God, for His Divine Father is their author; but there are some people in this world who still live in the old stone age, as far as their mental advancement is concerned; because the more ridiculous, absurd, and inconsistent their religion is, the greater their reverence and devotion to it. 

God created anthropoids from the very beginning of the animal kingdom, for Moses tells us by Divine authority that on the sixth day or sixth thousandth year period according to God's reckoning

of time, God created all animals that live upon the land of the earth; and lastly of them all, on the seventh day or seventh thousand year period of God's reckoning, He created man which also corresponds to our knowledge of geology; but God distinguished man, as so much higher than the other anthropoids of His animal creation that man is described as being made in the likeness and image of God, in that man was given rationality, freedom and liberty or free moral agency, with the power to will, understand, comprehend or perceive the relationship of objects; and He made man master over all things upon the earth that live in the air, in the sea and on the land. 

Our Divine Father created all herbs, fish, fowl, plants and animals after their own kind of families and species, and nothing within the history of man has been observed to change from one family of plants or animals to that of another or different family or to that which had no original of its kind within the knowledge of man, as invariably nothing of this character can be found, everything is by the unalterable decree of God, our Divine Father in heaven, as no change can take place but by the will, power and authority of our Divine Creator, as to create or change from one kind or family of animals to that of another is the prerogative of our Divine Creator only; and He has furnished us with but one exception, where He changed His glorious first-born Son of all creation, the Word, who was created a superangelical spirit person into the man Christ Jesus through the incarnation, and generation of the Word by the means of the Virgin Mary.

There has, by the skill and knowledge of man, been a decided development in many species of plants and in some animals from the wild state into which these things were permitted to lapse; but all things produce after their own kind or family far superior to that of the uncultivated, but will lapse into their natural state soon after man ceases to cultivate them.

It is not in the power of man, plant or animal, to choose and become of a different family or nature from that in which they were created; and man with all of his scientific knowledge and skill cannot produce a living organism either of plants or animals; and it can be taken as a scientific hypothesis that like produces like, the same as two things equal to the same thing are equal to each other. 

Science and the Christian religion never are in conflict, though some suppose them to be, for wherein there is a discrepancy or difference as to the same things there is a falsity in one of the two or both which will be found to be neither Christian nor scinetific; for

that which is scientific may be Christian, but that which is Christian is always scientific; but that which is scientific is Christian only when put to good uses; but there are many things in our sciences and religion which are in need of Divine sanction to make them true for they are not in harmony with either.

That our Divine Father hung the world on nothing; and that He created everything after its own kind were religious truths thousands of years before they were proclaimed to be scientific truths; and so it is true in a spiritual sense of all that the prophets, Jesus Christ and His apostles have taught us concerning Christ's life, crucifixion, death, resurrection and ascension, which all came to pass in accordance with the Divine revelations of history foretold, before they came to pass. The soul that sinneth, it shall die, was a

Thus the savior promised to Adam came after four thousand years, at the very time the prophets had foretold he would come. 

There has not, in fact, been a single prophecy which has not been fulfilled in the time appointed and with all the attending circumstances prophesied in the prophecy; and that there will be a resurrection of the dead our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ demonstrated when He arose from the dead, He being quickened unto the life immortal by the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father in heaven.

It is not in the power of any person but that of our Divine Father in heaven to perform a miracle or creative act, as no creature or dependent person can do these things of himself; but our Divine 

Father in heaven by the power of His omnipotent spirit can do these things by His spirit of Himself or by His spirit through other persons; for it is the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in every instance, through whatever person the creative act or miracle is performed, the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father is that which creates or does the miraculous acts. It is always our Divine Father in heaven who doeth all Divine works without exception by His all powerful spirit. If any person other than that of our Divine Father in heaven could of himself do a creative act or perform a miracle, we then would have a good right to doubt there being a Divine Creator; but in the very nature of the case there can be but one uncreate, absolute or independent person.

The prophets, Jesus Christ and His apostles and evangelists who are said to have performed miracles deny any and all such power as belonging to themselves; but to the power of the Holy Spirit of our 

Divine Father in heaven, they attributed all these powers, graces and supernatural gifts; and declared unconditionally and without reserve that they of themselves could do nothing save as the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven operated in and through them.

which would proceed from His Father not many days after He departed from them in His ascension into heaven.

The power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven enters the human soul through an exclusive worship and adoration of our Divine Father in heaven whose spirit, the Holy Spirit is; and communion with our Divine Father as the only living and true God is the prerequisite by which our Divine Father grants through His spirit all grace, power and authority. 

Christ tells us in His sermon on the mount how to worship our Divine Father in an acceptable attitude and manner after the following fashion: "So let your light shine before men that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven; keep your alms secret, then your Father who sees what is secret will reward you; pray to thy Father in thy secret closet, and He will reward you openly; for your Father knows your needs before you ask Him; so do not use vain repetitions like heathens; but when you pray say: Our Father in heaven, hallowed be thy name, thy kingdom come, thy will be done in earth as it is done in heaven; forgive our sins as we forgive our fellow-men; for if you forgive not men their trespasses neither will your Father forgive you; so when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face and retire to some secret place that your fast may be seen not of men, but by your Father in secret, and your Father who sees your secret devotions will reward you." 

Those who follow the instructions of our Divine Father's own incarnate Word, Jesus Christ, will never worship a Trinity of Divine persons, for He worshipped His Divine Father only; and He said further that "all true worshippers worship the Father in spirit and in truth for the Father seeketh all such to worship him." All Divine worship and adoration given to persons other than the Father is idolatrous worship, and wholly out of harmony with the teachings and practice of Jesus Christ and His apostles, however much or however many people have had the doctrine of the Trinity of Deities imposed upon them by baptism by the Antichrist and man. of sin, the Pope of Rome.

Jesus Christ, during His Galilean ministry came from across the sea of Galilee to His own home town of Capranium; and there was a paralytic brought to Him lying on a pallet. When Jesus saw the

faith of those who brought the paralytic, Jesus said to the paralytic: "Courage my son, be of good cheer, your sins are forgiven you."

Some of the scribes said within themselves: "This man speaks blasphemy;" but Jesus said unto them: "Why think ye evil in your heart?" "Which is easier to say: your sins are forgiven or to say arise and walk; but that ye may know that the Son of Man has received power and authority to forgive sins," He said to the paralytic, "Get up and walk, lift up your pallet and go home."

CHAPTER VI 

Jesus Christ, not having any power or authority of Himself was wholly dependent upon His Divine Father for His doctrine and works and for all that He is, has, and does, as not belong to Himself but to His Divine Father as Creator. Here after nineteen centuries, the world is still blindly groping about, wondering at Jesus' marvelous power, when of Himself He says: "I can of myself do nothing, it is my Father who does the works." Many people, looking at the works of Christ, are like children who think that it is the bell on the locomotive which makes the train go, because the source of power is hidden from their view, when it is neither Jesus Christ nor the bell that is the motive power; but the spirit of God moves Christ; and the steam moves the locomotive.

The disciples of Jesus Christ, like their master, were to depend solely upon the direction, power and authority of the Holy spirit of their Divine Father in heaven in all that they teach, do, and speak for it is not they but the Holy Spirit of their Divine Father which is to work in and through them the doctrine and purposes which their Divine Father would have taught and executed without any special thought or reasoning on their part.

People can commune with their Divine Creator and Father as spirit with spirit without any tangible object with which to come in contact such as a person; "for our Divine Father seeks such to worship Him as worship Him in spirit and in truth."

Now, there were with us seven brothers, the first one married a wife and died having no children, and left her to the second brother, the second died and left her to the third and so on until all the seven had her for his wife without any children borne by her. 

Now, in the resurrection whose wife will she be; for they all seven had her for his wife." Jesus answered: "Ye do greatly err, not knowing the scriptures nor the power of God; for in the resurrection they neither marry nor are they given in marriage, but are like the angels of God," immortal beings.

Every sentient being must have or rather be a spirit as well as a body to be a person, as a person is both spirit and body; and the appellative or name, Holy Spirit, is only the distinguishing title of the spirit of our Divine Father's person to distinguish it from the spirits of all other persons which our Divine Father has created. 

The only spirit that has not been created is the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father's person which is eternal only of all existing spirits.
