The union of spirits through faith in God must be supplied with confidence before God's Holy Spirit can work successfully in and through the spirit of man to the healing of his body and where this faith is lacking no cure is effected; but as soon as the union of faith with the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father is perfected, immediately the cure is effected by our Divine Father. When the faith of the spirit of man harmonizes with the power of our Divine Father's spirit either directly or through His indued servants, immediately the cure is effected, as the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father is the only source of Divine power by which cures are effected.

God's spirit.

It is a scientific fact that the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father so universally controls the universe that all His creation of suns, planets, and satellites, in peace and order move, so that our astronomers can calculate the very moment of the arrival and departure of the heavenly bodies to and from a given point in the heavens. 

These heavenly bodies travel billions of miles in their circuits, held in their respective zones by the power of the Holy Spirit of their Divine Creator which some people call relativity, and some others gravitation but which in reality are kept in their respective places by the omnipotent power of our Divine Father's spirit. 

Our Divine Father who created the human spirit of our rational soul with its many and various races, all of one blood and caused

the normal functioning of every human body to operate exactly the same, so that in the bodies of all mankind are contained the same organs and glands which carry out the same marvelous processes regardless of race, civilization, or intelligence; and has so ordered them that they are made to produce after their own kind according to His decree which is unalterable, and there is no crossing of man with other anthropoids, and what is said of man is true of all plants, animals and creeping things.

This creating and sustaining power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father can produce or reproduce any living organism different from itself which the spirit of no other person has the power of doing.

No person but our Divine Father is of Himself able to create or perform a miracle; and it is only the ignorant, stupid and uninformed in things Divine who attribute such things to the prophets, to Jesus Christ, the apostles, and the saints; for it is not in the province of any creature to perform a miracle or act of creation of himself, which belongs absolutely and unqualifiedly to our Divine Father.

Only our Divine Father can create or perform miracles of Himself and by Himself immediately or mediately through others. Immediately our Divine Father created His Son the superangelical Word, and also incarnated and generated His glorious first-born Son of all creation through the omnipotent power of His Holy Spirit by means of the Virgin Mary; but mediately through His superangelical Son the Word, He created all things else of His creation, and performed many mighty miracles through His Son the incarnated Word Jesus Christ during Christ's ministry; and many other instances by others too numerous to mention in this work. 

The spirit of our Divine Father is capable of making His prophets see in Divine revelations things which may be thousands of years in the future the same as if they were in one's immediate presence. 

Ofttimes the sympathetic action of the affection of our rational spirits of one person over the mind of the spirit of another person at a considerable distance without any direct communication of external apparatus, is a communication by affinity of spirits, sometimes spoken of as telepathy or mind reading but in reality it is the spirit of the individuals in communication or contact through the medium of God's omniscient spirit; and such power usually, because more intense, is caused by love, affection or intense longing for companionship on the part of the two persons for each other or even on

the part of one; but between our spirit and the Holy Spirit of our 

Divine Father, it is a keen desire on the part of the human spirit to become like its Divine Father in goodness, love and mercy by the full surrendering of the will of His spirit with all of its powers to the service of God.

Jesus' disciples said to Him: "We are in a desert place, send the people away to lodge in the villages and farms where they can get food," but Jesus said to them, "Give them some food yourselves;" but the disciples answered Him: "We have got but five loaves and two fishes." "Make the people sit down in rows of about fifty each," said Jesus. Then, Jesus took the five loaves and two fishes in His hands and looking up to heaven, He asked His Divine Father to bless the food in His hands, after which He broke them into pieces

and commanded His disciples to set them before the multitude. 

When all had eaten, and were filled, Jesus commanded His disciples to gather up the food that remained over and above what had been eaten, and they gathered twelve baskets full, thus displaying the wonderful power and goodness of our Divine Father in heaven through the power of whose spirit all miracles are performed.

A certain young ruler said to Jesus: "Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?" Jesus answered him, "Why do you call me good? None is good but the one Divine Father, He makes His sun to rise on the just and on the unjust, and sends rain on the good and the bad; but if you would enter into life, keep the commandments, of which the first and greatest of all the commandments is, 'Hear O Israel, the Lord thy God is one Father, and thou shalt worship Him with all thy soul, mind, and strength; and thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself!'" for on these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.

Before Jesus' crucifixion He said to His apostles: "You who have stood by me in my trials, and as my Divine Father has assigned unto me Royal power, so I assign unto you the right of eating and drinking at my table in my kingdom and of sitting upon thrones to rule the twelve tribes of Israel; and now my Divine Father if it please thee take this cup away from me; but thy will, not mine be done;" so they crucified Jesus Christ who called upon His Divine

CHAPTER VII 

It would be our delight to see men awake and make their escape from this Antichrist, the Pope of Rome, who claims to be the vicegerent of God and vicar of Jesus Christ, because it is a bitter and cruel bondage which is a snare of the devil and a delusion of hell which has caused more persecution, grief, sorrow and distress, suffering and bloodshed than all our modern wars put together; but if we cannot be so happy as to welcome you to our fellowship with the Divine Father, the only living Divine person and to His glorious incarnate, and only begotten Son Jesus Christ, still we will do our utmost to bless, instruct and ennoble the world by informing it of the prophecies of the Bible, and of history fulfilled in the workings of the Antichrist and his doctrines. 

The monotheism of our Divine Father was taught to Adam, our first parent, and transmitted by a special line of descendants chosen of God for sixty-two generations until the incarnate Word who, in the person of Jesus Christ, reconfirmed the monotheism of His Divine Father. Jesus Christ in His antemundane state as the superangelical Son of God, the Word, was the very one through whom our Divine Father created and taught Adam and his posterity, Abraham, Moses, and his apostles that the "Lord our God is one Lord," the Divine Father only, and that thou shalt worship the "Divine Father and Him only shalt thou serve." There is not a single exception in all the sacred writings where our Divine Father in heaven is said to be anything other than monotheistic or one Divine person only and we shall stand for this glorious truth, content to leave the result with Him whose spirit stretched out the heavens like a curtain, and whose spirit rules over all that is good and will finally overrule all that is evil with His glory, honor and power.

We who have a scientifically true and certain knowledge of this 

Divine truth that "the Lord our God, is one Divine Lord" only, and that He is our Divine Father by reason of His power to create and uphold all things of His Divine providence, so that nothing that is good will ever perish; and we do not hesitate to say that our heavenly 

Father is only the one Divine existence, as it is upon the impregnable 123

rock of holy scripture and of science upon which our affirmations are based; and we challenge any and all disputants to successfully annul the Divine record which is corroborated by science. 

That there is less than one percent of the ministry that know why they teach the doctrine of the Trinity when there is not so much as one single workable hypothesis in that doctrine which is either scriptural or scientific and is readily disproved by either or both of them to have no foundation in fact, whatsoever might be chosen as an illustration. It simply cannot be done, and there perhaps is less than one-tenth of one percent who know of its origin, so great, so holy, so sublime, so heavenly and so far beyond comprehension or the conception of man that no one scarcely dares to even question its validity, so great is the ignorance of most all people concerning it that no one attempts to explain it though they teach or are taught it every day. Any explanation whatever will show the doctrine of the Trinity of three Divine persons in one triune Divine person preposterous.

There is still small hope of salvation for the world, for we find in all ages how the grace of God has not left Himself without witnesses who spoke under the power and guidance of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father of repentance and reformation toward God; and our 

Divine Creator has Himself declared with an oath concerning repentance: "As I live saith the Lord, I desire not the death of the sinner, but that he should repent; adding also this good sentence: "Turn from your iniquity, O house of Israel!" say unto the children of my people: "Though your sins should reach from earth to heaven, and though they should be redder than scarlet and blacker than sackcloth, yet, if you will turn unto me with all your heart and call me father I will hearken unto you as to an holy people," for thus sayeth the Holy Spirit of thy Divine Father: "Let not the wise man glory in his wisdom, nor the strong man in his strength, nor the rich man in his riches, but let him that glorieth glory in the Lord his Divine Father to seek Him, and to do judgment and justice;" but woe unto them who have said: "With our tongues we will prevail; for

Christ Jesus is theirs only who are humble and not of those who exalt themselves over His flock," for Jesus Christ, the sceptre of the majesty of God, came not into the world in the show of pride and of arrogance, but with humility of mind and of spirit as the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father had before testified concerning 

Him saying: "Lord who hath believed our report, and to whom is the arm of the Lord revealed? For he shall grow up before him as

a tender plant and as a root out of the dry ground; he hath no form or comeliness, and when we see him there is no beauty that we should desire him." 

Let us call to memory the humility of David when he said: "Create in me a clean heart O God, and renew a right spirit within me! Cast me not away from thy presence, and take not thy Holy 

Spirit from me. Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation, and uphold me by thy free spirit." Wherefore, in faith let us also look up to our

Divine Father in confidence, for He is the creator of all things, and let us hold fast to these glorious and exceedingly precious gifts and benefits produced in us by the power of His Holy Spirit. Let us consider, and behold with our eyes His long suffering and the great patience He has toward His whole creation; but all these things must be confirmed by faith in Jesus Christ who spake unto us by the spirit of His Divine Father, and sealed this truth with His own blood that He is the Christ, the Son of the true and only living God, the Father.

Jesus Christ was called the "Word of God" both in the Old and also in the New Covenant, as He represents to us both the will and expression of God, since it was through Him, as the agent of our Divine Father, all worlds, principalities and powers were created and through Him our Divine Father initiated both the Old and New Covenants; and were it not for the holy offices of Jesus Christ in executing the covenants of His Divine Father as a willing sacrifice for our redemption who were lost and undone without an atonement for our sin, which required the blood of an innocent victim to purge us from our sin, we would all be lost. Unless we confess Jesus Christ to be our Divine Father's Son and Mediator there will be no reward left to us from the merits of His death; for, Jesus says: "Whosoever will confess me before men, him will I confess before my Father in heaven, and before His holy angels; but he who will deny me before men, him will I deny before my Father and His holy angels." This, therefore, is our reward, if we confess Him to be the Son of God by whom we have been redeemed, we are joined unto God by the blood of His Son Jesus Chris by keeping His commandments, but if we cast Him off, as a Divine person, and acknowledge Him not as the 

Son of God He will cast us off and say: "Depart from me, I know you not from whence ye are, ye workers of iniquity; for not every one who saith unto me Lord, Lord! shall be saved, but he who doeth the will of my Father in heaven."

If we refuse faith in Jesus Christ as God's Son and Mediator, and

decline obedience to the acknowledging His vicarious atonement by being baptized in His name for the remission of our sins as commanded by Jesus Christ and taught and practiced by His apostles, we cannot be saved. Who will be our advocate with the Father if we be found not to have done what Jesus Christ has commanded us to do? What plea shall we render unto our Divine Father for not recognizing His Son and Mediator as our sacrificial atonement for our sins by being baptized in His name, as into death? To refuse to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of our sins is a denial of His vicarious atonement for us, and all who are thus guilty need not hope in the mercy, and clemency of God; "for to sin wilfully after we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remains no more a sacrifice for our sins," but a fearful looking for the vengeance of God which shall destroy His adversaries. 

So while we are in this world let us give diligent heed to what Jesus Christ and His apostles taught and practiced, that we may conform our life, while there is yet time, to the holy covenant of our Divine Father; "for if we confess our sins He is just and merciful to forgive us, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness;" but if we do not repent of our sins in this world our sins will follow after us unto judgment to our condemnation, as there will not be any chance of repentance after death or in the day of judgment.

We seal our own fate according as we receive and practice or disregard the gospel of Jesus Christ the Son of God; for our Divine 

Father will not hold those guiltless who deny His Fatherhood and the sonship of His glorious, beloved Son, Jesus Christ, by saying that there are three Divine persons to be worshipped and adored coequally, and coessentially, with equal power, glory and majesty with neither before nor after the others. The Holy Spirit of our 

Divine Father knows all things beforehand and searches out every infinitesimal particle of our every thought, word and deed, yea even the deep things of God, and of all His universe which are all foreknown; and it will neither deceive nor be deceived, nor will it grant us absolution for our sins which have not been repented in this life. 

Jesus said to His disciples: "The Holy Spirit which my Divine 

Father will give you in my name, it will teach you everything that

I have said unto you the same as it has taught me . . . truly, truly, I tell you whatever you ask the Father in my name, He will give it to you; hitherto you have asked nothing in my name; ask and you will receive that your joy may be full."

Our Divine Father who, in the beginning, created us by the power

of His spirit, has the power to preserve and keep us eternally by the power of His spirit, and as an earnest of His intention to preserve His faithful children, He has bountifully manifested, when He raised up His Son Jesus from the dead. It was for this very manifest purpose that our Divine Father incarnated His glorious, beloved Son, the Word, to show in the most effective manner possible His power, love, mercy, goodness, pity, compassion and justice to His fallen creatures.

Notwithstanding, man's rationality, liberty and free moral agency God's omniscient spirit foreknows the ultimate choice of every individual from the foundation of the world, and therefore made all necessary provisions for the consummation of the good and the bad. 

Oh the marvelous intuition, conception, foreknowledge, wisdom, discernment and cognizance of God! The foreknowledge of whose spirit comprehends all eternity in every particle as well as in its ultimate, completed perfect state; and therefore, it was a small matter for 

Him to know even our most secret thoughts and acts before the world began. 

Understand then, dearly beloved, that our great and glorious

Divine Father hath beforehand manifested all things unto us by His holy spirit and made provision for our redemption before the foundation of the world, wherefore we should give praise, glory, honor, thangskiving, worship and adoration for our Divine Father's beneficent spirit of love and goodness toward His erring creatures for which reason we should say Abba Father, dear Father!

It is sinfully wicked to attribute Divine power to any person save our Divine Father only; for all prophecy, miracles and creative acts belong absolutely and unqualifiedly to our Divine Father's spirit and not to the agents through whom He operates as mediums or conductors of His Divine power; and it is essentially wicked, sinful, and degrading, yea, satanic for our Antichrist ministers to announce to the world that Jesus Christ or any other of the creatures of our Divine Father is coequal, coessential and coeternal with our Divine Father in heaven, the Creator of all persons and things other than Himself.

All Divine worship and adoration belongs individually and exclusively to the one person of our Divine Father only; the only true, and only living Divine person; and for this reason the Son of God, the Word incarnate, Jesus Christ says: "Thou shalt worship the 

Lord thy God, and Him only shalt thou serve;" and He also set His disciples an example of how to pray when He said: "Our Father in

heaven, hallowed be thy name, thy kingdom come, thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven." Some will contend that this is not the 

Lord's prayer; but it is as much His prayer as any prayer He ever prayed as it expresses His relationship to His Divine Father and His feelings toward Him.

The preachers of our modern world want to kill every one who opposes their antichristian orthodoxy of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person; and they challenge Jesus Christ and His teachings like the Pharisees and Sadducees of the Jewish Sanhedrim who thought by putting Jesus Christ and His followers to death they could end the whole sorrowful mess to all their predicaments; so they crucified God's glorious Son; but His Divine Father clothed 

His incarnate first-born Son of all creation with immortality and the life eternal; and granted Him power and authority to have life in 

Himself; and through His vicarious sacrifice, to give life to millions of others. So, the Sanhedrim, instead of beholding a dead criminal in the person of Jesus Christ, as they had expected, they, "Beheld the Lamb of God who taketh away the sins of the world." 

Jesus foreknew from the Divine revelations which He had from the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father what His Divine Father would have Him to do, and that His Divine Father would bring it to pass; and He therefore related them to His apostles before time, so that when they did come to pass they might believe; for, said He: “I have received power and authority to lay down my life and take it up again."

Our Divine Father is not only God or Deity in Himself because of His uncreate independent existence; but because He is the creator of all other spirits, persons and things, animate and inanimate, absolutely and independently; as it was His spirit that produced, by its all-powerful will, all things; for it is our Divine 

Father who only is unoriginate. It is impossible that our Divine 

Father who only is unoriginate, infinite, absolute and independent could be given anything or receive anything as not belonging to Him; for He is the author or fountainhead and source of all things as their Creator.

Our Divine Father who is the only person without an originator; as He is the only uncreate, cannot compromise His person, nature, essence, substance, power, being or authority with that of any other, as He cannot produce or reproduce His own person, being, and powers which are without an original, uncreate, and infinite; and it is the height of absurdities that Jesus Christ is said to be coequal,

coessential, and coeternal and equal in power, glory and honor with His Divine Father; as there is nothing that is not comprehended in that which is infinite and universal in power, wisdom, time and place.

All things are absolutely dependent upon our infinite Father for their existence and powers whether singly or collectively, as He is the one and only person without an originator or creator; but He is the originator or creator of all things else other than Himself, and therefore, no other person can share the infinite perfections, qualities, attributes and powers of His own self-consciousness inherent in His person, as anything created or produced in any way, cannot in the very nature of the case be the same as that which is uncreate. The uncreate is independent, and the create is dependent and the two are opposites, world without end.

Jesus Christ or any other creature can never become independent even in their immortal, glorified state, as the uncreate and independent must forever remain the same; and that which is created and dependent must forever remain a creature and dependent; and therefore, no one can ever become like His Divine Creator save in the power of choice in the presence of an alternative, and only in a moral sense can He pattern after Him in His own little way, as God has created him a rational creature with free moral agency, but is responsible to his Divine Creator for his own moral character, under the penalty of destruction to make good; but His commandments are not grievous.

Two persons are said to be one or as one when they are in harmony or accord of agreement, as touching anything to which each concedes by concurrence. Thus any number of people may be atone-ment with God when their wills are in harmony with God's will, plan or purposes, or in subjection to the Holy Spirit of God; and in this sense only can Jesus Christ and His infinite Creator and Father be one, one not in person, but one in agreement to His Divine Father's will as concerns Himself; and in this way does Jesus Christ explain his oneness with His Divine Father, when He says: "I do always the things that are pleasing to Him." But this oneness with 

His Divine Father does not make Jesus Christ a Divine person in the Deity no more than a person agreeing with the President of the 

United States would also make him president likewise.

Two persons, spirits or things which are units in themselves singly or individually do not change their status as units when in agreement with other units, for a unit cannot be more than that which it

is. There might be ever so many finite units or entities with different characteristics or natures; but there cannot be two or more entities, units, persons or spirits with separate volition and thought in one person, for nothing can be the opposite from what it is both at one and the same time. Therefore our Divine infinite Father precludes and excludes there being any other such person, spirit or being, such as our Divine Father is said to be, for infinity comprehends everything of the same kind, nature, essence or substance and cannot belong to more than one infinite Divine person who in Himself, of Himself, and by Himself comprehends the whole of Deity; and those who claim two or more Divine persons in the Deity are satanic liars and falsifiers of God's word; but all peoples, Churches, sects, denominations, and parties that use such terms, generally do so without knowing they are following the Antichrist and his satanic majesty the devil; for a Divine triune person has no signification either in fact or in truth; but many of these have committed this conundrum to memory when they were children and thought that it was a mortal sin to question its truthfulness, and got so in the habit of using these terms as sacred and Divine though they have never understood their meaning.

It is scarcely possible that among the myriads of millions of sentient creatures on this and other spheres that there are any two persons in thought and volition even approximately alike; and for anyone to affirm that there are three entities, units, persons, spirits and beings who are each infinite, absolute, independent, coequal, coessential and coeternal; and equal in power, glory and majesty are the biggest humbugs and deceivers of babes and weak-minded people that walk the earth; for such people are not exercising any religious reason or sense of truth whatever; and yet we hardly can call such people insane, because they use so little reasoning sense in religion which would prove such a hoax and riddle to even elementary graders in our public schools, as to dwarf all their reasoning powers, if permitted to apply such teachings to their studies, for how could they ever have three units or persons in one or one unit in three units or persons which are to be neither added or subtracted, for if they did subtract two Divine persons from the one Divine triune person they would still have one Divine person left of the one person from which they have already subtracted two persons, and if they added two Divine persons to the other one it would make but one Divine triune person; but three units, persons and beings with distinct or separate volition and thought which are independent of

each other; as neither is dependent upon the thought or volition of the others for his actions. Nothing in heathenism is quite so utterly ridiculous as the doctrine of the Trinity of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person.

Whenever anyone enters into harmony with God's plan of salvation, and accepts Jesus Christ, God's Son, as the Word incarnate whom our Divine Father indued with the power and authority of His Holy Spirit to act as our mediator and savior in the redemption of the world through the act of faith and repentance on the part of man, man immediately comes into possession of the way of life and truth; for, "no one," says Jesus, "cometh unto the Father but by me.' "" 

Jesus Christ the Son of God says: "No one has seen God at any time save His Son only, He hath seen Him." Jesus said to His disciples before His ascension: "I come from God, and now I return to Him;" "I ascend to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God."

Our Divine Father does not share or compromise His person, power and authority with anyone, as He is perfect or absolute in person, power and authority, and nothing can either be given to Him or taken from Him as not belonging to Him; and where there is unity or oneness between God and His creatures there must, on the part of the creature, be an absolute obedience, and complete subjection of the will of the creature in loyalty, love and devotion to God and His righteousness. Christ's subjection or subordination to the will, power and authority of His Divine Father was so perfect, absolute or complete that He could say in His prayer for His disciples, "As thou Father art in me, and I in thee, so may these be one in us that the world might believe that thou hast sent me."

This oneness of unity for which Christ prayed is that of such a unity more perfect in agreement than that which reigns in the councils and opinions of those who embrace the same notions, desires, aspirations, and purposes to be attained, as to think, act, and do as one mind, heart and soul under the directing power and influence of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven disregarding His own personal inclinations or desires save but that of doing His Divine Father's will. 

Oh, how I do wish, hope and pray that like my Lord and Savior

Jesus Christ I might become in mind, soul and spirit, perfect in obedience without any reservations or compromises to divide my love, affection, and devotion to Him to whom I owe all that I am,

have or hope to attain! The greatest possible honor that can come to Jesus Christ or any other creature of our Divine Father's creation is a perfect or complete surrender of all that we are, have and do, to our Divine Creator's will; for such consecration only is the highest possible state of glory, honor and blessedness to which man can attain; as it is the supreme state of exultation and glory. 

The oneness or unity between the creature and his Creator may be much more nearly perfect than could possibly exist between finite persons without the perfect mediation of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father as interpreter, because two finite persons have no perfect understanding of each other like the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father which is omniscient or all-wise and knows the spirit of man perfectly and can greatly assist our infirmities in coming to a complete understanding and unity of spirits, as it is able not only to reveal all things but able also to show each one when he is in harmony with his Divine Creator and Father.

Nothing can be in harmony which in itself is imperfect; and nothing is morally perfect until it becomes in perfect harmony or subjection to the Holy Spirit of our heavenly Father; and no one becomes a member of God's realm without a new and heavenly birth through the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father, wherein we become children of our Divine Father and are made partakers of immortality like our blessed Savior Jesus Christ through the resurrection from the dead. Membership in the Church militant with all of her sins and folly constitutes no one a member of God's realm. 

Jesus Christ dates the setting up of the kingdom of God or setting up of His Church from the days of the preaching of John the Baptist; "The Law and the prophets were until John, since that time the kingdom of God is preached, and all men hurry into it . . . from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violence take it by force, for all the law and the prophets prophesied until John." "Until John," gives the close of the Law; and, "From the days of John," the commencement of the kingdom of God and of the Church begins.

The first ray of God's coming kingdom flashed upon the vision of Simeon the aged patriarch and prophet of God who was a just and devout man which waited for the consolation of Israel; and the power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father was upon Him; and it was revealed unto him that he would not see death until he had seen our Divine Father's Christ. Great men, patriarchs, kings and prophets spoke aforetime of that which had now come to pass in

the little town of Bethlehem of Judea; and now, for nearly two thousand years, learned, wise, and holy men, have while worshipping Him disagreed and contended about who He is, where He came from as to His origin, the nature of His person, the source of His power, His relation to God and His relation to man. 

Great has been the amazement over this extraordinary personage who entered the world by birth without any reputed earthly father in the flesh, and left the world by ascending into the heavens. 

The angel Gabriel announced to the Virgin Mary her conception of the Child Jesus by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father; and He was called the "Son of God, . . . the Son of the Father, . . .. and the 

Lamb of God who taketh the sin of the world."

At the baptism of Jesus the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father descended in great power and authority upon Him by induing Him with the power of prophecy, of healing, of working miracles, and of preaching the gospel of the Kingdom. One of the notable miracles which the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father performed through His Son Jesus Christ was the raising of Lazarus of Bethany of Judea who was the brother of Martha and Mary, and a special friend to Jesus.

Any close student of the Bible will readily observe that no one does anything Divine or connects up anything with the Divine, but by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father; as it is the sole and only medium of transmission of power, of subsistence, and of authority between our Divine Father and all things else whatsoever its character, nature, essence, or substance, as all things created subsist and are endued with their nature, life and subsistence; and in the case of men and angels they are also endued with rationality or free moral agency by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father.

That which is spiritual is born of the spirit of God, the same as that which is flesh is born of the flesh. To be born of water does not mean to be baptized in water or with water, as so many ignoramuses interpret Jesus' words to Nicodemus to mean, for no one is born by being dipped in water or by having water poured upon him as Jesus fully explains to Nicodemus that which is flesh is flesh and that which is spirit is spirit. Ye must be born again not of the flesh or of water, but of the spirit of God. To be born of water is to be born of flesh; but to be born of the spirit is to be regenerated by the power of God's spirit unto justification through faith in God's 

Son as mediator and redeemer; for, says the apostle Paul, "Other foundations can no man lay than what is laid, which is Christ Jesus."

When Jesus asked His disciples: "Whom do ye say that I the son of man am?" Peter answered, "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God;" and Jesus commended him saying: "Blessed art thou Simon Barjona, for flesh and blood hath not revealed this unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven; and I say unto thee, that thou art Peter; and upon this rock of confession, 'Thou art the 

Christ, the Son of the living God,' I will build my Church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against her." The rock is the revealed truth which the Holy Spirit of our heavenly Father had revealed to Peter, that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of the only living and true God. "Who is a liar but he who denies that Jesus Christ is the Son of God?" But, if you say that Jesus Christ is a Divine person in a

Divine triune Deity coequal, coessential, coeternal and equal in power, glory and majesty, then have you denied that Jesus Christ is the Son of God or that He has a Divine Father which the Bible calls the doctrine of the Antichrist of which all Catholics and most all Protestants are guilty of teaching.

The terms God, Father and Creator are used in the scriptures when referring to the Supreme Being whom we call our Divine Father; for the Son of God cannot be Divine or uncreate or independent, and be a creature of our Divine Father whose Son He is, and those who say that Christ is coequal, coessential, and coeternal with His Divine Father are satanic liars whose aim is to deceive; for Christ is not the Divine Son, God-son or Son-God; but the Son of Him who is Divine, the Son of God or God's Son; and those who say Christ is the Divine Son are liars, villains and hypocrites. 

The rock upon which Christ said He would build His Church, is the unshaken faith of the disciples, "That Jesus Christ is the Son of God;" for it is the confession as well as the mode of baptism required by Jesus Christ and His apostles for membership in the Christian Church, that people confess that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, and be baptized in His name for remission of sins and for induction into the Church.

Hear Saint Peter and the rest of the apostles on the day of Pentecost when they were endued with a special outpouring of power and authority of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven which spoke through them saying: "Repent and be baptized 

Every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins and ye shall likewise receive the gift of the Holy Spirit." All of 

Jesus' disciple's preaching, teaching, doctrine, works, miracles, baptisms, prophecies, and prayers were rendered in the name of

Jesus Christ the Son of God; and it is a falsity to say that the Holy 

Spirit of our Divine Father speaking through the apostles and evangelists of Jesus Christ on the day of Pentecost commanded them to baptize in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins, and for induction into the Church; but at a later date commanded that all should be baptized in the name of the most holy Trinity of three Divine persons in one triune Divine person for remission of sins and for induction into the Church.

It is preposterous to say that the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven directed the holy apostles and evangelists on the day of Pentecost to baptize their converts in the name of Jesus Christ the Son of God for the remission of sins and for induction into the Church; and then sometime near the beginning of the fourth century through the Pontifex Maximus of Rome command all holding fellowship with the Church at Rome to baptize all their converts in the name of God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Ghost under penalty of excommunication and disfellowship with the holy apostolic see of Rome as unworthy brethren; but in subsequent councils the Church at Rome decided to enforce upon the Christian world her mandates of conformity and uniformity with the teachings and practices, rules and regulations of the bishop of Rome as the vicegerent of God and vicar of Jesus Christ; and this they did at the 

Council of Nicea by imperial authority of Constantine the Great to use the civil power of the state to enforce people to be baptized in the name of the Divine Trinity of Father, Son and Holy Ghost in accordance with the wishes of the Holy Father, the Pope, who as God's vicegerent and vicar of Jesus Christ and head over all the Church; and all who persisted in baptizing their converts in the name of Jesus Christ the Son of God for remission of sins and for induction into the Church should be punished with both ecclesiastical and civil penalties to the confiscation of their property, and disfranchisement of all civil rights. Henceforth all baptisms according to the teachings and practices of the apostles of Jesus Christ in requiring a confession of Jesus Christ as the Son of God and of baptism in His name for remission of sins and for induction into the Church were to be proscribed; and baptism in the name of the most holy Trinity to be substituted in its place, and enforced with all ecclesiastical and civil penalties upon non-conformists. It was in this way that the Antichrist, the man of sin, the son of perdition, the bishops of Rome was clothed with the power of Pontifex Maximus over all religion and morals in the Roman Empire, and those

who refused compliance were either banished, imprisoned or put to death.

The Roman Pontiff claimed the primacy over all the bishops of Christiandom and enforced both by ecclesiastical and civil penalties his mandates, of the triune God, baptism in the name of the Trinity, his change of Easter, and of the Christian Sabbath, and his appointment of holy days and obligations such as now observed throughout the world; but it was many years, in fact centuries before the ancient customs of Jesus Christ and His apostles were completely destroyed. 

The Churches in Asia, Africa, and all the East, as well as in Spain and England refused to comply with the Pope's mandates which he issued through the imperial decree of Constantine the Great; and he therefore set about to reduce all these Churches into dependencies of the "Mother of harlots and abominations of the earth," the Roman Catholic Church; and make of the Church at 

Rome the head of the "Imperial Roman Metropolitan See." So a persecution was waged throughout the Roman Empire against all who followed the teachings and practices of the apostles, who always and only baptized their converts in the "Name of Jesus Christ for the remission of their sins;" and kept their Easter on the fourteenth day of the month Nisan; and the Sabbath according to commandment which was Saturday the seventh day of the week instead of Sunday the first day of the week; which were all changed by the vicegerent of God, and vicar of Jesus Christ, the Antichrist and 

Pontifex Maximus, the Pope of Rome. 

Arius, a presbyter of the powerful Metropolitan Church of Alexandria in Egypt, with a vast multitude of Christians in all parts of the Roman Empire held strenuously for the teachings and practices of the apostles of Jesus Christ against the tritheism of the Pope of Rome. The countries which especially opposed the doctrines of the 

Pope of Rome were France, Spain, Africa, England, Germany, Syria, Greece and much of Italy, until the Roman Catholic historian, Reeves, confesses: "The whole world groaned to find itself Arian or Christian in contradistinction to Romanism;" and thus the proverb was verified: "All the world against the Roman Bishop and he against the world;" but the metropolitan see of Rome being situate at the head of the old Roman government, and the Pope having secured the imperial favor which was backed by the civil power of the government to bring into subjection their Christian brethren to the Roman Pontifical faith; and she was not loth to wage war and persecution above a thousand years against those who

followed the teachings and practices of Jesus Christ and His apostles until there were none left.

This homicidal schism which sprung up in the Church, because the bishop of Rome wished to usurp all power and authority over the Church to the exclusion of all others began to formulate doctrines and schisms for his own exultation and aggrandizement by proclaiming there are three Divine Persons to be worshipped in one triune Divine person, by saying that the Son of God, and the spirit of God are each Divine persons coequal, coessential and coeternal with our Divine Father, and equal in power, glory, and majesty with Him. 

The Pope of Rome making over the incarnate Word Jesus Christ God's only begotten Son into two and a third of a person by proclaiming that Jesus Christ is both a Divine person, and a human person, and a third part of that one Divine triune person which He calls the Trinity or three in one person, of which the Father and His Holy Spirit are the other two Divine persons comprehended in and consisting of the one Divine triune person through the hypostatical union of the three into one by absorbtion. After the Pope had conjointly or co-operatively molded the three Divine persons into one Divine person, the triune God, and by absorbing the humanity of Jesus Christ into the Divine through the joining of the Divine and the human natures of Jesus Christ into one through the hypostatical union, he called the three Divine persons, and the man Christ Jesus absorbed by the hypostatical union into the Divine, the holy and Divine Trinity of the one Divine person of the triune God, which is so simple and comprehensive that even a baby should comprehend and understand it in order to salvation, or be lost for its obstinancy and rebellion to the Pope of Rome. 

Thus, the three Divine one person is to be worshipped as a Trinity of Divine persons in the one Divine triune person, and the one Divine triune person in the three Divine persons, ex cathedra, by order of his holiness the Pope, whose conundrums the whole world worshippeth, love, honor and adore, so much so as to even be baptized in its name. Oh God, our righteous Father in heaven, what a blasphemy of Thy holy name; and what a travesty upon the

Christian religion of Thy holy Child Jesus is this doctrine of the Trinity!

The Divine Father, and the Divine Son, and the Divine Holy Ghost of the Pontifex Maximus of Rome when taken singly-as each one comprises but one third part of the one Divine person of the triune God-is not God or Divine without the other two Divine

persons, as there can be but one God; so neither is God without the other two, as God is but one Divine triune person and not three Gods; though all the three persons be Divine persons, they are not to be considered singly, but hypostatically or co-operatively as but one person without division or parts, with neither before or after the others, as all are coequally, coessentially, and coeternally the same and of the same nature, essence and substance; for such as the 

Divine Father is such is the Divine Son and such is the Divine Holy Ghost subsisting in the one Divine person of the person of the triune God. Although they have been arranged systematically so as to give our Divine Father the first place in the Trinity, His Son, the second person in the Trinity, and the Holy Ghost the third place in the Trinity, and are to be addressed as God the Father, God the Son and God the Holy Ghost, in the fashion of their precedence, as Christ the Son of God proceeds from the Father and the Holy Ghost proceeds from both the Father and the Son according to the Pope's infallible decrees. 

His holiness, the Pope of Rome, would have us understand that the three Divine persons of which the one Divine person of the triune God consists and subsists, as God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Ghost are all Divine; as they all partake of the same original stock in nature, essence, and substance, eternity, infinity, omnipotence, omniscience, omnipresence and immutability; that they are coequal, coessential and coeternal, and equal in power, glory, and majesty without division, parts or passions as there cannot be more than one Deity or Divine person properly so-called, and all other Divine persons are only parts, portions, divisions or installments of the parent or original stock before it became divided into the three Divine persons of the holy Trinity which compose the one Divine person of the triune God which finally split into three coequal, coessential, and coeternal parts or persons which must be united into one homogeneous whole by an hypostatical union of the three Divine persons conjointly through absorption or blending of their persons into one infinite, absolute and independent person; as it is impossible that there should be more than one uncreate, absolute and independent person in the Godhead of the Deity, and hence they are all alike, Divine; and of the same nature, essence and unity of person.

Can anyone who has so much as a thimble full of brains fail to see or understand that this doctrine of the Trinity of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person is a humbug, a conglomeration

of absurdities, inconsistencies and contradiction which cannot be corroborated by scripture, nature, science or reason? 

The Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven forewarned us through the prophets, through Jesus Christ and His apostles and evangelists of the rise of this Antichrist doctrine of the man of sin, the son of perdition, the Pope of Rome who would claim to be God's vicegerent, and the vicar of Jesus Christ preaching a different gospel than that enjoined by Jesus Christ and His apostles in their teaching and practice.

CHAPTER VIII 

Jesus Christ, as the "Word of God," was the beginning of God's creation, the only immediate created Son of our Divine Father's creation, as all things else were created through His Son, the Word, as His Divine Father's agent.

Jesus Christ is the only begotten Son of His Divine Father both in the antemundane creation and also in His mundane creation, as He is the only person our Divine Father ever created and also incarnated by the immediate power of His Holy Spirit without any other intervening agency; as all things else were created by our 

Divine Father mediately through His first-born Son of creation, the Word, thousands of years before the Word became incarnate and named Jesus by the angel Gabriel in his annunciation to the Virgin Mary of the incarnation of God's first-born Son of all creation, the Word, of which she was to be the mother, by conception and generation through the power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven.

The incarnation of the Word, our Divine Father's first-born Son of all creation did not change our Divine Father's status quo toward the Word, as it was only a change in the mode of existence of the Word, and not a change in His Divine Father, as the Word was always and only His Divine Father's Son from the inception of His creation, as well as after His incarnation, resurrection and glorification as our Lord and Redeemer. 

You will observe that none of the vicissitudes or changes through which our Divine Father's Son passed as the Word, as the incarnate Word, or as the resurrected Lord and Redeemer of mankind, He was ever and always our Divine Father's Son in whatever stage of existence the Word found Himself, as He was ever and always dependent upon His Divine Father for His creation, existence and powers, for all that He is, has and does; and for this very reason 

Christ attributes His person, life, doctrine and works to His Divine Father in heaven whose Holy Spirit operated in and through Him to accomplish the works of God, our Father in heaven.

It is quite impossible that of three Divine persons in a Trinity or 144

triune God coequal, coessential and coeternal with each other, there could be any such relationship as Father, Son and Holy Spirit existing between their persons; as there could not be three Divinely distinct entities, units or persons in one Divine person in which neither of the Divine persons are either before nor after the others, such as the holy Trinity is said to be; for, if God would be a triune person in Himself, how could the first part or so-called first person of Himself, cause the second part, or so-called second person of Himself proceed or separate from the first part of Himself; and how could the third part or third person of Himself proceed from the other first and second parts or persons of Himself and all three be comprehended in but the one Divine triune person of Himself without confounding the unity of His triune person with the Divine Holy Ghost which are distinctly entities, units and persons in themselves, of themselves and by themselves without being hypostatically melted or molded into one person who could be neither more nor less than one Divine person; and all this without any absurdities, inconsistencies, contradictions or falsities? Our ever-blessed and beneficent Divine Father who is the living God and only Divine person eternally subsisting of Himself and by Himself, would be in a pretty dilemma to give two-thirds of His person, power and authority to two of His coequals so that He would have to consult them in order to act.
