Shortly after the spirit of God through Jesus Christ had fed the multitude of five thousand people with five loaves and two fishes, an immense multitude followed Jesus attracted to Him by the wondrous miracles which the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father accomplished through Him; and the wonderful words of God which 

He spoke concerning the sacrificial offering of His body which was to be given as a vicarious atonement for all peoples down to the end of the world. "I am the bread of life . . . my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven; for the bread of God is He which cometh down from heaven and giveth His life unto the world. Your fathers did eat manna in the wilderness and are dead; I am the bread which came down from heaven that a man may eat thereof and not die; I am the living bread which came down from heaven, if any man eat of this bread which I shall give him he shall live forever; and the bread I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world. Except ye eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood ye have no life in you whosoever eateth my flesh and drinketh my blood dwelleth in me and I in him. As the living 

Father hath sent me, and I live by the Father, so he that eateth me, even he shall live by me. I am the bread which came down from

heaven, he that eateth my flesh and drinketh my blood shall live forever."

Jesus did not emphasize His literal body of flesh and blood so much as the truths which they represented, for He says: "The flesh profiteth nothing; the words I speak unto you, they are spirit and they are life."

It is the spiritual acceptance of the vicarious atonement of the flesh and blood of our Divine Father's only begotten Son Jesus Christ for the life of man individually by which man is to live forever; and not the mere eating of bread and drinking of wine in representation of His broken body and shed blood which are only the evidences representing the giving up of His life and the acceptance on our behalf of His sacrificial atonement for our sins. It means much more than mere form or ceremony, it means actual acceptance by repentance, faith and good works that man is restored through the resurrection from the dead to the life eternal at the appearing of Jesus Christ.

We are to apply the flesh and blood of Jesus Christ as spiritual food to our souls of which the bread and wine of the holy Eucharist are the emblems of the literal flesh and blood which we accept; and whosoever shall partake of the holy Eucharist unworthily shall be guilty of high treason against God by the shedding of the blood of the Lord in vain, as these emblems are the prototype of the essence and substance of the original body and blood of Christ. There is no efficacy in the emblems themselves but in the sacrificial offering itself which the emblems of bread and wine represent and when the original is accepted through faith and repentance on our part the salvation of man is complete.

The faculties, properties and powers of all being and life are resident in the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven, from which eternal source all things have been created and sustained whether directly or by the use of means, as all means as well as uses are the gifts of our Divine Father's Holy Spirit; and therefore all things are subject absolutely and exclusively to our heavenly Divine Father's spirit as our Divine Father's Holy Spirit is the motive or executive power of our Divine Father's person, existence and power absolutely and exclusively without limitation, whether immediately or mediately through created means; and no one can of himself do a Divine act save our Divine Father in heaven whose spirit the Holy Spirit is; and all other persons and things other than our Divine 

Father are the products of its power and may be used by it as the

conductors, mediums or agents of our Divine Father in heaven who operates only and always by His Holy Spirit whether immediately or mediately through others, it is our Divine Father who doeth the works by His omnipotent, omniscient spirit's power. 

There is absolutely nothing that has given life and being to itself; and our Divine Father in heaven only has had existence, life and power eternally in Himself, of Himself, and by Himself without an original or beginning; but all else has derived their existence, life and power from Him when He created them. 

Of the innumerable variety of life and existence in earth, sky, and sea it is all owing to the power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine 

Creator and Father.

All prophecy and all other events of a Divine character come to pass according to our Divine Father's will in accordance with the operations of His spirit.

It is the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven which creates all Divine agencies and offices in the Church of Jesus Christ, and ordains and sanctifies all who fill them. Thus, the Holy Spirit of 

God our heavenly Father set apart Barnabas and Paul for ministering to the Gentiles, for it was only and always the will of our Divine Father that His own personal spirit should create and control all things with absolute power and authority.

Our Divine Father attests His word and grace by sanctifying those whom He has chosen with the induement of His Holy Spirit of power and authority, as He did the disciples of Christ on the day of Pentecost, confirming with signs and miracles the true holiness and sanctity of the ministers of His word. 

Then Saint Peter arose and said: "Brothers, you are well aware that from the earliest days God chose, that of you all, I should be the one by whom the Gentiles were to hear the word of the gospel and believe it. God who reads the hearts of all attested this by giving them His Holy Spirit just as He gave it to us, in cleansing their hearts by faith; He made not the slightest distinction between them and us. It is by the grace of God through our Lord Jesus 

Christ that we believe and are saved in the same way as they." 

Then said James, the brother of Jesus: "Brothers, listen to me.

Peter explained how it was God's original concern to secure a people from among the Gentiles to bear His name. This agrees with the words of the prophets as it is written: 'After this I will return and build David's fallen tent. Its ruins I will rebuild and erect it anew that the rest of men may seek for the Lord, even all the

Gentiles who are called by my name.' "We therefore send Judas and Silas with the following message, our Divine Father approving with miracles, signs and wonders the good work that has been done among the Gentiles by the power of His Holy Spirit. We have decided not to impose any extra burden upon you apart from these essential requirement: "Abstain from food that has been offered to idols, from tasting blood, from the flesh of animals that have been strangled and from sexual vice."

The Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven has absolute power over all things without exception and it has full power to command, direct, approve or reject the acts of everyone, and it stopped Saint Paul from preaching in Asia, so Paul after passing through the inland districts came down to Ephesus and finding certain disciples there, asked them if they had received the Holy 

Spirit since they believed? And they answered him: "We never even heard of it." "Unto what then were ye baptized?" And they said: "We were baptized unto John's baptism of repentance." "John truly baptized with the baptism of repentance, telling the people to believe on Him who was to come after him, that is, on Jesus Christ." 

The inference here drawn from Saint Paul's language is that, had these disciples been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus they would have received the gift of the power and direction of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father the same as they; so Saint Paul baptized them in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ and immediately they were filled with the power and authority of God's spirit. The name of Jesus Christ is the only name in which the apostles and all their contemporary evangelists baptized their converts and believers; and the Church followed this doctrine and custom of the apostles upwards of two centuries from the beginning of the Christian era. 

After Saint Paul baptized these disciples at Ephesus in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ, Saint Paul laid his hands on them, and the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father came upon them, and they spoke with tongues and prophesied.

Our Divine Father in heaven by His Holy Spirit did some wonderful things through the Apostle Paul, for the disciples carried unto the sick folk towels and aprons which Paul had used; and many at their touch of them were cured of their diseases and infirmities, and evil spirit came out of those who were possessed of demons.

After a short stay in Ephesus Saint Paul said to the Church there: "I go to Jerusalem under the binding force of God's Spirit. What

will befall me there, I do not know. Only this I know that in every town the spirit of our Divine Father testifies through the prophets that bonds and afflictions are awaiting me. But, I set no value on my own life as compared with the joy of finishing my course and fulfilling the commission I received from the Lord Jesus Christ to attest the gospel of the grace of God," through repentance by faith in the vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ. "Take heed to yourselves, and to the flock over which the Holy Spirit of our heavenly Father has appointed you overseers, and anointed you guardians and shepherds of the people of Lord Jesus which He has purchased with 

His own blood.

Luke, the evangelist says, "On our way to Jerusalem we entered the house of Philip, who was one of the seven deacons formerly of Jerusalem, and he had four unmarried daughters who prophesied that persecutions awaited Paul in Jerusalem; and while we tarried with Philip a number of days a prophet named Agabus came down from Judea; and he took Paul's girdle and bound his own hands and feet saying: "Here is what the Holy Spirit says: 'So shall the Jews of Jerusalem bind the owner of this girdle and hand him over to the Gentiles.'

Paul is soon bound after his entrance into Jerusalem by the Roman commander to prevent his being killed by the Jews, but he allows Paul to make a speech in self-defense, telling about his conversion and of his baptism in the name of Jesus Christ by Ananias. 

Paul pleads that since no one keeps the Law, righteousness must be by faith, disclosed apart from the Law altogether; as it is attested by the Law and the prophets that we must be partakers of the righteousness of God through faith in Jesus Christ the Son of God. But, we must show our faith by good works of righteousness, as faith without good works is dead; and it is our faith accompanied by good works that will be counted unto us for righteousness; for it is the vicarious sacrifice of Jesus Christ which our Divine Father has put forward as the means of propitiation by faith and good works in the believer. Through faith in Jesus, Jesus becomes to us the Son and Mediator of our Divine Father whom our Divine Father has set to span the chasm, as it were, between the law and the New 

Covenant of repentance unto life through faith and acceptance of

Jesus Christ as His only begotten Son and sacrifice for man's redemption. We are therefore justified by repentance through faith in Jesus Christ as God's Son, the only legal sacrifice for our sins; and we are forgiven for our breaches of the law by faith in the

vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ made in our behalf the same as if we had, had God's pure law fulfilled. 

It was through faith that our Divine Father brought into creation all things; and it is by the grace of repentance through faith in His Son the incarnate Word Jesus Christ, our Divine Father has made our salvation to depend.

The apostle says: "Seeing we are surrounded with such a great cloud of witnesses who were justified by faith, let us lay aside every weight of sin which so easily besets us and run with patience the race set before us looking unto Jesus the author and finisher of our faith."

The claim of sin upon the sinner is mortal death which passed upon all the human race through the transgression of our first parents to all mankind, but God's first-born Son of all His creation, the Word, was made incarnate for the purpose of fulfilling the law of sin and death for man by sacrificing Himself in the behalf of all who, through repentance toward God, would believe on Him as their Lord and Redeemer; but if we do not repent of our sins, and have faith in the vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ as the Son of God, the law of sin and death will forever reign over our mortal bodies; for by the works of the law no flesh shall be justified. 

Thanks be to God our heavenly Father for His unspeakable gift, we are freed from the law of sin and death through a glad and glorious resurrection from the dead by repentance through faith in

Jesus Christ as God's only begotten Son. "There is now no condemnation and destruction for those who are in Christ Jesus, as the law of the spirit of life, through faith in the New Covenant, has set us free from the law of sin and death;" for God has done for us, what we through the weakness of the flesh, were unable to accomplish by the works of the law." "God sending His glorious Son the 

Word in the likeness of sinful flesh hath through His vicarious atonement for man conquered sin in the flesh by fulfilling the law's requirements in our behalf for all who live not after the flesh, but through faith in Jesus, God's only begotten Son.

To live through repentance and faith in the Son of God, is the same as fulfilling the law, which we were, through the weakness of the flesh unable to do. God has through repentance and faith the power or ability to perform in man His salvation, if man only has the good faith to receive it; but those who refuse to follow the directing power of our Divine Father's Holy Spirit cannot enter into

the realm of God because of unbelief or unwillingness to do these necessary things.

If you belong to Jesus Christ through faith in Him as the Son of God, then the spirit of God dwells in you, and you are in God's kingdom, although your body is a mortal thing owing to Adam's sin, but your spirit is ever living because of righteousness which is by faith in Jesus; and, if the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father which raised up His Son Jesus from the dead dwell in you, then will our 

Divine Father make the spirit of your mortal body live forever by the indwelling power of His spirit in your life. 

If we obey the voice of the Lord our Divine Father then will He say unto us as He said unto Moses: "Israel is my Son, even my first-born; I will put my name upon the children of Israel and bless them, for ye are the children of the Lord your God, and holy people with me. I have chosen you to be a peculiar people unto myself above all the nations that are upon the earth; for the Lord thy 

Divine Father has vouchsafed thee this day to be a peculiar people as I have promised thee; and that thou shouldst keep all my commandments; and I will make thee high above all nations which I have made, in praise, in name and in honor that thou mayest be a holy people unto Jehovah thy Divine Father, for I the Lord thy 

God hath spoken it." "All these blessings shall come upon thee, if thou wilt hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God." "Blessed shalt thou be in the city; and blessed shalt thou be in the field; blessed shalt be the fruit of thy body, and the fruit of thy ground; the fruit of thy cattle, and the increase of thy kine, and the flocks of thy sheep. 

Blessed will be thy basket and thy store; blessed shalt thou be when thou comest in, and blessed shalt thou be when thou goest out; and all the earth shall see that thou art called by the name of the Lord thy Divine Father; but, if ye will not keep my commandments, but corrupt yourselves, ye shall no longer be my children saith the

Lord, because ye have become a crooked and a perverse generation; for if ye live after the flesh and commit all kinds of abominations ye shall die; but if through the Holy Spirit of thy Divine Father ye mortify the deeds of your body, ye shall live; for as many as are led by the Spirit of God, they are the sons of God." "Thou shalt call me Father, and thou shalt not turn away from me."

We have received the outpouring of four Divine Father's spirit as an earnest of the Father's adoption whereby we cry "Abba Father." "The Holy Spirit of our Divine Father itself bears witness with our

spirit that we are His children; and if His children, then are we heirs of God, and joint heirs with Jesus Christ the Son of the Father."

We, as children of our Divine Father, anxiously await with eager longing for the "Sons of God," to be revealed; for the creation was not made futile of its own choice but by the will of God who made all things subject to Himself, the purpose being that all creation as well as man would one day be freed from its thraldom of decay, and gain that glorious freedom of the children of God through the atonement of Jesus Christ unto that state of immortality through the redemption of the body. "The Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven assists us in our weakness for we know not that for which we should pray as we ought, but our spirit itself makes intercession for us with groanings which we cannot utter; and the spirit of our Divine Father which knows the mind of our spirit interprets our intercessions according to the will of God." "This we know, that all things work together for good to them that love our Divine Father." It is our Divine 

Father who justifieth, and when He acquits who will condemn? 

We know also that those who love God are those who have been called in terms of His purpose, and have His aid and interest in everything. Our heavenly Father foreknows all things, and His election depends upon His choice and our obedience in conjunction with His mercy and compassion confirmed in the heart of the believer by the Holy Spirit through faith in Jesus Christ. "Confess with your words that Jesus Christ is the Son of God; believe with all your heart that the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father raised Him from the dead; and worship with your spirit our Divine 

Father as the only true and living God, and thou shalt be saved."

For, to worship your Divine Father with all your spirit, soul, mind and strength, and to love your neighbor as yourself is the fulfilling of the law.

In the Lord, there is nothing that is unclean of itself in food and drink; but that thing is unclean for a man who considers it unclean. 

There must be a consciousness of wrong-doing before there can be a conviction of sin; and to him that knoweth to do good and then does it not, to him it is sin; and he that wilfully and deliberately does that which is wrong after he has received the knowledge of the truth, there remains no more a vicarious atonement for his sins, but a fearful looking for his doom of destruction by his Creator in the day of judgment.

Man might unwittingly do what is wrong and not sin, for he is not aware that it is an unrighteous act and is not committing sin however much he might have transgressed the letter of the law of the Lord; but when the knowledge of the truth is known, and then he deliberately and wilfully transgresses, he becomes a trespasser and commits sin; for any action which is not based on good faith, it is a sin if he does it.

We should not be like worldly people are and try to please ourselves, disregarding the weaknesses and the needs of our fellowmen; but contrawise be helpful, kind and charitable toward our weak brother and assist him in his struggles to overcome temptation that he perish not for whom Christ died to save. Our whole aim in life should be to make of mankind an acceptable offering through the consecration of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven, the Creator and God of all.

The will of God is that we should show how greatly we love and adore Him by being helpful, courteous and polite toward others. such as we are sure Jesus would be if He were in our position and circumstances, and those who do these things will never perish. 

Let us thank God and take courage that the words of the prophets and of Jesus Christ are gaining strength as time advances, over the social and spiritual order of things, and that Christian revelation is coming into its own. Even the Churches are beginning to disregard their theological creeds, and slowly emerging from its reign of apostasy into the marvelous light and liberty of the one Divine 

Creator, our heavenly Father.

Freedom of interpretation and liberty of conscience are not so much under the ban of ecclesiasticism with their attendant inquisitions and dogmatic Church trials, because the freedom of speech and liberty of conscience have gained the ascendency and but few people are now burnt as heretics, or banished, or even excommunicated because of their liberal views or because they can no longer assent to or acquiesce in the absurd, inconsistent, contradictory, blasphemous doctrine of three Divine persons in one Divine Triune Creator.

People are becoming more tolerant and charitable; more friendly and neighborly toward all the Church as the intercommunion of the various denominations merge into one complete organic union under a single executive management letting the people retain the right of private or individual interpretation in religion. In this the Church of the various denominations, sects an dcreeds when organically

united in fellowship and executive management for the service of God, the evangelization of the world will be speedily realized; for then, the conscience of the believer can worship God according to the dictates of his own conscience and have the right of individual interpretation in every Church edifice, as the believers' conscience should be the highest appeal between every child of God and His Maker.

The ideal of universal voluntary service, worship and adoration can be attained only through individual interpretation, and the right to worship God according to the dictates of one's own conscience in a federated Church of Jesus Christ before such Church can claim to be truly Christian, for it is this kind of a union and fellowship for which Christ prayed and shed His most precious blood to save; and may God hasten the day when all the units of Christiandom throughout the world will see the beauty, glory, honor and power of Christ's ideal and decide in its favor by dropping all sectarian names, and be known simply as the Christians. 

Along with the absolute autonomy of individuals or of groups within the Church there should be perfect liberty to commingle by invitation of each to all the rest, to the use of their houses of worship so that this fellowship and union of truth and piety may be enhanced among the members of the groups within the Church; but wherein any individual or group cannot act with freedom of conscience they are not to be forced against their conscience in order to have a Church home within the various denominational edifices. In such a federation every individual member is guaranteed the absolute freedom of conscience. He ascribes to no creed, complies with no ordinance, and submits to no method imposed by an overhead body of eccliasiastics or Church dignitaries. 

The basic principle in a union Church of various beliefs and intelligences concerning Jesus Christ the Son of God, and His Divine Father should be that of love and helpfulness through fellowship, and not that of beliefs and opinions, as Christianity is the way of living the life of good uses, and not that of strife, contention and division.

Jesus says to the sick in body as well as to the sick in soul: "According to thy faith be it unto thee," which includes all Christians without exception, so that any Christian organization or Christian individual has a right to hold his personal belief and opinions in so far as he does not arbitrarily enforce his belief and opinions upon others however much he may personally hold them to be Divine;

for, if he does, he is no better than the Antichrist who enforced his doctrines of the Trinity of Divine persons in one Divine Triune Deity by persecuting inquisitions until the Saints of God were subjugated.

Any expression of faith by anyone, is but the testimony of his personal belief, and is not to be made a standard of measurement in any way for others; and so long as he does not arbitrarily attempt to enforce his beliefs in matters of religious belief and conformity upon others such should be their minister as he would be servant of all after Christ's own heart, and the beneficent spirit of our Divine 

Father in heaven.

Each individual should be instructed in the teachings and customs of Jesus Christ and His apostles, and be shown wherein the Antichrist, the man of sin, the son of perdition, who calls himself the vicegerent of God, and vicar of Jesus Christ, the Pope of Rome, has corrupted the Christian religion by interpolations, and false translations of the scriptures; and by changing the ordinances of God and of His Son Jesus Christ; but each one should be permitted to continue to follow the dictates of his conscience until his conscience is sufficiently enlightened to convince him of the error of his way, and he be constrained of his own convictions to follow the truth as he understands it. Any exclusiveness would not only be unwise, but a great wrong perpetrated upon the conscience and integrity of the excluded, as well as a great wrong committed against the moral law of God by using compulsion in the things Divine contrary to the will and spirit of God which forbids using arbitrary power in matters of faith in Divine worship.

Such a movement should include individuals, congregations, Churches, conferences, sects, denominations, and federations in so far as they granted Christian liberty to all alike of private interpretation, and to worship God according to the dictates of conscience.

The Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven is ushering in a new spirit of progress and enlightement, so that men no longer are bucked and gagged, flayed, thrown into dungeons or burned at the stake, because they cannot mentally swallow the whale of a monster of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person which has been advocated and enforced by the "Mother of harlots and abominations of the earth," the Roman Catholic Church.

The spiritual prophet sees the dawn of a new day of freedom for the press and of speech, of liberty and of conscience, and the right

of private interpretation in matters of religious faith; and a new 

Magna Charta of human progress is being written by infidel and saint alike; and those who try to stifle or cripple the freedom of their fellow-men are to be considered as reprobates and villains, the enemies of progress and of enlightenment, and belong to the dark ages from whence their doctrine come. 

People who know what truth is have no fear of the onslaughts of error; and they therefore do not conceive truth to be something that needs protection, far from it, truth is something to be discovered, appropriated and enjoyed forever. Liberty is the power of truth which of right belongs to every person to use all his faculties as he may choose in so far as he does not interfere with the equal rights of others. The principle of liberty is drawn from Divine revelations and nature; its protector is the law of God above that of the state; and those who are troubled or anxious about defending the tenets of their religion forget that the only real test of truth is the pragmatic one enunciated by Jesus Christ the Son of God who said: "By their fruits ye shall know them," and anything that calls for an inquisition of persecution to uphold its tenets in religion is of the devil and not of God; and if Christ were here and should reiterate what He said: "I am the Son of God; my Father is greater than I; my Father is greater than all; I can do nothing of myself, it is my 

Father who doeth the works," those who hold to three Divine coequal, coessential, and coeternal persons in the one Divine person whom they call the Triune God, would try to seek by every means to have him put to death for uttering what they would call blasphemies against their sacred, holy and Divine Trinity of three Divine persons in one.

Christ said He is the Son of God, and that His Father is greater than He; and greater than all without any reservations whatever; and those who make reservations or exceptions are liars, villains, heretics, and hypocrites, as any religious, Divine truth, is corroborated by true science; and Jesus Christ never taught an untruth when He said that He of Himself could do nothing whatsoever of Himself; and that it was His Divine Father who did His works through Him; and that there can be three Divine persons in one or three Divine persons at all is both scripturally and scientifically false; and whenever or wherever there is anything said contrary to fact it is false; and there are many such falsities to be found in all the creeds fabricated or instituted by these polyglot, heathenish, ecclesiastical hierarchies of Christianity during the whole of the Dark

Ages or from the close of the third century of the Christian era down to the twentieth century; and anyone seeking to verify this statement will soon discover it to be the correct truth. 

True religion like true science, is from the same original source, and can only be discovered by much hard labor, and the reader is directed through the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven to our Divine Father's incarnate Son the "Word of God" for the verification of all Divine truth.

The Church finds itself in such a quandry, because it has erred from the teachings of Jesus Christ and His apostles by following the decrees and councils of covetous, profane men, and formulating creeds after their own fallacious reasonings, instead of following the teachings and practices of Jesus Christ and His apostles. The Holy 

Spirit of our Divine Father is not destined to defeat in a world which its power has created and governs, and no amount of denunciation by humanity or the substitution of creeds, or the deliberations of councils however eloquent and scathing can convince the human heart that confides in its direction, that our Divine Father is not perfect, and that He needs Popes, creeds, and councils, and every human invention to make Himself better understood.

When our clergymen come to realize in the realm of human welfare that they should be the servants, mediums, or agents of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven for the fostering of the spiritual life of the people and not for the fostering of sects, creeds, and denominations which seek to rule and govern the kingdom of God instead of being ruled and governed by it; and which, for selfish purposes, they try to suppress freedom of conscience, of speech and of the press, and of individual interpretation which are essential to a full and free communion between their parishioners and their God, they will dispense with their exotic Te Deums, rosaries, and doxologies which foster division in the Church. 

It is not enough that man do unto others as he would that they should do unto him, as Christ, our great example, was not satisfied with doing that; for He completely gave Himself in loving sacrifice for His fellow creatures; and that is the only hopeful, prophetic transformation in the social relationship toward which the human race must ever look with wistful expectation if the realm of God and of His Christ will have become real and effectual in the life of this world.

Christ took the form of a servant, not because it is the most ef-

fective avenue to permanent influence but because of His love and compassion for lost humanity. Service is the only authentic passport to the conquest of the human soul, as well as the greatest spiritual soul developer.

CHAPTER IX 

The superangelical Word, our Divine Father's first-born Son of all creation who by the power of His Divine Father's Holy Spirit became the incarnate Word Jesus Christ, was clothed with a robe of flesh and clothed also with the omnipotent power and authority of His Divine Father's spirit for the work of the works of creation and redemption that He might be of the greatest possible exponent of His Divine Father in the plan and purposes for the good of His creatures; and as a servant of His Divine Father reversed for humanity the highest moral conception of greatness through holy precepts and a life devoted to self-sacrifice and good uses; and for such unselfish and disinterested service for self-aggrandizement. He wears the mantel of universal sovereignty; and there is none greater than 

He, save His Divine Creator and Father.

The incarnate Word, Jesus Christ, chose to be both the servant of God and also the servant of man, as every true minister should be; and as a result of this, His Divine Father exalted Him far above all lords, princes, kings, and potentates, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bow of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth, and confess that Jesus is Lord to the glory of God His heavenly Father. Jesus Christ was a perfect medium of the power and authority of the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father in heaven; so that His Divine Father in Heaven without reserve placed all things of His creation under His Son the incarnate Word, called Jesus Christ. The most significant form that anyone can assume is the form of a servant.

By service we help our fellow-men in their need; we leave behind us an influence that is lasting and glorious; we have a resemblance of God in His perfections; and, in all the alternative forms of life of which volition, good-will and good conduct are the preservatives and restoratives for self-preservation, let us select the highest, the most significant, that of service, the one which Christ chose as the crowning diadem of life—the form of a servant.

It is not our object to harangue or abuse those clergymen who seek their own livelihood to the subversion of the souls of men to 166

an antichristian, satanic barbarism, whose heathenism has outdone the heathen in their absurd, inconsistent, contradictory formulas which they call orthodox Christianity, declaring that there is one Divine person in the universe composed conjointly, coequally, coessentially and coeternally of three other Divine persons of the same nature, essence and substance without division or part who are equal in power, glory and honor with each other of which neither taken singly is God without the other two making each in himself a finite or dependent being upon the volition and choice of other Divine persons; for they say that it takes three Divine persons who are infinite, absolute, and independent of each other in volition and action to compose that one Divine Triune person whom they call God, which are coequal, coessential, coeternal; equal in power, glory and majesty with neither greater nor less than the other, and neither before nor after the other in time, power and wisdom, otherwise they could not be called the triune, three in one or one in three God. 

Those who teach the doctrine of the Trinity affirm that neither God the Father, nor God the Son, nor God the Holy Ghost taken singly or individually is God; but that each of these three Divine persons is only but one third part, portion, installment or division. of that triune person whom they call the Deity although He, taken singly or as a unit is no greater than either of the three Divine persons of which He Himself, the fourth Divine or triune person is composed, which is purely orthodox and cannot be changed even by the vicegerent of God, and vicar of Jesus Christ without speaking ex cathedra; for, when three Divine persons are joined hypostaticaly, it takes a man with all the powers of Satan to even presume to either unite or dissolve them into persons or units which the Pope of Rome can of himself, and by himself do when speaking ex cathedra. 

The paintings, photographs and the cartoons which they have made of their triune Deity, they represent God the Father as a longwhiskered old man; God the Son as a boy or young man; and God the Holy Ghost as a dove or parrot; but they have but a very few paintings or photographs, if any, of their triune God or three in one or one in three person hypostatically or conjointly joined together without division or parts as these three are all tied or grown together into one Divine triune person with neither greater nor less, and neither before nor after the others; and equal in power, glory and majesty with each other, and each with all the rest so that all three of their pictorial Deities represented by the old man, the boy and the dove who are the same in height, width, weight, thickness,

broadness and narrowness so that they are all three one and the same, and their glory, honor and majesty is precisely equal; and their creed says: "Whosoever will be saved, before all things it is necessary that they hold the Catholic faith; which except one do keep whole and undefiled without doubt shall perish everlastingly this is the Catholic faith, which except a man believe fully, he cannot be saved."

If three Divine persons constitute one Divine triune person then there are four Divine persons; and if Christ was a Divine person and a human person, then indeed, He was two persons, one a Divine person, and the other a human person; and if the human Christ was absorbed into the Divine Christ, by the hypostatical union of the human with the Divine; then there are four Divine persons and one human person, which make three Divine persons and one human person absorbed hypostatically into the one Divine person of the triune God who constitutes the first person in the Deity. Such is the doctrine of the vicegerent of God and vicar of Jesus Christ, the Antichrist, the man of sin, the son of perdition, the Pope of Rome. 

The people who teach such absurd, inconsistent, contradictory doctrines as the Trinity of three Divine persons to pure little innocent confiding babes and religiously ignorant people are criminals of the deepest dye for they not only steal from such their money, but also steal from them the truth to the destruction of their souls by making them place their faith in a falsehood, and all the words, language, propositions, expositions, consultations and deliberations, of these wise-acres in vindication of the said Divine and holy Trinity of the one Divine Triune God person is still a satanic lie, because it is inconsistent and contradictory with itself as well as with all other truth known to man in the scriptures, nature, science and reason, and shows in every proposition set forth to be made of falsities by denying in itself all that it affirms. 

These so-called orthodox ministers speak of the Trinity, of the hypostatical union, transubstantiation ad-finitum other purgatorial conundrums such as these without ever at anytime setting forth a single proposition by which they have ever explained in any deducible language the possibility of its truthfulness, as it cannot be demonstrated to be true by the scriptures, by nature, science or reason; but can be easily proven to be contrary to all of these; and the best and only way they argue to dispose of the lie is to say that it is orthodox, ineffable, above reason or unthinkable, and that

no one can form a conception of what is Divine, and is, therefore, not to be inquired into, but to be accepted on faith. 

If, according to these incongruous Trinitarian claims, we find that their doctrine is incompatible with every private knowledge of truth, how will they ever be able to prove their three Divine beings in one Divine triune person is a doctrine of Christianity, when neither Jesus Christ nor His apostles and evangelists never so much as mentioned it or never so much as baptized a convert in the name of the Trinity as the scriptures and the early Christian historians show in their histories, and writings of a private nature; that no baptisms were ever performed during the first two centuries of the Christian era in the name of the Trinity of Divine persons as God the Father, God the Son and God the Holy Ghost, or in the name of the Father, Son and Holy Ghost, as interpolated into the gospel of Saint Matthew.

There cannot be any divisions or distinctions drawn in anything that is infinite, absolute or independent, such as our Divine Father's person and spirit is said to be; as a person and His spirit are but one person and not two or more such as the Antichrist doctrine of the Roman Catholic Church teaches; and for anyone to say that these three Divine uncreate, absolute, independent or infinite persons are one person is an insult to the crudest mind or intelligence, if he has the least idea what the import or designation of the words mean; for there cannot be three infinite persons or things of the same nature, essence, substance or person as one excludes there being any other such person or thing without division or parts; as that which is infinite is a unit in itself and cannot be otherwise or infinity is destroyed.

No sane person, whosoever, who has ever given any thought to the subject of Christianity, can possibly conceive how God can be Christ's Divine Father, and Jesus Christ be the Son of God; and both of them infinite, absolute and independent; coequal, coessential, and coeternal; and equal in power, glory and majesty, as the parent is always the life-giver of the son, and must exist anterior to his having a son whether it be by creation or generation or both as in the case of Jesus Christ who was the created Word or first-born Son of His Divine Father's creation before He became the Word incarnate or God's only begotten Son by conception and generation by the Virgin Mary. God's glorious Son the Word was the first creature of His Divine Father's creation before all things else created; and in the fullness of prophecy concerning Him He be- 1

came incarnated by the Virgin Mary who begat Him by conception and generation through the power and operation of God's Holy Spirit, which makes the incarnate Word, Jesus Christ in this peculiar double sense, the only begotten Son of God by creation, and also by conception and generation by the power of His Divine Father's Holy Spirit which did not employ, save in the case of the Virgin Mary, any other agency in the full development of the incarnate Word Jesus Christ which was peculiarly the highest honor our Divine Father ever conferred upon a woman, that "all the world should call her blessed." Thus, the incarnate Word, Jesus Christ is the only object or person or thing of our Divine Father's creation that was not created either of a spiritual or material existence without the mediation of His glorious Son the incarnate Word, Jesus Christ anterior to the Word's incarnation in the flesh of man; so that both in the antemundane, and also in the mundane state of the Word is He God's only immediately begotten Son; begotten of 

His Divine Father's Holy Spirit in the beginning by creation, and in the end by conception and generation of the Virgin Mary. 

Our Divine Father in heaven as Creator, is the God and Father of the incarnate Word, Jesus Christ and of all things else through the Word as mediator of His Divine Father in the creation of all things else of His Divine Father's creation. 

Thus, God who became Creator and Father in the act of creating His glorious first-born Son of all creation, the Word, constitutes the one and only person who is Divine, uncreate, absolute and independent in His person and powers; and all things else are but creatures or created things, persons or beings of our Divine Father's creation; and are therefore, dependent and finite and not Divine in their person, being or state.

Our Divine Father in heaven has created all sentient spirits and persons which He desires to associate with Himself with rationality or free moral agency which is that power of truth called liberty, which every one has from God, and belongs to one to do as he pleases only in so far as he does not interfere with the rights of others by self-abuse or injury to others, as liberty and freedom are governed by God's inexorable law of truth and of right, and when one goes beyond that, he is an impostor, a villain and a reprobate. 

For this reason, no one has the right to teach untruths or falsities, and those who do, are as bad as "the Antichrist, the man of sin, and son of perdition," who calls himself the vicegerent of God and vicar of Jesus Christ, the Pope of Rome; for, those who are the

abettors of others' acts and words which are false, are alike criminals; and those who uphold these Antichrist doctrines of the Pope of Rome, our Divine Father will destroy in the day of judgment; for they cannot enter into His place as He will not permit any that teach falsehoods for Divine truth to be associated with Him, and with His angels and His saints; for evil communications corrupt good morals; and nothing but truth and right, can enter the pearly gates of heaven into the paradise of God; or worship before the great white throne of our Divine Father in heaven who reigns in absolute power, splendor, and majesty, to bless all who with a pure heart and clean hands seek to live the truth by doing the right. 

There isn't anything quite so wicked, degrading, bruttish, villainous, hellish and satanic, as this polytheistic doctrine of three Divine persons in the one Divine person of the one Divine triune person, or their three Divine persons in their one Divine person or of their one Divine person in their three Divine persons, which is a conglomeration of falsities, misrepresentations and contradictions to lead people away from the worship of the one and only living and true God our Divine Father in heaven.

The claim of Trinitarians that human sin was committed against an infinite God and therefore the sin was infinite and that it took an infinite sacrifice to atone for it in order to remove the punishment due to our sin, is absolutely false, as it is impossible for a finite person to commit an infinite act. All things infinite are the properties of our Divine Father only, as there is nothing infinite which does not belong to Him personally and individually, and absolutely without qualification; as the power of His spirit can operate in, by and through everything according as our Divine Father wills. 

Therefore, if any prophet, Jesus Christ, or any saint or sinner whatsoever or even an angel from heaven should create or do a Divine act of himself, the infinity of our Divine Father would be destroyed; and, for this reason no one can do a Divine or infinite act of himself save our Divine Father, whether immediately or mediately through His creatures, as it is our Divine Father's Holy Spirit only, that can do a Divine act of creation or perform a miracle. 

Neither the prophets, Jesus Christ, nor the apostles ever claimed the power to do a miracle or Divine act of themselves; but always claimed that this power belonged solely to their Divine Father in heaven whose spirit creates, sustains and controls all these things. by its omnipotent and absolute power. When all these august personages claim this Divine power for our Father in heaven only, it

ought to settle it for every one save Antichrists, heresiarchs, villains and reprobates, and the imps of hell, who wish to claim a like power with that of their Divine Creator, our Father in heaven.

The acts of all persons, spirits, beings and things without exception are finite acts, and limited by the infinite, absolute and independent power of our Divine Father in heaven; as He is the author or giver, and He is the dispenser or executor of all the power and authority exercised by others; and is not only able to terminate their power and authority but their person, spirit and existence also. 

All power and authority exercised by persons other than our Divine Father in heaven is delegated power or authority and belongs in an absolute sense to our Divine Father, and not to the recipient of it, as it remains the power of the giver absolutely and independently of the receiver who has his person or being, power and authority through the pure grace of our Divine Father.

It is by means of the atonement through faith and repentance toward God our heavenly Father that our existence, rationality and free moral agency may be extended indefinitely by our Divine Father in heaven. The atonement is very much like the infusion of healthy blood from the strong healthy bodies of men into the veins of a sick person whose blood has been depleted, which healthy blood acts as a preservative to the sick, bringing health and happiness; so Jesus 

Christ who is superior to sinful flesh offers His flesh and blood in our behalf to cure us of our malady of sin and mortality, that whosoever believeth on Him should not perish but have everlasting life through the resurrection from the dead to the life immortal and eternal.

The human family has, because of sin, become sick unto death through Adam's transgression, and the blood of Jesus Christ acts as a restorative, the same as a serum extracted from a healthy inoculated person applied in time to the sick, diseased body will save

the sick. So it is with the flesh and blood of Jesus, accepted in faith by him who is sick of soul. Christ gave His flesh and blood for the life of the world and it is a saving salutary healing to all them to which it is properly applied, as He was immune to the disease of sin and death, contracted by Adam and his posterity because He was a superangelical spirit personage and took upon Himself flesh and blood to provide a tonic or an atonement by which the sinner might be saved by faith through repentance toward God. So the giving by Jesus Christ of His body and blood as a vicarious sacrifice for penitent man acts like a tonic to Him by bringing him health and immortality and eternal life, because He as the "Word of God" was not of this "World," but from "heaven;" but He became incarnated in a robe of flesh and made an offering of it for an atonement for man's sin by which all the innocent or unaccountable and the penitent become reconciled through the answer of a good conscience toward God by an acceptance of faith in Jesus. 

All who come to the age of accountability or the knowledge of the truth must apply this remedy of faith and repentance toward God; as it is a personal affair which no one dare neglect if he would be saved; as our Divine Father in heaven simply furnishes the remedy which each, as individuals, who have received the knowledge of the covenant, may apply to themselves; but the ignorant or unaccountable who have no means of knowing of God's holy covenant of repentance toward God and belief in Jesus Christ as God's Son and Mediator; our Divine Father's remedy still applies for their salvation; for those who have the gospel of Jesus Christ will be judged by it, and those who have it not will be judged without it. 

All power and authority to forgive sin is the prerogative of our Divine Father only whose Holy Spirit is the executive power and authority which executes all things Divine or of God, whether immediately or mediately; and any person who claims this power or authority for himself is a criminal, a reprobate and a villain, because he claims to exercise the functions which belong to our Divine Father only. There is no Divinely constituted power or authority for the forgiveness of sins in all the earth, save the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven; and it only and always absolves the sinner from his sins upon repentance and restitution in so far as it is within the power of man to make amends without any intermediary to grant or withhold absolution from sin. 

All men are in the same absolute need of an offering for their sins which is provided always and only through the vicarious atonement

of Jesus Christ the Word incarnated, who was not of the family of Adam, but was the first-fruits of our Divine Father's creation; and 

He came to pay the debt for Adam and his family of millions of people which they were unable to pay and which He himself did not owe, so that whosoever believeth on Him, and trusts his soul to His tender care by following His gospel of a life of repentance and good uses shall never perish.

Had not our Divine Father given His glorious first-born Son of all creation, the Word, to the world the life of man would have terminated with his life upon the earth; for God's holy law had decreed the "soul that sinneth it shall die;" and "that flesh and blood cannot enter into the kingdom of God;" but through the atonement of Jesus Christ for man's sins, a repentance is granted which God's mercy claims; and man is restored to life through the resurrection from the dead at the coming return of Jesus Christ to the earth in the fourteenth millenium from the beginning of the world's creation, according to the general epistle of the apostle Barnabas, which will occur hard on the close of the twentieth century.

God, our heavenly Father, has accepted the atoning sacrifice of the body and blood of His incarnate Word Jesus Christ which He gave for us, as full payment of our debt to the Divine Majesty on account of Adam's sin of transgression by which we are held subject to death or mortality which could be removed by the payment of the debt; but man, who is subject to the debt, is not released immediately by Christ's payment, but conditionally by the grace of repentance through the resurrection from the dead at the coming of Jesus Christ.

Our Divine Father in heaven created our forefather Adam innocent and pure; but he had not as yet developed by experience either virtue or good character by obedience and devotion to his Divine Creator in whose image of likeness he bore, in liberty, freedom, rationality, and free moral agency, which made him responsible, because of his knowledge of discernment of his Divine Creator and His Divine providence over him, and his fealty to Him. 

Truth is paramount both to moral and spiritual development, and for this reason our Divine Father would not have you lacking in the knowledge of truth, which if followed, will bring joy, peace, happiness and salvation, as to know truth is to know God, and the workings of His Divine Providence which He carries on immediately and also mediately through the omnipotent power of His Holy

Spirit, which is the all inclusive power that is, and neither God, men, angels nor things can operate without it whether to do good or evil, and herein lies our responsibility or accounting with our Divine Creator; and, if you will diligently apply yourself to the study of the gospel of Jesus Christ as set forth in the teachings and practices of Christ, and of His apostles, taking heed to what Jesus Christ says of Himself, of His doctrine and of His works, you will find that He ascribes them all to the power and operations of the spirit of His Divine Father, for His Divine Father operates in no other way, nor can the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father operate in any way other than as our Divine Father chooses to operate, as our Divine Father's Spirit cannot operate contrary to our Divine Father whose spirit the Holy Spirit is, as any person, and His spirit is but one entity, unit, person or being and belongs to but one person individually; and, because of its infinite, omnipotent, omniscient and omnipresent power it has power and control over the person, being and spirit of all others whenever our Divine Father chooses to control them, or destroy them.

No one can know, comprehend or understand these righteous principles and apply them to his own life, and teach others of the love, power, and beauty of God's character manifested through His Holy Spirit without experiencing in his own life a great measure of peace, joy, happiness and blessedness which comes to such every consecrated soul.

There can be nothing given to an infinite, absolute, and independent person like the person of our Divine Father in heaven as not belonging to Him; as there can be but one uncreate, absolute, or infinite, independent person, and all things else are subject to Him, as He must comprehend in Himself, of Himself and by Himself all power and authority over all things visible and invisible, of persons, spirits, dominions, principalities and powers of every nature, kind, essence, substance or being; as He is the author thereof and all these things are dependent upon Him. 

Our heavenly Father is the only Divine person or Deity subsisting eternally of Himself without division, parts or associates; and all things else whatsoever are the objects of His creation, for He only is infinite, absolute or independent in His person and operations, and no other being can of himself do a miracle or act of creation; as it is only He who has this inherent quality, and all else originates from Him, and are dependent upon Him for their existence and powers.

The Holy Spirit of our Divine Father is all comprehending, as it searches all things, understands all, creates all things, does all miracles, and governs all things according as our Divine wills it to be whether immediately or mediately through His created agencies as it is the spirit of our Divine Father which performs it.

Our Divine Father only, exercises the power and authority of His Holy Spirit; as no other spirit, person or thing has the power or authority to command our Divine Father to do anything, so no Divine power is, nor can be exercised by others which is solely that power which belongs absolutely to our Divine Father in heaven; as no one can act of His own power and authority but He; and all others must act by reason of the power and authority received from Him; and all delegated power and authority exercised by others mediately is removable by our Divine Father at His will and pleasure; as all things else are subject to Him and owe fealty, allegiance, and fidelity directly to Him as the author of their creation, power, and authority which is merely delegated being, power and authority, which belong to our Divine Father, for there is nothing which has anything of itself save our Divine Father in heaven only, who has all things of Himself, by Himself and for Himself, save as He delegates being, power and authority for the good of His creature who are all subject to Him without exception, and removable by Him at His will, power, and authority.

It is also a misnomer to speak of the Divine Son or the Divine Christ, which means the God Son and the God Christ which is absolutely and positively wrong; as He is the Son of God or of the Divine, and the Christ of God, but not the God Christ, or anointed God, but God's anointed. Father as His Creator. Jesus summed up the essentials of His religion in His prayer to His Divine Father when He said: "This is life eternal that they might know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom thou didst send."

God could not be Father before He had a Son, and He became both Creator and Father when He created His first-born Son of all creation, the Word; and when God created the Word by the omnipotent power of His spirit, it did not change His person, nature, essence or substance, attributes and powers of being or existence, as these cannot be changed, altered, added to or subtracted from His person which is an infinite, absolute, independent, omnipotent, omniscient, omnipresent, immutable person, as any change whatever, save added titles, would destroy the perfection of the attributes of His person. There is no extraneous power outside of that of our 

Divine Father's person to change Him from an absolute and independent person to a dependent and finite being as becoming Creator and Father by exercising the power of His spirit in the creating of things.

All the works of God that any creature can possibly perform is simple filial, loving obedience to our Divine Father's spirit through which all the works of God are performed; and those who conform themselves to the directing power of our Divine Father's Holy Spirit are those through which the spirit of God will perform the works of God. Spirit operated.

All power and authority is restricted and constricted by the Holy

Father, to my God and your God. " "Tarry in Jerusalem for the promise of the Father until ye be indued with His Holy Spirit." 

Our Divine Father only has no origin or beginning since He never came into existence or being, and all things else have come into existence through the creating power of our Divine Father's spirit. 

Our Divine Father willed and He spoke, and the power of His spirit brought into existence that which He willed; and the first of His creation was His glorious Son, called "The Word of God," the firstborn or first created of our Divine Father's creation; and all things else of our Divine Father's creation were created through this glorious first-born Son, the Word.

All things that our Divine Father does He does through His omnipotent spirit's power which executes all things Divine without exception.

Our Divine Father existed as God per se before the creation of His glorious first-born Son the Word by which act He became Creator and Father in time called the beginning of God's creation;

but as God or the Eternal our Divine Father existed without time; as there was not a time when He was not God or the Eternal One, but a time only when He was not Creator and Father, which was before He had created His first-born Son of all creation, His glorious "Word."

It is a misnomer to say that God is the eternal Father or the eternal Creator, as He could not be Father before He had created a Son or some creature in order to be Creator and Father; but there never was a time when He was not God. Christ is not the eternal 

Son or God the Son, but the Son of the Eternal, or Son of God, because this relationship of God as Father and Creator originated from the time of the unincarnate Word's beginning, as God's firstborn creature of all creation.

Although the incarnate Word Jesus Christ could do no act of creation or perform any miracles of Himself, He was willing, yea anxious to be at His Divine Father's bidding in loving, filial devotion, so that whatsoever His Divine Father's spirit bade him do He was there to perform it. The Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven, is the Divine life, energy, motive or active force of our heavenly Father's person; the willing, choosing, designing, purposing or executive power inherent in our Divine Father's person; and the power of creating, performing miracles, or any other Divine acts is solely and exclusively the work of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven.

The gospel of Jesus Christ tells us: "The Father Himself who sent me hath born witness of me, ye have neither heard His voice at any time nor seen His shape . . . not any man hath seen the Father ... no man hath seen God at any time, the only begotten Son who is in the bosom of the Father, He hath made Him known unto you."

commandments, doctrines and covenants of both the Old and New
