Spirit of our Divine Father's person. The term Holy Spirit is the distinguishing title or name for the spirit of our Divine Father in heaven; for, if it were the name of a person, the Holy Spirit would have a spirit the same as all persons do; but the term Holy Spirit simply tells what kind of a spirit it is which our Divine Father possesses; for all persons must have or possess spirit in order to be a person; and the spirit of a person is not a person itself; for no person and his spirit can be considered two persons; and it is a misnomer to say that the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father is a person coequal, coessential, and coeternal with our Divine Father differentiating the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father as a different person coextensive 

Iwith our Divine Father.

Spirit does not have person but the person spirit; as the person is more than spirit, and therefore has spirit or it is not a person; and we know positively and are sure that the prophets Jesus Christ and Christ's apostles and evangelists ascribed the term Holy Spirit to our Divine Father's spirit which belongs to His person. 

Everywhere in the Bible, where there is a designation or explanation made concerning any miracle, or doctrine, or sign, or prophecy, it is always ascribed to the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven, and the Father designated as doing the Works. The Holy 

Spirit is the Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven and it has no existence apart from Him either as a person or spirit, as there cannot be a person without spirit as they cannot be separated one from the other without destroying personality.

This separating of our Divine Father in heaven into two or more homogeneous parts or persons which the Trinitarians call the triune God, cannot possibly be but one person in one God, as our Divine Father who is above all, in all and through all could not possibly be more than one person in Himself; and He is not composed of three or more other heterogeneous persons besides Himself and different from Himself. There cannot be any admixture or conglomeration of units, persons or beings in the one personal Deity whom we call our Divine Father in heaven. It is a false idea of personality to conceive of a person made up of two or more units in himself which

is contrary to all that we know of persons; as each person is but one unit in himself. It is foolishness to think of one person made up of three or four different units or persons that are similar in nature, essence, substance, qualities and quantities as himself who must think, act, will and choose conjointly all together; or it is foolish to think of a person made up of three or four different units or persons dissimilar in nature, essence, substance, qualities and quantities in a confused, diffused, discordant, mixed, mingled, and subordinate masses; thinking, acting, willing, choosing, designing, purposing and executing their passions and animosities in an evil distorted temper; so that one or more are put to death such as God the Son and Jesus Christ are said to have been to appease an angry God the Father who was angry with the world, and He took the life of His beloved Son to stanch His ire. This Trinitarian orthodoxy is wicked beyond description in whatever way you might look at it. 

Our Divine Father's volition of thought and action is exclusively His very own in an infinite degree, as He is not dependent upon the volition, of thought and action of any other person or being, but that of all others have this power only delegated to them according to our Divine Father's will as their God and Creator. 

Such a medley of contradictions as a triune person would destroy every sense of unity or of personality as neither of the persons in a three in one or triune God of coequal, coessential, and coeternal persons could have separate volition and thought or freedom of action which are requisite qualities or attributes of rational beings; and to say that there are three such rational persons, units, or things which compose or constitute but one unit in one person of a Triune Deity does violence to every private knowledge of fact, of truth, of reason, of science, and above all of the Holy Scriptures or of 

Divine Revelation.

This doctrine of the Trinity of Divine persons is not a doctrine of God or of Christianity. It is not a Divine doctrine, but the doctrine of certain heathen philosophers with a veneer of Christian names imposed upon the Christian world by the "Mother of harlots and abominations of the earth," the Roman Catholic Church. They have palmed off onto the Christian world after destroying the Christians and their records that this false, satanic Trinitarian triune God is the teachings of Jesus Christ which is the most profane, wicked, degrading, mean, insolent, hellish, and villainous thing that anyone could possibly say against the incarnate Son of God or His Divine Father; as it tends to destroy all sense of right, of justice,

of purity, of truth and of their sacred character and integrity, for it proclaims that those who teach such absurdities, inconsistencies and contradictions have but little concern for their own integrity, and none whatever for their Divine Creator.

The Trinitarianists have adopted the worst that they could find through a combination of the worst that they could find in the heathen philosophies with that of the Christian system so as to outdo the heathen pagans in their heathen philosophies with a veneer of Christian names added to make it sound as if it were Christian, although it is so absurd, inconsistent, contradictory, and ridiculous that it does violence to the human mind and understanding. This doctrine is so bogus and satanic that it tends to degrade and destroy the freedom of thought in the intellects of our children by trying to force their minds to accept on faith which all scripture, nature, science and reason condemns as false; for three persons or units in one person or unit is an anomaly from the truth. That there should be three Divine persons in the one Divine person of our Father in heaven is absurd and only as people are freed from these demoralizing influences that dwarf their minds, will they become truthful and virtuous men and women of the state.

CHAPTER X 

It is conceivable how our Divine Father in heaven could have a perception of Jesus Christ and the other objects of His creation before He created them; but it is not conceivable how God could create millions of objects without first perceiving the objects He created; for how could so many myriads of objects be produced by our Divine Father without perceiving aforehand the objects He created?

That our Divine Father had the knowledge or perception aforehand of all the dependent things of His creation can by no enlightened person be brought into question, as a concept should represent the real essence of the objects included under it; and for anyone to say that God had no perception of the nonexistent things He brought into being is a great fallacy, for the things that are, are all evidences of our Divine Father's foreknowledge for they are, so far as we know them, all dependent things of His creation; and since we know all animal and plant life upon the earth is in a continual state of dependency, we perceive even without Divine Revelation the independency of that being upon which all things else depends, such as God has revealed Himself to be. 

If the Church had not turned the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven awry by teaching that the spirit of God is a third Divine person of a Trinity of Deities or Divine persons, both religion and science would have been greatly advanced beyond their present stage of knowledge in the understanding of the people. 

The distorted, ambiguous, inconsistent doctrines taught by the Church since the first quarter of the fourth century A. D. of three 

Divine persons in the Deity of our Divine Father in heaven; and the final climax of adding to their creed the "Filioque" clause at the Council of Toledo in 589 A. D. stating that the Holy Spirit proceeds from the Son of God as well as from our Divine Father making it the Son or offspring of both the Father and His Son which was the crowning diadem of the "Mother of harlots and abominations of the earth," the Roman Catholic Church, and she has made all the nations of the earth drink of the cup of her whoredom and idolatry. 186

It took the "Mother of harlots and abominations of the earth" from the adoption of the Nicene Creed in 325 A. D. until the 

Council of Toledo to dress in full regalia their hideous monster the holy Trinity of the triune God.

When the "Mother of harlots and abominations of the earth," the Roman Catholic Church, had taken the Holy Spirit from our Divine Father and made of it a third Divine person proceeding from both the Divine Father and from His only begotten Son Jesus Christ they gave the Holy Spirit two fathers but no mother; but robbed our Divine Father of His spirit in order to make a "Third Divine" person in the Godhead of the Deity. Jesus Christ and His apostles forewarned their people of the great apostasy which should come upon the Church saying: "Let no man deceive you by any means, for the day shall not come except there come a falling away first, and that the man of sin be revealed the son of perdition who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God or that is worshipped so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God showing himself that he is God." 

Saint John, Christ's beloved apostle describes, "a great Red 

Dragon," as pagan Rome "having seven heads and ten horns, and seven crowns upon his head drew the third part of the stars,' bishops "of heaven, and cast them to the earth, and the dragon," pagan Rome, "stood before the woman," the Church, "which was ready to be delivered for to devour her man child," Jesus Christ, "as soon as He was born; and she brought forth a man child who was made to rule all nations with a rod of iron; and her child was caught up unto God and to His throne, and the woman fled into the wilderness," among the barbirians, "where she has a place prepared of

God that they should feed her a thousand two-hundred and three score years." This is a picture of the Christians under the power of the Roman Catholic hierarchy until the reformation which comprises the time between the adoption by pagan Rome of the reign of "The man of sin," in the fourth century until he was taken prisoner to France. 

The prophet Daniel, and John, Christ's beloved apostle, designates the time between the birth of Jesus Christ to the full strength of the millenial age will be "Time, times, and a half time" which is three thousand five hundred prophetic years. If we reckon the time given by the apostle Barnabas in his general epistle we will find that the millenial reign of Jesus Christ will begin at or hard on the

close of the twentieth century and continue a thousand years, after which Satan will be loosed for a short time, and he will gather all his forces on the great field of Armageddon for his last stand only to be defeated and destroyed forever.

The first creed formed for the purpose of excluding and persecuting Christians by excommunication, and fellowship of the 

Church is called the "Nicene Creed," which is as follows: "We believe in one God the Father Almighty, maker of all things visible and invisible, and in one Lord Jesus Christ the Son of God, begotten and only begotten of the Father, that is of the substance of the Father, God of God, Light of Light, very God of very God, begotten, not made consubstantial with the Father by whom all things are made both in heaven and in earth. Who for us and our salvation descended and was incarnate and was made man, suffered and rose again the third day, ascended into the heavens, and will come to judge the living and the dead. We believe in the Holy Ghost, the 

Holy Catholic Church anathematizing those who say that there was a time when the Son of God was not, and that He was made out of nothing or out of another substance or esssence, and is created or changeable or alterable."

The Roman Catholic Church dates from this period, as her doctrines were divergent sufficiently far from the teachings of Jesus Christ and the doctrine and practices of Christ's apostles as to be different and contrary to their teachings and practices. The Roman 

Catholic faith was gradually molded under the hand of the Emperor Constantine the Great whose decrees made the bishop of Rome the Pontifex Maximus of the Roman Empire and under whose auspices the Nicene Creed was born, formulated and prescribed for both pagans and Christians, as the creed was a compromise between Christianity and the paganism of the Roman people which was officially adopted by the Emperor and established by law. 

Since the Nicene creed was a new thing for the Church, and in most every respect contrary to the teaching and practices of Jesus Christ and His apostles who were indued and directed by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven, the Church, as a matter of fact, protested against the creed from every corner of the Empire only to be met with excommunication, confiscation of goods, and offices, and the members persecuted into subjection until they acknowledged the cannons and the creed adopted at this limited council of representative bishops of the Christian world with a

large minority protesting; but it was sanctioned by the Emperor and ratified by the civil magistrates and made the law of the Empire. All who adopted the creed and the cannons of the Emperor would be eligible to enjoy the privileges of the Church or hold offices in the government; and all who refused obedience to the acknowledgment of the creed and cannons adopted by the Emperor and the Catholic or Roman party, were anathematized as heretics and visited with penalties from both the ecclesiastical and civil authorities.

Whether this was giving the Church to paganism, or paganism to the Church can hardly be a question; for unconverted pagan sinners were now preferred to the highest offices in the Church; for, at the death of Auxentius, bishop of Milan, when the election was held, Ambrose the governor attended to preserve the peace of the Catholics who were factious. A child, perhaps instructed, shouted Ambrose! This was considered as a voice from God and the governor at the age of thirty was chosen bishop, which greatly accelerated his conversion, baptism and confirmation in the name of the holy, Divine and ever-blessed Trinity, God the Father, God the Son and 

God the Holy Ghost. 

Valesius, the Catholic historian says: "It is and ever was permitted to the Catholics to implore the aid of princes and magistrates against heretics that they may be restrained and kept in order." 

There is no room for comprehension or understanding, no conviction or persuasion, no thought or reason, and no scripture or science to be considered, if the Trinity is to be accepted at all, it must be accepted on blind assent in order to establish the doctrine under the Roman Catholic regime, since they use the weapons of oppression and of fear by calling in the sword of the civil magistrate; and the hard syllogisms of fines, imprisonment, excommunication and even death to make its mandates effective. 

The Christians which the Catholics called Arians proposed a confession of faith of the well-known truths always believed by all who were Christians; but all who adhered to the form of religion in which they had first received it were classed as heretics and persecuted as enemies. 

The Christians had no design to distress the consubstantialists; but believed in liberty to the extent that all had the right of individual interpretation of the Scriptures, and the privilege of worshipping God according to the dictates of one's own conscience. The

Christians have always been of this charitable and true spirit. The cruel spirit marks the false and cruel church under whatever name or creed it chooses to operate.

This Homoousian system of unity has always been a thorn in the flesh, and a sword piercing the spirit of those who wished to accept the holy scriptures as they were handed down to us from the apostles and evangelists of Jesus Christ; but the Catholics were not satisfied with the mere statement of scriptural terms and practices as articles of faith and of doctrine, for they insisted upon admonishing those who differed from them that they must not promulgate or teach anything contrary to the Nicene creed and cannons of the council if they did not wish to be denounced, anathematized and chastized with bodily pains and punishments.

The persecution of the Christians whom the Catholics called Arians, for more than a thousand years with both civil and ecclesiastical penalties which composed every conceivable engine of torture that the holy inquisitors could bring to bear upon the mind and flesh of those who would not submit to her apostate doctrines brought ruin and havoc to the Christians and established firmly the doctrines of the Antichrist who calls himself the vicegerent of God, and vicar of Jesus Christ, the Pontifex Maximus, the Pope of Rome.

Our blessed Lord and Savior Jesus Christ has taught us what we should believe concerning Him, and how we should act toward our fellow-men when He said: "Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy soul, mind and strength, and thy neighbor as thyself; for, 'God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believeth on Him should not perish but have everlasting life.'" Surely it is high time that the world is getting enough of these abominations of the vicegerent of God and vicar of Jesus Christ, "the man of sin, the son of perdition" who exalteth himself above all that is called God, sitting in the temple of God showing that He himself is God.

This would make Jesus Christ the Son of His Divine self and two other Divine persons besides which would make Him partially both the Father and Son of Himself, as there are said to be two other Divine persons who conjointly compose the triune God in conjunction with His own Divine person which would make Him as a man have three Divine persons for His Father, God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Ghost, of which neither is God without the other two, but all three are God conjointly without division or parts.

Our heart goes out for our deluded brethren in love, charity, sympathy, affection, devotion, and personal sacrifice, that we feel very much like the Apostle Peter felt, that we could be crucified head downwards for the salvation of our fellow-men, or find ourself in the greatest distress for the very necessities of life to bring to them the truth as it is in Jesus Christ or Lord, the only begotten Son of our Divine Father.

Who could ever so much as dream of Jesus Christ, casting people into prison, torturing, flailing, mobbing, burning and putting to death those who disbelieve or who are too ignorant, reprobate, or careless concerning the truth that He is the Christ, the Son of the living and only true God?

All who believe that Jesus Christ is God's only begotten Son and the mediator between God and man, and maintains that faith by good works of charity and brotherly love is accepted of Jesus Christ, and who is that villain that dare debar such an one from communion at the Lord's table or of fellowship in the Church? It is the individual's relationship to Jesus Christ through faith which decides man's relationship to his Divine Creator and which seals his destiny; and no ecclesiastical court has any right to stand between any person and his Divine Creator; and those who deny communion and fellowship to those who accept Jesus Christ the Son of God as their vicarious atonement and mediator between themselves and their Divine Creator, are criminals; for all of such faith are in harmony with God and with the gospel of Jesus Christ. And the Catholic faith is this: "That we worship one

God in Trinity and Trinity in unity, neither confounding the person nor dividing the substance. For there is one person of the Father, another of the Son and another of the Holy Ghost. But the Godhead of the Father, of the Son and of the Holy Ghost is all of one;

the glory equal, the majesty coeternal. Such as the Father is, such is the Son and such is the Holy Ghost; the Father uncreate, the Son uncreate, and the Holy Ghost uncreate; the Father incomprehensible, the Son incomprehensible, and the Holy Ghost incomprehensible; the Father eternal, the Son eternal, and the Holy Ghost eternal; and yet there are not three eternals but one eternal; as also there are not three incomprehensibles nor three uncreated, but one uncreated and one incomprehensible. So likewise the Father is Almighty, the Son almighty, and the Holy Ghost almighty; and yet there are not three almighties, but one almighty. So the Father is 

God, the Son is God, and the Holy Ghost is God; and yet there are not three Gods but one God. So likewise the Father is Lord, the

Son is Lord and the Holy Ghost is Lord; and yet there are not three Lords but one Lord. For we are compelled by the Christian verity to acknowledge every person by himself to be God and Lord, so are we forbidden by the Catholic religion to say that there are three Gods or three Lords. The Father is made of none, neither created nor begotten; the Son is of the Father alone not made nor created but begotten; the Holy Ghost is of the Father and of the 

Son neither made nor created nor begotten but proceeding. So there is one Father not three Fathers, one Son not three Sons, and one 

Holy Ghost not three Holy Ghosts. And in this Trinity none is before nor after another, none is greater nor less than another; but the whole three persons are coeternal together and coequal. So that in all things as aforesaid, the Unity in Trinity and the Trinity in Unity is to be worshipped. He therefore who would be saved, must think thus of the Trinity. Furthermore it is necessary to everlasting salvation that he also believe rightly the incarnation of our Lord Jesus Christ. For the right faith is, that we believe and confess that our Lord Jesus Christ the Son of God, is God and man; God of the substance of the Father begotten before the worlds; and man the substance of His mother, born in the world; perfect God and perfect man, of a reasonable soul and human flesh subsisting; equal with the Father as touching His Godhead; and inferior to the Father as touching His manhood. Who, though He be God and man, yet He is not two but one Christ; not one by conversion of the Godhead into flesh, but by taking the manhood into God. One altogether, not by confusion of substance, but by the unity of person. For as the reasonable soul and flesh is one man, so God and man is one Christ who suffered for our salvation; descended into hell, rose again the

third day from the dead; He ascended into heaven, and sitteth on the right hand of the Father God Almighty from whence He shall come to judge the quick and the dead; at whose coming all men shall rise again with their bodies and shall give account for their own works. And they that have done good shall go into life everlasting, and they that have done evil into everlasting fire. This is the Catholic faith which except a man believe faithfully, he cannot be saved. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy 

Ghost. As it was in the beginning is now, and ever shall be world without end, Amen."

What a travesty upon the life and teachings of Jesus Christ for a Church presumably Christian to alternately affirm and deny most every statement in its creed? All this speculative reasoning of these Trinitarian philosophers is not taken from the Bible but from the heathen Platonic and Alexandrian philosophers; and the erroneous opinions which those fell into who did not hold to the exactness of apostolic testimony.

The incarnate Word, Jesus Christ, is not by adoption God's Son, but by creation and also by incarnation is He God's Son. God has not produced anything by nature as nature is that quality or state of existence which our Divine Creator has given to the things of His creation; and everything has been produced by the omnipotent power of His spirit and given a nature such as He chose for everything; as all other persons, beings or things whatsoever are dependent upon our Divine Father for their creation, nature and powers; but our Divine Father's nature and powers have no counterpart, and cannot be produced or reproduced, neither created nor begotten; as He is infinite, absolute, and independent He can have no counterpart.

A person that is infinite, absolute, independent and uncreate cannot be divided in nature, essence or substance with that of any other person; neither can he be added to or subtracted from or multiplied. Therefore, the incarnate Word Jesus Christ being the firstborn creature of His Divine Father's creation, He cannot be of the same nature, essence or substance as that of His Divine Father's person; and Christ's Divinity, coequality and coeternity is all a hoax and a satanic lie.

Christ never compromised the person, spirit, will, power and authority of His Divine Father in heaven by claiming even the least infinitesimal part of the power or authority which He exercised was 

His own; but said honestly and truthfully: "I of myself can do nothing, it is my Father who doeth these works;" but since Jesus 

Christ did not deem it necessary to insert every doctrine that is true into an authoritative mandate, He summed up the whole duty of man in these two commandments: "Thou shalt worship thy Divine

Father in spirit and in truth, for the Father seeketh such to worship 

Him; and thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself."

These were authors of commentaries and of histories and found sufficient scope for their religious thoughts, and objects for their devotion without persecuting those who worshipped statues and dead men's bones.

As soon as the bishop of Rome had donned the robes of the 

Pontifex Maximus of the "Big Red Dragon," the Christian princes found that there was no safety outside of the Church of Rome as every priest of Rome labored to subvert their power and undermine their thrones; for all Catholic subjects were taught to hail every 

Catholic prince or adventurer as a deliverer, and betray a fortress, a city or a kingdom to any Catholic power. Women were taught to betray their husbands, children to rebel against their sovereigns, and soldiers to resist the officers. There was no compromising; every protestant was a heretic; and to murder them merited indulgences and blessings from the Church, as every Catholic was taught that all other persuasions were heretic and were to be avoided, abandoned, persecuted and destroyed. With the Catholics there was prosperity by patronage, safety by protection, and peace by union with those who permitted no peace except to those of the

Catholic faith. No pretext was too trivial, no error to obscure to be repented or punished with death.

Those who held Easter on the very night in which it was instituted by the Son of God were denounced by the law as worthy of death. Manicheans, illustrious for virtue were promptly burnt; 

Nestorians of the very same creed were outlawed, their property confiscated, and their Churches seized; Donatists were hunted down like wild beasts; Arians, for saying that Christ had a beginning were put to death; and even the semi-Arians, those noble Christian professors who held that Jesus was the Son of God, begotten of the Father, were called Arians and slaughtered. The Catholics blushed for no shame however wicked and murderous. Apologized for no falsehood; and conviction of crime caused no modesty. 

The Catholics adored with equal veneration Athanasius in his villainy; Anthony in his impostures; Ambrose in his wickedness; and

Cyril in his cruelty. The Catholic priests and prelates are an unmarried horde without sympathy for humanity who encouraged in the rulers a savage barbarity; and with a hideous superstition awed the humble poor into abject obedience; governed the great by the advantages of prosperity; and held over all the terror of earthly annihilation.

Reeves, the Catholic historian, informs us that Pope Christopharus took the Chair of St. Peter by violence and was overcome and cast into prison by Pope Sergius the third: "The slave of every vice and most wicked of men." His holiness Pope Sergius the third, a sovereign Pontiff of the Roman Catholic Church, the self-professed vicegerent of God and vicar of Jesus Christ clasp in the lewd embrace of a notorious prostitute. He publicly avowed his criminal connection with "Marozia" by whom he had a son who became 

Pope John the eleventh.

Bishop Purcell of the Roman Catholic diocese of Cincinnati, Ohio, in his debate with Campbell said: "I would not be surprised if these bad Popes were at this moment expiating their crimes in the penal fires of hell." Oh, mystery, Babylon! Thou "Mother of harlots and abominations of the earth," who can accept thy Trinity of fraud, rape, and murder, and believe that thou art the Church of Jesus Christ, the Son of God? Through what horrid scenes we have passed during the fifteen hundred years of the "Antichrist's" Papal rule!

And is this the history of a Church whose head claims to be the infallible vicegerent of God, and the vicar of Jesus Christ? Our

heart is sick at the recital of thy abominations; and our eyes abhor the printed page which relates the history of thy foul, villainous character and murderous acts!

This contumacy on the part of the ministry of all Churches is greatly to be deplored, and repented with a contrite heart and a submissive spirit ere destruction claims our existence. 

The Christians have the historians Hegesippus and Eusebius of the first ages of Christianity. The Catholics claim none before the sixth century. The Christians have many nations and kings in the first three hundred years of Christianity which was before the rise of Roman Catholicism and the Catholics claim no king till Clovis in the sixth century. In most every country, and in most every clime the Christians preached the gospel before the Roman Catholic Church was founded and the Catholic religion was resisted or rejected by all peoples where the gospel had been preached. 

The Christians not given up to plunder, suddenly found their kingdoms and their homes pillaged and themselves condemned as heretics, and all they held sacred profaned and anathematized by the imperious mandates of the Roman Pontiffs. 

We shall all be held accountable for our obedience to Jesus Christ, and no Pope, bishop, preacher, priest or layman has any right to demand that we obey them in matters of faith any more than we have to demand that they obey us, as every one must personally give an account of his conduct to God; and no one has any more right to our obedience beyond that of mutual love, good-will and helpfulness as there is no Divinely constituted authority in the earth; "But he that is greatest among you shall be your servant or minister; and he who desires to be first shall be last of all." 

In vain did Christ say: "I am the way, the truth and the life," to those who will not choose to enter through Him as the medium of knowledge, understanding and discernment of truth to His loving and indulgent Divine Father.

The painting of God as a monster with a lake of an everlasting hell of fire where He will burn, torture, lacerate, torment, maim, bruise, mangle, sear, scorch, singe and harrow with every pain that infinite knowledge can possibly devise, is below the thought of the crudest savages and cannibals that ever trod the earth; and can anyone imagine that he is a Christian who will thus blaspheme, berate, debase and abuse the mind of their precious children with such a hellish, fiendish, disgraceful, villainous, murderous and tyrannical

conception of God? But such is the orthodox doctrine of hell in the minds of common folk; but the word hell in a technical sense means destruction or annihilation of the body and its sensibilities in the grave. So the conception which many orthodox people have of a three-faced Divine triune monster giving eternal life to Lucifer and all the imps of hell that they might assist him in torturing forever fully ninety percent of the human race, are certainly monstrosities of the deepest dye; and any parent that is so hard-hearted and insane as to frighten his innocent babes with such fear of God is a villain of the worst kind; for no one can love, worship, honor and adore in the true spirit of adoration what is said to be far worse than the devil himself who is said to delight in the sufferings of others.

The councils of Ephesus and Chalcedon decreed that the Virgin Mary is the mother of God, and that she should be received by the faithful and honored in supplication and adoration with that of the 

Holy Trinity under the title "Theotokos" or "Mother of God;" and she sustains this supreme honor over and above our Divine Father in the Roman Catholic Church to this day. 

It is these corruptions of Christianity to which real Christians could not consent which brought on excommunication, persecution, suffering, and the inquisition and martyrdom of the Christians by the Catholics throughout the Roman Empire until it is estimated that above fifty millions of people have been martyred or destroyed by the Catholics because of their religious belief. 

The persecuted might have been orthodox, but the persecutors cannot be whatever their faith or creed. If the millions of Christians which the "Mother of harlots and abominations of the earth," the Roman Catholic Church put to death as heretics were enmies of Jesus Christ, God's glorious Son, why then, did they die for Him, His gospel to save and perpetuate. Why were their records destroyed, their property confiscated, themselves butchered, burned, sawnasunder, and martyred by every conceivable engine of torture the holy inquisitors could inflict upon those who died for the name and faith in Jesus Christ as the Son of God? There is but one answer:

They would not bow down to the Pope of Rome, the assumed vicegerent of God and vicar of Jesus Christ, the Pontifex Maximus of Rome, the Antichrist, who exalts himself above all that is called God; and sits himself in the temple of God showing that he himself is God," but who has no part or portion with Jesus Christ; for

Jesus Christ said so when He said: "The God of this world cometh who has nothing in me."

The Christians resisted the imperious mandates of the Roman Pontiffs, as the Christians rested their faith upon reason, scripture, traditions and customs handed down to them from the apostles of Christ and their contemporary disciples; but the imperial government of Rome and of Constantinople which was maintained by the arbitrary power of an absolute monarch who passed a decree that the Catholic religion should hold sway throughout his dominions to the exclusion of all others with the bishop at Rome as the head of the Church; and this is why the Christians were slaughtered. 

How could Christians enter into communion and fellowship with those who treated them with every kind of cruelty known to man such as excommunication, confiscation of goods, disfranchisement of offices and of suffrage, persecutions of bodily penances, banishments and in many cases death was the only relief, or abject subjection to a band of robbers and murderers whose chief was the Pope of Rome.

The Christians denied that the sins of the departed dead, by masses, alms or penance of the living, could be forgiven or atoned for by the living.

The Christians existed by the thousands before the Roman Catholic Church came into existence; and exercised faith in our Divine 

Father in heaven, and in His glorious Son, the incarnate Word, Jesus 

Christ before any creeds were formed to harass and curse mankind, and the world would by far, be better off without them. Every one that is slain for the purpose of enforcing a creed is murdered and every drop of Christian blood cries out to God against their murderers. The sword, spear, faggot and all other inquisitorial instruments of torture will enter into judgment against those who use them to their own destruction in the day of judgment. "Vengeance is mine saith the Lord, I will repay . . . with what judgment ye judge, ye shall be judged . . . condemn not and ye shall not be condemned.

With what measure ye mete out to others, it shall be measured to you again," by our Divine Father in heaven.

Our heart goes out in love, sympathy and good-will to those misguided, pure, innocent folk who belong to a Church corporation which commits murder, sacrilege and idolatry; and brands Christians as infidels and heretics because they cannot accept their creed

of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person, or a Trinity of 

Deities in one God.

Is an individual who is so wicked, sinful, and villainous that he has committed most every sin known to God, men or demons infallible in morals and religion and a fit personage to be called the vicegerent of God, vicar of Jesus Christ and the Holy Father by the faithful followers of Jesus Christ? Is such a reprobate a fit person to be the guide and instructor of the young in the ways of God, of truth, of righteousness and of the life eternal?

History records that a goodly number of the Popes have been guilty of branding Christians as heretics and having them murdered in the most hideous modes of persecution and execution that human genius could devise; and afterwards they were canonized as saints; and the more zealous murderers were venerated and worshipped, and hallowed by the Church as defenders of the faith. 

We may always be sure that_a religion that persecutes never came from our Divine Father in heaven. It must be said of every one who wilfully and purposely injures his fellow-men in any way: "Ye are of your Father the Devil, and the works of your father ye do." These horrid executioners and murderers of Christians produced the highest commendations of the Church of Rome, and merited indulgences equal to the zeal of crusaders. 

The word Trinity in the hands of the clergy during the Dark Ages, was almost synonymous with persecution; and to say that a minister is a Trinitarian was almost universally allowed to be a conclusive argument, "ergo," he is a liar, a villain, and a murderous persecutor.

How can that be called a Church of Jesus Christ which is established upon rules of faith, and upon teachings and practices which are not His; and which excommunicates or excludes from its communion those who do follow Him, and whom He will some day receive into His kingdom of immortality and the life eternal? 

Reader! Honesty is the best policy! If you are going to be a follower of Jesus Christ, you must not set up your own private or individual interpretation as a rule of faith and practice for all others. 

Accept Jesus Christ at His word which is always sensible and consistent in every detail, and when you find anything that does not sound right or is self-contradictory like the doctrine of the Trinity of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person be sure to search out the villain who started the falsity; and be not like the

Antichrist, the Pope of the Roman Catholic Church who excludes Christians from the Church because they do not follow his teachings, doctrines and practices, and worship him as the vicegerent of God, and vicar of Jesus Christ; but in excommunicating, and excluding the followers of Jesus Christ from His Church because they do not recognize him as the head of the Church, he excludes himself from Jesus Christ and the realm of God; for Christ says: "He that desires to be first shall be last of all," and "It were better for that man had he never been born," or that "A mill-stone were hanged about his neck and he drowned in the depths of the sea, rather than to offend one of his followers."

Our first allegiance is to God and truth, to the gospel of Jesus. 

Christ and to the apostolic testimony; and anything that does not agree therewith should be anathema as far as each individual is concerned, as nothing contrary to the teachings of Jesus Christ and of His apostles is of God. But our own private or individual interpretation is not to be made the standard or rule of faith and practice for others, save only as he is guided by his own conscience, as all must come to know or comprehend for himself individually what he understands God's word to teach him, as the conscience of every individual is the responsible factor between the individual and his God to the full extent of its enlightenment or knowledge of the truth.

Barring two or three interpolations, such as the Trinitarian formula of baptism inserted into the last chapter of Saint Matthew and the mistranslation of "The Word was God" in the first chapter of the gospel according to Saint John; and the personification of the 

Spirit of God, there would be but little chance for the Trinitarian doctrine of the Antichrist of "Three Divine persons in the one Divine person of the triune God." For there are many who are personally conscious of the inconsistency of these interpolations with the general teachings and practices of Jesus Christ and His apostles; but because of the ecclesiasticism of the Church, the Bible is interpreted and translated to harmonize with it until many passages of scripture bear but small resemblance to its original meaning; and are, therefore, contrary to the faith, teaching and practices of Jesus Christ, and His apostles, and every private knowledge of truth. 

These translators and interpolators are not only imbued with erroneous notions and falsities; but they are blasphemies against our 

Divine Father in heaven and against His Son Jesus Christ who stand

for the pure unity of our Divine Father in one person as the only true and living God and sole Deity, without any counterpart or associate of Divinity; and they who teach a contrary doctrine to that of Jesus Christ and His apostles, are the destroyers of the innocent, the pure and the righteous who are not aware of the contradictory absurd, and inconsistent doctrines palmed off on them as the teachings of Jesus Christ, for Jesus Christ and His apostles, and the prophets teach that the "Lord our God is one Lord;" and "There is but one God the Father."

From the days of Justinian in the first part of th sixth century, until the American Constitution of the United States was adopted, there was a penalty for the denial of the Roman Catholic Trinity of three Divine persons in the one Divine person of the triune God," upon the statute books of most all Catholic and Protestant countries. 

In the sixth century the Emperor Justinian sent forth his great general Belisarius to bring into subjection all unconquered Christian kingdoms and principalities within the Roman Empire to the Roman Catholic faith of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person. 

Nation after nation fell prostrate before Rome's conquering legions, out of which arose the Pope-King or "Little horn which grew into mighty strength until it conquered all the saints of God," spoken of in the prophecy of Daniel and also in the Book of Revelations to the Apostle Saint John, until all nations within the Roman Empire paid tribute and obeisance to the Pope of Rome as head of the Church.

About the close of the eighteeenth century, and the beginning of the nineteenth, the more pious of the clergy of various Protestant denominations in America beheld with emotion the moral desolations which prevailed in the ranks generally to an alarming extent. 

It was then that Jones, Smith, O'Kelly, Purivance and others whose names are enshrined in the affections of the lovers of true Christian Bible doctrine and of Christian liberty dropped their denominational Church names, and chose to be known simply as Christians, with the Bible as their guide, the right of individual interpretation, and the fellowship of all Christians conjointly in union with people of all denominations.

The Church of the Christians became an organized body fellowshipping Christians of all denominations December 25, 1793; and since that time all are admitted into full fellowship and communion

with Christians upon good character whatever their private interpretation of the Bible might be.

The Christian communion invites all of every denomination, sect, Church, creed or persuasion of good character to join with them upon their own private or individual interpretation, so long as they do not seek to limit arbitrarily the privilege of private or individual interpretation of others. The Christians fellowship and invite to communion at the Lord's table all Christians of every name; and leave or permission to observe or dispense with any sacrament is left to the voluntary choice of the individual conscience of each member as to mode and manner of worship. 

Child of God, whoever you may be or wherever you may be, remember that the Christians offer you a Church home where you can worship God according to the dictates of your own conscience; and their ministers are at your services whether you have ever belonged to any Church or not; and they will perform for you any Christian rite according to the dictates of your own conscience as they grant universal religious suffrage within the Church of the Christians. 

The Christians acknowledge no human leaders or their creeds as binding upon them in any way as there is absolute autonomy and fellowship to those of good character, and their only authority is Jesus Christ the Son of God individually interpreted, as every individual is dependent upon his knowledge of truth for direction in righteousness, and is responsible to God for his conduct. 

The liberty of Christians has given a new impulse to the reformation waive by joining with the Congregationalists whose onward roll will be commensurate or coextensive with eternity, as there are many converts in its communion who never have and never could submit to human dogmas; and those who aforetime were subject to human dogmas dropped their names of distinction with their reverend titles in order that there be but one Lord, Jesus the Christ over the Church, and His followers one in name and in union. 

Those who ascribe to a creed, follow the commandments and dictates of men, and all who do so put themselves under obligations to believe, preach, and teach that which is incompatible with the spirit and teaching of Jesus Christ, His apostles and His saints; and it soon narrows down to schisms and heresies among the people. 

The Church of Jesus Christ should include all who believe in His name, and are quickened at His word. The Bible is the standard of 

Christians, and is the real standard of measurement by which error

can with but little study be determined. There is nothing so orthodox as truth, and whether the theologian or general scholar be employed in ascertaining the nature of Christianity including both doctrine and discipline, it is of the greatest moment to investigate the state or condition of the Church of the Christians previous to its union with the civil power or its patronage by the emperors of the world in order to get a clear understanding of the many corruptions of Christianity.

The diversity of gods and of religious worship among the heathen was never known to generate animosity or kindle the flames of war between nations in order to propagate their religion among other peoples, as their gods were not so profane and vulgar as the triuneheaded monster of the Roman Catholic Church in whose name was committed every sin and outrage known to man against the Christians in order to subject them to their triune Deity. 

The heathen were much more humane and moral than the Roman Catholics, as each of the heathen nations readily conceded to others the right of forming their own opinions, and judging for themselves in matters of religious concern their mode or manner of worship; and left them both in the choice of their Deities and their freedom of worshipping them according to the dictates of their own conscience, and to be guided by whatever principles they might think proper to adopt.

To be sure no peoples would desire a foreign God whose maw could only be satisfied with blood, rape, murder, confiscation and destruction of their goods and property; and take from its worshippers the right to form their own opinions and worship according to the dictates of their own conscience.

CHAPTER XI 

Our Divine Father is the pure, unsullied fountain of all good; and He has not left Himself without witnesses, in that He has sent into the world prophets and holy men directed by the power of His Holy Spirit to teach and confirm His will through miracles, signs and wonders the doctrines of His love and charity; the forgiveness of our sins through repentance, and redemption by the resurrection from the dead through Jesus Christ His only begotten Son, our Lord and Savior.

There is absolutely no use of philosophizing about Jesus Christ when He tells you that He is the Son of God, and that He has a Divine Father and that the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father is the executor of all Divine acts whatsoever without exception; and the humblest, most ignorant child of God so acting in good faith is readily accepted by our Divine Father as an heir of God and a joint heir with His Son Jesus Christ upon his repentance; but those who do not repent of their sins, may believe, comprehend and understand the true relationship between the glorious Son of God the incarnate Word Jesus Christ and His Divine, infinite father, and philosophize all their days, and wonder and perish everlastingly.

Those who speak of Christ as having two natures; one human and the other Divine use terms without knowing Christ's relationship to either the human or Divine; for they speak of Him as speaking at times in His human nature and at other times in His Divine nature; and at other times they are at a loss to know which to ascribe His language or His works according as He shows power or weakness in knowledge, and in His works; but Christ says: "The doctrine I teach is not mine, but the Father's who sent me; the works that I do are not mine it is my Father who doeth the works.” 

Thus, Christ of Himself can do nothing; so He always teaches and works according as the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father teaches and works through Him. The Trinitarians will tell you that Christ is composed of two persons in one, the human and the Divine; that in His humanity 

He is but a man; but in His Divinity He is an eternal God; co- 208

eternal with two other Divine persons, Gods or Deities whom they call God the Father and God the Holy Ghost; and that the two combined persons of the human and the Divine in Christ make but one Christ not three Christs. Such people belie their own heart, their own conscience, their own intelligence, their own sense of truth and veracity; for no one can read the New Testament of our Lord and 

Savior Jesus Christ so much as one giving heed to what it says concerning Christ Jesus without seeing the many discrepancies, inconsistencies and contradictions with which the doctrine of the Trinity and also of two persons in Christ encounter, as the Bible plainly teaches that our Divine Father is the only person without an original or Creator, and all persons and things other than Himself are of His creation, and dependent upon Him for their existence and powers, and all that they are and have. 

Jesus Christ, the Son of God, was the preexistent unincarnate Word before He was incarnated; but upon His incarnation He was clothed with flesh and was called Jesus, and after His baptism and induement with the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father, He was also I called the Christ or anointed. 

Christ said to His disciples that the gift of the power and authority of the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father could not come to them unless He returned to His Divine Father as they always depended upon Christ instead of upon His Father the true source of all power and authority for direction and comfort in all things, instead of upon the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father from which He received His power and authority. So Jesus told them that He was going to return to His Divine Father; and that they should tarry at Jerusalem until they be indued with the power and authority of the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father in heaven. Christ told His disciples that they were to do nothing concerning the kingdom of themselves or of their own accord. Not even in the midst of persecution were they to be anxious what to do or say, for: “It shall be given you in that hour what ye shall say and do, for it is not ye that is to do the doing and talking, but the Spirit of your Divine 

Father is to act and talk through you."

Christ's disciples tarried in Jerusalem waiting for the fulfillment of the promise of power from the Father's Holy Spirit by which they were to receive the faculty of knowledge, wisdom and power to do the things our heavenly Father would have them to do and say; for they are to do and say only those things which the Holy

Spirit of their Divine Father in heaven said and did through them. 

This Divine power proceeded always and only from our Divine Father in heaven through His Holy Spirit to the prophets, to Jesus Christ and His apostles, and to the saints of God; but on the day of 

Pentecost the disciples of Christ received a special outpouring of God's Holy Spirit to endue them with power and authority for the work of the ministry by which they were enabled to preach, teach, prophesy, heal, raise the dead, cast out demons and perform signs and wonders as proof of their Divine mission. 

We wish to appeal to intelligent folk in scripture lore as it is little use to speak to irreligious people or even to scientists who are ignorant of the Bible; but unless they become informed in them they will not know or interpret history as they should, neither will they be led by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father unto regeneration without which they cannot be saved. 

People as a rule give credence to those things that they were taught in their childhood even though they do not know the reason why; and it is about as hard to get them to reason on Divine things by searching the scriptures or after scientific principles illustrating Divine truths, as it is for them to pluck the apple from their eye. 

There are so many things built on popular error without the least foundation in truth, such as the Trinitarian formula of baptism interpolated in the gospel of Saint Matthew which was never used by the apostles of Jesus Christ nor any of their contemporary disciples who baptized only and always in the name of Jesus Christ. 

The conscience of man is the only safe guide however mistaken, incorrect or erroneous it might be; as it is the prompter, rebuker, approver, accuser, and directer in all things that the human spirit feels that it ought or ought not to do to fulfill its duties and responsibilities; and one should always do what the highest conception of right his spirit discerns to be according to his conscience seeking at all times the guidance of the Holy Spirit of his Divine Father in heaven in prayer and supplication. The one who does this will never wilfully commit sin, for he will not deliberately and wilfully transgress what he perceives to be the will of God; but the spirit of man, however, needs instruction, teaching, training, and culture in things Divine, and a disposition to know what the will of God is by the process of discrimination between right and wrong, truth and error; for, if misguided it will lead you into all kinds of falsities, absurdities and inconsistencies such as the doctrine of the

Trinity, the time of Easter, the time of the Sabbath, the personification of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father, purgatory, oricular confession, infallibility of the Pope, masses and baptisms for the dead, baptizing babies, indulgences, transubstantiation; and everlasting suffering for the wicked which are all ecclesiastical falsities, frauds, or errors as these are all departures from the teachings of 

Jesus Christ.

The pagan Roman government allowed to every citizen the free exercise of his own reason and judgment in all matters of religion; and extended their toleration to every kind of religion from whence no danger to the public safety was to be apprehended; but at the same time they would not endure that anyone should deride or attempt to explode the religion of the state or that which had the support of the laws. For there existed between the government and the religion of the Romans such an intimate connection and interdependence on each other that whosever attacked or endeavored to undermine their religion could not of necessity appear to them otherwise than hostile to the state and inimical to the dignity and safety of the government. But, the Christians laid aside every sort of fear, and strenuously endeavored to make the Romans renounce their vain and silly superstitions by urging them to give up or abolish these sacred rights on the observance of which the Romans felt the welfare and dignity of the state so much to depend. 

The Christians intended no ill will toward the Roman state whatever; but because they opposed idolatry, they were looked upon and treated as enemies of the government. The Christians not only asserted that the religions of Rome were false; but also, that eternal salvation depended altogether upon the religion of Jesus Christ, through whom only man can be saved.

The Romans drew the inference that the Christians were not only arrogant and supercilious in their pretensions, but they were also filled with hatred toward the government; but the innocence, the beauty, and the excellence of the Christian system at last prevailed; and the Christians were permitted, after a long reign of persecution against them to exercise their religion in any part of the Empire under governmental supervision.

It was under the governmental supervision or regulation of the Church of Jesus Christ by the state where sin and corruption of the Antichrist overcame the Church, as the right of individual interpretation of the scriptures was forbidden and the teaching and prac-

tices of the apostles of Jesus Christ were infringed upon by the adoption of a Trinity of Divine persons dictated by heathen philosophers and the manner of teaching and practice established by law.

The liberty of the Christians to teach the Christian doctrine that "The Lord our God is the one Divine Father in heaven only," and that "The incarnate Word Jesus Christ is our Divine Father's Son and the first-born creature of all creation," became anathema by the Antichrist, the vicegerent of God, and Vicar of Jesus Christ, the man of sin, the son of perdition, the Pope of Rome; and the doctrine of the Trinity of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person adopted in its place.

When people begin to realize the great difference between the very simple gospel teachings of Jesus Christ of one Divine Father as the one and only Divine person; and the very much complicated and contradictory system of three Divine persons in one Divine person, they will not marvel that certain annotators of the Holy Scriptures in their compilations and comments have worked continually to squeeze into the Bible the doctrine of the Trinity by personifying the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven by using the masculine gender pronouns instead of the neuter or no gender pronouns; and using the word Trinity wherever they find the 

Holy Spirit of our Divine Father and His Son Jesus Christ used in connection with our Divine Father and the works of His Holy Spirit. 

To whom do you suppose Jesus Christ prayed continually, if it was not to His Divine Father only; as we have not a single instance of Him praying to any other; and to whom do you suppose 

He directed His disciples to pray in the prayer commonly called the Lord's prayer when His Divine Father is the only one He ever addressed in prayer? If there were three Divine persons to be equally served, worshipped, honored and adored; and Jesus Christ being one of them, he, as a man, was in duty bound to worship His Divine nature or person and also the Divine person of the Holy Spirit if they are likewise to be served, worshipped, honored and adored with the same glory and adoration as our Divine Father in heaven; and all the prophets, Jesus Christ and His apostles must be considered very inefficient teachers or false to themselves, to their fellow-men and to God likewise for not divulging or making known that which it was their Divine mission to do! But all these were not

false teachers or liars; but those who teach these things are liars and falsifiers of God's truths who claim there are three Divine, coequal, coessential and coeternal persons, and equal in power, glory and majesty to be worshipped, honored and adored with the same glory, praise and adoration.

It is God's glory to produce human beings who can stand the test against anything that diversity, or misfortune can bring to them for the sake of righteousness without being bribed to righteousness by prosperity and the promise of immortal glory or the life eternal. 

But, God does reward those who endure trials and tribulations with cheerfulness and thanksgiving for the sake of righteousness, and in this trial of creative strength in His creatures, His moral goodness is producing some such people. 1 Our Divine Father is not partisan to any Church, creed or sect; but honors truth, faith and works of charity as works of righteousness without regard to Church, creed or denomination; but God is against every one who does not seek the welfare and good of his neighbor; and any person or any Church, sect, or denomination that is unwilling to dwell together in communion, love and fellowship with all the followers of Christ, the wrath of God shall abide upon him; for Jesus has expressly said that this is the will of our Divine. 

Father in heaven.

It makes but little difference if we reject every man-made creed that was ever written, so long as we believe that Jesus Christ is God's Son and the mediator between God and man and do works of righteousness meet for repentance by acting the part of the good 

Samaritan; the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven will guide us into all truth and usefulness; and the Church by so doing will continue steadfast in the doctrine set forth by the apostles, in fellowship, in the breaking of bread, and in prayers. 

It is by the teaching of the true gospel that we are to be saved; and not by the false doctrine of the Antichrist of a triune Deity which caused a heresy and a schism in the Church during the fourth century of the Christian era. Therefore we have the greatest of reasons to believe that it is antichristian to preach or practice baptism in the name of the Trinity for the remission of sins, and for membership in the Church which Jesus Christ and His apostles never taught or practiced.

The only teaching and practice of baptism by the apostles and their Divinely appointed successors were in the name of Jesus

Christ only, for upwards of two hundred years, according to every authentic source of information. Thus their God is first Father, and then the Son, and in His glorified state, the Holy Ghost. Their God has passed through many alterations or changes; as He has existed. in various modes or natures which really means nothing definite or tangible, as they say God manifests Himself at times as Creator and Father, sometimes, as a Son or creature, and at other times as a Ghost or Spirit. Since the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father is the life and sustaining power of all things, it is the sustaining power of our spirit, as our spirit is the life of our body or soul; and as the body dies when the spirit is separated from the body, so also, will the spirit of the soul of man die if separated by sin from the sustaining power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father.

Our Divine Father's glorious first-born Son of all creation, the Word, was created an immortal spirit person; and as such was not

subject to death because of Adam's transgression, because He was a superangelical spirit being; and had not broken God's law like 

Adam nor like Lucifer and the angels who sinned by not keeping their first state of purity through obedience to their Divine Creator. 

But, preadventure, had He not kept His first state of obedience pure and undefiled, He would, like the angels who sinned, be subject to destruction the same as they.

It was the purpose of our Divine Father who foreknew all things before the beginning of His creation, the character and disposition of all things before they were ever brought forth; that His glorious first-born Son of all creation the Word, should become incarnate and assume the debt of man's mortality or death, by giving His own body of flesh for the redemption of the bodies of all the penitent, pure, innocent and the regenerated through the resurrection of their bodies at His second coming to a life that is eternal, immortal and that fadeth not away reserved in heaven forever with God and His holy angels and His saints. 

How great, grand, glorious and beneficent is our Divine Father in heaven who redeems us through faith in His Son upon our repentance and reformation by sacrificing His Son's body of flesh for our redemption in lieu of our eternal destruction from His presence and power.

Jesus Christ as God's incarnate Word and only begotten Son was not of Adam's race or of those who were born under God's broken law, and He was not, therefore, subject to death or mortality by reason of God's broken law, He not being of Adam's race was not subject to the penalty of Adam's sin through inheritance. For this reason the broken law had no claim upon Him; but, as Adam and all His posterity were subject to the broken law because of Adam's transgression, all of Adam's race or posterity are subject to death, the penalty due to the broken law; and Adam and his posterity must remain in the grave forever unless the penalty of death is removed by one who does not owe the debt, or is not subject to the debt will volunteer to pay the debt for those who are subject to it and cannot pay.

God's first-born, well-beloved and glorious Son the Word, freely offers Himself to His Divine Father for the purpose of removing the penalty of death from man due to his sin; and how does He do it? Since our Divine Father in heaven does all things of His own free will by the executive or operating power of His Holy Spirit He

caused His superangelical, immortal and glorious Son the Word to be conceived through incarnation by a virgin whose name is Mary. of the house or lineage of David. Through the incarnation of the 

Word, God's glorious Son is born as a babe and clothed with human flesh by a woman under the law of sin and death that He might offer His body of perfect manhood as a sacrificial vicarious atonement for man's sin that mortal man might be reinstated into life through the resurrection from the dead through faith and the acceptance of the grace of repentance of all who will come unto God by Him.

The penalty due to Adam's transgression is death to the human soul, and since man is possessed of no other, man at death without a redeemer would become extinct of life or cease to live; "But thanks be to God for His unspeakable gift, Jesus the Christ, God's only begotten Son, that whosoever believeth on Him shall not perish, but have everlasting life."

Because of Adam's sin, all of his posterity are subject to the death of mortality which is not removed directly by any act of man; but indirectly through the vicarious sacrifice of Jesus Christ through the grace of repentance or reformation of the sinner which is effective unto all of those who repent and those who through ignorance or innocence have not the truth, but have the answer of a good conscience toward God. Christ removes through this sacrificial atonement of His body the penalty of everlasting death to the souls of those who have sinned or inherited it, only in so far as man is penitent, innocent or unaccountable. 

Without the vicarious offering of Jesus Christ in our behalf there would be no salvation for man from death unto life, as man could not pay in his own room and stead the penalty of death due to transgressions past and live; but Jesus Christ who was possessed of an immortal spirit of a superangelical nature as well as a rational soul could surrender the latter in man's behalf to pay the debt of death for man's sin; and could still by the grace of His Divine 

Father live as an immortal spirit eternally.

This plan of our Divine Father for man's redemption through the sacrificial atonement of Christ's human soul or body of flesh and blood given by Christ and accepted by our Divine Father, as the full penalty due to penitent man's sin is magnificent. This plan for the saving of man from death and destruction is the most glorious scheme of redemption of which man can form conception; as the

vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ removes the penalty of everlasting destruction from the penitent sinner and the innocent by the vicarious sacrifice of Jesus Christ.

Man would have always and forever been subject to the mortality of death if it were not for the choice of our Divine Father in giving His Son; and for the voluntary sacrifice assumed by the incarnate 

Son of God through whose immolation the penitent sinner should not perish but have everlasting life. Could anything be more beneficent or magnificent, lovely or beautiful than the wondrous condescension and free grace manifested by our loving and adorable 

Father in heaven and by His glorious Son Jesus Christ?

CHAPTER XII 

Our Divine Father has appointed a day in which He will judge the world by His Son Jesus Christ in which the transition of the righteous will take place from this state of mortality to that of immortality. In that millennial day very early in the morning the trumpets of God will sound, heralded by the voice of Michael the archangel, and the Son of God shall come forth in the glory of His Divine Father; and clothed with the power of His Divine Father's spirit He will call forth from their graves, all the lovers of God, and of their fellow-men and will say unto them: "Come ye blessed of my Father inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world."

The power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father which raised up Jesus Christ from the dead will also quicken our mortal bodies and we shall rise triumphant from the tomb through a glad and glorious resurrection into the life of an eternal immortality to bask in the sunlight of God's love, and to live with Him in His house of many mansions, and worship before His great white throne surrounded by the crystal sea, and His ever-blessed angels and glorified saints. 

Oh, the joy, the blessedness, the hallowed ecstasy my enraptured soul feels even now at the thought of such wondrous grace and condescension that He invites us all to come and live with Him forever!

Our Divine Father who creates, forms and fashions all things by His spirit's power and determines their habitation and duration according to His own will and pleasure, desires the good and happiness of His creatures; and since we pass this way but once; if we do not make our calling and election sure by faith and good works we shall be lost in the second death, the death of the destruction of both body and of soul forever, as only the true worshippers of our Divine Father, who is the only true and living God, will be made immortal unto eternal life by the power of our Divine Father's 

Holy Spirit.

All life and being either belong to or are gifts from our Divine Father in heaven and all that He has given is terminated or pro- 232

longed by Him in accordance with His righteous plans or purposes. 

For even the Son of God Himself has said of Himself: "As the 

Father hath life in Himself so hath He given to the Son to have life in Himself. No man takes my life from me, I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it up again, this commandment have I received of my Father."

This opportunity of eternal life or of immortality is not an intuition of man, but the gift of our Divine Father, and in the day when all shall be resurrected for their reward of everlasting life or for their sentence of destruction, the righteous shall receive their body of immortality unto everlasting life; but the wicked and rebellious, the evil people who forget their Divine Creator, or go contrary to Him; also the evil spirits or bad angels who kept not their first estate will be all destroyed in the lake of fire, as it were, which God has prepared for the destruction of the devil and his angels. 

For in the "New Earth" into which the pure shall come, only the righteous will be made or permitted to dwell. 

Christ confined His worship to the one person of His Divine 

Father in heaven only; and directed His disciples to pray only to 

His Divine Father also.

If the Holy Apostles and their evangelists who wrote the gospel of Jesus Christ and their epistles would rise up from their graves, they would be swift witnesses against the idolatrous doctrine of the Trinity; and they would again confirm the sacred truth that "God is the Father, and the Father is God;" for how can that be scriptural or true which is not consentaneous to reason, or which depends on principles and opinions that sets all reason at defiance and mocks at every private knowledge of fact?

If these heresiarchs who teach the doctrine of the Trinity, of three Divine persons in the Deity must personify their ideas they should not call abstractions persons; and should be very careful to explain that these personified attributes are not to be understood as persons, as it is a confusion of the mind of people to call things by names the meanings of which they hold to be something altogether different from what the name or word usually signifies even though it carries a specious an dimposing air. 

When people use the term Holy Spirit, the designating title, appellative or name for the spirit of God, they should not speak of the spirit of a person as being another person in co-operation or conjunction with the person whose spirit it is, as it is the life, motive

and executive power of his person, and without it he cannot will, choose, design, purpose or execute anything, as there cannot be a personality apart from his spirit, for the body and the spirit constitute but one person and not two or more persons coequal, coessential and coeternal with each other as the antichrist doctrine of the Trinity teaches; for them to distinguish them as two persons is a misnomer, a falsity; it is a lie for them to make the spirit of God a person in itself in contradistinction from the person of our Divine Father whose spirit it is. 

The spirit of God or of God's person whose spirit the Holy Spirit is, is not to be spoken of as the person of the Holy Spirit, but the Holy Spirit of the person of our Divine Father whose spirit the Holy Spirit is, as we do not say the person of the spirit but the spirit of the person; and those who designate the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father as a separate and distinct person in conjunction or co-operation with our Divine Father are insensible of truth, and should be placed in a home for feeble-minded folk. 

It is quite impossible that any, of any intelligence whatever, could be so ignorant or stupid as not to be able to see or understand that the Holy Spirit is called the Holy Spirit because the spirit of God is holy; and that it is not a distinct person in itself or a person in addition to our Divine Father, as it is the spirit of our Divine Father's bodily existence. ;

Jesus Christ, who is the only begotten Son of His Divine Father, is more capable of having a full, complete, or adequate conception of His Divine Father, as He was with His Divine Father as a superangelical spirit called the "Word of God" before the worlds were created; and He therefore knows assuredly that God is His Father, and that His Father is His God and Father; and that all that His 

Divine Father does, He does by His spirit. Christ is not only the 

Son of our Divine Father in heaven because He was the product of His Divine Father's first creative act; but He is our Divine Father's 

Son also by His conception and parturition of the Virgin Mary who conceived Him through the executive power of our Divine Father's 

Holy Spirit.

The Holy Spirit of our Divine Father is the infinite, absolute and all comprehending power in all things human or Divine, as it is the motive or executive power of our Divine Father who is the God, Creator and Father of all things other than Himself without exception, as He only is uncreate or without derivation or dependency;

and He is absolute and independent in power and authority; and all things else are dependent upon Him for their being of existence, creation, and powers; and for all that they are, have, and do; and for this reason no one can operate independently of Him or successfully oppose Him, which they could do if there were other independent beings equal in power, glory and majesty.

In the day in which our Divine Father by the power of His omnipotent spirit created through His glorious Son, the superangelical Word all spirits, angels, persons and things they were good, pure, and innocent; but many of the angels as well as man fell from the purity of that good state in which God our heavenly Father created them. The bad angels were cast out of heaven unto the earth where

Lucifer, their leader, succeeded through the serpent in beguiling our first parents also into sin and rebellion against the holy commands of their Divine Creator, who said that they might eat if they wished, of all the fruit He had given to them except the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and of evil which they should not eat neither should they touch it, for in the day they ate thereof they would die. So our first parents being tempted by the devil fell into sin through disobedience and were driven from the garden of Eden with a curse of death resting heavily upon them that they should die within the millennial day in which they were created; but our 

Divine Father promised them that through their rearing of children He would provide them a savior who would crush the serpent's head by destroying the works of the devil by His own personal sacrifice, and He gave them a covenant by which they were to keep in remembrance the atonement of the promised seed of the woman by annual burnt offerings and sacrifices which were to typify the offering of the antitype, who through faith and devotion to Him by repentance and good works would remove the curse of death or mortality from them through the resurrection from the dead during his millennial reign upon the earth. 

Those who strive through faith and well-doing to keep themselves penitent toward God and charitable toward their fellow-men by faith in the Messiah or anointed of God, Christ Jesus will be raised immortal unto eternal through the resurrection from the dead at the appearing of Jesus Christ when He comes to take up His reign upon the earth at the close of this gospel age; but those who have done wickedly and repented not of their sins shall be raised unto the judgment of destruction, and have their part with Satan and

all the wicked angels in the lake of fire of annihilation called the "Second Death."
