Jesus Christ recognized no Divine power or authority but that of His Divine Father in heaven who is the source of all power, being and authority; and the historical student in Christian history will find that the Christians during the first two centuries of Christianity recognized Jesus Christ, His doctrine and His works as all coming from His Divine Father in heaven; and as Christ's Divine Father teaching and working through Him by His Holy Spirit; for Christ had told them that the doctrine He taught was not His but the Father's who sent Him; and that the works and miracles performed through Him were not His works; but the Divine Father was doing or performing these works through Him; and that of Himself He could do nothing. 

Christ ardently prayed that His disciples would be one in doctrine, love and fellowship as He and His father are one, in that, He always did the will of His Father; and thus we find that there was but one universal Church polity, and that these Christians universally knew themselves to be one in Christ in doctrine, love and fellowship although each Church was an independent organization which unanimously adopted the Holy Scriptures for their guidance into a true democracy of one organic union. 

The bishop or presbyter of the diocese had the right to excommunicate anyone guilty of moral depravity such as committing immoral acts or teaching doctrines contrary to the teachings of Christ and His apostles; and no excommunicated person was permitted in the communion of the faithful throughout the realm of the Church without the consent of the bishop or presbyter that excommunicated him.

Had the Jews understood that Jesus Christ was the promised 

Messiah they would not have killed God's glorious Son; and had they understood that it was He through whom God created all angels, worlds, principalities and powers; and who gave the law to 

Moses and talked with him, as it were, face to face they would not have rejected Him. But the Jews were not aware that Jesus Christ before His incarnation was He whom the patriarchs, Moses, and the prophets met with betimes in their journeyings and who led them for forty years in the wilderness; for it was through Him that God gave the law to Moses and protected them as a nation until the Word should come as the Messiah. The Jews did not understand

that the representative of God in the Old Covenant was now speaking to them face to face in the person of Jesus Christ in the New Covenant, and that God would through Him give to them the New Testament or covenant in His blood as an everlasting sign of God's love and propitiation.

It was the "Word of God," God's first-born Son of all creation through whom God created all worlds, principalities, and powers, through whom God gave to Moses the "Doctrines and Covenants," who became incarnate through His Divine Father's Holy Spirit, so that the Word was the representative of God, through whom God created the worlds, and through whom Israel received the doctrines. and the covenants, and the promises, and He is the very same representative or agent who fulfilled them unto Israel; for He who 

God's pure law fulfilled is Jesus the incarnate Word; and Christ whose truth with His blood was sealed is God's own glorious incarnate Word and first-born of all creation. 

What a tremendous struggle and wrestling with Israel it has been for our Divine Father to preserve Israel from self-destruction, for they would even fight against God; but God makes the wrath of man to praise Him; for through their rebellion the law which God had foreordained for their salvation was fulfilled in their crucifying the incarnate Word, Jesus Christ, God's only begotten Son. 

The world has ever fought against God and His regulations. What we need in religion is a Church that will meet our present religious needs, and that is found in a great measure in the Christian or Congregational form of government, as our religious needs are always and only to be found in a Church which is broad enough to accept all the followers of Jesus Christ upon their confession of faith in Him as the Son of God which is a Divine prerequisite for baptism in His name and entrance nto the Church. This was the confession of faith upon which Christ said: "I will build my Church and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it."

It is a great sin against God and a crime against our fellow-men for any Church professing to be Christian that will debar from entering into communion with Jesus Christ through it, more than twothirds of the Christian people who believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, but who are not of their persuasion. There are literally millions of Christians left without a Church home because the local Church in the community in which they live is so narrow and selfish as not to minister to their needs because their conviction of con-

science is different from the tenets or creed of the local Church. 

These narrow, selfish, impish ministers would rather by far see their Christian brother perish for whom Christ died to save rather than to minister to the needs of those whose tenets of Christian faith differ from theirs.

There will, undoubtedly, be a greater percentage of Church ministers in hell than there will be of any other class of professed Christians, because they will compass land and sea to make one proselyte to their little, narrow, selfish sectarian tenets of religion, and when he has become their finished product he is seven-fold more the child of hell, because more selfish, narrow, and egotistical, than he was before. The greatest obstacle to a complete Christian unity is the attitude of the ministry of the Church itself, as they absolutely refuse to do their Christian duty in bringing the people into unity and fellowship; for they seek to make or keep divisions through their divisive Trinitarian falsities rather than seek the consolidation of the Church by teaching the truths of the gospel of Jesus Christ. 

The attitude of many of the Protestant Churches have savoured very much like the encyclical letter of Pope Pius the eleventh which in effect said: "Let those who sincerely seek unity come unto me. 

Unity and peace will be found only in the acceptance of the authority of the vicegerent of God and vicar of Jesus Christ." But the world at large is not ready to accept the enforced falsities, the arrogance and assumptions of the Roman Catholic Church which assumes infallibility and the right to enforce her mandates over the hearts and consciences of people with penal punishments which not even God Himself ever did. The enforced doctrine of the Trinity, the personification of the spirit of God, hypostatical union or homoosian of the Son of God with the Deity, limbo, purgatory, transubstantiation, indulgences, masses for the dead, auricular confession, worshipping of angels and of saints, and many other such things too numerous to mention are all antichrist doctrines. Can there be any salvation in any such Church or denomination as such, when salvation is by the grace of repentance through faith in Jesus Christ as God's Son and mediator? The Church is simply an external organization where Christians may assemble together for fellowship and communion with each other; and all our rules and regulation if truly Christian, are only means of grace when they beget in us love, sympathy, kindness, goodness, charity, faith and brotherly helpfulness.

There have been thousands of Christian martyrs for God and truth because of the persecuting spirit of the apostate Church and we are not wholly exempt from such a wicked, hellish, brutish, villainous, impish, satanic, and malicious spirit yet; but we are making progress toward a larger, nobler, purer and more Christian fellowship.

The Holy Spirit of our Divine Father was the perceptor or giver of immediate knowledge to the prophets, to Jesus Christ, to the apostles, and to the apostolic evangelists of the Christians in the establishment of the Church and it revealed to them the things which were past, the things that were present and the things which were to come; and whatsoever they said or did in their Christian ministrations the Holy Spirit was the approver, executor and doer of it, as it is only and always the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven which doeth all Divine works both immediately or mediately; and those who refuse or disobey by neglecting to observe the things revealed by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven through the prophets, through Jesus Christ, or through their Divinely appointed evangelists will be cut off from the congregation of the righteous in the day of judgment to perish everlastingly. 

As those who do not give heed to obey the things which the spirit of God speaks and directs to be done through our Divine Father's representatives deprive themselves of every material assistance in obtaining everlasting salvation.

Christ is the legate of our Divine Father, and His apostles are the Divinely chosen witnesses in all that Christ taught and did; and they are to teach this gospel to all the nations; and only do and say those things that the Holy Spirit directed to be done or said. 

All who oppose the New Testament teaching and practice by substituting the doctrines and practices of the man of sin, the son of perdition and Antichrist of three Divine coequal, coessential, coeternal persons for our Divine Father in heaven such as the Roman Catholic Church and most Protestant Churches do, are traitors and criminals, villains and heresiarchs to the commonwealth of God and of His Christ. 

Those who form creeds and disciplines write and speak blasphemy against God; for they boldly assert that God's word is either too much or too little as a guide, and is therefore not sufficient for the rule of faith and practice of Christians. 

When men adopt their own creeds or disciplines as their rule of

faith and practice they are rejecting the only holy and Divinely inspired standard which points out the only way of salvation, as there is no salvation whatever in the observance of any other; and will any man be bold enough to affirm that God has given him the Divine commission to write out the Christian's creed or a creed for the Christians?

Christ taught that His Divine Father constitutes the absolute and only individuality and the only personality in the Deity, as His Father is both God and Father by reason of His creation of all other persons and things without exception; as all things else are but persons and things of His Divine Father's creation He is the God and Father of all things. Our Divine Father is the only uncreate; and the only absolute and independent person; and as such 

He is the monarch or daddy of all time, wisdom, power, might, strength and knowledge without equals or associates; and He is the only person in the godship of the Deity as He is uncompounded and indivisible in the unity of His person and powers. 

It is wholly absurd and inconsistent with scripture, science and reason that our Divine Father should be united with His Son Jesus Christ in person, in power, glory and eternity when our Divine Father is the Creator, God and Father of Christ's person; and it is worse than foolish to say that God created anything either of matter or of spirit out of His own person which also is incompatible with creation as neither His being nor spirit had a beginning or creation; but it is quite consistent to say that our Divine Father created all things else out of His power to produce according to His will and pleasure. God willed what He wished to produce, He commanded and it was made, and He said, "so let it be" and it stood fast. Everything save our Divine Father in heaven had a creation and a beginning of which our Divine Father's glorious Son, the Word, was the beginning of His Divine Father's creation, the first created of God's creatures.

Christ teaches us that God is a spirit-being personality which has neither flesh nor bones; and everything our Divine Father created is external to Himself and no part of Him. God is a simple indivisible, immutable unit in His person, spirit and power; and He is the only infinite, absolute and independent being and comprehends in Himself, of Himself and by Himself all power and authority in the one unit of His person without division, parts, or persons; and all extraneous persons, beings, spirits and things are the objects of

our Divine' Father's creation. Our Divine Father could not be a 

God of infinite power, knowledge, and authority if He had to compromise His person, power, and authority with two or more other Divine persons coequal, coessential, and coeternal, and equal in power, glory and honor with that of Himself, as infinity must be that which is absolute and independent. 

All power in heaven, in earth, and everywhere belongs to our Divine Father in heaven, and it is generated, bestowed, conferred, given or imparted to others as our Divine Father so wills to do. 

Even the power exercised by bad men and bad angels; and all who oppose our Divine Father do so through the power, goodness, and clemency of our Divine Father who is patient and long-suffering toward His erring creatures; but He has appointed a day in which all the impenitent will be destroyed at the day of judgment, and all power and being will be taken from them. 

It is this unwarranted assumption and abuse of power by such men as Victor the First, bishop of the See of Rome which caused the contention and apostasy in the Church; for, when Victor assumed to himself the authority to change the time, rules, and regulations for the observance of the Lord's Supper at the time of the slaying of the paschal lamb which was celebrated by the Israelites and also by the Christians of the early centuries of the Christian era on the fourteenth day of the month Nisan on whatever day of the week it chanced to fall as it was on this day of the month that our Lord instituted the supper of His passion; but Victor chose to change it to Sunday nearest the fourteenth of Nisan as the day on which the passion called Easter should be celebrated; and he set up a reign of persecution against those who opposed his will, and excommunicated many of the Christians, and deprived them of their rights by pronouncing them unworthy of the name of Christian brethren because they opposed his will in trying to change the times and the seasons instituted by our Lord. Victor opposed those whose sentiments with regard to Christianity were strictly correct and against whom he himself could find no fault or matter of offense that could be alleged against them save the keeping of these external rights and observances which he wished to change. In very much the same way he commanded the faithful disciples of Jesus Christ should no more baptize their converts in the "Name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins," according to the apostolic teaching and customs; but that they should hereafter be baptized in the

name of a Trinity of three Divine persons under compulsion of excommunication and his autocratic will finally gained the ascendency over the Church until about the seventh century the bishop of Rome held full sway over the Church. 

Shame, everlasting shame! that these ecclesiastical heresiarchs can find nothing but their own corruptions of Christianity to vex, excommunicate, disfranchise, persecute, confiscate goods, banish or put to death the saints of God and of His Christ in order to enforce their corruptions and will upon the people. Thus did Victor, the 

Roman prelate and those who followed him in office excommunicate the Christian world from communion and fellowship with the Church, and persecute unto death all who rebelled against him; but the Christian world was loth to follow the wicked presumptions of the Roman bishop in his corruptions of Christianity; and he rather excommunicated himself from all that is Christian and apostolic and from God likewise, even though he claims to be the vicegerent of God, and the vicar of Jesus Christ. 

Jesus Christ is distinctively the only religious teacher and guide proffered by our Divine Father in heaven to mankind, and those who refuse to hear Him and to follow His instructions shall be cut off from life and immortality; and since our Divine Father only knows, by the omniscience of His all-powerful spirit, the love, affection and devotion of each one personally; and comprehends from eternity our every thought, word and deed, and intentions; He only is capable of being our law-giver and judge; so, if we are not unduly narrow, selfish, covetous, vain, and egotistical, He will be able to use us in some small way against these destructive walls of partition and division which corrupt the Christian world into petty tribes, clans, and cliques called sects or denominations. 

We here repeat what we have reiterated before in various ways; that all these questions upon which the present states of Christiandom is divided into many sects, are questions and opinions enforced upon the world by the Antichrist doctrine of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person called the Trinity in unity and the unity in Trinity or three in one and one in three, doctrine which confounds, and perplexes the mind of every individual as unthinkable, absurd, inconsistent and contradictory to all who will honestly investigate it; and if accepted at all, must be on blind assent, as there is nothing in nature, science, or reason to corroborate it or demonstrate its

truthfulness; but on the contrary all these prove it to be false by every conceivable illustration or example.

Our Divine Father in heaven never had upon this earth a vicegerent nor Jesus a vicar to exercise their offices or authority; but many of our ministers are so zealous of their official dignity and the emoluments of their office that they are willing to hazzard most anything to keep them, yet there are but few who are brazen enough to confess that they believe that salvation is attainable only by believing in their little wishy-washy, namby-pamby creed, sect or denomination; but nevertheless they are ever looking for the loaves and fishes, and care but little whether Christians who will not renounce their faith to join them, perish for the want of the bread of life; and so long as they refuse to join unto them they will not minister to their needs or act the part of the "Good Samaritan” toward them. 

Oh, the foolishness, the cussedness, and the villainy of our Trinitarian friends trying to divide up the Godhead of our Divine Father in heaven into three Divine persons as if the person, nature, essence, substance, spirit, power, wisdom, glory, honor, eternity, infinity, independence, uncreatedness could be divided coequally, coessentially, coeternally, and equally divided in power, glory and majesty so as to communicate a Divine personality to His spirit and to His Son Jesus Christ making two more Divine persons exactly like Himself with neither before nor after the others; but God's person and God's spirit is not divisible, as a unit cannot be divided into two other units making three units in one and one unit in three, making three infinite, absolute and independent units in one person; and it is criminal to teach such a doctrine. 

Now, let the learned men who are solicitous about the protection and dignity of the Antichrist, the vicegerent of God and vicar of Jesus Christ, the Pope of Rome and his accursed Trinitarian doctrine which is a curse to man and a blasphemy against our Divine

Creator our Father in heaven, choose which side of this alternative they please, and look once more into the gospel, prophecies and epistles of the New Testament scriptures and they will find that the times and seasons clearly reveal that the Antichrist, the man of sin, and son of perdition has the so-called Christian world in subjection to his doctrines and authority, both Catholic and Protestants alike; but what credit, honor or glory of a Divine character people can hope to reap as a reward for following the antichrist doctrine of

three Divine persons in one only Satan will realize, for it is contrary to Divine revelations and every private knowledge of fact? 

By universal consent, it is an established rule of fact that light controls and illuminates darkness; that is, the obscure and ambiguous passages of scripture are to be elucidated and explained by the passages which are clear and perspicuous, for it would be preposterous to argue and measure the important pashages in which S there is no obscurity or ambiguity by other passages which are enigmatical or admit of many explanations. Now if this rule be applied in the present case as undoubtedly it should be, I think all who are capable of discerning truth will agree that the many passages of scripture declaring Jesus Christ to be the Son of God, and that God is His Father will be overwhelmingly founded by so many infallible proofs that no other interpretation foreign to it can possibly be allowed or be able to abide the truth; for according to the rules of correct reasoning, nature, science, and intellect will not concur or corroborate the proposition that the Son of God is coequal, coessential and coeternal; equal in power, glory and majesty with His heavenly Father, His God and Creator; and therefore the 

Trinitarian doctrine is absolutely and unqualifiedly false to all known truth which is legion in its condemnation as a falsity; and cannot even be conceived to be true. 

The Divine Revelations of the holy scriptures stand upon the impregnable rock of truth revealed and confirmed by the omnipotent power of God's Holy Spirit and by His Son Jesus Christ through the Holy spirit and when they both affirm that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, and not the Deity or a part of Him, and confirmed by many signs miracles and circumstances that He is the Son of God which is reasonable, consistent, natural, and demonstratively corroborated by many infallible proofs of supernatural acts which have no parallel and is unique in itself. Why, then, does the world wickedly contradict and gainsay the Divine record by following the antichrist doctrine of three Divine coequal persons in the Deity of which neither could be Father or Son.

It is a great pleasure to know the opinions, the practices and the usages respecting the offices, doctrines and prerogatives exercised by the independent congregations such as that held by the Congregational Christian form of government in an age supposed to be distinguished above all others for sanctity and the cultivation of true religion such as the apostles of Jesus Christ exercised; and to see

from what beginnings these episcopal dogmas, creeds and mandates which originated later and are still held by many to be Divine because of the unbroken succession of bishops however profane, wicked, and corrupt they might have been personally or deviated from the doctrines of Christianity and the practices of the apostles of Jesus Christ. Which succession is brought forward to interrupt the peace of the Christian world as of Divine succession in office which has no foundation whatever since the world no longer follows the teachings and practices of Jesus Christ and His apostles; but the antichrist doctrine of three Divine persons instead of the one Divine person as taught by Jesus Christ and His apostles. 

Oh the sin, the shame and the blasphemy these heresiarchs heap upon their own unhallowed and unsanctified heads who rise up and claim that they are the Divinely appointed representatives of Jesus Christ when many of them have confessed that their morals were the most wicked, sinful and degraded of men that ever trod the earth. Thus have the Roman pontiffs and those who follow them not only abandoned the doctrine and practices of Jesus Christ and His apostles, but in many cases sank to the lowest depths of moral depravity.

When the Roman pontiff who claims to be the vicegerent of God and the vicar of Jesus Christ speaks ex cathedra, he professes no limitation, but an infallibility far beyond that of Jesus Christ and His apostles, who claimed no power of themselves, but said and did only as the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven moved them, as all Divine prerogatives are executed by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father; but the Pope of Rome has dared try to change and enforce upon the people his changed times, seasons, and sacraments in a way different from those established by our Divine Father through His Son Jesus Christ, in that he substituted for our Divine Father, who is the true and only living God, three coequal and coeternal persons called the Trinity; and for baptism "In the name of the Lord Jesus Christ for the remission of sins" and for membership in the Church, he substituted his three Divine persons in whose names, at the commencement of the fourth century, all holding communion or fellowship with the Roman See must henceforth acknowledge as the only valid baptism under pain of excommunication, disfranchisement of offices, and persecuted as a heretic. 

It is not a thing to be held in wonder and amazement that the Church under such circumstances departed far from the apostilc

doctrine, customs, and practices when the Church became controlled by one man's whims, acting as the vicegerent of God and vicar of Jesus Christ in absolute disregard of either of them that all kinds of false doctrines such as three Divine persons in one Divine triune person, the hypostatical union and homoousian of Jesus Christ, transubstantiation, infallibility, auricular confession, purgatory, limbo, concubinage for the priesthood, ad infinitum other abuses too numerous to mention should creep into the Church. The bishop of 

Rome was exalted to the vicegerent of God, and vicar of Jesus 

Christ and the Virgin Mary to be the "Mother of God."

We have but little faith in this eclectic philosophy which claims that truth is to be gathered from all sects; but of this one thing we are confident, that Jesus Christ is, was, and ever shall remain the Son of God in whatever stage of existence He passed through from His creation, and incarnation to His glorification. 

All our moral and spiritual powers depend upon our volition of choice, past, present and future and are all governed by them, as all the distinctions and differences among men and angels; and the variations in the Divine decrees and proceedings of God with all sentient beings are governed according to their volition, and faith. 

For this reason we honor, bless, and sanctify in our hearts our Divine Father in heaven just in proportion as we accept and believe in His Son the incarnate Word Jesus Christ whom He baptized with His Holy Spirit and with power and sent Him into the world to be the propitiation for our sins that we, through faith in Him, should not perish but have everlasting life.

We have striven at all times to search out and demonstrate the grounds or reasons for the doctrines Divinely revealed in the scriptures; and determined the principles of the true relations of God to 

Jesus Christ and to all things, as all Divine things are performed only and always by the power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine 

Father in heaven; and without our Divine Father's Holy Spirit nothing can either be created or operate, as it is an absolute and independent power over all things without exception, as it is the omnipotent spirit of our Divine Father.

All power and authority without exception proceeds from our Divine Father through His spirit, as it was the operating or producing power in all creation, prophecy, miracles, and Divine healing without exception; as there is no power which is not comprehended in it and controlled by it. The power and authority of the Holy

1 Spirit of our Divine Father proceeds from our Divine Father to accomplish His plans and purposes; and all delegated power recedes by the Holy Spirit back to Him when its purposes are accomplished. 

In the strictest sense of the word, the Holy Spirit being the spirit of the person of our Divine Father in heaven, and its presence, power and authority ubiquitous or universally omnipresent it cannot proceed, or recede to any place; but the special gifts, powers, graces, privileges, agencies or activities operating in and through anything whether person, spirit, being or angel may be expressed as induements or baptisms of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven, as the Holy Spirit belongs exclusively to His person, for God is spirit, wisdom, love, might and power in the plentitude of His infinity; but the local induements of our Divine Father's spirit to men or angels in a specific sense may proceed to them and from them, as it were, at the pleasure of our Divine Father in keeping with the good faith of the person upon whom it is bestowed. Thus, the power of the Holy Spirit may be concentrated upon local objects or persons, such as Moses' "Brazen Serpent," "Ark of the 

Covenant," "Shekinah," "Moses' Rod," "Aaron's Rod," "Aprons and napkins" from Saint Paul's hands, and from angels, prophets and apostles; but this power is not resident in these things; but in the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father's person only, and subject always and only to Him, though unlimited in power, wisdom, understanding and duration.

There are rational truths as well as revealed or heavenly truths; and our Divine Father has endowed us with human minds and spirits by which to discern and deliberate upon many things which are not clearly revealed by Divine revelation; but that the Holy Spirit is the spirit of the person of our Divine Father in heaven is a Divine truth many times revealed in the holy scriptures. 

There are some philosophers in this modern world who teach that each and every rational being is possessed of a spark of the Divine and that the mind, spirit, will, body, essence, nature, substance and all the other attributes of God are divided among the myriads of sentient beings of the universe, so that all people individually are possessed of a small portion of our Divine Father; but the Divine revelations of the holy scriptures and pure common sense condemn such heretical notions; for, if this were so, every one could correctly interpret the times and the seasons which our Divine Father has kept in His own power; but the world has seen but few people that

could, even in a small way, with the aid of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father foreknow of these extraordinary happenings which are altogether dependent upon the will of our heavenly Father; and only those who have this special enduement of the Holy Spirit's wisdom and understanding revealed to them have the power of discernment or foreknowledge of these things before they come to pass. 

Our Divine Father only is self-conscious of all things through the infinite omniscient power of His Holy Spirit which controls and brings to pass everything according to His will; and the prophets, Jesus Christ, the apostles or any other creature cannot foreknow these things, only in so far as the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father is pleased to reveal these things to them. 

There are certain passages of scripture which have an arcane, hidden, mystical or spiritual sense, for "the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life," such as those words of Jesus when He said: “Unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood ye have no life in you." You must spiritually incorporate in your person, mental, spiritual and moral all that Jesus says to do in order to have the life more abundant.

The Bible speaks of the law, but the law had a shadow of things. to come; such was the law of the Passover, and the law of circumcision; but when it says, "Thou shalt not covet, steal, kill, commit adultery" and such like, you will not find the title of Law prefixed, for these are commandments, and are not made void or filled full among the events of the gospel.

Christ redeemed us from the curse of the Law which proclaimed the shadow of things to come; but He did not redeem us from trying to keep the ten commandments as the commandments relate to an anagogical, celestial, or spiritual sense which is binding upon all in every age, as no one could be virtuous, pure or rational that made no attempt to keep them; and of all the rational human souls that have been on this earth, we have no record where anyone obeyed more loyally, sacredly and earnestly the ten commandments than Jesus Christ who sealed His obedience with His blood.

The mere fact that Christ in His antemundane state existed as a superangelical spirit personage, as the unincarnate Word from the beginning of His Divine Father's creation, chose to become incarnated through the all-powerful spirit of His Divine Father for the purpose of receiving a human, rational sentient soul like that which we possess; and was tempted in all points like we are without

yielding to the enticements and temptations to sin that He might have the experiences and trials to which man is subject through the appetites and passions of the flesh that He might know how He ought to sympathize with the feelings of our infirmities; and be able to realize more fully the high content of God's love and mercy; and the many human weaknesses to which man is subject and his power to overcome them. But that is not all that the incarnation of 

God's glorious Son the Word teaches us, for in it all we see the mighty power of our Divine Father to not only clothe a superangelical spirit person with human flesh by incarnation, but also to change human flesh into an immortal person through the resurrecting of Christ from the dead; which shows us that He is able by the power of His Holy Spirit to translate the living righteous and resurrect the righteous who have fallen asleep in death, to glorified immortal beings.

The incarnation of His glorious Son, the superangelical Word, who became Jesus Christ crucified, dead and buried, whom our Divine Father raised from death is impregnable proof that God is able to revoke the sentence of death, and change our mortal bodies into immortal forms by the power of His Holy Spirit as easily as He created the human soul of His only begotten Son, and as easily raised Him immortal from the grave.

It was necessary for Christ's soul to be human in order that He might offer it in full payment as a vicarious atonement due to our sin because of Adam's transgression. Christ, by making His soul a sacrifice for our sins, we by faith in Him as God's Son and mediator, are restored either through the resurrection from the dead or translation into immortal bodies to life eternal; but the faithless and unbelieving, God will destroy in the day of judgment. 

By Jesus Christ sacrificing His own flesh and blood in man's behalf, the justice of God is satisfied by substitution in behalf of all who through faith and good works will repent of their sins and turn to God, and those who do not will perish everlastingly. So those who would be saved must accept the vicarious atonement of the incarnate Word Jesus Christ who appeared on earth in a human. body that He might give it in sacrifice to make an atonement for our sins; for by the grace of God through repentance and faith in 

His Son Jesus Christ this great salvation is sent; and those who do despite toward God's plan of redemption cannot be saved. 

Jesus calls Himself God's only begotten Son because He is the

only immediately created creature of His Divine Father's creation; and also the only person conceived and generated by the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father, as all things else were created by the power of His Divine Father's Holy Spirit through Christ as the unincarnate Word during His antemundane state of existence; and thus, Christ is the agent or medium between God and all things else of creation.

Some scripture language is used to accommodate itself to the thinking of the truth in the way of parables to illustrate doctrine, and whenever it speaks in either the Old or New Testament of God's appearance, it is to be understood that it is the Divine messenger or agent of our Divine Father speaking in His name and by His authority. Thus did the Word, the Son of God, the angel 

Gabriel, Michael the archangel, and various others in both Old and New Testament times who spoke in God's name and operated by His power and authority; for Christ, and all other messengers of 

God knew not the things of God save as the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father revealed the things of God unto them, as there is not anything which knows the things of God save the spirit of God only; but there are some who know some things of God through the revelations made by the spirit of God unto them in a limited way, save in the case of Jesus Christ, to whom our Divine Father "reveals all that He Himself doeth, and shows Him all things that He does." 

Our Divine Father, who as Creator of all things other than Himself, who alone is uncreate and eternal, is incapable of being added to or divided in His person, spirit and powers; but all things else being create and produced by Him, we are children of the Divine Father, but not Divine children or God children, as such terms as Divine children or God children are pure nonsense, as it is absolutely inconsistent with the nature of God to produce children by procreation or generation as of the same essence of person and substance with Himself who is uncreate and independent in His being, person and powers; and for this reason our Divine Father must forever remain a distinct entity, unit or person from that of all others without change forever.

We are children of our Divine Father by reason of our creation by Him, as to the flesh, or as man; and may, under certain conditions, become children spiritually or as immortal persons by adoption; but neither we nor any other creature of our Divine Father can ever become a part or parcel of our Divine Father's person for

that which is created can never become uncreate or independent of its maker.

It is perfectly proper to say that the incarnate Word Jesus Christ is the Son of God, the Son of the Father, the Son of the Divine, the Son of the Deity, the Son of the Eternal; but it is wrong to say that He is the Divine Son, the God Son, the Eternal Son, the Son Deity or God the Son, as such expressions are pure nonsense or falsities and contrary to fact to speak of Christ as being one of a family of Deities.

Some commentators, who perhaps know languages, but do not know truth, intend to say by their explanations and comments that God as a Divine person, is not the Father, nor the Son nor the Holy Ghost, nor is He a distinct person from any of these three, so-called Divine persons; but all three of these Divine persons taken conjointly is He. What nonsense is this? It needs no comment to show its hideousness or its falsities; but such is the doctrine of the Trinity of three Divine persons in the one person of the Deity. If the three 

Divine persons when taken singly is not God; but that one Divine triune person of which the three Divine persons conjointly compose is He, are there not four Divine persons in the Deity? The three 

Divine persons and the one Divine person which the three Divine persons conjointly constitute make four Divine persons of which none is God without the others! The absurd idea that the person of our Divine Father in heaven is distributed into three Divine persons, divisions or installments which must be taken conjointly and cooperatively before either of them can act, is below the thought of the crudest savages. Was there ever anything so false, absurd, inconsistent, contradictory, supercilious and overbearing on one's intelligence as this doctrine of three Divine persons in one? 

That infinite, immutable, unchangeable being whom we call our Divine Father cannot be conjoined to other persons nor distributed into various persons; for He is uncreate, absolute and independent; and it is He only who creates, upholds and governs all things by the infinite power of His Holy Spirit.

The Divine nature, essence, substance, or spirit of our Divine Father's person is impassible to others, as person or personality cannot be transferred to other persons when it is infinite, absolute, independent and uncreate, so that others can partake of the nature, essence, substance, powers, and attributes of His person which is

uncreate, unbegotten, and not produced in any way; as all else is begotten and exterior to Him, as objects of creation. 

God is in Christ, in the prophets, in Christ's apostles, in the saints, and we trust in us also by the power of His Holy Spirit; for if the Spirit of our Divine Father dwell not in us we are none of His. Christ was in God and God was in Christ in similarity or likeness of spirit or communion by affinity of spirits and not in person, when Christ was in spirit wholly consecrated and devoted to His Divine Father and His works; and only in this sense can the uncreate our Divine Father and His creature be said to be one. 

Our Divine Father, and His Son Jesus Christ are one in harmony of spirit and of purpose during the time in which Christ remains in filial obedience and devotion to His Divine Father; but, if it were possible, that there should ever come a time when Christ should fail to be the obedient Son in whom His Father is well-pleased through rebellion against the authority of His Divine Father, there would be no unity of contact or agreement or oneness left in any respect as two or more cannot be one in diversity, but in agreement only. 

Just how the Trinitarians figure their God the Father, God the Son and God the Holy Ghost who are interdependent upon the Divine triune person which the three Divine persons who conjointly compose the one Divine triune person who is two-thirds greater than anyone of the three Divine persons of which He is composed, cannot operate of Himself, is wanting of an explanation; unless you admit that neither can be God without the other two, as they are all dependent upon each other of which neither is infinite, absolute or independent in Himself, but all independent of each other, and hence three distinct unrelated coequal Gods, which is an antichristian lie; for three dependent Divine persons, cannot compose conjointly an uncreate independent one with neither before nor after the others, and coequal, coessential, and coeternal with each other according to your "Athenation creed?"

For anyone to say that the doctrine of the Trinity or triune God is scriptural or scientific or true, we deem that Satan and all the imps of hell are incapable of telling a greater falsehood; and those people who call themselves Christians and will thus dwarf and abuse the minds of their children with such infernal, satanic, hellish, villainous nonsense are villains and criminals, for it is the worst crime that they can possibly curse not only the minds but the souls of their children; for this is the doctrine of the Antichrist, "the man

of sin, and son of perdition," the Pope of Rome who calls himself the "Vicegerent of God and vicar of Jesus Christ." 

For God's sake, for Christ's sake, for your country's sake, for the 

Church's sake, for your home's sake, and for the sake of your dear, sweet, heaven-kissed babes, be done with this doctrine of the Trinity which is a snare of Satan and a delusion of hell; and stand up for truth and God's righteousness; and let this doctrine of the Trinity with its millions of inquisitors and murderers, with their millions upon millions of martyrs, be hurled into darkness and oblivion before it becomes the destruction of your soul, and the souls of your children! 

When our Divine Father purposes or chooses to do anything His spirit wills and executes all Divine things; for God in person is ever upon His throne of power and authority over all things; but His 

Holy Spirit operates throughout all time and place at will and may operate specifically or locally in a countless number of places at one and the same time because the presence, power, and authority of our Divine Father's spirit are present everywhere at one and the same time as the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father is ubiquitous or omnipresent in all time and place.

What a very foolish notion some people have of trying to make Divine persons of the spirit of God and of His Son Jesus Christ; and then in some way or other by the use of nails, hinges, screws, buckles or by the cobwebs in their brains fasten their extra two

Divine persons onto the Godhead of our Divine Father; and call them a Trinity of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person. 

If our Divine Father alone is not God then He also is a dependent, finite being or person, and is not able of Himself to do anything; but there is a feeling contrary to nearly all the creeds of 

Christiandom which proclaim He is but one Divine person of three Divine coequal, coessential and coeternal persons, that our Divine Father in heaven is the only living and true God notwithstanding the many creeds proclaiming the doctrine of a Trinity of Divine persons, as Protestants especially nearly always address their petitions to Him in the name of His Son Jesus Christ. 

If it were not for the ministers and creeds keeping these Trinitarian falsities continually before the people, all people who believe in God would readily accept our Divine Father in heaven as the one true and only living God, who is called Creator and Father by reason of the dependency of all things upon Him for their being and powers, and all that they are and have.

CHAPTER XIII 

The terms Creator and Father belong to the same person and that person is generally conceded to be life-giver, which means Creator or Father and as such He is said to be God or called God because He is the life-giver, creator or Father of all things; and He is therefore the God, or Divine person from which all other persons, spirits, beings and things originated. The Father only has independent activity, power and authority, as all things else are dependent upon our Divine Father for their existence and powers, and for all that they are, have and do, as none but our heavenly Father possesses anything of Himself, as He possesses everything and all things of Himself; for He only is uncreate, absolute and independent in His person and powers without an originator or creator.

Every human soul, is a sentient, rational soul, and dependent upon God for its existence, power and actions whether good or bad; but which is circumscribed in every way as being no part of God; and so it is with the spirit world likewise of every name and order, save the spirit of God only, is dependent upon God our heavenly Father for their existence and power of action including even His glorious Son, the incarnate Word Jesus Christ.

God's glorious Son, the incarnate Word Jesus Christ in whatever stage of development, whether in His antemundane or mundane state, has no more connection whatever with His Divine Father's person, nature, essence, substance, attributes or powers than any other creature of our Divine Father's creation; save in that there is perhaps a closer affinity of the spirit of Jesus Christ with that of His Divine Father's Holy Spirit than that existing between the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father and the spirit of any other person, as they all alike are dependent upon our Divine Father's Holy Spirit's power for their being and powers; and for all that they are and have.

The incarnate Word Jesus Christ who in His antemundane or preexistent state through whom our Divine Father created all angels, worlds, principalities and powers; and also the agent through whom 254

our Divine Father held communion with Adam, the patriarchs, Moses and the prophets face to face as the God of Israel; for He was the Divinely appointed agent of Jehovah, and spoke in His name and authority; for, said Jesus: "No man has seen God at any time, the only begotten Son who is in the bosom of the Father, He has declared Him."

Jesus Christ, without the power of the Holy Spirit of His Divine Creator was like, or in same category with other men as He had no community spirit being, person, nature, power or authority with that of His Divine Father; for He is dependent in every respect the same as anyone else, upon His Divine Father for all that He is, has, and does. It was the Holy Spirit of Christ's Divine Father which did the 

Divine works through Jesus Christ and enabled Him to perform the Holy offices of a heavenly ambassador, for Christ had no power to do a Divine act of Himself, and apart from the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father no Divine act can be performed, as it is the executive power and only means by which our Divine Father performs His works both immediately and mediately.

As the power and authority of our Divine Father only is infinite, absolute, and independent, our Divine Father does not, and cannot dispense with the smallest infinitesimal particle of His person, spirit, power and authority any more than He can dispose of His personal existence; for all the power He confers on others is always and only 

His very own, or He could not confer it, and none can do a Divine act but He, through His Holy Spirit whether personally or through 

His agents.

Much was conceded in the first centuries of the Christians to the ignorance, weaknesses and prejudices of the Jews from which Christ the author of Christianity came, and for this reason we have deemed it necessary to approach the Fatherhood of God from every conceivable angle to demonstrate the correctness of the Israelitish view of God subsisting in one person although they ignorantly worshipped God's glorious Son the Word for our Divine Father Jehovah, because the Word instructed them, protected them, led them for forty years in the wilderness, and gave them the law, and finally settled them in the land of Canaan.

The monotheism of the Israelitish people was absolutely correct, for "The Lord our God is one Father only, even though the Israelitish people mistook our Divine Father's glorious Son and agent, the Word, for their Divine Creator and Father, because it was through

the Word, God's glorious Son that they received the Law, the commandments, and the doctrine and covenants of the Old Testament; and by the incarnation of the Word the New Covenant through Him also was given to Israel.

We are all aware that the Divine character of Christianity can be proved only from the prophecies; and from the writings of Christ's apostles and evangelists; but yet, we can call to our aid the sciences in corroboration and confirmation of the correctness of that complete inspiration to which the prophets and the apostles testify; for no truth of inspiration can annul a scientific truism, for they are the same. But science can add weight to the consistency and plausibility of inspirational truth by a scientific illustration or demonstration of its consistency; for there is no such thing as inspirational truth which is not scientifically true, or it is not inspirational truth or it is not scientific; for inspirational truth is scientific. It must be so; or it is not inspirational truth, as it is impossible for God to be wrong. But there are many, many falsities taught by Trinitarians, and of others not a few who claim for their falsities inspirational truth, which things are scientifically false, as well as inspirationally condemned as untruths; of such are all the doctrines of the Antichrist, against both inspirational and also scientific truth. 

It is an inspirational as well as a scientific truth that our Divine Father in heaven is uncreate, absolute and independent in His spirit, person, and powers; and the Word, our Divine Father's first-born 

Son of all creation is our Divine Father's greatest minister; but it is a crafty and mendacious lie to say, as many do, that God is three Divine persons; and that the Virgin Mary is the "Mother of God." 

Our Divine Father can, through His omnipotent spirit effect by His fiat, word or volition anything that is consistent; but we do not believe that God could cause the Virgin Mary to be His own mother, or the author of His own person, existence and powers; neither do we believe that He could conjoin three Divine independent, absolute infinite persons into one Divine triune person; and both they who thus teach the Trinity of three Divine persons in the Deity as coequal, coessential and coeternal are incapable of trust and dependence on their word.

It is impossible that our Divine Father could be equaled, duplicated or compromised in any way, because His infinitude and absoluteness in everything comprehend all things within His power and authority with no exceptions.

That which is false or a lie cannot be good, but that which is truth is good, for it is the truth which brings freedom and salvation. 

God is truth, and love; and since Christ is God's Son and Mediator, He is God's chosen way to truth and love, and no one comes unto 

God but by Him.

Since God is life and power, love and truth, so He who seeks love and truth, life and power seeks that which is good, and what is good belongs to God and cannot be evil; and God desires all to seek these good things through service. There is no good save that which is of God, because God is good in an absolute sense; and there is no truth save that which is of God, for God is truth; and there is no love save that which is of God, for God is love, and he that loveth is of God. There is no absolute truth apart from God, for God and truth are one, and that one is a concrete, absolute, and immutable unit.

The essence of good, of truth, and of love is spiritual and dispels all falsities and evils while the natural man of himself favors evils and falsities because he does not seek ardently enough truth and love which are altruistic and unselfishness; for selfishness, and covetousness are evil and tend to destroy those who are not solicitous of love and truth; which soon become a cipher or a blank in the mind of those who are without understanding or comprehension; and such become fanatical and seek to abuse and persecute with inquisitorial powers those who differ from them. 

Man, by the abuse of his powers of freedom, of rationality or free moral agency may seem in externals to be different from what He is inwardly and personally; and consequently can do what is good, and speak what is truth, and feign himself an angel of light when inwardly he is a demon.

The origin of all moral evil comes from the abuse of the capacities of free moral agency peculiar to men and angels which is called rationality and liberty as these two capacities are both in the evil as well as the good; but only when they are rightfully used do men and angels become like God in character, and the abuse thereof make men and angels like demons.

Our Divine Father does not suffer any person or unit to be divided, consequently it must be both in good and in truth or it must be both in evil and in falsity. If the tree is good its fruit is good, and if the tree is corrupt its fruit is corrupt, for no one can serve both God and Mammon at one and the same time.

Because of man's liberty and rationality it is quite possible for him to be in heaven in his understanding as to what is good and god-like; but in his love and affections he may be living in hell as the transgressor of everything that is good and holy. 

Heaven is conjunction or harmony of the human soul or spirit with our Divine Father's Holy Spirit; and not so much as many suppose the external associating with angels and saints; but the qualities of love and truth in saints and angels which make heaven wherever you may be.

Men, angels and all things that exist and live, live and exist in, by, and through the power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven; as our Divine Father only has life and being in Himself without origin, all things else must receive their origin and life from Him; who was able of His omnipotent spirit to give origin and life to all other persons and creatures of every kind and order. "The kingdom of God is within you;" and if you would preserve your mind, soul and spirit unto the life immortal and eternal you must get in harmony or conjunction with your Divine Father by the fellowship and communion of your spirit with the Holy Spirit of your Divine Father by prayer, supplication and good works. If you refuse or neglect to commune and fellowship with the Holy 

Spirit of your Divine Father in heaven while you live and have the opportunity here on the earth, you will not have the chance of communing with God, His holy angels and His saints in heaven. 

God, our heavenly Father who is perfection itself has decreed that only the good shall be saved; and it is impossible for Him to change; as that which is perfect cannot change or be changed; and hence all changes must be wrought in His creatures and things of His creation to harmonize with His will or be destroyed. 

The Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven enters into our life through the active desire of our spirit for Divine goodness, truth and love which can best be affected through prayer, and a prayerful study of the life, teachings and practices of Jesus Christ and His apostles. For Jesus says: "He that abideth in me and I in him, the same beareth much fruit, for apart from me ye can do nothing."

To will evil and do evil in so far as the moral and civil laws do not hinder or prevent is satanic fredom which is slavery because it leads to hell and destruction; but to will good and do good in so far as opportunity is granted and strength supplied is heavenly free-

dom which leads to heaven and God. Therefore, true freedom is to do always and only that which is good, because there can be no just penalties, but a reward to all who, through faith and good works, accept Jesus Christ the Son of God as their Lord and Savior.

Christ has simplified all the commandments of God for us by summing them up on these two principal commands, "To love the 

Lord our Divine Father above all things; and to love one's neighbor as himself;" but how can one love God above all things who is a murderer, a thief, an adulterer or a false witness? Does not reason itself teach us that he who does not show due regard for his fellowmen cannot love God? 

Our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ understood the Law and the

Covenants, and what God commands better than any man; for it was He who in His antemundane state appeared many times as His Divine Father's representative by whose hand Adam was formed out of the dust of the earth and who breathed into his nostrils the breath of God's spirit, and Adam became a living soul; who talked with Abraham, Jacob, Hagar, and Lot; who talked with Moses, and gave him the Law, the Covenants, and the commandments; who appeared to the prophets and gave them His Divine Father's message; who led the children of Israel forty years in the wilderness; who became the incarnate Word, Jesus Christ; who was baptized of 

John in the Jordan; who was indued or anointed with the power of the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father; who gave us the "Sermon on the Mount;" who was transfigured in the presence of Peter, James and John, while He talked with Moses and Elias about His death which He should accomplish at Jerusalem; who raised Lazarus from the dead; who told the Samaritan woman that He was the Christ of God, the Messiah; who said to Pilate, "I am the Son of God;" who was the one whom the Jews accused of blasphemy; who was condemned by Pilate to die for our sins; who gave His sacred body and blood as a vicarious atonement for our sins as an atonement; whom Joseph placed in his own new tomb; whom our Divine Father's 

Holy Spirit raised to life the third day from the dead; who was the one who appeared, ate, talked, walked, and blessed His disciples after His resurrection; who gave His disciples instruction for the recovering of the power and guidance of the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father; who ascended to His Father and our Father, to His 

God and our God from Mount Olivet near the city of Jerusalem in the presence of a host of His disciples; and who sat down at the

right hand of His Divine Father in heaven until the restitution of all things shall come to pass at His second appearing. Yea, and a host of other memorable things did Jesus Christ our Divine Father's glorious Son, the Word incarnate for the instruction of His Church and the saving of His people of which the world to-day has no knowledge, because "the man of sin. " and the "Mother of harlots and abominations of the earth," the Roman Catholic Church have destroyed the records of the saints, so as to enable them to change the times, and seasons; and destroy the knowledge of the pure, and true worship of our Divine Father in heaven and of the knowledge of His Son Jesus Christ in the earth by the substitution of a Trinity of Deities of Divine persons without origin. 

It is through man's rationality and liberty that our Divine Father seeks by His Holy Spirit to reside in every one's life, as it is through the inflow of His Holy Spirit into our life by which His spirit is to be received and operate in us to our regeneration and salvation. 

It was the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven operating through the Word, His glorious first-born Son of all creation that He formed the worlds and flung them out in space and guided them by the power of His Holy Spirit so that they ever in peace and order move.

Christ was so completely filled with the spirit and mind of His Divine Father, and so desirous and anxious to do the will of His Divine Father that the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father completely controlled and governed His words and acts, so that He was to all intents and purposes possessed of the mind and power of His Divine Father's spirit; and so faithfully did He perform the tasks assigned 

Him by His Divine Father that He could say truthfully, "He that seeth me seeth the Father who sent me, for the works I do are not mine, but the works of the Father's spirit through me." "I of myself can do nothing, it is my Father who doeth the works." 

Without liberty and rationality man could have no reformation or regeneration or conjunction with God, neither could man accept 

Jesus Christ as His Lord and Savior. Christ will be the Lord and

Savior of all who accept Him as such; but the acceptance of Christ is something more than mere assent; for it involves the keeping of 

His commandments, which are not grievous; for if we confess Him as our Lord and Savior, and do not try to keep His commandments we are liars and hypocrites; for no one can truly love or accept

Jesus Christ as His Lord and Savior who does not delight to obey Him.

Many of our shrewdest and best educated men who are rational in some things are very irrational in others; and therefore liberty and rationality in religion cannot be given to those who are born excessively foolish or stupid; and among them are many of our 

Doctors Divinitis who will permit the publicans and sinners to go into the kingdom before them, because they have hardened their heart against the true ways and teachings of the Lord by denying that the Holy Spirit is the spirit of our Divine Father in heaven; which denial, if persisted in and confirmed is the sin against the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven, which has no forgiveness, either in this world nor in that which is to come. Those who say that the Holy Spirit is the third Divine person in the Deity of the Trinity of the triune God, deny the existence of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father; and in so doing cut off from themselves the only conjoining means of communion and fellowship with their Divine Father in heaven through whose spirit all Divine communion and fellowship must be had. 

Since the Holy Spirit is the only means of all our Divine Father's operations, liberty and rationality in things Divine it cannot be given to those who attribute all things to nature as the pantheists do, or attribute nothing to our Divine Father in heaven as the atheists or agnostics do. Liberty and rationality can scarcely be given to those who have strongly confirmed themselves against the gospel of Jesus Christ by the falsities of heathen philosophies, and man-made religions and creeds, for a confirmer of falsities is a denier of the truth; and those who put their trust in falsehoods will utterly perish, for there is no way or means under heaven whereby we must be saved, save through Jesus Christ, God's Son and Mediator. 

Liberty, rationality and salvation can be safely given to those who, whatever their religion might be, have not so confirmed themselves in error as not to repent and accept the truth when it is one clearly presented to them.

It is the duty of those who read these lines to consider the correctness, the truthfulness, the inspiration, and the Divinty of these facts, which have been gathered from the scriptures, from history, from the sciences, from nature, from our common rationality, and from the various Churches and creeds; and learn for yourselves the many truths; and the many falsities pointed out which the "Mother

of harlots and abominations of the earth" has palmed off onto the world as the doctrine and practices of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ.

We have learned to discern between truth and error through many years of toil in study and research that our children and children's children could by reading these lines have a clearer conception and understanding between truth and error and grow up to be good and useful men and women in the world by becoming established in the truths of the gospel of Jesus Christ the Son of God. 

Our Divine Father who in Himself is a unit of one person can never be a unit of more than one person and it is therefore a great falsity to say that He has become three distinct Divine persons or units in Himself, which statement is contradictory to all truth and cannot be divided into three persons and three units in one unit called a triune or three in one God; as a unit of one person is a unit in himself, and each of three persons is each a unit in himself and three units or persons cannot be three and one at the same time and in fact can never be true because it is a contradiction in terms as the affirming of three units are one, goes just so far to prove one are not three and cannot be reckoned thus in any calculations whatever because it affirms the impossible, and is therefore a falsity. 

Those who kid themselves into using these fallacious terms which mean nothing but confusion, because that which contradicts or destroys itself is nothing but a lie and they are foolish, silly, stupid and irrational people who teach their children conundrums for religion which are lies. It is wicked, sinful, degrading, satanic, brutish, villainous and unchristian to thus abuse the minds of your children by stuffing them full of such nonsense; and especially wicked is it to tell your children these lies are of Divine Revelations, and are not to be doubted or questioned as the truth even though they do contradict the scriptures, every scientific truth and every private knowledge of fact. It is something dreadful, appalling, terrible, degrading, and satanic, not only to abuse the mind of your children with such lies, but also to blaspheme the name of your Divine

Creator by saying that He is the author of the doctrine of the Trinity which is a medley of lies and contradictions instigated during the fourth century of the Christian era.

Some will say that we are using strong language in condemning the doctrine of the Trinity; but someone must speak in strong, plain terms of its sin and wickedness, shame and wrong, in order to save

the young and rising generation from its ravenous, villainous and leprous infections.

Every villain, imp and reprobate wants no one to say a word against them and their wicked chicanery; and we are well aware of all the malice, hate, scum and froth that these satanic dregs of human society who strut about in sheep's clothing will heap upon our humble frame for calling upon God, His angels, and His saints to put an end to the big fat salaries of those who traffic in human souls by keeping the Church divided, and persecuting those who dare raise a finger to end that slavery; for it makes very little difference to some of them just what portion of humanity is sunk into hell or oblivion so long as they do not belong to their Church, or just how many of their own parishioners go to hell just so long as they can fleece them out of their money.

Instead of preaching the gospel of Jesus Christ they are telling lies about Him and preaching the gospel of the Antichrist, the man of sin and Pope of Rome, telling the people lies by saying that the only true and living God is three Divine persons in one Divine triune person which is to be worshipped as a Trinity in unity and unity in Trinity, or three in one or one in three persons without confounding the persons; and those who refuse to thus worship shall perish everlastingly in an ever-burning, suffering, painful, torturing and afflicting hell of fire and brimstone where the people who do not accept the doctrine of the Trinity never, never die but burn and simmer on in pain and suffering forever; and they exort the people in long prayers and dissertations to give, give, give for the spreading of their gospel!

We need again the strong right arm of the holy Nazarene carpenter Jesus Christ to once more plat a bunch of heavy cords and cleanse the Church of these grafters who commercialize the Church of our Divine Father, the only true and living God who for a pretence make long prayers while they, like vampires, suck the lifeblood from their victims who think these hellions are doing them 

God service.

Can anyone imagine that it is a delight to battle against such a turbulent stream of sin and wickedness and speak against the immoralities, antichrist doctrines, selfishness and covetousness of the ministry of the Church? It is indeed hard to alter the immoralities, graft and chicanery of the ministry of the Church who always seek the high places and the big salaries, the honors and emoluments of

office contrary to the teachings of Jesus Christ who said, "Beware of covetousness."

No one is necessarily reformed by miracles, signs, wonders, visions, threats, punishments or other external apparatus or paraphernalia, because they compel or force upon our rationality and liberty depressive feelings contrary to our free moral agency; but truth when. rightfully understood or comprehended will, by the converting power of our Divine Father's Holy Spirit, bring the sinner to repentance and reformation; for, says Christ, "No one can come unto me except the Father draw him."

These uncontradicted evidences that the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven is the only motive or executive power that is Divine which is corroborated by many infallible proofs herein produced and acknowledged by our Divine Father, by Jesus Christ, by Christ's apostles and evangelists; and by all the prophets, and by all truly 

Christian folk to be correct; but nevertheless they should be illustrated and expounded for those who have not had the opportunity of investigating the Christian records of history and of the Holy Scriptures, in order that they might be enabled to discern what is truth when they do read the scriptures; for our Divine Father in heaven desires that all should know the truth by having a correct understanding of the operations of His Holy Spirit by actual knowledge and discernment of truth so as to be able to discriminate between right and wrong of themselves that they be led not astray by all kinds of flimsy arguments from fallacious premises and at last deny the truth; for the spirit of man is such from the laws of Divine 

Providence that man should act from his own knowledge of truth, of fact, and of consistency according to his own understanding, and not from any outward compulsion.

Worship has in former years, in most part, been compelled by fear, dread, and terror of punishment both civil and ecclesiastical, and of an everlasting hell of suffering hereafter; and every evil vice, sin and wrong was practiced upon the feeble minds, hearts and consciences of the people, cowing them into subjection and servitude to a villainous ecclesiastical hierarchy. No true worship can be performed in a state of fear, for it takes freedom from reason, joy from worship, and liberty and rationality out of all acts of devotion and adoration, while love opens the interiors of the mind, heart and spirit of the soul through joyful, loving, willing voluntary service, devotion and adoration to our Divine Father in heaven, the God of

all love and beneficence; and all who preach an everlasting hell-fire for those who do not believe in their three in one headed monster of a Divine triune person consisting of three Divine persons, commits one of the most heinous crimes that can possibly be visited upon his posterity either in this world or the world to come. Such a doctrine is more terrible, brutal and villainous than Satan or any of the imps of hell would have the heart to think of visiting upon their fellow denizens.

All persons, beings or things that live, live from our Divine Father, as it is from Him that all things have their creation of existence, of life, and of power; but since our Divine Father of Himself created only His first-born Son of all creation immediately, He chose to create all things else of His creation through Him; and placed Him over or above all things else of His creation by placing all things under Him and making all things subject to Him as His mediator. 

It is to be understood that it is the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven from which all power, gifts, graces, favors or induements of Divine uses, goods, benefits, blessings, services and acts of a Divine nature proceed; and the only means by which and from which all power and offices of a Divine nature are derived; for there can be no such a thing as a departure of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father from our Divine Father's person, as it is pure and simple nonsense to speak of the spirit of an ever-living person departing from the person whose spirit it is, as God is spirit, life, power, love, truth and light in operation, as all things coming from God are created, given or bestowed through the Holy Spirit of our 

Divine Father and in no other way.

The spirit of man is the life giving properties of man's person, and is the motive, executive, willing, choosing, thinking, designing and purposing power of man's person by which he lives, moves and has being, as the spirit of man cannot be a person apart from the person whose spirit it is. A spirit must be the spirit of something whether of some person, being or thing or it is not the spirit of anything, as it is not a person in itself apart from the person whose spirit it is. Thus the spirit of our Divine Father whose spirit the 

Holy Spirit is, is not a person apart from our Divine Father's person, for it is the spirit of our Divine Father's person, as our Divine Father is not a person without a spirit but a person with a spirit, for there cannot be a person without spirit; and the spirit of our 

Divine Father is the Holy Spirit,

It takes both body and spirit to make a person, as the body without the spirit is dead, and as such the person is destroyed, and so long as they are separated neither can be called a person. Thus God without His spirit, which spirit the Holy Spirit is, is not a person without it, but with it; and it is a falsehood or a lie to say that our 

Divine Father in heaven is the first Divine person in the Trinity called God the Father; and that the spirit of our Divine Father in heaven whose spirit the Holy Spirit is, is the third Divine person in the Trinity called God the Holy Ghost. The Holy Spirit is the spirit of our Divine Father's person, and is called the Holy Spirit, because the spirit of our Divine Father is holy; and it is given this name or title to distinguish the spirit of our Divine Father from all other spirits which belong to men or angels.

Our Divine Father without His spirit, called the Holy Spirit, could have no existence, but with it He has a personal existence as such; but He is not two or more persons, but one only. 

We do not know what an immortal or spiritual body is, save that it is of God and imperishable so long as He wills it; but this we do know, that, that is but one person the mind of whose spirit reaches as far as his self-consciousness does. The mind and will of the spirit of our Divine Father which searches and knows all things, is infinite and universal, and all things are made and controlled by it, for by it our Divine Father did foretell through the prophets, Jesus Christ and His apostles future history down unto the end of the world; as it determines and brings to pass all things in accordance with our Divine Father's will and purposes, as there is no power, knowledge or anything whatsoever of being, power or authority but what is of our Divine Father in heaven; and all sentient rational creatures are accountable to Him for the exercising of this power and authority which our Divine Father has given them to use for their own good and for His glory, else all these things will be taken from them and given to those who will bring forth good fruits.

The Divine teaching of Jesus Christ that the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father was the motive and executive power of His Divine mission and all that He spake and did the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father was the prompter and executor of it; and the teaching by the ministry of the Church that the Holy Spirit is the third Divine person in the Deity merits the severest condemnation by Divine authority for such impudence and satanic blasphemy of the Divine record; and our Divine Father will not hold those guiltless for such

blasphemy of the record He has given us through His all inspiring spirit.

Christ teaches us that the Divine Providence of His Father in heaven is over all His works, so that even a sparrow could not fall to the ground without His notice, and that He has every hair of your head all numbered. Our Divine Father knows everything in the minutest detail, including the electrons of the largest dynamo ever assembled, yea even those of the great sun in the heavens, or the little fire-fly of the harvest-moon so that none of them are lost or unaccounted for by Him. How marvelous God is!

There is nothing that can happen by chance in the order of our Divine Father's providence, and those who trust in Him need not fear but that all things will work for good to them that love Him; and yet, there are those who do not recognize that our Divine, adorable and beneficent heavenly Father is the author of their being and all that they are and have. 

In so far as we are able we should seek to know what is good, noble, virtuous and true by trying to find the truth, and do the good and the truth; but the greatest truth or commandment of which man can come into possession is, that, "The Lord our God is one Father," who is life, wisdom, power and love; as only he who has this faith can have that holy resignation, confidence, peace and consolation which come to the soul of him who thus confides in our 

Divine Father.
