There are those who think that there is no Divine providence; and that all things are left to the chance of nature; for they observe that the worldly people oft are more successful in many respects than those who believe in God; but, it is because the worldly by deception and tricks can inflict injuries, wrongs and misfortunes upon the believing and pious without any compunctions of conscience which the Christian world refrain from doing. 

It is the Spirit of God and not the mere trusting to nature or natural causes of heat and light by which all things are governed; for the natural heat and light of the sun come from that which is dead or inert; and it is not possible that a thing that is dead can produce the millions of variety of living objects which were produced by the power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven; and if you think that what is dead can give life to itself or that it can confer life upon others, you are insane, for life must come from life, and this can exist only through the Providence of a

Divine Creator, for all life is a continual change of development in all finite things, and our Divine Father has so wisely arranged the changing existence of the living by the constant, the fixed and the sure as an abode or dwelling place for that which is living. 

Man's prudence or wisdom is as nothing, as there is not any form of knowledge but what God is the author and also the revealer of it; as it is not right or proper that any man should take any glory to himself save obedience or faithfulness to the pleadings and leadings of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven. 

The spirit of man is the thinking function of man and has control over the bodily passions and appetites only in so far as man will cultivate the keeping of the promptings of his spirit by bringing his body into subjection to the spirit; but all spirits are ultimately subject to the governing of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father or we are none of His, for it is to this end that our Divine Father created all things, or they will, otherwise, be destroyed like the tares of which Jesus spoke in His parables. 

Since, then, it is man's spirit that thinks, wills, chooses, designs, purposes and executes all things according to its will in so far as it is able and not hindered by external power or circumstances, and forced from its natural pursuits; it is free to act according to its freedom and rationality in its free moral agency, choice or volition; but the highest freedom and the noblest choice is its subjection to the will of God's spirit.

It is always best to trust God and His Divine Providence whatever betide, as man looks upon the outward appearance, the temporal and transient things of life; but our Divine Father looks upon the eternal things, upon the heart and its affections, and to temporal things only in so far as they agree with eternal things; and He will destroy a world as in the days of Noah, and make a new one to advance righteousness, truth, and justice; He has done this once, and 

He says that He will do it once more for the elects' sake.

We are to understand by temporal things, such things as dignities and riches which perish with men's lives or terminate with man's life upon the earth, such as the Papal jurisdiction of the Antichrist assumed by the Popes of Rome who have exalted their claims of dominion even unto heaven and to God's throne by claiming both temporal and spiritual jurisdiction over the whole earth as the vicegerent of God which Jesus Christ or His apostles were never so vain to claim; but the Pope seats himself in the temple of God claiming

infallibility for himself and jurisdiction over all the Church of the only true and living God our Father in heaven.

The Popes do not recognize the incarnate Word Jesus Christ, God's only begotten Son, as the head over all the Church; but set themselves up as such power or authority not only over the Church, but all temporal things as well, as the vicegerent of God, claiming the jurisdiction of God in the earth. If any king should permit his subjects to govern all things of his kingdom, he would no longer be king; but would be merely a so-called king, for he would only have the title of the dignity, but in reality have no power or authority; and government cannot be predicted of such a king who only acts as a figure-head of power and authority; so it is with the Pope; if they are permitted to rule and reign over the Church and change the commands, laws, times and seasons; and appoint holy days and. obligations at will, contrary to the commands and laws of our Divine Father in heaven; and all peoples acknowledge his doctrines, precepts and acts as Divine, such as the worshipping of His Trinity of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person, Sunday worship in the place of sabbath worship, baptism in the name of the Trinity instead of in the name of Jesus Christ, hypostatical union or homoousian of the human with the Divine, etc. Then is such an one the "God of this world;" but an enemy of Jesus Christ "who has no part with Him.”

What we here said of the head of the Roman Catholic Church should with equal propriety be said by anyone who sets himself up as authority, dictator or president over the Church. Jesus warned

His disciples to be aware that no selfishness, covetousness or pride, arise in their heart which brings forth death, for the devil is all such in himself to such a degree that he adores himself and favors no one who does not adore him; and other devils who like himself aspire to power and authority, he hates, because he wishes to be worshipped exclusively, and have all power and authority; and be the sole Lord of the world, and be a God whose subjects obey his every nod and beck with no freedom to act save but by servile worship toward himself.

This makes it clear how it is that every villain or demon who assumes to be the head of the Church of Jesus Christ is filled with the lust of power, of greed, of selfishness, of covetousness, of dignities, of riches, and of authority contrary to the teachings of Jesus Christ who said, "Love not the world, neither the things of the world, but

set your affections on things above and be ye not called Father, Papa, Pope, President or Ruler, for one is your Father who is in heaven; and be ye not called teacher or master, for one is your master even Christ." Thus spake the great leader and head of His 

Church Jesus Christ the Son of God, the "Alpha and the Omega," the beginning and the end of the creation of God, "The first and the last." "The Beginning of God's creation," as a superangelical spirit, God's glorious Son the Word; and the end of God's creation, the Word incarnated, Jesus the Christ. It is He which was with His 

Divine Father before the foundation of the world, He which now is with His Divine Father in heaven, and He it is who is to come at the end of this gospel age even Jesus Christ, who spoke and operated always and only by the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father in heaven, and has revealed to us through His beloved apostle John the things which must soon be fulfilled in His bride, His body, the Church, so He commanded John to write the vision, and John says: "I, John beheld the Holy City, New Jerusalem of which the Lord 

God the Almighty Father, and the Lamb, His Son Jesus Christ are the temple, and the city hath no need of the sun neither of the moon to shine into it, for the glory of God did enlighten it and the Lamb is the light thereof."

It is only by and through Jesus Christ the head of His Church, and by no other person that the spirit of God is to reveal to the 

Church the everlasting gospel; and anyone claiming any special revelation for the Church of Jesus Christ other than that which has been given to us by His apostles and evangelists of the first century of the Christian era is a liar and a villain. Christ is not going to entrust the direction of His Church to any mortal person. 

When John, in his Patmos visions, fell down before Jesus Christ for the purpose of rendering him Divine homage and adoration, Christ said to him: "See thou do it not, for I am of thy fellowservants, and of thy brethren the prophets; and of them which keep the sayings of this book, worship God. I am the root and offspring of David, and the bright and morning star."

It is through Jesus Christ, the Word incarnated of the root and offspring of David through whom our Divine Father Jehovah gives the concluding revelations to His servant the beloved apostle John by means of visions in the Isle of Patmos for the guidance and governing of His Church until the end of the world; and these visions are the completion of all Divine prophecy in the Christian Church;

and by this special economy, prophecy is still continued, is always speaking, so that a succession of new revelations is rendered unnecessary through these special revelations by visions of the vicissitudes of time through which the Church must pass down to the end of the world.

How admirable and marvelous are the power and wisdom of God who completes the voice of Divine revelations in prophecy which is to continue in the Church through the testimony of Jesus Christ to His beloved and chosen apostle until the end of the world, so that no further revelation of Divine prophecy is to be given other than that which is delivered to us by the beloved Apostle John in his book of Revelations. 

The record is complete without any assistance of any extraordinary messenger or any succession of messengers whose testimony at all times would be liable to suspicion and be subject to infidel and malevolent criticism, and justly so, however much the succession might appear unexceptional to ingenious minds.

It makes but little difference whether you belong to any local organization called the Church, as it has become a band of robbers and a den of thieves much like the Jerusalem temple cleansed by the scourge of Jesus Christ; if you are in the kingdom of God, into which every saved soul is immediately translated, you are saved whether you belong to any local Church or not, as a goodly portion of those who do belong to the local Church are liars, villains, and reprobates, thieves and hypocrites because they teach many false doctrines of a sectarian nature in order to deceive and build up the local organization by denying the truth. 

The apostle Paul in speaking of the glory of God says: "God who commanded the light out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of 

Jesus Christ." This glory John saw in the face of Jesus Christ on the Isle of Patmos, Paul on his way to Damascus, Moses when he received the law and the commandments, and a mighty host of others who have testified in the Old and also in the New Testaments of the glory of God in the face of the Word, God's glorious only begotten Son, first by creation and last by incarnation. 

People do not behold in the so-called vicegerent of God and vicar of Jesus-Christ, the Popes of Rome; presidents, apostles and bishops of our modern commercialized Church organizations, the glory of God in their faces like that of Jesus Christ or like that of Moses

when he received the Law, or like that of the evangelist Saint Stephen, the deacon, as he sat before the Council of the Sanhedrim; but our Divine Father in heaven does not recognize these impostors and antichrist institutions as belonging to Him whatever, nor does He recognize any federation of Churches, sects or denominations as belonging to Him, as every local Church founded under the guidance of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven was a distinct local organization in itself with no authority whatever over that of any other, as all recognized Jesus Christ as the head and governor of His Church, and any person who claimed jurisdiction or authority over the Christians was anathema, and treated as an impostor, liar, villain and reprobate and called usurpers, thieves, and heretics, as each Church organization was considered as a complete unit in itself, and responsible to no man upon the earth; but all were exhorted to follow the teachings and practices of Jesus Christ, as taught and practiced by the apostles, under the direction. of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven.

Our Divine Father has no vicegerent and Jesus Christ has no vicar for their substitutes; therefore, no committee, synod, council, convention or convocation has authority or jurisdiction over the Church, for all are equally independent of each other and all dependent or accountable unto God for their stewardship.

The ruling principle of man's life should be to get things that are good and put them to more beneficial uses than they were before he got them, for the good of all humanity, as the greatest reward and glory can come only through the greater service or use made of anything; and when it is not beneficial, it becomes a curse. 

It is a characteristic saying of Jesus Christ: "He that hath an ear let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the Churches," as all the things He said or did our Divine Father's Holy Spirit said or did through Him, so that the doctrine He taught and the works that He did were not His, but that of His Divine Father in heaven; for 

Jesus tells us many times: "I of myself can do nothing, it is my 

Father who doeth these works."

The solemn warning of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father through His glorified Son Jesus Christ not to add anything to the prophecy given to the beloved apostle John on the island of Patmos, as the end of all Divine revelation to His Church, and there is a curse pronounced upon the person of those who shall ever claim a Divine revelation later than this for the Church; for the prophecies

of the book of Revelations is a completion of all revelations from God to man. There are no acceptable substitutes, subtractions, divisions alterations or anything to be added to the gospel of Jesus Christ as incomplete; and those who do are heresiarchs, villains, and reprobates, and under the curse of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven; for all that He has ordained is not to be amended, added to, or abridged in any way. 

Any Church, society, convention, sect, cult, denomination or whosoever that will teach doctrines and precepts as Divine, which are not found in the teachings and practices of the New Testament writings of the apostles and evangelists of the New Testament times or use the name Christian for those who do not follow strictly the doctrine and practices of Christ's apostles, are traitors and robbers to the Church of Jesus Christ, and destroyers of God's holy covenants; and let not such think that they can escape the damnation of hell, and their sure destruction in the day of judgment, for such are not of the Church of Jesus Christ, but of the "Synagogue of Satan;" and no marvel, for Satan transforms himself into an angel of light seeking whom he may devour by signs, seals, indulgences, baptisms for the dead by living proxies, celestial marriages, polygamy, adultery, changing of sacraments, changing of commandments, worshipping of men and angels, and still claim to be Christians and members of the Church of the living God, the pillar and ground of the truth when Christ's disciples did not preach or practice them.

CHAPTER XIV

Jesus Christ accomplished our redemption, so far as regards the payment of the redemptive price was concerned when the precious blood of Christ was spilled on Mount Calvary. It was here that His sacrificial body was offered upon the alter for our sins. He took the emblems of His blood and entered into the Holy of Holies of heaven itself with the memorial of His blood there to appear in the presence of God for us having obtained eternal redemption for us from all our sins and ceremonial defilements and inadvertances by remaining within the veil of the inner sanctuary, and so long as He thus remains there is no necessity of any sacrifices or oblations being offered by any priesthood whatever to intercede or offer up sacrifices after the manner of the Law; and any who claim such Divine com- 274

Unless God is one person or a unit in Himself, a complete entity, no one can have a clear perception of God; and to formulate the unity of God in any other way is to make it unnatural, absurd, inconsistent and contradictory to all known truths which even to our own mind would be falsities, a snare, a lie and inconsistent with unity which would be to blaspheme God's name and person.

We have millions of people who have gone to Church and Sundayschool all their life who do not know that every week of the year they transgressed God's hallowed and sanctified day, the holy Sabbath appointed by Him as a memorial of His finished creation, and have transgressed the first commandment laid down by Jesus Christ by calling our Divine Father in heaven a Trinity of Divine persons coequal, coessential and coeternal with each other; and, so it is with millions of people, they cannot give you an intelligent answer as to what or who God is or what He is not; yea, even many of the professors of our seminaries, colleges and universities know so little about God that they continually contradict themselves or say things which they have not the least idea of their truthfulness or meaning, so they simply teach what they have been taught without knowing that these are falsities and antichristian doctrines. For example, if we say, as most people do, that Jesus Christ is Divine, we then put Him on a parity or equality with our Divine Father in heaven, then we are forced to say the Son of God or God Son or God the Son which admits of no creation or relationship to any other but an independency of being such as an uncreate or unoriginate person who cannot be son to anyone; and it is a misnomer to call such an one a son; but that He is God's Son and first creature of creation; and that God is His Father and Creator; and that He is the Son of the Father the scriptures positively do teach in hundreds of places, for Divinity cannot be derived from Divinity for that which is derived is a creature and dependent; for God cannot be derived from 

God; for that which is uncreate or without origin cannot produce that which is uncreate or without origin, therefore there can be but

one uncreate or without origin, and He is therefore absolute, independent, infinite, omnipotent, omniscient, and ubiquitous or omnipresent in His spirit and powers; and no one but an ignoramus will contend against this Divine truth, "That the Lord our God is one

Father," and not three or more Divine persons such as the Antichrist, the man of sin, and son of perdition, the Pope of Rome who claims to be the vicegerent of God and vicar of Jesus Christ has set up as an object of worship.

He that is created, begotten or produced in any way is the Son of the one by whom He was produced; and since our Divine Father produced all things by the omnipotent power of His Holy Spirit which is the motive and executive power of His person, He can do nothing but by His spirit; and for this reason when the Holy Scriptures tell us that Christ as the incarnate Word was conceived by the Holy Spirit which incarnated Him in the womb of the Virgin Mary, we are to understand that the Holy Spirit is the spirit of our Divine Father's person, and, as such power of His person is exercised through His spirit, Christ is the only begotten Son of our Divine Father because He is the only one conceived and generated by incarnation through the power of God's spirit of all who were born of woman.

We need not tell you after a few moments reflection that the doctrine, "That the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven is a Divine person coequal, coessential, coeternal, and equal in power, glory, and majesty with our Divine Father" is false; and that Jesus

Christ the Son of our Divine Father in heaven is another Divine person, is also false; as it is a contradiction to say that a person's spirit is a separate and distinct person, unit, or entity from that of himself; and also that our Divine Father's Son and creature likewise is coequal, coessential, coeternal and equal in power, glory and majesty with that of Himself who is uncreate or unoriginate, absolute and independent, is false. What a hellish, satanic, villainous doctrine is the doctrine of the Trinity of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person which robs our Divine Father of His Holy Spirit and also of His Son in order to make two more Divine uncreate, unoriginate, independent, infinite, absolute, omniscient, omnipotent persons who are each equal to our Divine Father!

How could it be possible for the independent, absolute, uncreate, unoriginate infinite Creator, our Divine Father in heaven, who alone

is from all eternity, be placed upon an equality or parity with two others which the Trinitarians themselves affirm were begotten or proceeded from our Divine Father who was neither begotten nor proceeded from anyone?

The doctrine of the Trinity is wholly absurd and inconsistent with truth, and the people who reason thus, have very little, if any sense of honor or of truth whatever or even faith for their own integrity, as to affirm that this conglomeration of Trinitarian nonsense, absurdities and contradictions is Divine; for they cannot help but know, if they understand what they affirm, that this doctrine of the Trinity is a straight-out medley of lies and contradictions which is contrary to scripture, nature, science, reason and every private knowledge of fact. 

If God had any desire that we should believe in the Trinity of the Antichrist which is contrary to all truth and reason, do you not suppose that God would have had His Son, the great and glorious primate of His creation, the incarnate Word Jesus Christ, or some of His apostles to have revealed to us that fact, and not have left such important doctrines and articles of faith and practice to be accidentally found out through the agnostic, heathen, Platonic and Alexandrian philosophers, three or four centuries after He had declared by His Holy Spirit through the beloved apostle "John on the 

Island of Patmos" that all Divine revelations were closed?

It is a mighty good thing that salvation is not dependent upon the explanation of words and phrases; for there would not be so much as one Trinitarian saved, as there is not so much as one of them can explain their three Divine coequal Deities in one Divine person; but neither God nor demons are so depraved, vulgar and profane as to ask anyone to explain the absurd conundrums formulated by the Antichrist, the man of sin, the son of perdition, the man who calls himself the vicegerent of God and vicar of Jesus Christ, the Pope of Rome, as the persons to be explained by them separate the understanding from the very things which they say are to be believed in order to have salvation or they will perish everlastingly.

Those who change the natural, the scientific or rational sense of units, person or spirits into a conglomeration of nonsense, hide the real and true meaning of God's holy word by burying it underneath a pile of fallacious rubbish and garbage of darkness and oblivion too astute for the wisest of men to decipher its meaning so they say

it is Divinely ineffable, or so holy that it is above reason and is to be accepted on faith under the penalty of eternal damnation for all who fail to accept it.

All the laws of our Divine Father in heaven have for their end the regeneration and consequent salvation of man by the reversal of the state or condition in which through Adam's sin man is born, so that all there is for man to do for immortality and eternal life is to be regenerated by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven by faith in Jesus Christ as God's Son and Mediator and repentance toward God.

God has made man in His own image and likeness in that He has given him rationality and liberty to act as of himself by which he comprehends, understands, wills, thinks, chooses, discriminates, and decides his mode of action in the presence of an alternative which nothing else of all creatures of earth have the privilege of doing; and therefore, man is the only responsible being unto God His heavenly Father, because He is given the power to thus act of choice, with full knowledge of His indebtedness to His Divine Creator for all that He is, has and does. For this reason our Divine Father has given to man rationality that he might freely act of his own choice in his free moral agency to choose either good or evil, for which he alone of all creatures of earth is responsible to God for the usage of his freedom, powers and talents to the blessing of his own soul and the good of his fellow-men or for their degradation and destruction. 

God is good and beneficent to offer to give to us all that is His in full enjoyment and pleasure to our highest developement and welfare if we will only make use of the means provided by asking His forgiveness and love by utilizing the means of grace which He has provided.

Every one should think from the Lord to himself, as all good things come from Him; and in this way he would always think what the 

Lord would have him to do; but instead most every one thinks from himself to the Lord; and in this way he always thinks what he would have the Lord to do for him, when there is only one thing needful, and that is the salvation of man's soul, and all other necessary things will be added in God's own good time. 

No one is receiving, has received or can receive anything but that which comes from our Divine Father in heaven but all that which man receives he may make good uses or evil uses of it for the time being, but which determines his final destiny; for most every evil

which comes to man, comes to him by his receiving that which comes from our Divine Father, but most men use it as that of his very own, instead of giving the Lord the praise, the honor and the glory, as it is He only who is the author and dispenser of all good things; and thus all the blame to reach His highest good rests on man who receives, for he receives it of the Lord and not of himself, and thus every man is his own evil or his own good to the extent that he acknowledges that all things are of the Lord and nothing of himself.

Since all things are of our Divine Father; men, angels or all things else whatsoever, have nothing of themselves, but of our Divine Father only who has all things of Himself, and all things else receive from Him all that they are and have; and as man is not of himself but of the Lord, our Divine Father in heaven, therefore, man and all things else without any exception belong to our Divine Father in heaven who is the Creator of man and all things else, spirits, persons and beings without any excepton; but our Divine 

Father approves of what man does with that which he has received only in so far as he does not use these blessings to his own injury and to the injury of his fellow-men.

Our Divine Father in heaven puts man in possession of everything which man has; but that does not make man the owner of anything, as to our Divine Father, but only as to his fellow-creatures; for as to God our heavenly Father everything belongs to Him, and all things are ours only in the Lord, as those who claim ownership are like those who occupy the house or property of another, when, as soon as they are placed in possession persuade themselves that they are the real owners when they have it not of themselves, but of another who is the real owner, and God will bring them into account for the talents He has given them whether they have occupied them for good uses or bad uses. Those who have made good uses of them, to them more shall be given, and he shall have an abundance, but those who have made bad uses of their talents God shall take away from them all that He gave them.

Falsity may be assented to or even confirmed so long as truth is not seen or known; but the moment that it is understood or known, falsity is destroyed, as everything that is confirmed with a correct. understanding by the will of our spirit remains eternally true; and so long as man is true to his conscience and its sense of right and

truth he will follow his understanding in his thoughts and actions the same as a blood-hound follows the scent.

Our Divine Father is going to make a new heaven and a new earth out of the human race in which dwelleth righteousness; but only those will be admitted into this blessed, happy state who worship our Divine Father in heaven exclusively as the only Divine person, because He will not suffer His person, glory, honor and power to be divided or diminished by those who worship bishops, presidents, Popes and champions; and those who wish to do so will be debarred from the paradise of God; for they are contrary to the truths of Christianity and the nature of our Divine Father. 

The Divine love of our heavenly Father provides the means whereby every one who so wills to be saved can be saved by complying with the conditions of repentance toward God and the acceptance of the vicarious atonement of our Divine Father's Son Jesus Christ; but those who have not the privilege of knowing of the vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ, His atonement applies to all who have the answer of a good conscience toward God; for all who seek to do God's will whether they have heard of the gospel of Jesus Christ or not are the same as babes in Christ Jesus until they have consciously and deliberately rebelled against God.

There are many who have the gospel in its mutilated form handed down to us by the Antichrist, the Pope of Rome, who are so selfish as to think that those who have not the gospel will not be saved; but our Divine Father has revealed by His Holy Spirit through the apostles of Jesus Christ that those who have not the Law and the gospel will be judged without them; but those who have the Law and the gospel will be judged by them so that all fare the same according to their opportunities, and all will be judged as righteous who have the answer of a good conscience toward God whether with the Law and the gospel or without them such will be saved. 

Christ is the bridgeroom, head and founder of His Church. Christ is not a polygamist with innumerable brides or wives, neither does 

He recognize co-bridegrooms or co-husbands to His bride, the

Church, as Popes or presidents, as Christ does not believe in His bride committing whoredom, fornication, or adultery by recognizing any person other than Himself as the bridegroom of His bride, the

Church, nor does He want His bride to recognize any person as the bridegroom or head of His Church other than Himself and those

who do act in any other name He does not recognize as His bride, but antichristian.

Both the Law and the gospel of Jesus Christ have been the means of salvation to many of the human race; but there are many millions more who have the law and the gospel who make no effort whatever to live up to their provisions which will be the means of their condemnation because of their failure to use them; but those to whom the means of salvation have not been made known will be judged by their conscience in the light of nature. Those who know their Master's will and refuse to do it will be beaten with many stripes; but those who know it not, will be treated with every leniency, and will receive but a very few stripes, if they live up to the light which they do have, and will be pardoned through the merits of the vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ, though they do not know of these provisions made by our Divine Father in heaven through His glorious Son the incarnate Word Jesus Christ. 

It is not so much our saving of the heathen by bringing to them the gospel, as it is to save ourselves by bringing to them the gospel which Christ has commanded us to do; and we are under obligations to do it to the saving of our souls. 

The means of salvation has been provided for every one, and that all who live with a conscience that is devoid of offence toward God are accepted with Him; but be it known unto you all that no one is saved because our Divine Father has said unto you that Jesus Christ is His Son and your sacrifice which He has proffered for your acceptance; but because you live in accord with the provisions whether you have the gospel or not, as there are some who fulfill the royal law without the message of Divine revelation. 

Jesus Christ, men and angels, and every rational person, spirit, or being is the recipient of life and being from God who became Father of them in His creation of them; for all men, angels, persons, spirits and beings, celestial and terrestrial, are creatures of our Divine Father's creation; and as our Divine Father is the only person uncreate and unbegotten, He for this reason is God, Creator and Father of all other persons without exception. 

Our Divine Father in heaven who only is God by reason that He is the only uncreate or unoriginate eternal person subsisting in but one person in Himself, of Himself and by Himself without division or parts; and all others are but creatures of His creation; so that no Divine attributes can rightfully be ascribed to any other person.

God through His creation of other persons was their Father by reason of His creation of them of which the Word was His first-born Son of all creation, and no Divine titles are applicable to Him as a creature, Son or agent of His Divine Father.

That God our Divine Father consists and subsists in but the one person only; and that He alone is Divine is scriptural, scientific, consistent, reasonable, sensible, and in perfect harmony with every private fact of knowledge or of truth; and is demonstrable by all scientific and Divinely known truths; for that is one person or spirit. only which hears, sees, smells, tastes, feels, perceives, understands, wills, chooses, deigns, purposes, executes and operates according to the will of His spirit and own thoughts and notions; as each person is such in himself that his perceptions reach as far as His self-consciousness does; and the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father has all these powers in an absolute and infinite degree.

CHAPTER XV 

The body apart from the spirit is dead, as the spirit is the lifegiving, functioning, motive or executive power of the body of one's person, as it is the spirit which gives the body all of its perceptions or functioning powers such as willing, choosing, designing, purposing, executing, hearing, seeing, smelling, tasting, feeling, thinking, loving, hating, joy, sorrow, shame, contempt, meekness, kindness, sympathy, charity, forgiveness, and every known virtue or vice.

Our Divine Father in heaven appointed His glorious first-born Son of all creation, the Word, not only to create the human race but to instruct it also, so the Word placed the man and the woman He made in a garden called Eden; and He said to them, "yea, hath 

God said that ye may freely eat of all the fruits and vegetables of the garden with but the one exception of the tree of knowledge of good and evil, of it thou shalt not eat neither shall ye touch it lest ye die."

God's glorious Son the Word looked after and took care of the man and his wife and warned them against the partaking of the forbidden fruit; but Satan, more cunning than the inexperienced couple beguiled the woman into partaking of the forbidden fruit who gave also to her husband and he likewise did eat of it which God commanded they should not do; but God foreknew they would fall to the test, so as to show them how dependent they are on Him in all things; and God had provided that through their rearing of children, He would send to them His glorious Son the Word incarnated in a robe of flesh by being conceived and generated by a virgin woman born under the law which they transgressed; and in order to redeem them from under the curse of the law of sin and death, the Word became incarnated and was called Jesus the Christ, God's only begotten Son.

The time between the promise of the redeemer to Adam until the redeemer came into the world was some four thousand years; but to our Divine Father it was as yesterday as "a thousand years is with the Lord as one day, and one day as a thousand years." During these four thousand years from the time of the promise of the re- 296

deemer until He came, God's glorious Son the Word, looked after the care of Adam and his posterity through all their generations until He came as the incarnate redeemer. During all these long centuries, God's glorious Son, the superangelical Word and firstborn creature of all His Divine Father's creation was instructing Adam and his generations through the Patriachs, Moses, Isaiah, Elisha, Elijah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, Daniel, and a host of others, giving them laws and rules for their instruction and conduct, by which they were to keep in remembrance through sacrifices and burnt offerings, the promised redeemer, until the promised redeemer should come. So the oldest male child of each father's household was chosen with but a few Divine exceptions as the representative of his father's household in the line of descent until the promised redeemer should come after sixty-two generations. Every care was taken to keep the pre-chosen line of descent from being broken, and the laws, rules and regulations were such as to keep ever fresh in the minds of the people through which the promised Messiah or redeemer was to come, so God through His glorious Son the Word, calls Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob whose children were called Israel by Divine appointment. The Israelites migrated into Egypt and served the Egyptians four hundred years, until the Son of God, by Divine command, calls Moses to lead the children of Israel out of 

Egyptian bondage, and God's glorious first-born Son of all creation, the Word leads and guides, protects and preserves them from their enemies for forty years in the wilderness until He brings them safe into the land of Canaan which our Divine Father in heaven had promised to give to Abraham and his children as a possession of inheritance forever.

It is our Divine Father's first-born Son of all creation, His glorious Word who guided the children of Israel by the means of cloud by day and by a pillar of fire by night during their forty years stay in the wilderness; who was called the angel of the covenant, who gave Moses the ten commandments and the law on the Mount of Sinai, and thus the promised redeemer, the unincarnate Word, God's first-born Son of all creation, was ever with the children of Israel leading, guiding and protecting them until His incarnation when He gave to them by the grace of God a New Covenant in His blood by offering Himself as a vicarious atonement, so that whosoever would be penitent and accept Him as their Savior and Redeemer should not perish but have everlasting life. So precious was

Israel in the sight of our Divine Father in heaven that He gave His only begotten Son, His first-born of creation, the glorious Word for the preserving and salvation of the human race. What more is there that people could ask of God? How beautiful, how merciful, how gracious, loving, and compassionate is our Divine Father in heaven toward us! Oh let us be thankful and bow down, let us look up in praise and adoration to our Divine Father, for His mercy endureth forever to them who call Him Father! It is our Divine Father who has all power and authority, and any person, angel or spirit other than our Divine Father who claims any Divine power, authority or acts for himself is a falsifier, a rebel and an heresiarch to God our heavenly Father who only is Divine and can of Himself do Divine acts, or do Divine acts through others by the omnipotent power of 

His Holy Spirit.

Anyone of sound reason; especially after it has once been explained, cannot help but see, if they have any understanding of things whatever, that there cannot be a division of the Divine person power, unity, spirit or attributes of our Divine Father in heaven among a diversity of persons, beings, things, or spirits, as there cannot be a diversity in unity or a plurality of infinites, of uncreates, of omnipotents, of omnisciences, of Deities, of Gods, of Divine

Fathers, of Eternals or of Creators, as one such person excludes all the rest; and hence all must be in subjection to Him in His undivided unity of person, power, and authority which is absolute and independent of all others individually or collectively. 

The unity of person or identity of person, of existence or of power is not possible to a diversity of infinite, omnipotent, independent beings, as the unity of person, power and authority is not possible to more than one such person or being, for one such person excludes there being any other; and as there cannot be a diversity or plurality of persons in a person as two are opposites to one and cannot be true for they are contrary to each other, which would be the same as saying, that thing is that which it is not; and, if any should say that one is from the other, then that which is derived in any way, it will be found to be dependent and finite, as there cannot be but one infinite uncreate, independent or absolute being; and therefore, God subsists in but one person or unit; and He is the source from which all things else derive their existence and powers, as only He who is underived, uncreate or unoriginate is God; and all things

else derive their existence and powers from Him as their Creator, and giver of all that they are and have. 

God, our heavenly Father, remained God, after the creation of His first-born of all creatures, persons or spirits was created; with the additional titles of Creator and Father by reason of His firstborn Son's creation; and it is an error, a misnomer and a falsity to speak of Christ as the Divine Son, the Son God, the God Son, or God the Son; and they are demons, heresiarchs, reprobates and villains who will intentionally, knowingly, wilfully and deliberately misrepresent Jesus Christ in that way. It is satanic and unchristian to represent our Divine Father as changing His person, nature, essence, substance, unity, power, authority and attributes in His creating and begetting of the incarnate Word Jesus Christ, as Father and Creator are merely added titles which were applicable to Him and to Him only upon the creation of His first-born Son of all creation, the Word, but this did not add another Divine person to the Deity or to the Deity's person, our Divine Father, or add another coequal, coessential, coeternal, person to the godhead of the Deity to be worshipped as Divine, for the originating of the Word by His creation by the Father, the Word was not made a Divine person but the Son and first-born creature of God. Thus the Word's originator is His God, Creator and Father by reason of His origination of the Word. But this creation of the Word by the Father does not affect the Divinity of the Father's person, power, nature, essence, substance or unity as He cannot be either diminished, added to or changed, as all the powers, attributes, qualities of our Divine Father are inherent in His person without division or parts; and it makes no difference how He exercises His person and powers He is the only uncreate, absolute or independent one.

Our Divine Father who is form, existence and symmetry in Himself and is of one unit or one person only, operates of Himself, because He is uncreate and independent in His person, existence, and powers as He only is eternal in Himself, of Himself, and by Himself; but all things else are objects of His creation and exist from 

Him in time through creation by Him.

There can be no reciprocation with the Divine person and attributes between our Divine Father in heaven and any other person, as this would compromise or destroy the unity of His person and Divinity which consists and subsists in but one person only, as it cannot belong to more than one person, nor can it be transferred

divided or added to, parceled out or diminished, as it is a unit in itself and even our Doctors Divinitis cannot change it; but there are millions of the followers of the Antichrist, the man of sin who calls himself the vicegerent of God and vicar of Jesus Christ, who say that the Pope of Rome has done it. But this is impossible, that the Deity could be divided into a diversity of persons even by our Divine Father Himself, who can do everything that is an object of power, but He cannot deny Himself or perform that which is contrary to Himself, as His uncreativeness, absoluteness, and independency, and oneness cannot be changed either by Himself or others, for in the very nature of things He is the absolute power and controller of all things without reservation or limitation; as no other person can be Divine or a part of the Divine, for that which is Divine is uncreate, absolute or independent which belongs solely to our Divine Father in heaven.

Since our Divine Father in heaven is the Creator of all things the terms God, Father or Creator are applicable only to Him, as His Divinity is dependent upon His independency, absoluteness and uncreativeness of His origin which no other person whatsoever possesses, as there cannot be more than one absolute and independent person. For example, we call Christ the Son of God, of the Eternal, of the Divine, of the Deity, of the Father, of the Creator, and of Jehovah and the mere fact that we say He is of or from God is absolute and unqualified proof that He is not the Deity or any part of Him, for the title Son of God or any other of these synonymous titles distinguishes Him from God, as it would for one to say that he is from Boston would distinguish his person from the City of Boston as no one would claim that they are synonymous or alike. 

Men can make Boston, but it takes God to make men, so God can make the incarnate Word Jesus Christ, but ever so many people like Jesus Christ could never make God or any part of Him or be a part of Him.

Jesus Christ who is the only begotten Son and heir of our Divine Father in heaven is the greatest creature of all our Divine Father's creation, as well as the first who had precedence over all others in creation, so much so that our Divine Father created all things else of His creation through His Holy Spirit by His agency. No one can be great with God save through love, obedience and service even if that special service is rendered by the choice of our Divine Father as to who shall render it, as there are but few who would want to

be crucified for the sins of the world even though it were God's choice that it should be so; for the great majority even of professed 

Christians shun to keep oftentimes even the small courtesies of life to those in need if they have to make any sacrifice to do so. Christ who being the superangelical Son of God in His antemundane or preincarnation state of existence was more competent to do the wondrous and glorious services which He performed than any other creature of our Divine Father's creation, and for this reason our Divine Father chose Him as His agent in the creation of all things, and in the redemption of the world through incarnation, and selfimmolation as a vicarious atonement for the sins of man as the Son of Man though He be God's only begotten and well-beloved Son.

Our Divine Father and His glorious Son the incarnate Word, Jesus Christ, are one in all that His Divine Father would have Him do no matter how difficult a task His Divine Father assigns Him to do, as our Divine Father never assigns anyone a task to perform, but that He gives Him the help, power and authority to perform it. 

This oneness Jesus expresses in a prayer, “As thou Father are in me, and I in thee, that they, my disciples, also may be one in us 

I in thee, and thou in me, and I in them." Christ prays that we might be one with Him, the same as He is one with God, His Divine Father in heaven. So we are to be one in Christ the same as Christ is one with His Divine Father in obedience, love, communion and fellowship of spirit. "Believe me, the words I speak unto you, I speak. not of myself, but the spirit of my Father which dwelleth in me speaks the words and doeth the works through me. Believe me that 

I am in the Father, and the Father in me or else believe me for the very works' sake, for I can do nothing of myself, it is my Father's spirit doing these works through me."

It is through obedience and devotion to God then, that a person becomes one with God, not one person, but one in conjunction of harmony and agreement with the Divine will and purposes, in all that which God would have him to do; and those who quote the words of Jesus with the intention of trying to enforce the false idea that there is no difference between Christ's Divine Father and Himself, when He says times and again that "My Father is greater than I, my Father is greater than all, I can do nothing of myself, it is my Father who doeth the works;" and those who contend that Christ is coequal, coessential, and coeternal with His Divine Creator and

Father are stupid, silly ignoramuses, and deceivers of themselves and others.

The spirit of creating, of life, of wisdom, of knowledge and of power is individually fixed and inherent in our Divine Father in heaven forever in whom there is no variableness neither shadow of turning while all created things are finite and changeable by virtue of their creation, for all such in their nature are recipients of our Divine Father's great condescension of creation and owe their existence of contiguity to the power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father, and this is the only way that anything can come into existence and conjunction with His Divine Creator, our heavenly Father. Thus, it is plain that everything Divine belongs absolutely, or exclusively to our Divine Father in heaven; and that nothing of the Divine can come into the possession or be appropriated by another as his very own, as nothing of the Divine can be disjoined from the Divine for all that is belongs to Him without exception; but the power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father may be communicated to any person of our Divine Father's creation so as use His agency or person as a medium through which prophecy and the working of miracles may be performed when such person is subservient to the will of God.

The Divine is Divine only in itself and is incommunicable so that which proceeds from God of any tangible material nature cannot be of His own person but a creation, as God does not dispense with anything of Himself in either person or power as not belonging to Himself.

Our Divine Father is the only uncreate, unoriginate, eternal existence, and the source from which all things else received their origination or beginning as an existence, of which God's glorious first-born Son, the Word, was the beginning of God's creation, the first-born of God's creatures. But there is a great diversity of difference between the creature and his Divine Creator in their person, nature, essence, power and authority as the creature is dependent in all things while the Creator is independent in all things. God, our heavenly Father, is absolute and independent in all things, while God's glorious Son the incarnate Word, Jesus Christ, is finite and dependent in all things, as all that He is, has, and does, belong to His Divine Father the author of His person, doctrine, and works, as His God, Creator, and Father.

Some who read these lines will complain of useless iteration of

pleonastic words and tautological sentences; but are you sure that you understand these things? Perhaps, there are those who have less education than yourself; and many others there are who have deep-seated bias, and are prejudiced against anything that they have not received from the Antichrist, the man of sin and son of perdition, the Pope of Rome, who calls himself 'the vicegerent of God, vicar of Jesus Christ, and Pontifex Maximus with complete ecclesiastical and civil jurisdiction over the world by virtue of his office as God's representative. 

All who follow the direction of God's Holy Spirit in obedience to the gospel of Jesus Christ will abide forever; for the power of our 

Divine Father's Holy Spirit will take charge, and care for all who are children of God, but none others; for man's liberty and rationality or free moral agency are from God and not from himself; but 

God has given them to us to act as from ourself that we may choose to make our wills and affections His; and when we refuse to permit our Divine Father to direct that which we have from Him, we will be lost beyond recovery; for all things which we have from our 

Divine Father are for good uses only, and all who deny our Divine 

Father's ownership in them will perish everlastingly; for such an one denies or does not acknoweldge that he is from our Divine Father or that he owes his being and allegiance to Him. 

A person may know at any time whether he belongs to our Divine Father or not, as it depends upon his own spirit of self-surrender and obedience to will to do the will of God; for the spirit of God always bears witness to our spirit of approval or disapproval, and therefore each one can know personally whether he is approved or disapproved by his own spirit's approbation or disapproval in his relationship to God.

The Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven is the creator and dispensor of all powers and gifts according to our Divine Father's will and purposes, as this power on Christ's disciples was greatly manifest on the day of Pentecost when a diversity of gifts were given according to the office each was chosen to fill such as prophecy, interpretation, faith, discerning of spirits, wisdom, miracles, tongues, healing and teaching. These gifts of the Holy Spirit are to be had from our Divine Father only, whose spirit the Holy Spirit is; and our Divine Father's glorious incarnate Word Jesus 

Christ said: "If ye who are evil know how to give good gifts to your

children how much more will your Father in heaven give the Holy 

Spirit to them who ask Him."

There is no media between the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father and us save in exceptional cases our Divine Father sends special agents in the form of prophets to declare His will and purposes, but further than that our Divine Father always deals with us directly, as the Divine wisdom, knowledge, power, miracles, discernment of spirits, and every gift and grace come from our Divine Father through His Holy Spirit whether immediately, or mediately, as in the case of the prophets, Jesus Christ and His apostles who operated and taught by the direction and power of the Holy Spirit of our 

Divine Father. "When ye are persecuted for righteousness' sake take no thought aforehand what ye shall say or what ye shall do, for it shall be given you in that hour what ye shall speak and what ye shall do, for it is not ye that speaketh but the spirit of your 

Father in heaven speaking and acting through you, and ye are not to do anything of yourselves."

We are not to do like the Roman Catholics do, who confess to the priest, who confess to the bishop, who confess to the archbishop, who confess to the cardinal, who confess to the Pope, who confess to Jesus Christ, who confess to the Virgin Mary, "Mother of God," who confess to the Trinity, who confess to the triune God; and thus many a poor penitent soul has died in his sins before he could get returns through all this media of confessions; and the priest has cast many a soul into purgatory where either himself or his friends were made to pay a considerable sum of money to get the priest to say masses for his poor soul before he would release him from purgatory.

Our Divine Father in heaven rules everything by the omnipotent power of His spirit so that all contrite confessions come directly into the presence of our Divine Father and are forgiven while we are yet speaking without any mediator or sacrifice other than that made by Jesus Christ when He died on Mount Calvary nigh unto 

Jerusalem in Judea of Palestine. 

The Holy Spirit of our Divine Father governs all life, being, power, wisdom, knowledge, understanding, perceptions, and motives, and foreknew what all of our thoughts and actions would be before creation.

As the spirit of a person is all inclusive in the person whose spirit it is, the Holy Spirit is inclusive in the person of our Divine Father

in heaven whose spirit the Holy Spirit is and cannot be considered. as a unit, entity or person apart from our Divine Father's person whose spirit the Holy Spirit is; and apart from our Divine Father's person neither the Holy Spirit nor the person of our Divine Father could have any existence, as it takes both the body of His person and His spirit to constitute a person, as that which is without spirit is without life and there cannot be such a thing as a person without life or spirit; and to ascribe the workings of the Holy Spirit of our 

Divine Father to other individuals whose spirit the Holy Spirit is not, such as to the prophets, to Jesus Christ, to Christ's apostles or to any other's indued with the Holy Spirit, the spirit of whose person the Holy Spirit is not, would be like ascribing the work of a painter to the brush or instrument that is moved by his hand instead of to the person whose spirit governed the brush by the means of his hand.

It is by the means of our Divine Father's spirit that people have both body and spirit called person; when the two, body and spirit are united; but when the spirit is separated from the body it is no longer a person, it is a corpse which was the body of some person when the spirit was united with the body. So it is with the spirit of 

God, if taken from our Divine Father it destroys our Divine Father's person or personality; and it is a falsity and a misnomer for anyone to say that the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father, and our Divine Father are two persons which the Antichrist doctrine calls God the Father and God the Holy Ghost. So the Holy Spirit is the motive or life-giving properties which is the existence and the life to the immortality of God's person whom we call our Divine Father.

It is in the province of our Divine Father in heaven through the omnipotent power of His spirit to give form and life to material things by bringing the spiritual and material together and to separate the one from the other whenever it suits His Divine Providence and purposes so to do, and to reunite them through the resurrection from the dead. As the life of our body is dependent upon the breath of our spirit which in turn is dependent upon the breath of God's spirit He can withdraw His breath from us forever when it is to the welfare of His creatures to do so; for the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father acts upon both what is spiritual and what is material according to His will; so if the life of God's Spirit which gives existence and life to our spirit abides in us we shall live forever in the spirit; for as our Divine Father has independent life in

Himself by His spirit which is absolute and independent, so will He give life unto us if we abide in His love through obedience. 

The end for which God created us is that there might be an eternal conjunction or communion of His spirit with all the rational spirits of His creation; and this is possible only where the spirit of the Divine Father can be in His subjects as in Himself which is to occupy our bodies as dwelling places or tabernacles of His Holy Spirit. If we would be eternally the recipients of the life, love, wisdom and power of our Divine Father's holy spirit which can be had only through faith and good works, seek the gift of God's spirit of the life eternal by preparing yourself through faith and good works for a glad and glorious resurrection at the appearing of Jesus Christ on His return to earth.

The conation, force, motion, power and executive ability of our Divine Father in heaven is exercised only and always by His spirit for He operates in no other way but by His spirit whether immediately or mediately, and no Divine power can be exercised but by our Divine Father's spirit.

Our Divine Father's first-born Son of all creation, the incarnate Word Jesus Christ, who now sits at the right hand of the power and majesty of His Divine Creator and Father, who, having performed in His own person all that His Divine Father had promised to Adam, the patriarchs, Moses and the prophets, "that the promised redeemer would fulfill in the redeeming of the human race by giving His flesh for the life of the world." He has accomplished in His vicarious death on Mount Calvary all that the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father had foreordained that He should accomplish as our 

Lord and Redeemer.

God created men and angels rational beings with the power of discriminating between the good and the evil, that man might know the truth and do the good; for truth and good enters into charity, and purifies the mind, body and spirit of the person for the reception of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven which enters only where love to God and love to one's neighbor are manifested; and just to the extent that one loves to serve is he in the Divine favor, and just to the extent that one loves to rule is he opposed to his Divine Creator. "Christ came into the world not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give His life as a ransom for many."

In a broad sense, spirit, may be spoken of as synonymous with

character, good or bad, as a person may show a kind spirit or an evil spirit according to its training, characteristics or disposition in its treatment of others; but it is all foolishness and nonsense for one to try to think of character or spirit separate or apart from the person whose spirit or character is under discussion, for character or spirit apart from all personality is an illusion, a mere phantom of the brain, a nonentity or nothingness; as no one can be a person apart from his spirit, as spirit is synonymous only with person, as there is absolutely no such a thing as person without spirit, as a person is a person only inclusive with spirit and not without it, as it is the life, motive or executive power of one's person; and when 

Jesus Christ tells His disciples so many times that the gifts of the Holy Spirit proceed from His Divine Father, it is not to be understood that one part of the person of our Divine Father proceeds from Himself so that He becomes divided into two equal parts so that the spirit or executive part proceeds from the material part, so that the material part is left without a spirit, and the spirit part is left without a body; but it is to be understood by the Holy Spirit proceeding from the Father, that it is the power, authority, gifts or induements of the Holy Spirit which proceed from our Divine Father and not a person proceeding from His person which would be the same as saying that He is proceeding from Himself, which is pure nonsense. Our Divine Father without His spirit would have no existence nor could our Divine Father have any life, motive or executive power without His spirit, for the spirit of a person does not exist apart from the person whose spirit it is as the spirit of God is the spirit of God's person, and without His spirit He would not be anything, a mere nothingness or nonentity.

No doubt, the Son of God, Jesus Christ, will class with Annas, the Jewish high priest, Caiphas, Herod, Pilate or a Judas, anyone who thus crucifies Him with their blasphemies by calling Him God the

Son, the Son God, the God Son or the Divine Son instead of the Son of God or the Son of the Divine Father; for there is nothing so wicked, mean, insolent, ungodly, villainous and satanic as to accuse the loving, compassionate and beneficent Son of God as claiming an equality with His Divine Father in heaven, the Creator of His being, and the giver of all that He is and has. Let no one try to persuade you that Jesus Christ claimed to be on an equality with 

His infinite, omnipotent, uncreate, independent, unoriginate God,

Creator and Father for it is the greatest of all blasphemies against God's loving, filial, dutiful, Son and Mediator. 

Oh, the pity, that those who wish to be known as friends of Jesus

Christ have joined with the antichristians, the enemies of Jesus Christ in order to gain popularity, fame, renown, wealth and position in the Church. By joining themselves to the man of sin, the 

Pope of Rome who has blasphemed the holy name of Jesus above fifteen hundred years, they become enemies of God by calling His Son Jesus Christ a Divine person in the Godhead of His Deity by saying that His Son Jesus Christ is coequal, coessential and coeternal, and equal in power, glory and honor with His Divine Father. 

It is simply the worst crime of which anyone can be guilty to brand the Son of God as a usurper, impostor and rebel by claiming equal power, glory and honor, with equal right to His Divine Father's throne, worship and adoration; and it is using mild language to say that all who say such things are heresiarchs, rebels, villains and reprobates to our Divine Father and to His Son Jesus Christ. 

Evils and falsities are in complete opposition to goods and truths, because evils and falsities are diabolical and infernal, while goods and truths are Divine and heavenly; and there never was so wicked, sinful, degrading, hellish, villainous and satanic a lie ever uttered against Jesus Christ as, "that He is a person in the Godhead of our Divine Father in heaven," because it is not only a lie, but the most destructive lie that was ever fostered upon the world of mankind; for it has caused, in order to maintain it, more suffering, bloodshed, heresy and division among the followers of Jesus Christ than any lie that men or demons have been able to bring against the Church; and still this very evil, heathenish, and antichrist doctrine of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person was born, reared and developed within the Church until it became the most bloody, brutish, villainous, ungodly, satanic, hellish and murderous monster which ever appeared upon the earth to curse and destroy the gospel of Jesus Christ, by destroying His followers, and causing infidelity, misery and crime in the Church through persecutions, and causing the non-religious world to reject it as unreasonable, absurd, inconsistent, contradictory and unscientific.

The day is at hand when the world will begin to see and know that this antichrist doctrine of the Trinity of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person is not the gospel of Jesus Christ, but the

Doctrine of the Antichrist whose doctrine is in opposition to Jesus 

Christ as the Son of God.

The devil is straining every fiber of his being to engage all the Doctors Divinitis as his coadjutors to assist him in overthrowing the doctrine that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, by making out that He is a person in the Godhead of the Deity; and that He has no 

God nor Father as He is coequal with two other like persons in the Deity of which He is called the second Divine person in the Trinity of three Divine coequal, coessential, coeternal persons.

These Antichrist coadjutors would persuade the world that the title, "Son of God," is a misnomer when applied to Jesus Christ, as the Son of God as such, for they say that Christ Jesus is as much God or Deity as our Divine Father in heaven; and that there is none greater than Christ is great, although Christ says: "My Father is greater than I, my Father is greater than all." Oh, they say! "Christ is here speaking in His human nature, but in His Divine nature He is God, and the title "Son of God" is not applicable to Him in His Divine nature, as He is God incarnate and at His death the human nature was absorbed into the Divine nature by the hypostatical union or homoousian of the Son of God into God," which scheme of the Antichrist denies both the Father and the Son which the scriptures condemn as the antichrist doctrine which they foretold would come into the world!

We are well aware that we will be cursed and condemned as a heretic by the churchmen for calling the attention of the world to the falsities of these Trinitarian doctrines of the Antichrist; but we would by far, rather prefer to have the curse and wrath of men pronuonced upon us in performance of our duty, than to have the wrath and curse of God pronounced upon us for the non-performance of our duty, when we feel in conscience bound to expose the antichrist doctrine of the Trinity for the relief of the world from the thraldom of slavery to the Antichrist, and his minions. 

There are many ministers of this satanic antichristian Trinitarian doctrine who would much rather that we would not say anything about the absurdities, inconsistencies and contradictions of their satanic doctrines; which are blasphemies of God and a curse to mankind; but for us to speak or not to speak of these things is to us no more a question as to what we should do, our duty and our responsibility are clear, although we admit that our free moral agency and rationality give us the power to refrain from speaking; but what

good merit or virtue would be derived for acting like Jonah to shirk responsibility until it is literally and physically forced upon us to our own condemnation, "For he that knoweth to do good and then doeth it not to him it is sin," and sin when brought to full fruitage brings forth death and destruction.

Freedom and liberty in the strictest sense belong only to the good and the true; for anyone who abuses his freedom and rationality by thinking and doing what is evil is not in freedom but in slavery, bondage, death and destruction.

The Holy Spirit of our Divine Father apart from space fills all space, and apart from time fills all time, for it is the infinite life, power, and authority of our Divine Father's person; and only so long as the spirit of man retains conjunction with our Divine Father's eternal life-giving Spirit will he have life in himself from God through the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father; as our Divine Father's spirit of life and power operates everywhere and in everything according to His will.

In the spiritual world the same as in the material world everything derives its existence from God and is terminated at His pleasure, so God has appointed a day of judgment in which He will terminate the life and existence of all that is out of harmony with Him by withdrawing the life-giving and sustaining power of His spirit from all such, and cast him, as it were, into a lake of fire of annihilation or oblivion, without a trace of life or being remaining to curse and blight the things of His kingdom.

The spirit of our Divine Father being ubiquitous or omnipresent in power, discernment, understanding and executive ability cannot go or return from anywhere as to be absent or not present; even in hell or the most secret places; for apart from the spirit of God's power and presence nothing can exist, not even our Divine Father Himself; for no person, being or thing can exist apart from it, as all things are dependent upon our Divine Father's omnipotent, creative, and life-giving spirit, as all being, power and authority are derived. from it and controlled by it, save that our Divine Father permits men and angels to exercise their rationality or free moral agency, but limits to some such power in duration of time who choose to use it for evil or bad uses.

The Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven is the means of all contact, conjunction, communication, executive power and authority between our Divine Father and His creation; and only as

our Divine Father gives power and authority can others work; for without the motive or executive power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven neither our Divine Father nor any other person can do anything, as the absolute and independent spirit of our Divine Father is the sole or only means by which our Divine Father conjoins the universe or all creation to Himself with absolute power and authority over all things.

The presence and power of our Divine Father's Holy Spirit is in contact with everything, and there is absolutely nothing that exists apart from its power and authority; and those who conjoin themselves to God by obedience and devotion will not come into judgment of the second death, but will be made immortal and given the life eternal.

In God's favor there is life and love, joy and peace, happiness and heaven, but in rebellion there is misery, hell and destruction. Therefore, man must be at one with God by correspondences which means subjection to the will power and authority of our Divine Father in heaven through the full obedience of our person to Him, as our Divine Father and all things of His creation must act only and always from the omnipotent power of our Divine Father's Holy Spirit and not otherwise, if they would be in love and union with our 

Divine Father.

Our Divine Father cannot and does not act contrary to His Holy Spirit, but always in harmony with it; and all things of our Divine 

Father's creation, and there is no person, being, or thing which our Divine Father has not created other than His own person, must act from the omnipotent power of our Divine Father's spirit, though there be many who do not act in accordance with the will of our Divine Father; but those who knowingly, wilfully and deliberately refuse to do our Divine Father's will, and repent not of their evil ways will be destroyed in the day of judgment.

The uses and means for receiving and retaining the spiritual conjunction with the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father are many and various, such as all things which teach us the knowledge and the acknowledgement of God, such as the attributes and powers of man for accomplishment of good and truth by reading of good books, hearing lectures and sermons on Divine things, reading the scriptures, prayer, contemplation, and even the material things such as food, clothing, habitation, recreation, preservation and health besides our mental, moral, and spiritual powers for love, truth, wisdom and

knowledge should be regarded as gifts and blessings from our Divine Creator.

The essence of all spiritual love, human and Divine, is doing good to others for the sake of others; and this readily brings one into conjunction with God through correspondences or likenesses with the Divine attributes. All works of charity are well pleasing to God and rewarded by Him; for the purposes of God are that everything 

He has created be appropriated to good uses for His glory and for the good of His creatures. Therefore, let no one think that the Lord our God is with those who merely go to Church and worship Him with their lips, for I tell you it not so; but He is with those who worship Him by doing His commandments through the performing of good works such as giving to charity and neighborly conduct. 

It is the Spirit of God which impels and compels nature to act; but God has given to man rationality and liberty or free moral agency so that he might act of choice, as of himself; to do God's will, or even to act in a finite way and for a limited time contrary to our Divine Father's will, as it has pleased God to grant man the power to love, honor, worship, obey and adore Him as from Himself through voluntary service and adoration. Thus, while God furnishes the motive power for every individual to act, He does not compel man's obedience in any given way, but gives man the power of voluntary choice, and puts him upon his own responsibility after giving him instructions concerning the doing of His will, as to how He desires man to perform it; and so long as man seeks to do his 

Creator's will, so long shall he be in God's favor which is life eternal and everlasting blessedness; but he who chooses to rebel against our 

Divine Father's authority shall be cut off from life. 

That there is a spiritual world distinct from the natural or material world and far superior to it is a matter of revelation as well as of personal knowledge; and the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven is just as essential to His life, being and executive powers as our spirit is to us, for there can be no such thing as person without it; and this is the reason why many of those who have written on the origin of plants and animals could not do otherwise than ascribe their origin to a Divine Creator who planted in nature from the beginning of things the power of life and reproduction, as nature which in itself originally had no life of itself, and had no power of producing itself from a dead, seething, burning nebulous mass of gaseous nebulae before the earth was sufficiently cooled for the sus-

taining and reproducing of life, as everything we see in nature is dependent upon something former to itself, so there was a time when nature was not, and that less than fifteen thousand years ago, as the present is to be judged by what we see of the past in its entirety, for the oldest things preceded man according to zoology and Divine revelation only a few thousand years, as man was made in the sixth grand division of time as the crowning work of our Divine Father's creation of the things of this earth. Nature in its first stages preceded man only a few thousand years in its first stages of development as all our plants and animals can very hurriedly be traced back to its original stock.

Many of the animals placed on this earth by the Creator had but a very short duration, as there are so very few specimens found; but they served their purpose of showing the marvelous power, genius and variety of conception of our Divine Creator, and man has preserved only what was especially beneficial or useful to him. 

That which is dead can contribute no more to the production of nature than a tool in the hands of a workman, for it is only the omnipotent spirit of our Divine Father in heaven that can impart and sustain life in that which in itself was formerly dead, and give to it, its nature and powers of reproduction, producing after its own kind and nature; and so inexorable or unchangeable is this law of 

God in nature that no earthly power that be, can materially change their course of nature; for the powers of God in nature are so strongly fixed that as soon as man ceases to work for their domestication they take the course God implanted in their original state, and everything after its own kind and family.

God, our heavenly Father, saw fit to give rationality and liberty or free moral agency to man after His own likeness, and therefore man is capable of reasoning, and capable of being governed by civil, moral and spiritual laws, while all other anthropoids such as the gorilla, the monkey, the orang, the chimpanzee and the baboon and such like other animals are irrational and irresponsible, because they are incapable of perceiving or knowing the rightness or the wrongness of things through their senses, and they can be trained to do only a very few things by association without perceiving the reason why; for they have no initiative or power of discernment by which they lay up or store away provisions for themselves or build a shelter as a home to protect themselves from the elements of inclement weather.
