Ignorance might excuse those who never heard of our Divine Creator and Father, if they perceive that man sprang from monkey and that he has developed far beyond his maker in knowledge, wisdom and power who was irrational, irresponsible and unaccountable to anyone; but those who have an experimental knowledge of an intellectual certainty of our Divine Creator and of His dealings with man know of the falsity of these monkey doctrines, for these falsities of evolution cohere with evil the oftener they are repeated which make people feel that they are irresponsible, irrational creatures who owe no allegiance to a Divine Creator; and such evils as evolution cohere with hell, and hell with destruction of man's soul in the second death at the day of judgment.

Those who ascribe creation to chance or nature, and say that nature produced them, merely perceive that these things exist, and they say these things because they have turned their minds away from thinking about the Divine; and those who do these things are unable when they want to think rationally and spiritually cannot, because they have thought sensually and materially so long that they have become fixed in their character and thought just like others who are doomed for hell and destruction.

Those who ascribe everything to nature differ from beasts only in having the power to think rationally, if they would; that is, in being able to understand, but who have averted themselves from thinking about the Divine when observing the wonderful things of nature. They become sensual and do not reflect that the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven only has power to organize and furnish with untold millions of fibers and vessels, heart and pulmonary tubes, viscera and brains woven out of the purest substances with every tissue corresponding to the will of our spirit, shows how wonderful God is above all that man can do or think or even comprehend the smallest part. Those who think that a monkey formed these things shows how dull, vulgar and profane such peoples' minds are; and what thick darkness they are in concerning spiritual things when all of these manifest proofs of a Divine Creator go to show that our Divine Father in heaven brings about all that comes to pass through the omnipotent creative and sustaining power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father who gave existence and its nature to all things. "God is love," and God's spirit is life, love, wisdom and power, and man cannot become the express image and likeness of God until

He becomes perfected in love toward God and toward his neighbor; for the spirit of man controls the will and governs the body in conformity or obedience to its mind in so far as the body is capable of performing or doing what the spirit desires, as it is the media of all Divine and spiritual contact. It is therefore incumbent upon our spirit to will to be governed by the highest, holiest and most amiable conception of what we believe the will of our Divine Father in heaven, so that we may have contact, communion or conjunction with the Holy Spirit of our Divine Creator in all things, so that our conscience or the mind of our spirit may be at-one-ment with the 

Holy Spirit of our Divine Father.

Our Divine Father knows our many imperfections through the media of His omnipotent, ubiquitous spirit which wishes our perfection; but our Father knows our frame, that we are weak in will, in knowledge, in body, in understanding of what is truth and right, so He has given to our spirit that power of discernment called conscience which registers the highest conception of truth and right according to its knowledge and judgment of what is truth and right, and it is the deciding factor as to our duty and responsibility; and our only unerring guide, not as to what is truth and right, but as to what is our duty and responsibility; as to what we think is truth and right; and in our imperfect state of existence we are to follow conscience when we do not know what is truth and right, as conscience is the arbiter of what we feel, as to what is right and wrong. 

By unerring guide we do not mean that our conscience is perfect or unerring as to truth and right, as it is not immune to falsities, error, misconceptions or mistakes; but it is the highest arbiter of what we believe to be the highest good, truth, right, or proper thing to do. Conscience is not a pefect guide; but to follow its highest conception of right at all times is to free one from wilful and deliberate sin; is to free one from moral transgression so far as he individually is concerned; but the moment the knowledge of error or wrong through an enlightened conscience enters his consciousness that his former status was wrong he is duty bound to live up to the enlightened intelligence or he will be guilty of wilful sin, though it be a complete reversal or facing about as to what he formerly believed to be right and proper for him to sav, do, or think. If we do not follow conscience in its highest conception of truth and responsibility as we understand it, it will immediately accuse us of wrong doing even though we may have done what is right in what we

thought to be wrong, as our conscience only decides for us what is our highest conception of right even though we err in our judgment. 

Conscience is generally right and one must follow it right or wrong if he would shield himself from conscious transgression which is sin though he might be doing what is right. Our highest conception of right, duty and responsibility, however, is not always right, far from it, but conscience is always to be followed at all times through the changing scenes and vicissitudes of life; and if we do this we shall never wilfully and deliberately commit sin, and will be forgiven through the vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ for all such inadvertences or transgressions of God's law of truth and right because of ignorance of right and truth when we have sought to do the will of God in all things.

A transgression of God's law in good faith of doing God's will unknowingly and ignorantly is not a wilful, deliberate sin so long as one does not refuse to repent of error when knowledge of truth and right presents itself. It is our bounden duty to change our conduct in thought, word, and deed so as to be in harmony to our highest intelligence as to what is right; and strive to be in perfect conformity with a progressive enlightened conscience which should always change with its knowledge of truth; for God desires that we live up to our enlightened and highest conception of duty and of responsibility or sin lies at the door; and must be repented, confessed and forsaken before we can be right with God. 

Rationality, knowledge or understanding belongs to every normal person by creation, and the discernment of one's spirit called conscience is the capacity to understand things interiorly as the deciding factor as to what is just and right, good and true, for by it man is distinguished above all the other creatures of the earth as the crowning work of God upon the earth.

The spirit of man is not alone in general but in every particular the perpetual conatus of the human soul for the reason that it is the life and volition or functioning executive of our body as it cannot act without it, for the spirit of life acts through the blood; and the moment the body is injured to the extent that the spirit which is the life in the blood of the body can no longer act through the body for the repairing of the body separation takes place and the body dies and the spirit departs to its own place. The good spirits go to the place known as paradise where Jesus' spirit went between His death and resurrection; and those who are good, come into this

place of waiting until the day of the resurrection when they shall enter into the kingdom of God, and forever shall they be with the Lord; but the spirits of the wicked go to their waiting place of torment called hell; and those who come into this place of torment stay here until the day of judgment when they shall be called forth from their graves and be cast into the lake of fire which God has prepared for the wicked, the devil and his angels; and the devil and his angels and all the bad people who have lived unrepentent toward 

God shall suffer everlasting destruction.

The life of the soul is the spirit and its affections, and those who live after the spirit shall regain through the resurrection from the dead the immortality and everlasting life that was promised to Adam had he not have sinned; or the life everlasting promised to those who through faith and repentance toward God accept the vicarious atonement of God's Son and Mediator Jesus Christ. Those who accept Jesus Christ as God's Son and Mediator will be ransomed through Jesus Christ's vicarious atonement unto immortality and the life eternal through the resurrection from the dead at the second coming of Jesus Christ.

CHAPTER XVI 

The soul of man which includes the complete form of man's nervous system with all of its senses and affections belong to the spirit of man whose spirit of understanding and will reaches as far as his self-consciousness does; for that is one person whose spirit knows and feels itself and its own thoughts and notions; for these are the requisite essentials necessary to the spirit of man for the giving of life to the body as that which gives existence and life to our spirit is the infinite ever-living Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven so that we have nothing of ourselves; for we exist only by the holy condescension of God's grace; and those who rebel against 

Him cut off themselves from life, heaven and immortal happiness. 

Thus, for anyone to be selfish, covetous, simonious, ambitious, inordinately desirous of place or power, lovers of self instead of lovers of God and of their fellow-men; who seek personal aggrandizement to the subverting of the will and rights of others to that which is wrong, infernal, or satanic; for these are an abomination in the eyes of the Lord however much it might be esteemed, as wisdom, power, glory or success in the earth or in hell, all such glory, honor, wealth, and position will mean death and everlasting destruction in the day of judgment.

There is nothing in this world quite so precious as being one with Jesus Christ who is one with God, for to be one with Christ is to be in conjunction by correspondences with that which is in harmony or accord with the Divine; for Jesus Christ is in harmony or accord with the Divine in that He always subjects His will to the will of 

His Divine Father in heaven.

Theological students of God's word, power, spirit, character and person, have a peculiar delight and love for knowing, understanding the Divine, the scientific, the moral, the natural and the logical truths and doctrines of the scriptures; and when the holy apostolic writers say from the very lips of God's glorious first-born Son of all creation, the incarnate Word Jesus Christ, that the first and greatest of all the commandments is: "Hear, O Israel! the Lord our

God is one Father," our mind, heart, soul and spirit, consciously and 318

intelligently understands and readily assents that the Lord our God can be but one God or Father; and that to worship Him in spirit and in truth is far better than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.

Our Divine Creator and Father can do no Divine act through one who does not act synchronously with His Holy Spirit; but our 

Divine Father is not dependent for His acts upon anyone; but, as a matter of choice He can act by the omnipotent power of His Holy Spirit of Himself directly without any intervening agency as in the creation of His glorious first-born Son of all creation, “The Word of God" who became the incarnate Word Jesus Christ; but it appears from the teaching of the holy scriptures that God chose to do all other of His acts of creation by the omnipotent power of His Holy Spirit through His glorious first-born Son of all creation, the Word, who became Jesus the Christ. 

Divine love in our person cannot be elevated through anything of honor, glory or gain as an end, but only through the love of good uses, and not for the sake of self, but for the glory of God, and for the sake of our fellow-men, as this love is given by our Divine Father for good uses of charity and of good will toward our neighbor or when man flees from evils as sins. Therefore, it is that heavenly love by which the will of our spirit obtains the means to overcome evil by doing good, for love flourishes when accompanied by good works.

Any rational person can see and intellectually comprehend that so far as one flees from theft, and turns away from cheating, so far he loves sincerity, rectitude, and justice; and so far as he flees and turns away from revenge and hatred so far he loves his neighbor, God and truth; and yet our Divine Father in heaven knows the degree of sincerity, rectitude, justice, charity, chastity, and love of the human heart far better than the individual himself, as our finite minds are incapable of giving to God or to anything else its true worth or value; but for anyone to wilfully and deliberately transgress God's holy commands after so many unerring proofs "That the 

Lord our God is one Father;" and will still persist in his idolatry of worshipping three persons as Divine will have no excuse for their sin of idolatry in the day of judgment.

Those who worship any person or persons other than that of our Divine Father in heaven as Divine are as much idolaters as those who worship idols because all persons other than that of our Divine

Father in heaven have been made or created; and all who worship a plurality of persons or things as Divine show but little if any respect whatever of love, honor or obedience to Jesus Christ and His Divine

Father, when they place God's glorious first-born Son of all created persons, the incarnated Word Jesus Christ on an equality with His 

Divine Creator.

The fact that the Word, God's Son and agent, acted synchronously or in harmony and conjunction with the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father which created all worlds, principalities and powers through Him is sufficient evidence in itself that God's Son cannot be a person in the Divine Godhead of His creator and Father or be a person coequal, coessential and coeternal with Him, for the Son is a created, finite, and dependent person of our Divine Father. 

Christ, the incarnate Word never claimed to be Divine or a part of the Deity nor the whole of Him, but with ever the greatest condescension confessed that He of Himself could do nothing but that it was the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father doing the works of His Father through Him, and that He acted synchronously with the power of the Holy spirit of His Divine Father. 

Christ acted in harmony or unison with the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father in heaven; and without the operating or executive power of the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father working through Christ, Christ could do nothing as He must act synchronously with it or He could not act at all, for it was the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father which did the Divine works of the Father. 

When men and nations live by the spiritual truths and the Divine ideals in the way in which Jesus Christ lived them every heart will be a miniature heaven and every home a paradise; as the greatest, the most sublime, the most wonderful, the most marvelous, the most beneficent, and the most surpassing virtue of Jesus Christ is His love and obedience to His Divine Father.

It is nothing short of criminal to give to children the low, mean, vulgar conception that God is no greater than a glorified man or a person in the likeness of a dove or a pigeon as represented in our picture cards and other paraphernalia used in the Churches and Sunday schools to present to the minds of children and stupid people that God has a face like a Santa Claus, and that His spirit looks like a dove. Those who teach such absurdities, inconsistencies, and contradictions hold that things spiritual and theological transcend the understanding, and are therefore to be held as true, and believed

apart from the understanding; but this is only a hallucination of their brain as no one can believe that which he cannot form a conception or mental picture of; and they do not want to admit that their doctrine of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person is a jumble of falsities, absurdities, inconsistencies and contradictions. 

Such people seem to ignore the capacities called rationality and liberty or free moral agency; for no one can truly believe that which contradicts his own private knowledge of fact; and therefore, most all our present day clergymen deny to their parishioners the powers of rationality or liberty to think for themselves, which they through duress, force them blindly to assent to their absurd, inconsistent, contradictory statements of their doctrine of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person under the threatened penalty of damnation and of heresy. Those too, who hold that no one is able to do good as from himself also deny rationality and liberty; for to do good through obedience of the will and the understanding is the only merit of acceptance with God, for faith without works is dead; and those who hold that man cannot do acts of commendation are false and irrational people and instead of such being in freedom they are in slavery to an infernal insanity. 

Freedom and rationality are the two great gifts of our Divine Father in heaven which place man over and above all other animals; for it is only man, of all the animals that is responsible to his conscience before God which either approves or disapproves his every act, thought, word or deed before God and before his fellow-men. 

This monitor called conscience which is the power of man's spirit to approve or disapprove the acts of the flesh has been given him by our Divine Father to be continually with him to guide him in the way of life and salvation; but it is within the power of man to so abuse and wrong his conscience, that his conscience will condemn him and deliver him into torments of sorrow, contempt, remorse, woe, and even physical and mental pain in trying to reform him and keep him in the way of life and salvation so that he perish not of his own sin and folly.

So great, so grand, so glorious, and so sublimely marvelous is the goodness and the wisdom of our Divine Father in heaven in trying to protect man from moral degradation, sin and folly that He has not only provided all the necessary material things for man's welfare and happiness; but has furnished him with a conscience to guide him in the discernment of duty and responsibility and to assist him

in the discernment between truth and falsity, and between good and bad; and our Divine Father even gave His only begotten Son to redeem man from death and from hell by repentance through good works, and through faith in the vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ as their price of redemption.

Man has been given by his Divine Creator the choice of heavenly freedom, and of infernal freedom, and his conscience tells him which one he is in, but the exercise of freedom in doing what is evil brings slavery and destruction, and it is therefore not true freedom but only a so-called freedom which some people call license, and there is therefore no true freedom only in the Lord; and the moment man departs from the Lord he immediately enters the realm of slavery and of bondage.

It is impossible that there could be any true freedom save in the Lord as it is through Him that freedom or salvation is wrought, and He is the only good portion of all life, because He is the giver of it, for the very spirit of life and of breath in man is in man continually from the Lord as man has nothing of himself. He is therefore dependent upon the Lord for everything, and there is none, not one save our Divine Father in heaven who is not dependent. 

Man's love for his neighbor is the love of good uses for his sake; and man's love to the Lord is the doing of good uses for the Lord's sake; for the true Christian knows no good or welfare of the kingdom of God. His readiness to sacrifice himself like our Lord and 

Savior Jesus Christ for the salvation of his fellow-men is the only true altruistic or Christian life that one can live; and all such good uses are saving uses to the one who does them, for by these uses is man saved. Christ saves us that we might save others by bringing others to the knowledge of Him who is God's Son and Mediator. 

The love of good uses are spiritual and celestial when a man does them for the sake of others which are apart or distinct from what is one's own; for whoever loves good uses is spiritual-minded and does good works of charity for others outside of self for whose good he is moved and all such uses are heavenly uses. But there are those who invert the Divine order, and put self in the Lord's place, and the world in the place of heaven; and they therefore try to convert all uses for the sake of self by selfishly and covetously converting all uses to the attaining of power, prestige, property, houses, dividends, bank accounts, stocks and bonds so they will have a fortune to bequeath at death to their children; and as a consequence such people

look backward and away from the Lord, and away from heaven to self and to the world; and the looking backward from the Lord and from heaven is looking toward hell and to the end of destruction of their being in the second death.

Faith alone will not save and especially faith in something which our Divine Father has not appointed such as the doctrine of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person which doctrine is silly, stupid, idiotic, inconsistent, absurd, inconceivable, contradictory and a monstrous lie. You must have faith in the truth that Jesus Christ is the Son and Mediator of our Divine Father in heaven in order to salvation, because it has been so appointed by our Divine Father in heaven that all must be saved through Christ His Son. Faith that our Divine Father is the only Divine person or God and that Jesus Christ is our Divine Father's Son is essential to salvation. 

All truth is a part of religion and heaven, and all error is a part of falsity and hell; but by this we do not mean all truth is Christian truth or God-like truth; because "The devil is a liar," and all who teach the absurd doctrine of the Divine triune God in three Divine persons are liars also and are not to be followed; but we do mean that truth, good or bad, is profiitable for those who know the bad through the observance of good and truth in morals and religion which God does not suffer to be divided, consequently it must be both in good and in truth or it must be both in evil and in falsity. 

God created all things from His Divine love, wisdom and power which is the essence of goodness and truth, as it is not possible that the world could be created out of nothing, for nothing is nothing, a nonentity of being; but love, wisdom, goodness, truth, strength and power are all in all with God whose will controls them all through the omnipotent power of His spirit, as the phenomena of willing, choosing, designing, purposing, and all executionary powers of God's Spirit subsist in the one person of our Divine Father in heaven as surely and truly as do the phenomena of the material world subsist in but one sphere, for only that one being of our Divine Father is independent of all others and He only can claim these qualities of Himself; and all things else owe their existence to His creation of them. 

If you are willing to speak spiritually you will find that the power of every man, animal, bird, beast and creeping thing in which God has planted the seed of reproduction have no other source from which life could have its origin and nature save but in a Divine

Creator, as the sun is only a means which God has created of sustaining life which the Divine Creator has given; but the sun itself cannot give life because it is in itself dead and inert, nor can there be any possibility of the seed producing its own origin and nature, and therefore the form and life of the seed is not of itself, but from its Divine Creator; and if the sustaining power of our Divine 

Father's omnipotent spirit were withdrawn the effect itself would perish.

Every created thing is endowed with power, but this power does not act from these things themselves, but from Him that bestowed it, of which Jesus Christ, the incarnate Word, is the greatest example or exponent of the power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father operating through Him, and not He of Himself doing the works. Most of our scientists have not taken this fact into consideration which is an historical fact, which cannot be gainsaid or successfully contradicted.

God's abode is in goodness and in truth; and so long as man dwells in good and in truth he dwells in and bears the stamp, image and likeness of God; but man not remaining in good and in truth, but becoming an admixture of good and of evil, of truth and of falsity, the image, character and likeness of God is lost in him through disobedience; but Jesus Christ is morally and spiritually the image of God because He lived the truth, and abode in goodness and in truth.

Man in this life can hardly enter into unbroken conjunction with good and truth or with evil and falsity, but is in a state of regeneration, and he is such as is his life's ruling love; and he remains in that state of fixedness in which his character is formed whether of good and of truth unto eternal life or of evil and of falsity unto destruction, for such as his ruling love is at the time of death such will he be in the world to come; "For unto every one that hath shall more be given; and he shall have greater abundance, but he that hath not, shall be taken away even all that he hath or seemeth to have both of life and of goods."

At the day of judgment God's holy angels will take every one just as they find him, and cast him into the balance and if the good and truth in his character outweighs the evil and falsity he shall be rewarded; but if not, the good and truth which he does possess will be taken from him and he will be cast out with the unbelievers. 

Divine or heavenly love is such that it is always seeking ways

and means of doing good by sharing all goods, benefits and blessings in its posssesion with others; and God is not only willing but anxiously desires and craves that the people ask largely and often. for all the good things that they can possibly give to others for the sake of others. For a man to always selfishly do just as he pleases, and disregard the needs of his neighbor is pure downright slavery; and therefore the Lord desires that all we do, we do from Him and not as from ourselves.

Our Divine Father is greater than all for He is the author of all, as we have nothing of ourselves; and Jesus Christ His glorious incarnate Word, who was the first-fruits of our Divine Father's creation is the greatest creature of our Divine Father's creation; and we can scarcely conceive of the inexpressable joy Christ felt when at the close of His earthly ministry He contemplated His speedy return to His Divine Creator and Father when He said to His disciples: "I ascend to my Father and your Father, to my God and your 

God," "I go to prepare a place for you, that where I am you may be also." If Jesus Christ is God incarnate, how could He say to His disciples: "I ascend to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God?" Could He ascend to Himself? Or how could He say to

His disciples after His resurrection, "I have not as yet ascended to my Father." Ignorant, stupid, and blind, and devoid of understanding are those who hold that God's glorious Son the Word, is God incarnated or that He is a Divine person coequal, coessential, and coeternal with His Divine Father in heaven!

The only Divine in Himself, of Himself, and by Himself is our Divine Father in heaven to whom no other person can approach in person, existence, perfection, power and authority, as He only can look to Himself and speak of Himself as Divine, Deity, God, Father and Creator; but it pleased our Divine Father that in His Son Jesus 

Christ we are made replete with all the fullness of God, for in Christ dwelleth all the fulness of the Law and the prophets; for as the blessed Paul in his epistle to the Colossians says: "It pleased the 

Father, that in Him should all the fulness dwell . . for in Him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily;" and "No one cometh unto the Father but by Him." So our Divine Father can look to none anywhere save that of His own creation; and all must look to our Divine Father as their Creator, and the giver of all that they are and have. The Father only is uncreate, underived, unoriginate, and unbegotten, and He therefore is the sole and only

Deity from which Jesus Christ the incarnate Word and all the other persons, spirits, angels and things whatsoever derive their origin for it was from our Divine Father through Him as our Divine Father's agent in the creation of all these things that all things else exist. 

Our Divine Father only can look to none as His God, Creator and Father; or to any other person as possessing Divine attributes, power or authority, as He only is uncreate, absolute and independent in His person, being and powers; and all creation is relatively nothing as compared to our Divine Father in heaven who is the only absolute, perfect, uncreate, omnipotent, infinite, omniscient, omnipresent or eternal person, and He only is comprehended in the Godhead of the Deity.

God is not the eternal Father, or the eternal Creator; but He is the eternal God, as His existence is without origin; but there was an exceedingly long duration of time anterior to the creation of His glorious Son the Word, which time our Divine Father spent in holy contemplation as God before the creation of His glorious Son the "Word of God" by whose creation He became Creator and Father; but He existed as God myriads of years in duration of time anterior to the Word's creation. Therefore, the incarnate Word Jesus Christ is not the eternal Son but the Son of the Eternal, as an eternal Son is an utter impossibility, as there must always be a time anterior to the son's creation in which the Word was not existent; for there is no conceivable way in which God could become Father without His first-born child of creation, as an eternal person cannot have a God, Father or Creator neither can he be a son of anyone.

Father, creator and creature are simultaneous meanings whether the creature be created or begotten; but as to God our Divine 

Father He was God or the Eternal before He became Father or Creator, therefore, we apply the term God in speaking of Him in His eternal state, past, present, and future, but as Creator and Father we speak of Him as such in relation to His creation, because, as creatures we may appropriately use any of these terms in regard to our relationship to Him; but we cannot appropriately use the term eternal in expressing our relationship to Him as our eternal God,

Father, Creator or Deity for we are not eternal and He could not be our eternal God, Creator and Father; for He could not be anything to us before our creation which is not eternal but in time, and that but a short time ago.

All things are dependent upon our Divine Father, and operate

from Him; and for this reason Christ truthfully said of Himself: "I of myself can do nothing, it is my Father who doeth the works." 

Therefore Christ is not Divine, but only the Son of Him who is Divine, as no dependent person or creature can be a Divine person though he be a creature or the Son of the Divine, as no one is dependent who is Divine, for the Divine person can have no God, Creator or Father, and the incarnate Word Jesus Christ has all of these, therefore Christ is neither God, Creator nor Father, but the 

Son of God His Creator and Father.

We fear no censure from conservative denominational sources that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, of the Father, of the Creator, of the Eternal; but that Christ Himself as the Son of God is a creature of the Divine, of the Eternal, of the Father, and dependent upon His Divine Father in all things; for those who do not acknowledge Christ to be the Son of God are of the Antichrist who deny the Father and the Son who the apostle Paul says are anathema or cursed of God, because they do not believe in God's only begotten Son Jesus Christ who said: "I am the Son of God."

It is the narrowness and bigotry of the exclusionists in doctrinal standards of the Catholic and Evangelical Churches holding the doctrine of the Trinity which has so cursed the world with the idolatry of a Trinity or plurality of Divine persons which has been the greatest of all enemies to the Church, for they ban all who differ from them from the Church and anathematize all as heretics who do not accept their three Divine persons in one Divine triune person as one God.

Any exclusive fellowship founded upon theological opinions is unfairly exclusive to any believer in Jesus Christ as the Son of God which was the only apostolic test for baptism, entrance into and fellowship by the Church; and this should be all the requisite requirements to Christian communion and fellowship that the Church should practice. No one has a right to set any other theological standard besides that laid down by Jesus Christ which was voiced by Saint Peter when Jesus Christ asked His apostles, "Who do men say that I the Son of Man am?" and Peter answered for the apostles, saying: "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God;" and Jesus answered: "Upon this rock I will build my Church." This confession, "Thou art the Christ the Son of the living God," is the rock upon which Christ said: "I will build my Church and the gates of

hell shall not prevail against it;" and therefore it should be the only basis of union, of communion, and of fellowship in the Church. 

We should be one in Christ, as He is in God, and, as God is in Him; and as God is in Christ so Christ should be in us, for Christ says: "Abide in me and I in you . . . he that abideth in me and I in him, the same beareth much fruit . . . at that day ye shall know that ye are in me, and I in you . . . I in the Father, the Father in me, and I in you.” Christ is in God, and God is in Christ; and we are in Christ, and Christ is in us; but all are in God and from Him who are led by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven. 

There is no communion, conjunction or reciprocation of spirits save that between our minds which conjoin when two persons mutually or reciprocally will to agree as touching anything that they ask of God as from Him or of one another as from God, God will grant it to them. Thus the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven wills to draw near to man's spirit, and to conjoin His spirit with the spirit of man; but man often turns back and goes away and no conjunction is effected which is true of all those who are in hell; but those who are in heaven are in conjunction with the spirit of the Lord.

Since our heavenly Father wills conjunction of His Holy Spirit with man's spirit in order to save him, He provides as well as demands that there shall be something in man reciprocal, which he wills and does from freedom, and not from restraint; and this is a mutual love and good-will toward God and toward our fellow-men as a prerequisite to God's acceptance of him; for when man looks to our Divine Father in heaven as the author of all good, and to himself as the recipient of all this vouchsafed grace, then God looks upon man with approbation in so far as he shuns evils as sins. 

Every one's spirit should be free in its willing, choosing, designing, accepting, rejecting and executing powers; and move by voluntary action as the conscience of every one's spirit should in worship be in accord with his reason and understanding; but no one should act solely as from himself; but try to think and do as from the Lord. 

That is, he should be willing that good and truth and right should be the ruling power of his life, not as being compelled, but from freedom in accord with reason.

God has purposed that man in his worship should have full freedom, in his spirit in thinking, willing, believing, loving, adoring and worshipping in joy and gladness; and every one acknowledges that

it is impossible to compel anyone to think or believe to acceptance that which is contrary to the mind of his spirit, and to will what his spirit forbids him to will, for he still will say: "The world does move;" and therefore one must will and believe in accordance with an enlightened conscience guided by reason and the knowledge of truth.

Some people have a very stubborn, rebellious and infernal spirit for accepting truth; for they fear if they should investigate these religious matters or think them through that their conscience would compel them to accept truths contrary to their established way of thinking and the things they have been taught to hold as sacred and Divine; and therefore they think that ignorance is bliss; but instead it is slavery, hell and destruction, for such people are not willing for 

Divine truth to rule in their life.

We have herein stated many Divine truths which are absolute facts; but contrary to the popular acceptation of religious teaching such as: Christ is not Divine, nor the Divine Son, nor the God Son, nor the Son God, nor God the Son; but the Son of the Divine or the 

Son of God and nothing more nor less; that our Divine Creator was God before He became Creator and Father or the life-giver to other persons; and that our Divine Father only is God or Divine; and that all other persons are persons of our Divine Father's creation, are Divine truths and truisms which stand the test of Divine revelations, of nature and of the sciences, so far as man is able to comprehend or investigate these Divine truths; but those who gave heed to these Divine and heavenly truths since the fourth century of the Christian era were treated as liars, thieves, robbers, murderers and outlaws. They were excommunicated, tried as heretics, disfranchised, property confiscated, condemned and persecuted by both ecclesiastical and civil courts until millions suffered as martyrs and many other millions brought into subjection and slavery to the "Antichrist, the man of sin and son of perdition" the Pope of Rome; and the world made to acknowledge his three Divine persons in the one Divine triune person which he set up for men to worship in the place of the one living and only true God our Divine Father in heaven.

There are a very few Churches to-day that allow people to worship our Divine Father in heaven according to the dictates of one's own conscience in the Church, for they have their set rules, creeds, disciplines, dogmas, catechisms, and forms of worship which they

compel, contrary to scripture and moral rights to bring others into subjection to themselves or weed them out of their communion and fellowship by dictating to them their creed, rules, laws, and doctrines to be conformed unto under penalty of excommunication. Yea, even 

Christ Himself, would they put out the Church were He to go there to worship His Divine Father and Creator; for there they worship a three-headed triune monster as one person which they have created out of their own deranged minds of idolatry and abominations. 

The greater portion of the people who have joined the Church membership are deprived of their full liberty and rationality for they are driven through duress to acquiesce in the ordinances, creeds, disciplines, interpretations or rather paraphernalia of the Church for the peace and harmony of the local organization, so the people stifle their conscience in order to have a Church home, and be admitted into the communion and fellowship of the local Church of the community in which they live because often there is no other alternative by which they can have a convenient Church home. 

Those who insist upon a condition, state or position for the sake of maintaining sectarian divisions on the part of the Church against any of a Christian character of other persuasions who believe Jesus Christ is the Son of God in order for membership in the Church are criminal, satanic, antichristian, wicked, sinful and disgraceful, and unworthy of the name of Christian.

It is almost impossible for anyone to follow his Lord and Master according to the dictates of his own conscience in any sectarian Church and exercise his liberty and rationality who continually transgresses against his standard of truth and of right as he understands God's word to teach and his own conscience to approve. 

It is simply up to every one to preserve his faculties of liberty, of conscience, and of freedom to think and to act as rational beings in accordance with their reason in matters of religion and of worship, by letting all sectarianism be relegated to the limbo of the past, as it is a curse in the earth; for, if we do not overthrow this overlordship of ecclesiasticism in the Church, and call for a truce of liberty and of freedom we will be held forever as slaves and as serfs to a diabolical system of heresiarchs from whom we will never be able to secure liberty of conscience and of freedom to worship God according to an approving conscience, so long as we maintain sectarianism in the Church.

We have no criminals quite so bad as our bigoted narrow-minded

clergymen who as sectarian vampires take from the people the right of liberty and of conscience, and the very principles and means of our salvation by taking from us the Son of God by making Him another Divine person coequal, coessential and coeternal with His God, Creator, and Father who is in heaven. 

The deafness, thoughtlessness, and blindness caused by these sectarian opiates injected into the minds of the people by those who call themselves ministers of the gospel of Jesus Christ, but who are ministers and teachers of these satanic sectarian doctrines are beyond the power of human tongue to describe or portray. 

From careful observation it may easily be seen that a faith induced by fear or duress upon the minds, hearts, and consciences of the people is criminal, and that such is not faith but fear; for there is nothing rational, sensible or consistent in it, and nothing spiritual; and it is this way with everything confirmed that is not looked into with some rationailty of understanding of comprehension and discernment before it is confirmed. 

How can a doctrine be a matter of faith of which one can have no clear understanding or comprehension? It is nothing but blind assent which is minus of all intellectual properties; and such is the doctrine of the Trinity of the triune God, as it is nothing more than a conglomeration of lies, absurdities, inconsistencies and contradictions which have been forced upon the world through duress. 

The people have not been persuaded by the gospel of Jesus Christ or the teachings and practices of Christ's apostles, presbyters, bishops, and evangelists of the first two centuries of Christianity; but they have been succeeded by subjection to the Antichrist, through persecutions, excommunications, fines, imprisonments, banishments, and confiscations; and the substitution of spurious teachings and practices of the "Mother of harlots and abominations of the earth," the Roman Catholic Church which has set up the "abominations of desolations" of idolatry by substituting three Divine persons, Gods, or Deities with the Virgin Mary as the "Mother of God;" and the people having been held in bondage to the Papal 

Beast above a thousand years no longer perceive the blasphemy and profanation of the religion of Jesus Christ by these falsities through which they are now held in bondage to the Antichrist, the man of sin, and son of perdition, the Pope of Rome. 

This bondage and blasphemy, in a measure, takes place every time some dogma of religion is imposed upon the minds, hearts, spirits

and consciences of the people, and the people subjected without their perception or understanding just what these sinful, wicked, degrading, infernal designing persons have done to bring the people into subjection to himself; and thus the people are bound not by faith and understanding, nor by an enlightened conscience, but by a diabolical lordship that has usurped authority over the gospel of Jesus Christ, our Divine heritage by interpolating, mistranslating, and enshrouding in mystery through false traditions, and the destruction of all Christian records of the first centuries, so that but little of the true teaching and practices of Jesus Christ is left extant to the world, and it is in this way that the Antichrist, the man of sin, the Pope of Rome has taken away the rationality and liberty of the people by destroying their understanding of the things Divine. 

The spirit of man is such by the will of our Divine Father that it should have the voluntary right, liberty and freedom to will, to choose and to act in accordance with its reason and understanding in things Divine, and those who still teach Trinitarian lies concerning the Deity abridge and curb in every way the Divine right of the people to spontaneous worship founded upon a clear understanding of our Divine Father.

Jesus Christ the Son of God has made it clear to us that His Divine Father does not want compelled worship and adoration, for such worship is corporeal, lifeless, darkened, sad, and spiritless, while voluntary worship and adoration in spirit and in truth must be in freedom in accordance with reason and the understanding which is living, vital, genuine, spiritual, joyous, exultant, sublime, filial, devotional, sacred, and heavenly, as it is filled with the spirit of truth, love, praise, thanksgiving, and adoration from the heart and spirit of an enlightened mind. 

There can be no virtue or merit appropriated to man except what he does from freedom in accordance with reason, because freedom belongs to the will and reason to the understanding; and whatever is done in accordance with these two is appropriated in true worship from the heart in spirit and in truth, as no one can be reformed into states or conditions which do not spring from liberty and rationality; and therefore, enforced worship like blind worship is not true worship and adoration at all.

That is not true worship which is in any way forced or which is done in a state of blindness of the understanding; consequently those who worship three Divine persons in one Divine triune person are

either forced or blind as to both God and truth as those who claim to worship three Divine persons in the unity of one Divine tirune person are stupid, ignorant, silly and have no clear understanding of either truths or Divine things, for a Trinity in unity means according to their creed three persons or units in one person or unit, which is the same as saying that, that is that which it is not which is a contradiction in terms and cannot be true; and those who worship a conglomerate mass or admixture of three Divine persons in one Divine person are ignorant, stupid and blind, and have no clear understanding of truth or of things Divine, as one unit cannot be three units or three persons one person or one unit three units or one person three persons; and all who worship such falsities and contradictions which can have no tangible existence as such are antichristian, ignorant, stupid and blind, and apostate from Jesus Christ.

The prophets, and Jesus Christ in quoting the prophets concerning His mission said: "Jehovah hath anointed me to proclaim the acceptable year of Jehovah, and the day of vengeance of our God; and Hosea says: 'Come let us return unto Jehovah, after two days

Thou art my Son, this day have I begotten thee. I will give thee the nations for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession. Thou hast made Him a little lower than Deity.

Thou hast made Him to have dominion over the works of thine hands, thou hast put all things under His feet.”

The gospel writers have recorded that on three different occasions while the incarnate Word Jesus Christ was performing His Messianic ministry as God's Son and Mediator there were on three different occasions a voice heard from heaven in approval and confirmation of Jesus Christ's baptism by John the Baptist in the Jordan; "And Jesus, when He was baptized went up straightway out of the water, and lo, the heavens were opened unto Him and the power of God's spirit descended and lighted upon Him;" and a voice came from heaven saying: "This is my beloved Son in whom I am well pleased;" and at the time of Christ's conference with Moses and Elijah on the Mount of Transfiguration; and also at the time of His triumphal entry into Jerusalem to offer Himself as a vicarious atonement for our sins.

The imputation of the merits of Christ's sacrifice in our behalf is something more than the forgiveness of our sins upon repentance, as we think of forgiveness, for it also involves the resurrection from the dead unto the life eternal for all who through faith and good works acknowledge Jesus Christ the Son of God as their Lord and Savior. 339

It is believed by the generality of the Church that our Divine Father sent His Son the incarnate Word Jesus Christ, so as to make an atonement for the human race; and that this was affected by 

His fulfilling the law through the passion of His cross in dying for every man, for it was by His death that He took away from us the penalty due to our sin, which condemnation fell on Him when He made satisfaction to Divine justice for all innocent or irresponsible folk, and all those who through faith and repentance would come unto God through His vicarious atonement. Without the expiatory sacrifice of Jesus Christ as a propitiation to Divine justice as a satisfaction to be made in behalf of mankind the human race would perish with the world, because of their inability to satisfy Divine justice for the death which they through Adam have inherited; but a repentance through the atonement of Jesus Christ is granted the sinner by which the flesh and blood of Jesus Christ is accepted in the place of the penitent sinner, and all such are restored through the resurrection from the dead to the life immortal and eternal. 

The gospel teaches us that had not Christ have given His flesh for the life of the world mankind should have perished, but that through the sacrifice of Jesus Christ satisfaction is tendered in behalf of all who through faith, repentance and good works accept for themselves the satisfaction which Christ tendered in behalf of all; but only those are benefited who in so far as they are able rely upon Christ's sacrifice and accept it in their behalf, and those who are too young to know of it or have not had the opportunity of knowing of Christ's vicarious atonement for them will be saved through the answer of a good conscience toward God.

In this way the Divine attributes of truth, love, mercy and justice of our heavenly Father are satisfied with the repentance, reformation, faith and good works of the penitent sinner, as there is nothing of vengeance in the spirit of our Divine Father in heaven which is goodness, love, mercy and compassion incarnate and seeks every possible means for the safety, joy, peace, happiness, health, protection, good, salvation, and life of the sinner; and our Divine 

Father will abandon him only when help has been refused, rejected and spurned until the close of one's earthly career. 

Man is not saved by his own merit or righteousness, nor is he unreservedly saved by the merit or righteousness of Jesus Christ without any merit or righteousness of his own, but it takes the two con-

jointly as there is no forgiveness of sin without repentance and reformation, nor is there any reward without faith and good works. 

Man is not saved alone by repentance, faith and good works, but these are requisite conditions to be met before the merit or righteousness of Jesus Christ's sacrifice is awarded him; for it is only to such that the sacrifice of Jesus Christ is substituted for the death of man due to Adam's transgression in us or our transgression through him as our representative. Death is removed from us conjointly by the sacrifice of Jesus Christ for man and man's repentance toward God, otherwise neither taken alone would be sufficient in itself for man's redemption; but by the grace of God the two taken conjointly, the active faith and repentance of man removes the curse of death from man at the coming of Jesus Christ through the resurrection from the dead to immortality and everlasting life.

Death or mortality is not overcome by those who persist in sin, for at the day of judgment the souls of those who have persisted or continued in sin shall be destroyed in the second death; but those who through faith, repentance and good works seek for life and immortality shall through the resurrection from the dead by the grace of God through the vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ in man's behalf be given immortality and the life eternal.

The debt of mortality which we have inherited through Adam's transgression is effective upon all, and only those who answer with a good conscience toward God will God through the resurrection from the dead award the life eternal, but the bad and all disbelievers will He utterly destroy.

All humanity will be resurrected without exception, the good unto the life eternal, and the bad unto the judgment of destruction.

It is not in the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father, neither in His nature to place or assign anyone to Hades, and every fellow that gets there does so of his own free will, and even then God is so good, gracious, merciful, loving and kind that His compassion will not permit anyone to thus suffer on forever and He has, therefore, appointed a day in which He will judge the world by His Son Jesus Christ, and all those who have cast their souls in that unspeakable place or condition where they have become incorrigible or incurable sinners will cease to exist in what the scriptures call the "Second death;" for our Divine Father in heaven has a very intense aversion and holy horror to anything that causes sin, suffering, pain, sorrow, distress or injury to His faithful, noble, pure, virtuous and righteous people; and will not permit the wicked to forever harass the good nor themselves to suffer on forever; and He will, therefore, weed out and destroy with an everlasting destruction everything that causes harm or injury.

There is something peculiarly strange or should we say thoughtless, about the minds of people who speak of Jesus Christ as being the Son of God; and then in the next breath say that Christ is 

Divine when that which is Divine can have no God or Father, for that which is Divine pertains only to the Deity and cannot belong to any other person, being or thing other than He; and, as our 

Divine Father in heaven is the God and Father of Jesus Christ by reason of His creation of the person of Jesus Christ, Jesus Christ is neither a person, part nor portion of the Divine one, but a creature of the Divine one; for our Divine Father is the only uncreate, and the only infinite, absolute and independent or unoriginate person. 

Therefore, as He only is unoriginate or uncreate, the Eternal One subsisting alone without division or parts, there is no Divine person other than the one uncreate, unoriginate person of our Divine Father

in heaven; and our Divine Father Himself cannot change it, as it is not an object of power to make any person or creature Divine. 

Man, who is a finite and dependent creature of our Divine Father may do that which is contradictory, absurd and inconsistent; but our Divine Father can never do wrong; and this is the reason why our Divine Father in heaven who consists of but one person, properly so-called, cannot take other persons into the Deity of His person which is uncreate or unoriginate; and cannot be altered, changed, added to, or subtracted from; for His person is independent and absolute in both person and power; and all things else must of necessity be from Him and dependent upon Him for their existence. and power; and for all that they are, have, and do. 

Nevertheless, our Divine Father in heaven has given to man wondrous responsibiltiy by creating him a rational, free moral agent like unto Himself with the power of choice; but it is pure nonsense for anyone who has any respect whatever for his own integrity for either God, truth, or his fellow-men, to say that there are more Divine persons than our Divine Father in heaven by personifying the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven and calling our Divine Father's Son Jesus Christ a Divine person in the Godhead of the Deity coequal, coessential, coeternal and equal in power, glory and honor with His Divine Father or originator.

It is too bad that the Christian world has been outraged, jockeyed, fooled, and scourged by the Antichrist, the Pope of Rome through fifteen hundred years with his monstrous apostate doctrine of three

Divine persons in one Divine triune person until to-day this apostate doctrine of a three in one Divine person is being palmed off on the world as the gospel of Jesus Christ; and that it is a great sin for anyone to question this conundrum as a thing of Divine revelation and that they must acquiesce in the opinion of the Church under the penalty of eternal damnation; for there is nothing so sacred and 

Divine as the holy and ever-blessed Trinity of three Divine persons in one, and anyone saying that there are not three Divine persons should be punished in an everlasting, searing, scorching, burning, plaguing, tormenting, suffocating, painful hell which shall never end in suffering or duration.

Just how these antichrist doctrinists of the three in one God after they have hypostatically conjoined three Divine persons into one Divine triune person who in turn has absorbed through the homoousian of Jesus Christ the Son of God into the Deity of the triune

God expects Jesus Christ to return to this earth in the same or like manner in which He ascended into heaven is more than God, demons, men or angels will ever be able to figure out.

Any rational person, or persons reaching their teen age that are so ignorant, stupid and silly as to be so blind and devoid of understanding as not to be able to perceive, comprehend or understand that three persons, units or beings cannot be one person, unit or being at one and the same time, are scarcely fit to enter the first grade of our primary schools; and for ministers who call themselves ambassadors of Jesus Christ to go behind the sacred desk and proclaim that there are three infinite Divine persons hypostatically united into one Divine triune person whom we call our Divine Father in heaven are all falsifiers, villains and criminals who have no proof to corroborate their doctrine of the Trinity of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person, as all true scripture, nature, reason and science are against them. "Who is a liar, but he who says that Jesus 

Christ is not our Divine Father's Son?"

This is a terrible charge of villainy and criminality the clergymen of our forty-five thousand churches who are supposed to be above the average in intelligence, because it makes them incriminate themselves by upholding these falsities of the Antichrist which Christ and His apostles forewarned should come into the world, and "All the world followed after the Beast;" for those who say that

God became incarnate, or that Jesus Christ is a Divine person in the Deity, or that He was hypostatically absorbed into the Deity or that Jesus Christ is homoousian with the Deity are Antichrist and against the teachings of Jesus Christ; for the Son of God can never, never be nor become so great as His uncreate, unoriginate, infinite, omnipotent, Divine Father.

No man has seen God at any time, and the only way that man can come into conjunction, communion or contact is through correspondences of the spirit of man with the spirit of God. 

The gospel tells us that in the resurrection we shall be like Christ; for we shall see Him as He is; and also "like the angels of 

God" in spiritual likeness; but not that we shall be identically the same in character, as character is made up of the acts of the individual's life and is not transferable, as such identity cannot be transferred in any absolute sense; and for this reason we cannot be identically like Christ save in immortality and rationality.

This spiritual likeness to Jesus Christ, is likeness in fellowship,

labor, communion, and correspondences from our spiritual affinities through the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven which are the only characteristic likenesses to be had between men and angels with their Divine Father and with one another. Christ defines His spiritual relationship with His Divine Father and with us as follows: "I in thou, thou in me, and I in them, that they may be one in us. . . In that day ye shall know that ye are in me and I in thee ... the works that I do, I do not of myself, but the spirit of my 

Father which dwelleth in me doeth the works." "I came forth from my Father and am come into the world, again I leave the world and go to my Father.' 

Jesus Christ is not God incarnate or He could not have come forth from God and returned to God, neither could He have sat down on the right hand of God or make an atonement to God for our sins as it would be nonsense to say that He sacrificed Himself to 

Himself for the redemption of man.

There are those who read through the prophecies and conclude that the agent of our Lord God Jehovah is God because He speaks in the name of our Divine Father in heaven and under the power, direction and authority of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in the first person singular and conclude that the angel or agent speaking for our Divine Father is our Divine Father Himself; but Christ informs us that no man has seen God at any time, for no man can see God and live." Our Divine Father generally speaks through agencies who act in His name, and under His power and authority. 

The incarnate "Word of God," through whom God created the worlds and all things; and through whom He gave us the Law and 

Covenants, and the New Testament ought to be a competent witness, interpreter and expounder of the Law and the prophets; but most all our "Doctors Divinitis" have doctored His words and works until they have completely lost sight of Christ's origin, doctrine and works.

There are many scriptural titles applied to Jesus Christ in both the Old and also the New Testament such as King, Messiah, Son of God, Son of the Father, the Word, the Word of God, Master, Teacher, Son of Man, Son of David, the Prophet and the angel of the covenant which are among the more prominent ones evinced by the prophets, Jesus Christ and His apostles of which the following are a few samples from the Old Testament: "Afterwards the sons of Israel shall return, and shall seek Jehovah their God and David

their king and I will raise up a shepherd over them who shall feed them, even my servant David, he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd; and I, Jehovah will be their God; and my servant 

David a prince in the midst of them. . . that they may be my people, and that I may be their God, and David my servant shall be king over them, and they shall have one shepherd; then will they dwell in the land, they and their sons and their sons' sons even to eternity; and I will make a covenant of peace, and it shall be a covenant to eternity with them. . . I will make a covenant to eternity with you, the sure mercies of David: Behold! I have given him for a witness to the people, a prince and a law-giver to the nations."

The gospel informs us of a certain rich young ruler who said to 

Jesus: "Good master, what shall I do that I may have eternal life?" 

Jesus said unto him: "Why callest thou me good? There is none good but the one God; and the first and greatest of all the commandment is: 'Hear O Israel, the Lord our God is one Father, and thou shalt worship Him with all thy soul, mind and strength, for the Father seeketh such to worship Him.'"

While Jesus was hanging on the cross He prayed to His Divine 

Father in heaven saying, "Father, into thy hands I commend my spirit," and having thus said He gave up His spirit into the loving care of His Divine Creator. The spirit of God dwells with those of a humble spirit and of a contrite heart.

There is a oneness or likeness of correspondence or conjunction between the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven with His creatures only, when they come into harmony and agreement with it, as Jesus says: "In that day ye shall know that I am in my Father, and ye in me and I in you. Believe me that I am in my Father, and the Father in me or else believe me for the very works' sake; the works that I do, I do not of myself, but the spirit of my Father which abides in me doeth the works, for I of myself can do nothing." 

The works performed by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven through His Son Jesus Christ were correspondences by which Jesus Christ worked in perfect harmony with the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father in heaven else the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven could not have performed these Divine works through Him.

The holy scriptures are the truth and the life to those who understand their meaning, and observe to do according to their com-

mands; but they have but little value for those who falsify or misunderstand them.

Jesus Christ, and His personal disciples, and the prophets of old spoke or prophesied as they were moved by the Holy Spirit of our 

Divine Father in heaven, which Spirit is the ever-living Spirit of our heavenly Father's person, and cannot be separated from His personality; and when men prophesied they were moved by the spirit of God, and not from any knowledge or power they possessed of themselves.

Christ Jesus is the living truth of God's word by keeping the sayings of His commandments which are the statutes and judgments of the Divine will, as Christ did always and only that which was commanded Him by His Divine Father in heaven; and to be in 

God's will is to live in the provisions of the gospel of Jesus Christ which is the Divine truth and the Divine good which is salvation, because in them will be found the life-giving properties of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven; and those who do not thus live by the gospel of Jesus Christ the Son of God, but in evils and falsities of the Antichrist doctrines of idolatry of a plurality of 

Divine persons or Gods shall perish everlastingly, for it is only in obedience to truth that one can be saved.

A person can have no true faith, if he has no conception of truth, of right and of wrong. Faith is of the understanding, which is to know, to think, to reason, to discriminate, to draw conclusions as to correspondences as to what is right and wrong; for if a man does not know or understand what he believes, and why he believes it, he may well believe he has faith, and yet not have it, because he does not have a perception of the truth, and ignorant assent is blind faith like those who say that there are three Divine persons in the Deity of our Divine Father in heaven and simply say that God consists and subsists in three Divine persons in one Divine triune person and let it go at that without any reason, explanation or understanding of what they speak; for, if they should examine the doctrine of three Divine persons in a triune God, they will find it to be contrary to all truth in toto, as it is contrary to all truth or sense of the understanding.

From what is truth no just person can dissent; and just in so far as man shuns evils, errors and falsities, just in so far has he saving faith, because to confirm the contrary is for a man to believe in and worship evil; and evil inwardly hates truth; and this is why the

Antichrist has so many millions of followers, while to accept the Divine truths of the scriptures that, "The Lord our God is one Divine Father; and that Jesus Christ is His Son and that the Holy 

Spirit is the spirit of our Divine Father in heaven, are but few,' which are in saving faith; as to believe in God, is not only to think that He is, but also to do His commandments by living a life in conformity with good and with truth.

Those who are in evils through error and falsities have no saving faith, no matter how much they may suppose themselves to have it; for there can be no substitution of evil for good or of falsities for truth by the Lord; and those who are careless and indifferent as to what they believe, do or worship are not acceptable to the Lord as the mere thinking a thing to be true, no matter what the grounds for so thinking, is not saving faith; for those who wish to do the truth and the good by believing and acting in conformity with them seek the light and a clearer understanding or comprehension of them that their works may be wrought in God.

There may exist in the understanding the thought that such and such a thing is true, but there must be a consent of the will through the understanding or comprehension of them before the conscience can acknowledge it as a thing that is good, true, right or commendable before it can become saving faith. 

What nation is there that is not aware that it is evil to steal, kill, lie, commit adultery and blaspheme? For a nation without such prohibitory laws cannot long endure; and for this reason our Divine 

Father has caused it to be proclaimed from the height of Mount Sinai the great oracles of the Law covering all moral and religious duties; and for this reason it was called God's covenant until the 

Messiah should come, and God would make a New Covenant through Him.

It is by the means of this law called the covenant and the testimony by which conjunction was to be had with the Lord; and the testimony bore witness to the Covenant which God had inscribed in two tables; the one bearing our relationship and duties toward 

God; and the other bearing our relationship and duties toward our fellow-men. The first covenant was ratified by a promise; but the second covenant was ratified with the precious blood of God's glorious

Son, the incarnate Word Jesus Christ. 

Our present generations justly accuses the pastors of our Churches and the editors of our religious journals and periodicals for the

chaotic condition of the Church, as about fifty percent of the sins of the world is the direct cause of their departure from the teachings and practices of the Church as directed by Jesus Christ and His apostles for the governing of the Church; for they refuse to agree together and will not permit the people to do so. 

The decalogue is the greatest bulwark of the Christian world, and is the common doctrine into which people are commonly initiated into the Christian religion. Christ came not to destroy the law and the prophets, but to fulfill them and establish them by granting clemency to those who will repent and turn from sin unto God and His righteousness. Grace, is only the grace of repentance, and without repentance the penalties of the law are in full effect upon those who do not repent.

When our ministers say that we are no longer under the Law but under grace they should not forget that the penalties of the Law apply the same now as it ever did to those who are impenitent and obstinate; and to say that the law no longer applies is so only in the limited sense of repentance toward God of all our sins and the acceptance of the sacrificial vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ, God's glorious Son in our behalf, otherwise the penalty of God's broken law is in full force of all its rigor of death and destruction to those who remain unrepentant toward God. 

Jesus said to the rich young ruler: "If you would enter into life, keep the commandments;" and it is a great falsity for anyone to think that faith exempts him from trying to keep the decalogue or the ten commandments; and all who do not try to keep them are lost; for salvation comes to those only who through faith and repentance toward God persist in the works of righteousness; and whether they have heard of Christ or not does not bar them from the grace of God through repentance, as God's grace is not limited by the accidents of the flesh, and every one will be judged by the enlightment of his own conscience. 

Every one is that which he wills, as saving faith is the internal acknowledgement and the living of the truth which is a state of charity, and a state of charity cannot be attained by those who have no Divine understanding or comprehension of truth, as faith in the unknown or that which does not enter into the perception, is a blind faith and fraught with heresy, for God never ordained that man should believe any doctrine of which he could have no clear understanding, as a thing that is not intelligible cannot be a matter of

active faith. For this reason the doctrine of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person cannot be a matter of faith, as that which is contrary to nature, person, science, reason, scripture and every private knowledge of truth and of right can have no intelligible understanding, comprehension or knowledge of what is inconsistent with reason and every private knowledge of fact, as there cannot be three units or persons in one unit or person; and those who are so blind, ignorant and stupid to assent to such a heretical proposition which in itself is a contradiction in terms and a lie on the very face of it cannot be accredited as from God, but from the Antichrist and the devil who were liars from their beginning. 

Real faith, is the acknowledgement that a thing is so because he understands and sees that a thing is true or consistent, for anyone who is in real faith thinks and says, "This is true because I understand and see its consistency and harmony with reason, and all things."

Faith is of truth, and truth is of faith, as there must be an understanding between them or it is not faith but blind assent; for when a person does not understand or know truth of anything, he does not know whether it is true or not; and therefore, as yet he cannot have a confirmed faith; for one cannot be said to believe that which he cannot intellectually comprehend. And if it be not possible for one to know whether a thing is true or false, that is, if we cannot form a clear conception or formulate a mental picture of that which we are being taught as Divine we find ourselves in the great dilemma of doubt and fear, and when one positively knows of the many absurdities inconsistencies, and contradictions taught by the antichrist doctrine of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person of the Godhead, one perceives that our modern Church ministry has become the greatest set of liars in the whole world. 

It is common among the clergy, when asked by the laymen concerning the doctrine of the Trinity, for them to reply: "No one can comprehend these spiritual and theological matters, because they are supernatural and transcend the reason and all scientific investigation, as they cannot be worked out by mathematics or by any other scientific principle; and therefore, the triune God of the 

Holy Trinity of three Divine persons in one is to be accepted on faith alone however much it might contradict every Biblical, scientific and private knowledge of fact or of truth," for he that ques-

tions the doctrine of the three Divine persons in one "shall without doubt perish everlastingly."

Many of the clergy will deny the antichristian threat of everlasting destruction to those who reject their doctrine of the Trinity; but we refer you, for the sake of those who wish to look it up, to the doctrine of the Trinity as stated in the "Athenation creed" in the forepart of this work to which this penalty of destruction is attached and in a great measure it was enforced upon all non-believers by the inquisitions of the Antichrist. 

Spiritual truths can be comprehended just as readily as natural ones for God is the author of them both; and those whose affections are exercised by truth have special revelations of discernment which the natural do not have; and those who lack wisdom, let them ask of
