Jesus Christ in His gospel says: "No man has seen God at any time, the only begotten Son who is in the bosom of the Father, He hath declared Him; and the Father Himself which hath sent me hath borne witness of me. Ye have neither heard His voice at any time nor seen His shape. . . If I honor myself my honor is nothing, it is my Father which honoreth me of whom ye say He is your God; but ye have not known Him; and if I should say I do not know I would be a liar like unto you."

CHAPTER XVIII 

Our Divine Father in heaven who is the only uncreate, unoriginate person or being in whom alone all find life and being through creation, as all other persons and things receive their existence from Him as nothing can subsist of itself that has come into being. However extended its duration it is subject to our Divine Father in heaven who is the only unoriginate, uncreated person, being, or thing as all else receive their origin, being, life and power from Him. 

The power of all being, life, power and authority is resident in the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father's person; and only as our 

Divine Father so wills do other persons and things receive being and life from Him who is the only uncreate and unoriginate person; and as the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father is not a person in itself but the spirit of our Divine Father's person; and, as neither the person nor the spirit of our Divine Father has any existence apart from each other our Divine Father and His Holy spirit are but one person, the same as man and his spirit are but one person; as every person has form of body and spirit; and without either body or spirit there can be no such thing as person, for these are inherent qualities of person, and cannot be added to, diminished or changed as one or the other cannot be said to be a person unless the two elements of spirit and of body are united, for the body without the spirit is dead, as it is the spirit which gives life to the body; and the body and the spirit are but one person for both the elements of body and of spirit are essential to personality. So the person of our Divine 

Father in heaven is composed of two elements, the body called the essence, and the spirit, called the Holy Spirit, for our Divine Father's person and His Holy Spirit are the two necessary elements which constitute Him a person excluding all others. 

Since the terms God, Father, Creator and Holy Spirit are essential titles to express the relationship of God to creation we must not confound the titles which apply to our Divine Father as belonging to other persons besides Him, for these titles belong to our Divine Father only and exclusively of all other persons; and it is a misnomer to use them in any other way, as all things other than our 361

Divine Father's person was created by the infinite, omnipotent power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father. 

All that man is, has, receives or possesses are the gifts of the Divine Father whose all-powerful executive spirit is the maker and giver, the upholder and sustainer of all things both of our Divine Father and all things of His creation as our Divine Father acts only and always by the power of His Holy Spirit. 

It is to be understood that Christ, angels, saints, prophets, apostles and all other agencies of God have no power of themselves, and are not to ascribe any merit, praise, glory or honor to themselves in the performance of the duties God has assigned them to do; for, if they do, they are amenable to be punished like Moses who took glory to himself at the Rock of Horeb, and he was not permitted to enter the land of Canaan, or they may be cut off from the living like Ananias and Sapphira who sought false praise. Jesus Christ was always careful to ascribe all power, honor and glory to His Divine Father from whom He received His being, power and authority; and all who claim that Jesus Christ teaches that He is a Divine person coequal, coessential and coeternal, and equal in power, glory, and honor with His Divine Father are liars, thieves and villains who disgrace God's holy anointed Jesus the Christ by saying these things concerning Him contrary to His character and teaching for He always confesses that what He is, has and does is the gift of His Divine 

Father; and those who teach otherwise are wicked, satanic blasphemers and falsifiers of Christ's words and works.

This is a terrible indictment to bring against the clergy who have infused into the minds of their parishioners this antichristian rebellion against the teachings of Jesus Christ, for, instead of saying: "The Lord our God is one Lord," they say that the Lord our God is three Lords or Divine persons of which neither is God without the other two, for they are a Trinity in unity and a unity in Trinity of one person; and thus they have substituted in the place of our 

Divine heavenly Father's person God the Father, God the Son and God the Holy Ghost which is the satanic doctrine of the Antichrist. 

Our Divine Father enjoins upon whomsoever He wills as His agents in the performance of His works and operates through them by the power of His spirit in delivering a message or performing any work; and no one can operate by His spirit contrary to His will and purposes; and for this reason no person other than our 

Divine Father can do a Divine act as He operates by His Holy

Spirit only as He so wills to do; and all who fulfill God's will and pleasure in things Divine must act in co-operation or conformity with God's spirit the same as a radio with its station. 

All Divine acts or messages of whatever nature or kind that have been performed in connection with the things of this world and its inhabitants, God, our Divine Father in heaven has performed through agents, as no Divine act can be performed save but by His spirit. Even though these agents spoke in the first person, as from themselves, yet, it was not them doing the speaking, as they acted merely as reproducers of that which God's spirit spoke through them; as it was the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven speaking through them or doing the works of God by them, as the consciousness of their person being obsessed by the Holy Spirit they spoke and acted in full conformity with it, so that they could not do otherwise than to speak and act as they were moved by the 

Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven.

There is no possible ratio between what is infinite and what is finite however perfect the finite might be in its sphere, as each individual person can exercise only such powers as God has ordained that he should fill, and beyond that he cannot go; and this is confirmed by the fact that those who are in a state of purity or innocence attribute nothing of good to themselves, but regard all things as received from our Divine Father in heaven; for they wish to be led by the will of our Divine Father's Holy Spirit instead of by the will of their own only in so far as the will of their own spirit conforms itself to the will of the spirit of God, for in God they find everything that is good, and everything that is true, and in willing and choosing what is good and true is loving the Lord our Divine Father with all the soul, mind and strength and loving one's neighbor as himself; for, "Whosoever will not receive the kingdom of God as a little child shall in no wise enter into it. 

All who are willing to be led and instructed by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven like His glorious Son the incarnate Word Jesus Christ who claimed absolutely no power or authority as His own; but said positively and unreservedly, "All power and authority are derived from and belong to our Divine Father in heaven. 

I can do nothing of myself, it is my Father who does the works." 

Those who are indolent hermits, monks, or misers are such as those who have acquired the prerequisite conditions for hell and destruction, as their wealth or poverty is not subservient to that of

good uses, and that which is not devoted to good uses either among the rich or the poor brings no reward, and no salvation, for salvation lies only in good uses; and he who does not devote his person, time, wealth and goods to good uses of charity will receive no reward from our Divine Father whose very nature is love and charity. 

The rich and the poor alike that perform good uses with all that they are, have, and do come into heaven; but they who do not perform good uses, but are selfish and covetous come into hell, as it is one's life which counts for good or for evil; and there is no dignity, honor, blame or condemnation but according to uses; and therefore, every one is rewarded, loved or esteemed, honored and blessed as he performs good uses as from the Lord and not as from himself. 

Every one coming into heaven will be fed, housed and clothed gratuitously, as his food and drink will be his good works; his spirit essence his house; and his clothing righteousness; but those coming into hell are those who despised good uses of charity while they were in this world, and therefore, they shall on the day of judgment be destroyed in the second death in the lake of fire and brimstone prepared for wicked people, the devil and his angels for their everlasting destruction.

Those who have adopted the opinion that heavenly happiness consists in an idle life of leisure, and inactivity in which they will be served by others and by the angels of God, are in a state of selfishness and covetousness which would mean every one desiring the service and the happiness of others for himself, and what every one would wish for no one could have for such state would be an idle, wanton state of existence, and not an active life of service; and it would stupefy and derange all godlike qualities which would kill all happiness; and they would be cast out of heaven into hell, for the very word heaven means service where every one must seek his own good in the service he renders to others; and the greater the service, the greater the good and the happiness. 

Heavenly joy, bliss, peace and happiness consist in giving and not in receiving, "For it is more blessed to give than to receive;" and he that seeks or covets for himself the least that belongs to another curses his own soul; and he that seeks the preference of others to himself finds the greatest good in preferring others to himself, for he seeks the good of uses as a matter of performing the good of uses as heavenly services which does not consist in the out-

ward splendor of material things as silver and gold, but what persons in themselves represent of the Divine qualities in service. 

The spirit of God is the instrument by which God acts, wills, chooses, designs, purposes and executes His plans and purposes, just as one's spirit lives, acts, feels, chooses, designs and purposes by reason of the life that is given it through the sustaining power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven, as no one has the power, save our Divine Father, to act from Himself, and all others must act from Him though they act as from themselves; but he who ceases to act as from the Lord ceases to be alive unto God by refusing to recognize our Divine Father as the source from whence he received his existence and powers; and by so doing such an one dooms himself to perdition by cutting himself off from the source of all life.

Our Divine Father's glorious superangelical Son and first-born of all creation passed from a spirit, being, personage through incarnation into a body of flesh and blood like unto His human brethren and by way of the cross He passed again from the flesh into a glorified personal existence which is immortal and eternal. 

This shows how our Divine Father in heaven can change the habitation of His creatures from one form of existence into another at will through the infinite, omnipotent power of His Holy Spirit; and as the incarnate Son of God the Word lives and reigns triumphant through the power of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven, let us also take hope and live in faith that the prayer of God's glorious Son the incarnate Word Jesus Christ will also be answered in our behalf; "That where Christ is there also shall His followers be through a glad and glorious resurrection from the dead unto the life which is immortal and eternal."

The spirit is essential to the life of the body, but the body is not essential to the life of the spirit of a person as has been shown by our Divine Father by many infallible proofs in that our Divine Father by the infinite power of His Holy Spirit resuscitated through His Son the incarnate Word Jesus Christ the lifeless bodies of several during Christ's Messianic ministry on the earth, as well as Christ Himself rising gloriously from the tomb in accordance with the promise of His Divine Father to raise Him from the dead, thus proving that our physical form is not essential to the life of our spirit.

The sacred scriptures inform us that our Divine Father by His spirit raised up His Son Jesus from the dead without any mediating person or agent coming between our Divine Father and His glorious Son the incarnate Word Jesus who arose from the state of death to the immortal state of life. In those instances in which others were raised to life there was, so far as the scriptures inform us, a mediating agent between the dead and our Divine Father in which the deceased were raised to life; but all these were restored simply to their living, physical, mortal state of life and were subject again to mortality and died again; but the Son of God whom our Divine 

Father raised from the dead without any intervening agent was blessed with immortality and an endless life.

By all that has been said it can easily be seen and understood that our Divine Father in heaven only is Divine in His person and spirit, and power. That this is true is deduced from the connection of cause and effect, and the truths of Divine revelations; but this conclusion is not generally arrived at by those who become irrational by perjuring continually their reason with falsities or by those who have no desire to understand, because it is opposed to the false ideas which have been taught them all their lives as Divine truths, until they have become established in error, and they are therefore unwilling to understand any reasons because of the resistance they would meet from the ecclesiastical powers which control the Church; and the fear of ostracism, vengeance, persecutions and excommunication from the Church whose tenets have become established in error, they fear to depart from it and in this way they force themselves to continue in error and falsities. 

That the Holy Spirit, is the spirit of our Divine Father in heaven is a truth of God, of heaven, of Jesus Christ, of the prophets, of angels, of saints, of the apostles, of martyrs, of the first Christians, of science, of reason, of the heart, of the mind, of the spirit, of the conscience, and of most all demons save our Doctors Divinitis who proclaim it is the third Divine person in a triune God. Consequently the motive or executive power which goes forth from God goes forth from His spirit because it is the executive power of His person, the same as man's spirit is the executive power of man's person which acts through his physical body to perform the works of man; but the spirit of God is not thus limited to a material organism like the spirit of man.

The ruling love or delights of man's spirit becomes his universal delights in the world to come, which in the case of Christians is from the Lord, while the delights of those who are evil are that of self; and therefore, anyone who has this knowledge can ascertain and know what his own state after death will be, if he knows what his ruling love is, in its relation to the things Divine. 

It is quite impossible for those who are in the love of self to clearly discern what their ruling love is, because they love what they call their own, and call such evil good, because of the falsities they have been taught they have adopted and confirmed themselves in what they call truths however absurd, inconsistent and contradictory they might be with the Divine teaching which says: "Blessedness consists in giving;" and they are unwilling to permit themselves to be filled with any other than love of self which is to appropriate everything to their own lusts of greed, selfishness and covetousness, and they therefore, spurn the teaching of the Lord by loving themselves above all else; but those who are in heavenly love follow Divine instructions; and just as soon as they are brought into contact with the evils in which they were born they see them and seek to shun them for truths; but those who do not know truths, neither the scriptures, readily accept heresies and oppose truths to their own destruction.

Children do not readily see evils and falsities in the things they are taught; and they may be born and reared in the greatest of errors without perceiving them; and even the falsities which arise in themselves may be hidden from the eyes of their understanding, because they were born, reared, and educated in evils and falsities; and, as a rule, they are ever ready to resist, resent, and oppose everything strange; and when they are grown up they know not what is truth or what to believe; and the limited time they have from secular duties is generally passed in worldly sports; and their religious life generally remains in the groove in which they were reared, and they are too ignorant to know why they have remained so. 

On the other hand those who are in heavenly truths accept instruction and carefully weigh all the evidence and try every spirit by the Divine word of the gospel, and bear fruits of good which grow and develop into works of charity which corresponds in every way with the Divine will; and all such are able to discern the difference between truth and error because they are ever examining the

things which come into their lives by the Divine standard of truth, who take nothing for granted as truth or correct until they have thoroughly tested and proved its consistency with reason and with scripture.

There are those who apply teachings and practices to the Church other than those handed down to us by Jesus Christ and His apostles who are impostors, schism makers, heresiarchs, destroyers of the truth, and enemies of God, for the kingdom of God consists in doing those very things of charity and of worship promulgated by Jesus Christ and His apostles for the worshipping of our Divine Father; and not to do just what Christ has commanded and substitute other things, is rejecting Him, as they are not Divine injunctions and are contrary to Jesus Christ's teaching, and cannot be in harmony with the Divine; and those who by semblance of goodness and honesty, justice and truth mislead the simple in mind and heart into falsities are villains who not only destroy themselves but destroy the simplehearted ones for whom Christ died. "The mother of harlots and abominations of the earth," the Roman Catholic Church is the most insane of all the Churches, for they cherish the notion that heaven and hell are both alike subject to their power, and that they can remit sins, grant indulgences, and save the dead; claiming to themselves Divine jursidiction over all civil and ecclesiastical affairs by virtue of their infallibility and Divine succession as the vicegerent of God, and vicar of Jesus Christ. 

The Catholics by their Trinity, confessional, purgatory, limbo, masses for the dead, and indulgences; but the Mormons are a close second with their baptisms by proxy for the dead, seals, celestial marriages, the Deifying of Jesus Christ and the rejection of the scriptures as a sufficient guide to salvation. 

The Divine order of heaven is the kingdom of God in man which is subjective; and the Divine truth that goes forth from the Lord is what constitutes Divine order; and any subtractions, additions or changes in the teachings and practices executed by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven through His Son Jesus Christ and His apostles are heresy and corruptions of the truth and of the 

Divine order of things.

Our Divine Father wills the salvation of all and the destruction of none; but it is inconsistent with His Divine majesty to say that 

He is able to save all apart from means which He has provided

without destroying the rationality and liberty of man; but without rationality and liberty man would not be man. Therefore, it is far better that those who would be saved by means should be saved; but those who will not be saved by means should be destroyed; for it is inconsistent that God should save people against their will; so our Divine Father in heaven has provided means of repentance through the sacrificial atonement of Jesus Christ that whosoever believeth on Him should not perish but have the life eternal; but they who are in rebellion against God and every principle of truth and of righteousness have no claim upon His love, mercy and goodness, and to use force would never bring salvation to those who are obstinate and rebellious.

By the use of means man, if he will, is brought back to the Lord and to salvation by repentance and faith in Jesus Christ as God's

Son and Mediator; in this way he receives the kingdom of God within himself, and enters heaven through the obedience of His will; and by this act of faith it is evident that the Divine mercy is not mercy apart from means but with it. 

Entering heaven is not so much of an external act as it is an internal one, for if we could be saved apart from means every kind of error, falsity and sin would run rampant; and heaven itself would become the home of every foul and wicked spirit; but thanks be to 

God for His infinite wisdom who has provided the use of means of escape for all who wish to be pure, virtuous, loving, thankful and appreciative to live apart from the associations of hell; for the wicked harass, vex, and torment the righteous in this world so that it will be a great relief to them to be rid of all such when they get to heaven where the righteous are eternally at peace. 

There are literally millions of people in the world who try to get themselves and their friends to heaven in a different way from that which our Divine Father has provided. The Roman Catholics have their purgatory, sell indulgences and say masses for their dead; and the Mormons baptize the dead by living proxies, and sell seals to their membership for families and friends by which these persons are to be united in the next world; and in this way many innocent children have been dragged down from heaven into hell so as to be with their families.

Many people seem to have the idea that entering heaven is merely gaining admission to some far away mansion, and that those who are let in are filled and thrilled with ecstatic and heavenly joy; but such

people are ignorant of what heavenly joy consists, and where it is to be found; and therefore it is well to tell you, if you would know when, where, and how it is to be attained. Read very carefully the 

New Testament given to us by our Divine Father in heaven through 

Jesus Christ His only begotten Son; and it will tell you what heaven is like, and how to find the kingdom of God which is nearer to you than hands and feet, "for the kingdom of God is within you, and if you have on the wedding garment of righteousness, of faith, repentance, and charity you are in the kingdom of God already."

Be assured of this serious truth that faith alone on your part, or mercy alone on the Lord's part will not save you, for you must be born again through the re-creation of the Holy Spirit of your Divine Father in your person or regenerated by the conversion of all your loves and affections into works of righteousness; for it is the subjection of your will and goods to works of righteousness for which 

God will supply you with life and every good thing forever. 

How beautiful, grand, glorious and sublime God is! He who has taught us that everyone is just such as his will and his own acts make him to be; and that our Divine Father will not destroy man's rationality and liberty to save him; but He will perpetuate them so long as man will permit Him to do so; and for this reason it is evident that no one can be received into heaven from mercy apart from means.

Every one from his birth is initiated into the civil and moral life of his country and follows them very much according to custom, and some the spiritual in very much the same way; but it is the province of the spiritual man to act in what he believes to be right in the eyes of the Lord while the common man acts in a moral and civil manner without reference to his Divine Creator. In most respects the common man and the spiritual man act the same outwardly but inwardly their motives are different. 

The evil in man is the hell in him which is his own lusts and passions; for God wills him only that which is good. Man is therefore, the cause of his own evil and punishment which our Divine Father in heaven seeks, through His Son Jesus Christ, to eliminate from man; and the Lord is in no way the cause of man's hurt, for your 

Divine Father is doing all that infinite wisdom, love and power can do to lead man away from evil and sin in order to get him safely to heaven; but there are so many who reject or spurn His proffered

mercy; and proceed to cast themselves into hell against His will to save them by means in spite of all He has done for them. 

It is so far from our Divine Father casting anyone into hell that He tries in every way to get man to reform to prevent him from coming into that terrible place of torment where He is compelled by His goodness to destroy the incorrigible man like one does a sick or wounded beast to keep him from suffering.

Our Divine Father has surely tried to save man, in that, "He gave His only begotten Son that whosoever believeth on Him should not perish but have everlasting life;" and Christ so freely offered

Himself a willing sacrifice to His Divine Father for the salvation of man, so that all regenerated sinners, the innocents, and the pure might live with Him in heaven forever; and all those who do go down to hell and destruction must force themselves to trample the flesh and blood of a crucified Savior beneath their feet before they can cast themselves into hell; and, it is terribly wicked, sinful, and ungodly for anyone to say that God casts people into hell when He tries in every possible way in keeping with man's free moral agency to prevent them from coming into that bad place; and it is sheer wickedness, infernal and satanic to say that God casts people into an everlasting hell of fire where there will be suffering, pain and torture forever.

All who go to hell do so because it is their choice to love sin and wickedness, for always and only that which is good and truth comes from our Divine Father in heaven, and it is the rankest blasphemy to charge God with unfriendliness toward the wicked, and no one can receive moral evil unless he wills it and loves it, and for man's voluntary acts of evil God is not responsible or to blame for all acts of evil are against His will and His laws; and every evil has its own punishment; and the one doing the evil is the one doing the punishing, and man doing the evil punishes himself the same as the one who places his hand in the fire is the one who inflicts the pain, and so it is in all moral and spiritual affairs, the one who goes wrong inflicts the punishment upon his own soul.

There are some people in this world who are so intensely wicked that even after the Lord Jesus Christ has spanned death and hell to rescue them from these, will not have Him as their Lord and Savior, and they turn their faces toward the Antichrist and recognize Him as their law-giver by worshipping his Trinity of coequal persons as Divine and keeping his sabbaths instead of those appointed by the

Lord until they refuse any longer to look upon the torn thorncrowned brow of the Christ and reject His proffered mercy, love, and sacrifice in their behalf; and they put their trust in falsities and rush headlong into the swift rapids of evil and plunge into hell and destruction. All who are in hell are there because they so willed to love the evil of which hell is composed.

The riches, wealth and honors of this world tend to make people haughty, proud, vain, insolent, malicious, contemptible, stupid, ignorant and insane toward spiritual and heavenly things, as they tend to close up the windows of the soul which is covetousness; and all such will not find Jesus Christ in their heart for that is selfishness; but you will find Him in service to your fellow-men that is righteousness; and righteousness is good uses which is the rule of God, for Christ said, "In as much as ye did it unto the least of my brethren, ye did it unto me." Therefore, those who live in good uses of charity are in the realm of God, for such as man's love is such is he.

There is no excellence in anything without great labor, and especially in the knowledge of the things Divine, for the ecclesiastical forces in the Church have buried the truth beneath a mountain of falsities and error and there are but a precious few who delve deep enough to find the pearl of great price by searching and thinking until they find God and see Him in the splendor of His beauty. 

Those who read this book with discretion will find a golden thread of truth, if they will take pains to follow through to its conclusion the story of redemption, it will bring them face to face with their 

Divine Father in heaven; for to see truth and know it experimentally is to see and know God, for God is truth, love, and power more than He is some tangible thing; and He can be seen and viewed abstractly if not concretely, as He is separated from everything material to us. 

God in His infinite wisdom knew that the best way to get us to understand Him was to send His glorious Son the Word, into the world in the form of man to teach us both by precept and example how to live and act in accordance with His will. 

The Bible is the only Divinely constituted authority for the Church and for individual conduct, and it includes within its embrace the whole world of mankind. The teaching and practices of 

Jesus Christ and His apostles, as Divinely commissioned by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven, is the only correct or right rule of faith and practice upon which all Christians can be

⚫ united into one Church, and have that liberty, equality and union for which Christ prayed that His followers should have. 

We have no Divine assurance that those who accept a different gospel than that which Christ and His apostles have given to us will be acceptable to our Divine Father, for no other Divine foundation can anyone lay than that which is laid by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father through Jesus Christ our Divine Father's only begotten Son; and just to the extent that we know God's law and keep it will it bring us into that union and fellowship which is had among the angels of God and His glorified saints. Too long has the Church spurned the prayer of our Lord Jesus Christ in not accepting His word and conduct as the rule of our faith and practice. 

How often did Jesus Christ appeal to the scriptures, and to His own words and works as the expressed will of His Divine Father in heaven whose spirit directed Jesus Christ in what He should say and what He should do? Was it not upon the confession of Saint 

Peter and the rest of the apostles: "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the Living God," that Jesus said, "I will build my Church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it?" Who, then, will presume that the declaratory truths upon which Jesus says, "I will build my Church," is not a sufficient confession of faith for acceptance of membership in His Church?

However sacred to us have become the creeds, liturgies, and ceremonies under which we have been reared; yet, we dare not say that the proclamation which Christ makes; that He accepts into His 

Church all those who confess that He is, "The Christ, the Son of the living God," is not a sufficient confession of faith. If Christ accepts into His Church those who confess that He is, "The Christ, the Son of the living God," what right has any man or set of men to require more than this?

Those who ignore the proclamation, "Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God," as the ordinance of God and of His Son Jesus Christ for entrance into the Church are heresiarchs and enemies of God and of His Son Jesus Christ; for Jesus Christ accepts all of a Christian character into His Church who confess Him to be "The Christ, the Son of the living God."

Jesus taught us in many parables, aside from His personal example, the way to live the life eternal. How marvelous were His words and works in revealing to us the nature of God, and the entrance into His kingdom! Let us deny ourself of our own fantastic notions in follow-

ing the example of Jesus Christ who pleased not Himself but did always the will of His Divine Father who sent Him. Christ declared that the words which He spoke were His Father's words and that He of Himself could do nothing. Christ claims nothing for Himself but obedience to His Divine Father's will and He attributes His person, doctrine and works to His Divine Father. 

The Bible plainly teaches that everything is dependent upon our infinite, omnipotent Divine Father for their existence and powers. 

All truth is of God, and there is no error, inconsistencies, contradictions or falsities in Him or His works; and it behooves those who would know God to know truth also, for no one can truly know God who accepts the Trinity of the Antichrist, who claims that there are three Divine persons in the Deity. It seems that these man-made rituals, liturgies and creeds have bound the people with cords too strong for truth, reason, and the sense of right to prevail. 

We believe many things which are so high a grade of wisdom that we may never fathom or comprehend their philosophy; but we insist that nothing can be true that squarely and positively contradicts the teachings of Jesus Christ and our own private knowledge of fact.

Our purpose in this work is to secure a candid and an unbiased hearing from the people by directing their attention away from their Church affiliations to the teaching and practices of Jesus Christ and His apostles and in their words and works confide. 

We believe with all our heart, mind and spirit that Jesus Christ is the Son of our Divine Father in heaven, the only true and living God; and to believe in His word, and to follow in His example is a sufficient creed for the rule of our faith and practice. It is dangerous and clearly unphilosophical for us to pretend to be wise above the range of Divine revelations and of the human faculties. 

To give heed to and observe the law of our Divine Father delivered unto us by our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, the Son of the Father is the greatest liberty and freedom that it is possible for a human being to attain. Surely Christ knew His relationship to His 

Divine Father and to His fellow-men far better than those narrowminded bigots and impostors who formed the Nicene and Athenatian creeds contrary to His doctrine of one Divine Father and forced them upon the world through a reign of persecution which lasted above a thousand years until the world was forced to acknowledge this three in one Deity of the Antichrist.

Jesus Christ in His prayer to His Divine Father for His disciples said, "This is life eternal that they might know thee, the only true 

God, and Jesus Christ whom thou didst send." Jesus laid the foundation of His Church in the unity and sole Deity of His Divine Father in heaven; and we should accept His inspired earnest words as true notwithstanding to the contrary the many hymns and doxologies recited and sung to a Trinity of Deities. All such hymns, doxologies and creeds teaching a Trinity of Divine persons are inconsistent with scripture, nature, science and reason. We do not say these things in disrespect for the integrity of those who still hold to these erroneous forms of doctrine and opinion fostered onto the world by the Antichrist; but we say them because of our high regard for Jesus' words, science, and reason which condemn them as falsities. 

It is absurd, contradictory and inconceivable to the mind of man as to how anyone could possibly form a just conception of a triune being without being able to formulate how a person can be one and three and three and one at the same time which is a contradiction in terms and contrary to all truth and fact known to man; and, for anyone to profess that there are three infinite persons in one whose attributes individually are infinite, absolute and universal such as those of our Divine Father in heaven are said to be has a deranged mind filled with hallucinations such as only insane people have when they are delirious. One infinite person would naturally exclude there being any other, as one infinite, absolute, independent, unoriginate person would comprehend in himself, of himself, and by himself all perfections and can belong to but one person; and that one person who is thus constituted is our Divine Father in heaven, for He only is uncreate, absolute, and independent in His person and powers.

Our present generation is not responsible for the sins of our parents; but we do say that in so far as it is within our power to correct these great wrongs of the Antichrist that we will be held responsible before God unto future generations if we neglect our duty; and since the light and knowledge of the truth have come we do no longer have an excuse for condoning the sin of idolatry of worshipping three persons as Divine or Deities. Truth is paramount both to authority and sacred association; and our first allegiance is to truth founded upon good substantial, sound evidence such as that revealed in the word of God and corroborated by science and reason

that there is but one Divine person, and He the only true and living 

God the Father.

Since we are taught of God, of Jesus Christ, of His apostles, and of the prophets that Jesus Christ is the Son of God and that faith in Him as such is the entrance into His Church and His kingdom, why then is it necessary to divide the Church of the living and true 

God into so many contending denominations, sects and creeds? Are not the statements of Jesus Christ and of His apostles far better as a guide to faith and practice than the statements of those arch heretics, narrow-minded bigots and impostors who formed the Nicene and Athenation creeds, which creeds declare that there are three Divine persons in one Divine triune person, three in one, or one in three God?

These creeds have been formulated to suit polytheism and idolatry by denying the unity of God to consist of but one Divine person as taught by Jesus Christ and His apostles; and they tend to bring man into subjection to the creature instead of the Creator. 

These heresiarchs were not satisfied with the formulating of these polytheistic creeds for they enforced them upon all others by entering upon a reign of persecution and subjugation to them which lasted above a thousand years until all Christiandom bowed to the sway of these antichrist doctrines. 

Happily those days of the Antichrist's persecution unto death for all dissenters of his creed of three Divine persons in one Divine triune person, has been given a respite from such inquisitions, so that the true followers of Jesus Christ can once more as in the apostolic days, assert their pristine prerogatives of holding the teachings and practices of Jesus Christ and His apostles as their only creed, Christian their only name, and Christian character their only test of fellowship.

Christ and His apostles, through the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven forewarned the Church against the apostasy that would come upon the Church and the attendant persecutions that would immediately follow the setting up of the Antichrist in the transition from the "Dragon" of pagan Rome to the establishment of the "Papal Beast" of the Roman Catholic Church called, "The mother of harlots and abominations of the earth," which was to take possession of the Church after the "Dragon" of Rome had surrendered his power and his seat to the "Beast" of the Papacy which came to pass in the fourth century of the Christian era.

The transition from the "Dragon" of pagan Rome to the "Beast" of papal Rome was accomplished by the conversion of Constantine the Great, Emperor of Rome to the antichrist doctrine of the Pope, the bishop of Rome who persuaded the Emperor to adopt and establish a polytheistic creed of three Divine persons in one under imperial decree which was accomplished at Nicea in the year 325 A. D. disfranchising, excommunication, confiscating of property and of offices all who would not adopt the creed. This gave the bishop of 

Rome the preeminence over all the Churches in matters of morals and of religion to the exclusion of all others throughout the Roman Empire; and the Christians were driven into the "Wilderness" among the barbarians and their property confiscated to the Antichrist, the bishop of Rome and to his ecclesiastical See.

Between the council of Nicea and that of Constantinople, a period of fifty-six years, the Trinitarian creed grew to full stature with a full set of teeth to destroy or devour by assimilation the remaining Christians by adopting what was called the Athenatian creed which defined more minutely the polytheistic doctrine of three Divine persons in one; and the Trinitarian formula of baptism was interpolated into the gospel of Saint Matthew contrary to the apostolic teaching and custom; and all compelled to baptize in the name of the Trinity of God the Father, God the Son, and God the Holy Ghost, instead of only in "The name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins," and for admission into the Church according to apostolic teaching and custom.

So much of the data of historical events of the Christians of the first three hundred years of the Christian era have been destroyed, and those which have not, have been in most part interpolated, mutilated, misrepresented, misinterpreted and mistranslated by the Antichrist school so that there is little left to us but the acts of the apostles by Saint Luke of the actual teachings and practices of Christ's apostles which, taken together with the writings of Saint Paul give us a fair outline of the Christians of the first two centuries of Christianity.

Those who have read and those who care to read the acts of the apostles and the Epistles of Saint Paul will soon discover how great innovations the antichristian Trinitarian doctrine of the Antichrist have made in the teaching and practices of Jesus Christ and His apostles.

Our Divine Father in heaven, who alone is the essence of love,

life, power, wisdom, knowledge, time, unity, infinity, absoluteness, and independence subsisting in the one person of His sole eternal being as the only Divine person, Deity, God, Father, Creator, omnipotent, omniscient, omnipresent, ubiquitous, universal person from which all things else receive their origin, of which, God's glorious superangelical Son, the Word, was the origin or beginning of our Divine Father's creation and heir of all things; so that there is not anything of all creation of which He has not been made king, prince, prime-minister, Lord, Master and heir, not only of the things of earth but also the things of heaven such as angels, principalities, powers, cherubims, seraphims and the creatures which worship before God's throne being made subject to Him. 

Our Divine Father has made all things of His creation in subjection to His glorious Son the incarnate Word Jesus Christ whom He has appointed heir of all things, and all things are subject to our Divine Father through Him as our Divine Father only is superior to His Son the incarnate Word Jesus Christ as His God, Father, Creator and Lord.

Our Divine Father in the beginning placed His first-born Son of all creation, the Word, over all things else which He did through the Word create as His agent; and as it was through Him that He chose to create the worlds and all things so also it was through Him that He chose to redeem the world from sin and death its penalty, and how does He do it?

Our Divine Father appoints His glorious Son, the Word, the firstborn creature of His creation to act as His agent and mediator to redeem His fallen creature, man, through the redemption of the debt of man by one who was not of Adam's race and not subject to the debt because of Adam's transgression; and the two principal factors to be considered are: First, what was the debt; and second, what it required to redeem it?

Our first proposition is that of Adam's sin of transgression who was created innocent and pure, in the image of God's likeness of rationality and liberty or free moral agency; but with sentient perceptions, appetites and desires; and placed in a garden called Eden near the head-waters of the four rivers, Pison, Gihon, Hiddekel, and Euphrates which garden Adam was to cultivate for a livelihood. 

Our Divine Father's glorious Son, the superangelical Word was appointed by His Divine Father with potential powers of authority to engineer this Eden project; and He told His ward of His Divine

Father's rules and regulations concerning his precarious existence which depended upon his conduct and his Divine Father's pleasure or it would become lost, forfeited or taken away. 

Adam could not be in the likeness of God without becoming a sentient, rational person with freedom and liberty or free moral agency given him of his Divine Father by which he had the choice of choosing in the face of an alternative; but with the choice is involved grave responsibilities of duty and of obedience toward His Divine Creator. So the Son of God busied Himself with planting every kind of tree in the garden of Eden that was good for food; and the tree of knowledge of good and of evil also in the midst of the garden as a test tree, the fruit of which was not to be eaten nor handled by man, for in the day that he ate thereof he would die in accordance with the command of his Divine Father. 

The Son of God told Adam that the Lord God his Divine Father commanded that of all the trees of the garden he may freely eat with but one exception of the tree of knowledge of good and of evil he should not eat of it neither should he touch it lest he should die the death of mortality. and

Adam entered bravely upon his task of securing provisions for himself, but he became discouraged and the Lord God said that it is not good that man should be alone, so the Lord God commanded His Son to make a help-mate for Adam of Adam's own flesh and blood. So the Lord God caused a deep sleep to fall upon Adam,

God's Son took one of Adam's ribs and made for him a wife and brought her unto Adam, and officiated for Adam, and the woman's nuptial tie by which the woman became Adam's wife; and Adam called his wife's name Eve because she is the mother of the human race.

Adam informed his wife of all that the Lord God had commanded concerning the fruits and vegetables of the garden, but when she saw the tree of knowledge of good and of evil that it was delightful to the eyes and desirous to make one wise she ate of the fruit and gave also to her husband and he likewise ate also of the fruit; and their eyes were opened and they saw their nakedness and hid themselves from the presence of the Lord among the trees of the garden for they were afraid, because they had eaten of the forbidden fruit which the Lord had commanded them that they should not eat lest they die. 

The Lord called unto Adam and said unto him, "Because thou

hast harkened unto the voice of thy wife and have partaken of the forbidden fruit which I commanded that you shouldst not eat thereof, cursed is the ground for thy sake, and thou shalt live by the sweat of thy brow;" and the Lord said unto the woman, "Because you have partaken of the fruit and also given to your husband, you shall bring forth children in pain and sorrow, and your desire shall be unto your husband, and he shall rule over thee; but in your bearing of children I will raise up for you of your seed a redeemer who shall bruise the serpent's head, but He shall bruise thy heel."

CHAPTER XIX 

The whole human race is represented in Adam, and the fall of Adam was the fall of the human race; but our gracious heavenly 

Father has something far better still in store for those who are regenerated by faith and repentance through the vicarious atonement of the redeemer, the incarnate Word, Jesus the Christ; so the 

Lord drove Adam and his wife from the garden and placed impassible angel barriers between them and the tree of life in the midst of the garden, so that they could no longer eat of it and live in sin and rebellion forever; but cut them off in death reserving them in this state unto the restoration of all things at the end of the world, when all shall be brought forth through the resurrection from the dead, those who have done good will be resurrected unto the life eternal; and those who have persisted in evil shall be destroyed.

It is our moral, rational, intellectual freedom, liberty and free moral agency which make us in the image, likeness, and prototype of our Divine Father in heaven in day in which we were created. 

But alas! We have become impure, we are all undone, and who is able to save us from the body of this death? We have sinned, and we are no more worthy to be called children of God because of the loss of these life sustaining qualities of immortality which our Divine Father gave to man on the day in which He created him. 

But thanks be to God that through Jesus Christ the incarnate Word God's glorious first-born Son of all creation has offered Himself as the price of man's redemption that whosoever through faith and repentance would accept Him as their vicarious atonement should not perish but have everlasting life through a glad and glorious resurrection at the reappearing of Jesus Christ at the end of this gospel age.

It was this power of choice to live up to our responsibilities or to neglect duty which was abused by our inexperienced first parents which gave them the opportunity to disobey and sin against their Creator. The penalty for their disobedience was death, and trans- 381

missible to their posterity, so that through their disobedience all the human family is subject to mortality. 

Our father, Adam, had no sooner sinned when our great, loving, beneficent and compassionate heavenly Father promised a redeemer by which we could safely pass through this mortal state, and be given the life eternal by our acceptance and obedience to Him. But the penalty of death due to Adam's disobedience in breaking God's law will forever be visited upon the human family, as it has been decreed that flesh and blood cannot enter into the kingdom of God. To pass this mortal state occasioned by the fall to that immortal state and likeness of God promised to those who follow the teachings and practices of the gospel of the redeemer, is our present inquiry.

God's glorious Son, Jesus Christ, who in His antemundane, preincarnate state was called "The Word of God," was chosen by our Divine Father to act as His mediator or agent in the things pertaining to this world, as both in creation and reconciliation of man He was given the preeminence over all things as God's Son and heir; but not solely because of this relationship does He hold this exalted position; but God chose Him because He is the greatest, grandest, sublimest and most devoted character to His Divine Father of all His creation; and since He was superior to all of Adam's race who fell by transgression into a state of death, He was anxiously solicitous to be of service to His Divine Creator and Father for the redemption of man. It was His Divine Father's good pleasure to choose 

Him as the instrument or agent of man's redemption which was accomplished by our Divine Father through His first-born Son of all creation being made incarnate in fulfillment of the promise which He had made to Adam after his transgression that through their bearing of children He would give them a savior who would redeem them, if they would continue in well doing. 

It is estimated that more than four thousand years elapsed between the time the Savior or Redeemer was promised until He came in fulfillment of the promise; but God's glorious first-born Son of all creation, the Word, foreknew before the foundation of the world the plans and purposes of His Divine Father that through Him the world would be redeemed, and when He revealed the promise of His Divine Father to Adam that through their bearing of children He would raise up for them a redeemer, He then knew that He was the

one who should come in fulfillment of the promise. Oh the joy, the ecstasy of such Divine service!

It was the plan of our Divine Father in heaven to incarnate His first-born Son of all creation, the Word, in a robe of flesh and make Him like unto those He was sent to redeem. So our Divine Father sent the Angel Gabriel to a city of Galilee called Nazareth unto a virgin whose name was Mary of the house and lineage of David; and 

Gabriel said unto Mary, "Thou art highly favored of God; and blessed art thou among women; for behold thou shalt conceive a son by the power of the Holy Spirit of thy Divine Father in heaven; and thou shalt call His name Jesus, the Son of God. He shall be great, and God shall give unto Him the throne of His Father David. 

Mary accepted with gratitude the message of God's angel in these submissive words, "Behold, the hand-maid of the Lord, be it done unto me according to thy word." God's promise was fulfilled to the

Virgin Mary. After the angel had departed, Mary arose and went in haste unto the hill country of Judea to visit her cousin Elizabeth, the mother of John the Baptist. When Elizabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven overshadowed with Divine power the virgin whose name was Mary, and Mary conceived God's glorious Son and the "Word of God" became incarnate; and when the Word was born of the Virgin Mary she called His name Jesus by Divine appointment.

Jesus grew in knowledge, in stature, and in favor with God and men and when He was about thirty years old, He entered upon public life, and began immediately to fulfill the plan and mission for which our Divine Father had incarnated Him and sent Him into the world.

Our Divine Father had sent Jesus' cousin John the Baptist to baptize the people unto repentance, and to announce the arrival of the long-time promised Messiah and the commencement of His ministry.

The incarnate Word, Jesus Christ, in order to fulfill all righteousness came unto John the Baptist to be baptized of him, but John forbad Him saying: "I need to be baptized by thee, and why comest thou to me?" But Jesus answered, "Suffer it to be so, for it behooves us to fulfill all righteousness," so John baptized Him; and when 

Jesus was baptized the power of the Holy Spirit of His Divine Father descended from heaven and abode upon Him; and a voice

from out of that excellent glory said, "This is my beloved son in whom I am well pleased."

Thus the man Christ Jesus, the Son and heir of our Divine Father in heaven instead of being possessed of a human, rational spirit like unto us, He was animated by the superangelical spirit of the "Word of God" the pre-existent, superangelical Son of our Divine Father in heaven, so that His mundane state of existence was that of choice and not of necessity or of the accidents of the flesh as He did not belong to Adam's race.

It was the choice of our Divine Father; and also of the Word, God's glorious Son and heir that He, the Word, who was not subject to death or mortality like unto us on account of Adam's sin, should assume a human body of flesh and blood subject to all the trials, hardships, pain and suffering of man that He might make an offering of His body of flesh in sacrifice for our sins in order to free us through repentance and reformation from the penalty of mortality due to our sins through the resurrection from the dead unto the life eternal and immortal.

In order to redeem us from mortality to which we, through Adam's transgression are subjected, it necessitated that the offering in our behalf be made by one who was not subject to the penalty of God's broken law, as Adam and all his posterity were subject, as it necessitated that the offering be made by one who could pay in our behalf which He personally did not owe; the glorious Son of 

God became incarnate in human flesh and offered His body as a vicarious atonement to pay the penalty of death due to our sin inherited from Adam; and this He accomplishes for all the penitent, and those who have the answer of a good conscience toward God through the resurrection from the dead to the life eternal and immortal at His coming.

According to God's plan of salvation, man is taken from the grasp of death, the penalty due to God's broken law which forever consigned him to be cut off from life and from God's holy presence; and commends him through the sacreficial atonement of Jesus Christ to God's love, clemency and mercy, for all who through faith and repentance toward God will accept the vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ and acknowledge Him as their Lord and Redeemer. When the atoning blood of Jesus Christ, God's sacrificial lamb was shed for man on the cross, all legal and ceremonial sacrifices of the law and their obligations ceased. Through Christ's sacrificial death for

man all ceremonial sins and inadvertances were cleansed away. That is, they were abrogated or legitimately commuted. 

Mount Calvary is the place where a righteous Savior died as a sacrificial offering to make an atonement for our sins. Without the law there could be neither justice nor mercy for they would have no claim upon the creature, as there could be no transgression without law. But there is a law given and a penalty affixed, and were it not for the atonement, no one would be saved of Adam's race; for we all have sinned and fallen short of fulfilling God's law. Through the atonement by Jesus Christ, made for man, a "Repentance unto life," is granted to man which our Divine Father's mercy claims, otherwise justice would claim the creature, man, and man would be lost forever, as justice would execute the law and its punishment upon him.

Through the vicarious sacrifice of atonement made by Jesus Christ for man our Divine Father excuses those sins which have been committed involuntarily through ignorance; and is effective unto salvation to those who are innocent, or repentant ones, those who are not innocent; but the deliberate or voluntary transgression of God's law is not only mortal death but spiritual death also and is effective not only because of Adam's sin inherited by us but also because of unrepentant, deliberate sin on the part of those who do not repent and turn to God; for only those who answer to God with a good conscience of innocence or repentance will be rescued from the penalty of the law through the resurrection from the dead to the life immortal and eternal; and all others destroyed in eternal death at the day of judgment.

Through the atonement of Jesus Christ for man both the law and the penalty for sin are satisfied, and the sinner is made at one with 

God by repentance through God's only begotten Son our Lord and 

Savior Jesus Christ as mediator between God and man. God hates sin, because it is the great destroyer, but He cannot forgive sin without repentance and acceptance of Jesus as His Son and Mediator, as His mercy and favor grants absolution only when we repent and accept the atonement of Jesus Christ in our behalf in acknowledgement of our sin. Which repentance and acceptance of

Jesus Christ and His atonement on our part, our Divine Father accepts as a full satisfaction for His broken law and restores man through the resurrection from the dead, to the life immortal and eternal.

The atonement brings to pass the resurrection from the dead, and the resurrection from the dead brings back men into the image and likeness of God. Thus man is restored to life through the resurrection from the dead because of the atonement made by Jesus Christ for man, and because of man's concurrent repentance or innocence in connection with the atonement which has satisfied God's law, so that all who will repent of their sins, and accept the atonement made by Jesus Christ in their behalf will be saved.

Both good and bad people will be resurrected but not at the same time. The good people will be resurrected first and enter into everlasting joy, peace and happiness of a life which is eternal and immortal; but the wicked people will be resurrected later and come forth for judgment and everlasting destruction. Thus both good and bad will be resurrected from the dead because of Christ's superhuman atonement for all mankind; but only those will be accepted of God unto eternal life who repent of their sins by returning to righteousness and allegiance to our Divine Father, truth and virtue; but those who accept and follow the idolatrous worship of the Antichrist of three Divine persons, called the Holy Trinity by the "Mother of harlots and abominations of the earth," it will be just too bad for them; for the fourteenth chapter of Divine Revelations of Saint John tells us that, "The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God which is poured out without mixture into the cup of His indignation, and they shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the Holy Angels, and in the presence of the 

Lamb; and the smoke of their torment ascendeth up forever and ever; and they have no rest day nor night who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name." 

In view of God's wrath pronounced upon His children of disobedience who die in the services of the Antichrist, the Papal "beast;" that even after the resurrection from the dead, justice exercises all of his demands upon idolatrous worshippers, and will execute his judgments of the law upon all who refuse to repent of their abominations in this life and accept in their behalf the mediatorial, vicarious atonement of Jesus Christ the Son of God for their sins; for, unless accepted in good faith and acted upon it, the atonement of Jesus Christ for them is of no avail; and the judgments of the law will be executed upon all such to their utter destruction in the day of judgment; for the mediatorial atonement of 

Jesus Christ for the remission of their sins has absolutely no effect

upon the penalty of the law for those who refuse to repent of their sins and idolatrous abominations of worshipping three Divine persons as one; and they, therefore will forever and anon be cut off from God's holy presence to perish in the second death, the death of the soul, of body, mind and spirit. But, mercy claims that which is her own, and only the incorrigible, deliberate, unrepentant sinner is lost or claimed by the law. No mercy can be shown to the unrepentant sinner and he must therefore stand the judgments of the law, and meet his doom of destruction, of annihilation in the day of judgment.

But whosoever will may come and drink of the waters of life freely, and be saved from the penalty of death due to his sins through restoration to life and immortality by repentance through faith in the mediatorial, vicarious atonement of the Son of God in his behalf, by accepting Christ Jesus, God's only begotten Son as his Lord and Savior who at His coming will reclaim Him from death through a glad and glorious resurrection to life and immortality. 

Come, for all things are now ready! Heaven awaits your coming. 

Confess your sins, and bow down. Worship before God's great white throne! Christ and His bride, the Church welcome you upon the terms of the gospel of Jesus Christ. Behold! Now is the accepted time; now is the day of salvation, for all who repent!

The Word, God's incarnate Son Jesus Christ, is God's legal substitute for all sacrificial offerings for sin and all ceremonial inadvertances made under the law, and you are now to enter into the holy of holies of heaven itself by a new and living way by doing your bit in proclaiming to a lost and despairing world that the Church for which Jesus Christ shed His most precious blood to save is called "Christian" by Divine appointment.

Christ fulfilled God's pure law in His own behalf, and also suffered the penalty of God's broken law in behalf of the human race, as Adam, our representative, could not suffer the penalty of mortality or death in his own room and stead to satisfy the penalty due to his transgression and live, so our Divine Father anxious to save man from such a direful fate seized upon His plan of sending His own beloved Son and first-born of His creation, His glorious Word to be our redeemer and savior by incarnating the Word by the power of His omnipotent spirit in a robe of flesh and blood like unto us whom He was sent to redeem. Christ, the incarnate Word, assumed a body of flesh and blood that He might make of it a

vicarious offering, as a sacrifice for our sins, as a substitute in lieu of the death penalty due to Adam and his posterity because of Adam's transgression; and it is effective unto salvation for all the innocent and those who through faith and repentance will accept His vicarious atonement in acknowledgement of their sin, and turn in their allegiance to God through reformation and good works. 

Jesus said: "Truly, truly, I tell you, those who listen to my word, and believe in the Father who sent me hath eternal life, and they will incur no sentence of judgment, but have already passed from death unto life." "The time is coming, is now here, when the dead will listen to the voice of the Son of God, and those who heed will live; for as the Father hath life in Himself, so hath He given to the Son to have life in Himself; and hath granted Him authority to give life unto others, since He also is the "Son of man." Do not wonder at this, for the time will come when all who are in their graves will hear the voice of the Son of God and come out; the doers of good will be raised to life everlasting; and the doers of evil will be raised to sentence of judgment. I do nothing of my own accord; I pass judgment on no man, it is my Father who passes judgment, as I can do nothing of myself, it is my Father who doeth these things; but if I judge, my judgment is just; for the spirit of my Father is upon me; He hath anointed me with His spirit; for I seek not the doing of my own will; but the will of my Father who sent me. The works which my Father doeth through me is my testimony to the world that the Father hath sent me. My Father hath borne testimony of me, and I am come in the name of my Father." "It is the will of my Father who sent me, that every one who sees the Son and believes on Him should possess eternal life, and that I should raise him up at the last day. Stop murmuring because I said, I am the bread of life which came down from heaven. No one is able to come unto me except the power of the Holy Spirit of my Divine Father draw him, and all who listens to its call comes to me, and I will raise him up at the last day." "I am the bread which came down from heaven, and the bread which I will give is my flesh for the life of the world. Just as the living Father hath sent me; and I live by the Father; so also he that feeds on me, shall live by me also; for such is the bread which came down from heaven and gives His flesh for the life of the world. I will be with you but a little longer and I will petition the Father that He give you another comforter, even His Holy Spirit, that it may abide with you forever. You do

not know the Father, but I know Him, because I came from Him, and He sent me."

Before Christ's crucifixion on the last great day of the feast of the Passover, Jesus stood in the temple and cried aloud: "If anyone is athirst let him come to me and drink; and he who believes on me," as the scripture says, "Out of his life shall flow the spirit of the living God." "I am the light of the world, he who follows me shall not walk in darkness, but he shall enjoy the light of life." So the Pharisees said to Him: "You are testifying to yourself, therefore, your evidence is not valid." "Though I testify to myself my evidence is true, because I know that I speak under the power of the spirit of God. The spirit of my God is upon me, I came from 

God and I return to Him; but you do not know where I came from or where I am going. I am not alone, for my Father is with me; so there is myself and my Father who sent me; and He has borne witness of me in many mighty works; and it is written in your law that the evidence of two witnesses is valid. I testify of myself, and the works that my Father does through me bear testimony that He has sent me. Unless you believe that I am the Christ, the Son of

God, ye shall die in your sins, and that where I am ye cannot come.' 

"When you will have lifted up the son of man, you will then know that I am the Son of the Father whom ye call your God; for

I do nothing of my own accord, but as my Father has taught me so I do. Were I to glorify myself, my glory is nothing, it is my Father who glorifies me, of whom ye say He is your God." 

Jesus in His prayer to His Divine Father says: "I thank thee 

Father, Lord of heaven and earth that thou hast hidden these things from the wise and prudent of this world and hast revealed them unto babes." Yes, our Divine Father has revealed unto babes by the power and majesty of His spirit that which our man-monkey scientists by delving into the earth will never know; for man has never as yet beheld anything but what is dependent, whether it be mind, matter, substance, or spirit, it had a creator which gave it existence, form and life; "for no man can see God and live."

All things which man has seen are dependent and finite and receive their being, form and life from our Divine Father who is invisible to the sight of man, though He be the possessor of all things visible and invisible as He only is uncreate, absolute and independent in His person and powers. 

Those scientists who boast that they have progressed beyond their

Creator, the "Monkey-Scientist" who kept grooming himself until he developed himself into a man, better take a little heed to themselves, as pride always goes before a fall; and they had better not boast themselves against their irrational, uncouth creator lest he suddenly turn them into some Tasmanian devil, or satanic imp; for if a monkey can make a man he is greater than the greatest scientist known among men and deserves the highest niche in the temple of fame and it is high time that our evolutionist scientists build an altar to their monkey God to whom they owe their being, and all that they are and have.

The human or even the superhuman so long as it does not include the one and only Divine person of our heavenly Father has no being, life, power, person, or authority of himself as He is the only unoriginate, uncreate, self-existent one; and all things else receive their origin and powers from Him, so there is no one that can grant power to do a Divine act but He; and as the forgiveness of sins is a prerogative of our Divine Father only, He may grant to others under His power and direciton specific instances of forgiveness through His delegated agencies; but such power cannot rightfully be claimed as belonging to anyone save our Divine Father in heaven; and in this sense only does Jesus Christ save His people from their sins, sicknesses and death by the power and authority of 

His Divine Father.

The power of doing a Divine act is superhuman and superangelical and super-creatorial, that is, a creature has no power to do a Divine act of himself, but our Divine Father may do Divine acts through him such as creating and forgiving of sins under the direction and power of the Holy Spirit, so it is not the creature but our Divine Father doing His works through them. Anyone claiming the power or authority to forgive sins should be prepared to heal the body also as an earnest of such Divine power and authority from our Divine Father in heaven who is absolute in all these things; for he who cannot heal the sick, is not to be depended upon to forgive sins; for he to whom God grants the one, He grants the other also; and it is a falsity, a swindle, and an imposition on the credulity of the ignorant for any minister to sell indulgences, seals, masses or any services whatsoever as a means of forgiveness of sins. 

It is not in the province of any creature, whether man or angel to forgive sin which is a personal transgression against a personal moral law of God and can be absolved by our Divine Father only

who is absolute in all things Divine; and He gives no one the power or authority of acting for Him; but He will act through men and angels who are in subjection to His spirit and purposes when He wills to do so; but the prerogative of forgiving sins is exercised only and always by the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven whether immediately or mediately through others and not others acting for Him, but in conjunction with Him, as the prerogatives of our Divine Father's Holy Spirit are not transferable to any other person or persons, as all Divine acts are done always and only by it; and there is no such thing as apostolic succession, as this office has nothing to do with the granting of this power whatsoever, as all such things are dependent exclusively on the will, choice, and induement of the power and authority of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father and not upon the accidents of position in the Church or upon some ecclesiastical election to position in the Church, as most every kind of demon, villain, bastard, reprobate, or heresiarch has filled the office of Pope, president, and bishop in the Church. 

The forgiveness of sins is not a prerogative of the Church or of any ecclesiastical See, but solely of our Divine Father in heaven and every one is directly forgiven by our Divine Father in heaven upon his repentance and reformation as truly as if he had some Divinely authorized person like the Son of God; for no one has the right to act in such matters as forgiveness of sins only by special direction of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven; and those who assume such office of their own accord or by human appointment are villains and reprobates if they assume to exercise the power of forgiving sins which is a prerogative of the Divine Father only. 

Our Divine Father in heaven has through His prophets, through His Son, and through His Son's apostles given us sufficient examples of the workings of His Holy Spirit in the office of forgiveness of sins that no one needs to be in ignorance of its operations. 

There must be a special or specific induement of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven such as Christ received at His baptism, and such as His disciples received in the cenacle of Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost after Christ's ascension, before they have a right to operate in the name, and by the power and authority of our Divine Father in heaven in the forgiveness of sins. Then and only then has man the right to act as a mediate between God and other creatures of His creation; for without the power and authority of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father no one can operate

or perform that which is Divine however much he may claim Divine power and authority.

Thus, our Divine Father, gave to His Son Jesus Christ, and to His apostles the Holy Spirit, the key of all power and authority, that by it whosoever they bound on earth should be bound in heaven. You will observe that it is through the Holy Spirit of our 

Divine Father that sins are forgiven or retained; and not by any special virtue of any ecclesiastical office held by Jesus Christ or His apostles; but all such power is exercised by the Holy Spirit of God; and they are to act in accordance with its dictation and execution, and in no other way. The absolving from sin and the retaining of sins is not left to the caprice or discretion of either Jesus Christ nor yet of His apostles but with the spirit of God the executor of all things Divine.

Our blessed Lord and Savior Jesus Christ gave His apostles authority to preach, baptize in His name, confirm, ordain, receive members into the Church or excommunicate in accordance with His instructions under the guidance and power of the spirit of His Divine Father; but He left the questions of sin to the absolving or retaining power of the spirit of His Divine Father which alone is infinite wisdom, knowledge, and power and the executor of all things Divine. Christ taught us however that we should quickly seek to right any injuries committed against our fellows, and seek diligently to come to a rightful agreement with the injured; and with contrition, deep, sincere, and positive ask God's forgiveness for transgressing His holy laws. This means that God requires us to be in agreement or reconciliation with our brother as well as to have repentance toward God for transgressing His commandments. When we do this our sins go before unto judgment and are cleansed away through the vicarious atoning blood shed by Jesus Christ for our sins. No priest or preacher is necessary to pronounce or grant absolution in order to forgiveness, as auricular confession to a minister, if necessary would many times force a contingent upon us poor mortals by which our forgiveness would not depend so much upon our repentance, as it would on our confession to a minister which would make the penitent subservient to the will of man and his passions and whims. Oh God! What a wicked system this is which is antichristian and more cruel than the grave! This system of auricular confession, purgatory, by which masses and indulgences are sold for the salvation of both the living and the dead is the

greatest source of revenue to the Antichrist, and his "Mother of harlots, and abominations of the earth," the Roman Catholic Church, as it secures to its devotees a hope which can be purchased with money; and no one is able to say the amount in billions of dollars that have been paid into the coffers of the Roman Catholic Church for the souls of her parishioners in purgatory.

Martha, after the death of her brother Lazarus said to Jesus: "Lord if you had been here my brother would not have died; but I know that whatever you ask of God, He will grant it to you." Jesus said unto Martha: "Did I not tell you, if you would only believe, you shall see the glory of God?" Then they removed the stone to the entrance of the tomb, and Jesus lifted up His eyes to heaven and said, "Father, I thank thee for listening to me. I knew that thou wouldst always listen to me, but I spoke on the account of the people, that they might believe that thou hast sent me; and that I do nothing of myself; but that all things are done by the power of thy Holy Spirit."
