Let us in word and deed show that we are in truth grateful, thankful, and appreciative toward our gracious Divine Father in heaven. for the gift of His incarnate Son the Word, Jesus Christ through whose vicarious sacrifice as an atonement for our inherited and penitent sins He redeems us at the resurrection of the just; and He says unto us: "Let not your heart be troubled, you believe in God, believe also in me, in my Father's house of many mansions, there are many abodes; if it were not so I would have told you, I go to prepare a place for you, that where I am there ye shall be also." 

Then Jesus prays for His disciples: "Holy Father I am no longer in the world; but they are in the world. Consecrate them dear Father with thy Divine power; and as thou Father art in me and I in thee so may they be one in us and we in them."

Jesus having rested in the tomb after His crucifixion over the Sabbath day, very early Sunday morning came Mary of Magdala with other women to the tomb of Jesus to perfume His body with spices and ointments, but they found not His body in the tomb; so Mary tarried at the tomb weeping over the loss of the body of her beloved Lord; for she knew not yet the scriptures that Christ should rise the third day; and while she tarried Christ, whom she mistook to be the gardener, appeared to her and was made known unto her when He saluted her by name; and immediately she clasped Him by the feet and said: "Rabboni," my great master! Jesus said to her, do not cling to me, for I have not yet ascended to my Divine

The gifts of the Father's Holy Spirit were profusely bestowed upon the disciples during the feast of Pentecost; and the Apostle

Again David says, "Why did the Gentiles rage, and the people vainly conspire? The kings of the earth stood ready; and the rulers mustered together against the Lord and His Christ." "That the people of Israel together with Herod, Pontius Pilate and the Gentiles have mustered together to carry out what the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven has through David foretold they would do is now come to pass; but I wist that through ignorance ye have done these things; and exort you one and all to repent, and 'Be baptized every one of you in the name of Jesus Christ for the remission of your sins,' and ye shall receive the gifts of the Holy Spirit the same as we; for this promise is unto you and unto your children and to as many others as the Lord our God shall call."

To be baptized into Jesus Christ is to be baptized in His name, as Lord and Redeemer, which signifies a burial with Him through His vicarious atonement into His death; and those who thus acknowledge His vicarious atonement for them by being baptized in His name receive remission of sins, as it is both the faith in Christ's vicarious atonement for our sins, and the work of following Him by baptism into His death for which one is honored of God with the gifts of His Holy Spirit of forgiveness of sins, of immortality and of the life eternal. "A repentance unto life" comes by and through

Christ's vicarious atonement for man, and "There is no other name under heaven given among men whereby we must be saved."

Saint Luke tells us, "The multitude of Christian believers were of one heart and one soul," as every one of them did not consider anything in his possession as belonging to himself; and Joseph who was surnamed Barnabas sold a farm and brought the money and laid it at the apostles' feet. So mighty grew the word of God and prevailed that the Church now numbered about five thousand. 

So great was the multitude of believers that there arose a complaint concerning the distribution of provisions, as certain of the Grecian widows had been neglected in the daily ministration and Peter said that, "It is not proper that we should quit preaching, and serve meals." "We therefore recommend brethren that you look out seven men of your number, men of good reputation who are filled with the Spirit of God for wisdom and goodness; and we will appoint them to make distribution of provisions; but we will devote our time to the ministry of the word."

The Church set seven men before the apostles to act as deacons over the Jerusalem Church, which men the apostles by direction of

the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven set apart by the imposition of hands to the work of serving tables, and for the looking after the widows, the poor and the sick folk; but certain ones who belonged to the synagogues of the Lybians, the Syrians, the Alexandrians, and the Asiatics started a disputation with Stephen, one of the seven deacons; but they could not meet the spirit of wisdom with which Stephen spoke; so they suborned witnesses who agitated the Jews by saying: "We have heard Stephen speaking blasphemous words against Moses and against God; and the people brought Stephen before the Sanhedrim and the rulers of the Jews, who, when they heard the bold speech of Stephen gnashed upon him with their teeth, and cast him out of the city and stoned him to death, while Stephen called upon God saying, "Lay not this sin to their charge," he expired saying, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."

A great persecution arose against the Church and the faithful followers of Christ were scattered far and wide throughout Palestine. 

Philip, one of the seven deacons, traveled down to Samaria and preached Christ to them, the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven working through Philip to the performing of many miracles, so the people attended as one man to what was said by Philip, seeing the many miracles that God through him had performed. When the apostles at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had accepted the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John who came down and prayed that the Samaritans might receive the gift of the Holy Spirit, for as yet this gift of the Holy Spirit was not given to any of them, only they were baptized in the "Name of the Lord Jesus Christ." Then Peter and John laid hands on them and they received the gift of the Holy Spirit and prophesied. 

The Roman Catholic Church and most all her dissenters of Protestant denominations would declare the multitudes baptized only in the name of Jesus Christ by the apostles and evangelists of Jesus Christ illegal and invalid; and they would condemn, excommunicate and persecute as heretics Christ's holy apostles, and evangelists should they baptize people now as they did then only in the "Name of Jesus Christ for the remission of sins" and the receiving of the gift of the Holy Spirit which was God's approval and seal of acceptance by Him of their acts.

When a certain sorcerer by the name of Simon saw that through prayer and the laying on of hands the gift of the Holy Spirit was conferred by the apostles on believers, he offered the apostles money

that this gift of the power of God's spirit might be given to him, "So that on anyone on whom I lay my hands he may receive the gift of the Holy Spirit;" but Peter answered: "Death to you and to your money for thinking that you can buy the gift of God's spirit with money."

The gift of the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven, is not a gift of His persons or that of any other person; but it is the gift of the power and authority of the spirit of our Divine Father's person to operate through the believing and obedient to the extent of performing Divine acts severally as our Divine Father chooses to operate according to His will and not otherwise, whether it be wisdom, knowledge, power, discernment, prophecy, miracles or teaching; as only those upon whom our Divine Father confers the power of the gift of His spirit, are the only ones that can do these things; and even then, it cannot rightfully be said that such individuals do these things, as it is the Holy Spirit of our Divine Father in heaven doing these things through them. The gift of God's spirit is the gift of acting as a medium or conductor by which you become the agent through which God's spirit acts in all the holy offices in the Church, as every one that God so chooses has his special work which is diversified according to the offices; and two persons seldom receive it in the same degree and for the same purposes, as the gifts of the Holy Spirit are numerous and diversified.

CHAPTER XXI 

Baptism in the "Name of Jesus Christ" is the symbol of the efficacy, regeneration, sanctification and cleasing power of Christ's blood in washing away or purging the believers from their sins. It also represents the believers' confession of faith in Jesus Christ as their Lord, Savior, Redeemer and Justifier; and of their dependence upon Him as their only means of salvation. Christ Jesus is the way, the truth, and the life and no one can come unto the Father but by reason of His vicarious sacrificial atonement. "His precious body and blood is that blessed bread from heaven of which if a man eat worthily thereof he shall never die but is passed from death unto life eternal and immortality."

It is the command of Jesus that repentance and forgiveness of sins should be preached in His name among all the nations as His vicarious atonement for the penitent sinner is the only means provided by our Divine Father in heaven whereby man must be saved. 

Were it not for the vicarious atoning sacrifice of the blood of Jesus Christ for our sins, even the penitent sinner would be lost; but the combining of the two elements of repentance toward God and faith in the atoning blood of Jesus Christ our redemption is effected. It is through the atoning blood of Jesus Christ that the penitent sinner obtains forgiveness of sins of which baptism in His name points out the manner in symbolical form just how the believers' sins are cleansed away. It is by being baptized, washed, cleansed, purified, sanctified and healed by the blood of Jesus Christ that the penitent sinner becomes a child of God by adoption. It is through repentance of sin and active faith in the atoning blood of Jesus Christ as Savior, Lord, and Redeemer that the penitent sinner's sins are cleansed away and he made at-one-ment with God.

Because of sin we are mortal beings and subject to death which would be final had not Jesus Christ died as a vicarious sacrifice or substitute for us to relieve us from the penalty of the law of sin and death; but through His death as a vicarious sacrifice for us we are to become dead to sin; for as many as are baptized into Jesus Christ, are baptized through faith into His death when they are baptized in 420

His name, so that like as Christ was raised from the dead by the spirit of His Divine Father in heaven, even so we also who follow Him in faith believing we shall likewise be raised at Christ's coming according to the Divine promises. "Now, if we be dead with Christ through His vicarious atonement, we shall also live with Him, knowing that Christ being raised from the dead dieth no more; death has no more dominion over 

Him; for in that He died, He died unto sin once; but in that He liveth He liveth unto God eternally. In like manner we should reckon ourselves to be dead unto sin that we might live unto God through Jesus Christ our Lord."

Being baptized in the "Name of Jesus Christ," is the most apt figure of our death, burial, and resurrection through Him, as Christ chose that His followers should be immersed in water in representation of His death, burial and resurrection. 

Jesus says: "He whom God has sent speaketh the words of God; for God giveth not His spirit by measure unto Him, as the Divine Father loveth His Son and hath given all things into His hand. He that believeth on the Son of God hath everlasting life, and he that believeth not on Him shall not see life; but the wrath of God abides on him."

There was always complete harmony between Jesus Christ and His Divine Father, as Christ chose His will and acts to be always subject to His Father, the author of His being, doctrine and works; and all that He is, has, and does are in perfect conformity to the will of His Divine Father. O Israel, the Lord thy God is but the one Divine Father; and thou shalt love Him with all thy heart, soul, mind and strength, and Him only shalt thou serve;" and the second commandment is like this, "Thou shalt love thy neighbor as thyself." On these two commandments hang all the Law and the prophets. 

Why does our Divine Father in heaven require absolute and unqualified Divine worship to Himself alone? It is because no other person, spirit or being possesses Divine qualities, as all others are but creatures and objects of His creation and cannot have or possess Divine attributes; but attributes only such as creatures possess which are subordinate to and dependent upon the will and spirit of their Divine Father for their existence of being and powers and all that they are and have.

THE END.
